title: Colts release QB Jones, turn to Richardson for next start
summary: The Colts have released quarterback Daniel Jones and are turning to Anthony Richardson Sr. to start going forward, coach Shane Steichen announced.
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts have released quarterback Daniel Jones , coach Shane Steichen announced Friday.
Anthony Richardson Sr . will serve as the starting quarterback, Steichen said. Richardson, the Colts' pick at No. 4 in the 2023 draft, will make his first start since the 2024 season when Indianapolis hosts the New York Giants on Nov. 29.
The move comes after the Colts benched Jones during their 26-3 loss to the Houston Texans on Thursday night. Jones was 12-for-27 for 144 yards with an interception as the Colts (3-8) lost for the sixth time in seven games. Richardson entered the game with about seven minutes left and didn't complete either of his passes.
Of 31 QBR-qualified quarterbacks this season, Daniel Jones ranks last in Total QBR, yards per attempt and yards per dropback while leading the NFL in interceptions.
"Can't say enough good things about Daniel. Just the ultimate competitor, ultimate teammate, the toughness that he brought to our football team," Steichen told reporters. "... Gave this organization everything he had."
Steichen said Jones did not ask for his release and that the Colts decided to make the move for "where we're at in our season."
Jones had returned to the Colts for the 2026 season after signing a two-year, $88 million contract in March that included $50 million fully guaranteed at signing. He had led the Colts to an 8-2 start last season before sustaining a hairline fibula fracture and struggling before ultimately tearing his Achilles in the other leg.
This year, Jones had thrown for 1,974 yards with seven touchdowns and 13 interceptions. The Colts largely steered toward the start of a rebuild when they moved on from multiple former Pro Bowlers ahead of last week's trade deadline to acquire draft picks.
Jones had been considered a possible trade candidate for the Colts, but they chose to retain him at the deadline -- then released him two games later.
He will be subject to waivers through Monday afternoon but could sign with another team if he clears them.
Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

title: Rams' suspended Nacua has MCL surgery, likely done for regular season
summary: Rams WR Puka Nacua, who is serving a three-game suspension while on IR, had surgery on his MCL and likely will miss at least the rest of the regular season.
full_text:
LOS ANGELES -- Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua , who is serving a three-game suspension while on injured reserve, will likely miss at least the rest of the regular season after having surgery on his MCL, coach Sean McVay said Friday.
McVay said Nacua will miss "a couple months" after having the procedure Tuesday. Nacua suffered an MCL sprain and turf toe injuries on the Rams' final offensive snap of their Week 9 victory over the Washington Commanders and was placed on IR on Nov. 12.
"There's a lot of thought and conversations that go into whether you're going to [have surgery] and what's the best plan of action for return to performance for him, not exclusive to this year, but for his career moving forward," McVay said. "And so he was very thorough and deliberate about that, but I did think that this was a possibility.
• March 2026: Woman in Los Angeles files lawsuit accusing Nacua of "unprovoked antisemitic statement," biting her on shoulder. Nacua denies, later enters rehab center. • Nov. 8: Suffers PCL/MCL sprain, turf toe injury in game vs. Washington. • Nov. 12: Nacua placed on injured reserve, to miss at least next 4 games. • Nov. 19: NFL suspends Nacua for three games for personal conduct policy violation. WR to serve ban while on IR; eligible for reinstatement Dec. 14. • Nov. 20: Announced Nacua had MCL surgery on Nov. 17 and is likely out for at least the rest of the regular season. NFL unaware of surgery when it imposed suspension, source tells Adam Schefter.
"I knew that that was a serious injury that he sustained, whether he got it fixed or not with the shot that he took to his knee, he had the toe injury. And so in my mind, this was kind of always a direction that we had to plan upon anyways."
The NFL on Thursday announced Nacua has been suspended for three games for violating the league's personal conduct policy. The suspension came after a woman in Los Angeles filed a lawsuit in March alleging Nacua made an "unprovoked antisemitic statement" and bit her on the shoulder.
The NFL was unaware that Nacua had already undergone surgery when it imposed its suspension, a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter on Friday.
"Based on the steps and the protocols that took place, [the suspension was] something that we thought was a possibility," McVay said. "And it's an unfortunate thing. It's a learning op. It's something that obviously happened a while ago that there's been a lot of discussion and dialogue behind the scenes and we'll learn from it, we'll grow."
In seven games this season, Nacua had 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns.
His injuries happened on a third-down play with the Rams attempting to end the game with a conversion. Nacua rushed for 5 yards but took a hard hit and briefly stayed on the ground before walking off the field.
When asked whether Nacua could return for a possible playoff run, McVay said, "That would be getting way far ahead, so haven't thought about that."
Nacua is playing on the final season of his rookie deal and is scheduled to be an unrestricted free agent this offseason.
author: Sarah Barshop

title: Stroud stays in 'groove' with another 3-TD night in Texans' blowout of Colts
summary: C.J. Stroud had his third straight game with at least three touchdown passes and led the Texans to their fourth win in six games Thursday night against the Colts.
full_text:
HOUSTON -- C.J. Stroud continued his resurgent season Thursday night, tossing three touchdowns in the Houston Texans ' 26-3 win over the Indianapolis Colts .
Stroud had his third straight game with at least three touchdown passes, adding 194 passing yards and an interception to post a passer rating of 118.2. He has reached at least three passing touchdowns in four out of his past five games, totaling 16 touchdowns and four interceptions in that stretch.
"I knew what type of player I could be in this league," Stroud said. "And to just get in that groove and have a rhythm, it's been amazing. Honestly, I would be lying to you if I said it didn't feel good."
The Texans (4-6) have won four of their past six games as they look to become the second team in NFL history to reach the playoffs after an 0-4 start (1992 Chargers , then in San Diego). Houston has a 38% chance to make the playoffs after Thursday's win, according to ESPN Analytics, and will host the Baltimore Ravens next week.
A big reason for the Texans' recent bounce-back is because of Stroud's play, but he isn't taking all of the credit.
"I'm very grateful for this opportunity to even play in the NFL," Stroud said. "People probably think I'm crazy for always saying that, but, man, I really did not expect my life to be like this. It's nothing but the grace of God that I'm sitting up here and to be playing the way that I am.
"It's nothing but the credit to the team. Just the way the defense prepared us in training camp. The way the offensive line's been blocking their tail off giving me a shot. The way the receivers have been running routes, getting open."
Defensive Player of the Year contender Will Anderson Jr. , who had a sack for a safety and two tackles for loss, had the highest praise for Stroud, who he said has "continued to take that leap every year."
"He's a top quarterback in this league, no matter what his year may have looked like," Anderson said. "Trust me, it's 32 other teams that would love to have C.J. Stroud on their team. So, I'm just happy he's here."
Stroud got back on track after a shaky performance in a Week 10 loss to the Cleveland Browns . Even though he threw for three touchdowns, the offense struggled in the second half, totaling only seven points after jumping to a 17-0 first-half lead.
Through 10 games in his fourth season, Stroud is up to 2,656 passing yards, 22 touchdowns and only four interceptions with a 103.6 passer rating. He is on pace to throw for 4,515 passing yards and 37 touchdowns, both of which would be career highs.
Texans coach DeMeco Ryans attributed Stroud's success to his offseason work.
"All of that is paying dividends now from the work prior to these moments," Ryans said. "He's been ready for these moments, and he's executing at a high level in these moments, scoring the points that we need to score, making the plays we need to make. Just keeping the offense out there on the field, making great decisions with the football. That's probably the one thing I'm most proud of him making great decisions."
author: DJ Bien-Aime

title: Ravens send Humphrey home, say he'll be inactive Sunday for 'criminals' comment
summary: The Ravens have sent cornerback Marlon Humphrey home from the facility, and he will be inactive for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
full_text:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey was sent home from the team facility and will be inactive for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers following a recent derogatory comment he made about the city of Baltimore on his podcast, coach Jesse Minter announced Thursday.
Minter said the punishment is for one game only for Humphrey, who will not practice the rest of the week.
The Ravens' discipline comes one day after Humphrey apologized for his remarks.
• Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey will not play Sunday against the Panthers, coach Jesse Minter announced Thursday, after the cornerback's quip on his most recent podcast that Baltimore was "best at making criminals."
• Humphrey apologized for his comment Wednesday after he received heavy fan backlash on social media.
• Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott said Wednesday that Humphrey's apology was "not enough" and added that, "Baltimore is a city full of young Black boys who look to the Ravens as a beacon of light in their lives and to have someone that looks like them who wears a Baltimore Ravens jersey relegate them to becoming criminals cuts deeper."
• Humphrey, 30, is the longest tenured defensive player on the Ravens. Selected by Baltimore with the No. 16 pick in the 2017 NFL draft, he has been to four Pro Bowls, the most by a Ravens defensive back.
"He's very remorseful. I think he understands that words mean a lot, especially to people in this city," Minter said before Thursday's practice. "When you say something like that, it's not a reflection of our team and our organization and how we want to operate."
On an episode of "The Marlon Humphrey Show" released Wednesday, Humphrey took a swipe at the city when asked what Baltimore was best at making.
After first mentioning "The Star-Spangled Banner" and National Bohemian beer, Humphrey quipped, "They're best at making criminals."
After Wednesday's practice, Humphrey said he regretted those remarks.
"I would like to apologize for some comments on my podcast I had to the city of Baltimore," Humphrey said. "As you guys know, I've been here my whole career. Spent lots of offseasons here. Welcomed a son here and I'm an investor in the city. And obviously, I do know the effect that words have and just like to apologize for those comments."
Humphrey received heavy fan backlash on social media Wednesday afternoon. The podcast episode featuring Humphrey's "criminals" comment has since been deleted from his YouTube page.
Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott acknowledged Humphrey's apology in a statement posted to social media, but noted, "a verbal apology is not enough. Baltimore is a city full of young Black boys who look to the Ravens as a beacon of light in their lives and to have someone that looks like them who wears a Baltimore Ravens jersey relegate them to becoming criminals cuts deeper.
"I wonder how he would feel if prominent Baltimoreans used their platforms to imply that Baltimore once produced great defensive backs but we have recently lost our way."
Scott then added, "They wouldn't do that because our team and city are supposed to be united as one. Baltimore versus the world."
Scott concluded his post by inviting Humphrey to sit down with him and some Baltimore citizens "who have re-entered into our community and are now preventing others from making the mistakes they made."
Humphrey, 30, is in his 10th season with Baltimore and is the longest-tenured defensive player on the Ravens. The No. 16 selection in the 2017 draft by Baltimore, Humphrey has been to four Pro Bowls, which are the most by a Ravens cornerback.
Minter spoke with the 10-player leadership council to inform them of his decision to send Humphrey home.
"He did it with conviction and he did what he felt was best for the team," Ravens middle linebacker Roquan Smith said.
Before departing the team facility on Thursday, Humphrey did not talk to his teammates.
"I was definitely surprised at the choice words," Ravens offensive tackle Ronnie Stanley said. "And I think Marlon is unapologetically himself and he's always been like that since he's been here. But at the same time, I think he's taking a step back and realized the maturity that he needs to take to say things the right way."
Those inside the Ravens' locker room commented Thursday that Humphrey has been a good teammate and plays hard in games but he has "a unique" personality.
"In this day and age, I think it's important for these guys to understand that, yes, you have freedom of speech," Ravens defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver said. "You can say what it is you want to say, on your phone, on your platform, whatever that is. But that doesn't give you freedom of consequence."
Humphrey's punishment comes at a time when the Ravens (4-6) are reeling after losing five straight games. With Humphrey out, the Ravens will increase snaps for Chidobe Awuzie and T.J. Tampa .
Players acknowledged the news surrounding Humphrey has been talked about in the locker room, but they hope it won't become a distraction.
"I think everyone's focused on getting the win," Stanley said. "We have enough things to worry about. It's something that came up one day and we talked about it, but today no one's talking about it."
author: Jamison Hensley

title: Sources: Tom Brady buys shares in Chelsea after Birmingham exit
summary: Seven-time Super Bowl champion quarterback Tom Brady has invested in Chelsea soccer club, sources confirmed to ESPN and NFL Network.
full_text:
Seven-time Super Bowl champion quarterback Tom Brady has bought shares in Chelsea soccer club, sources confirmed to ESPN and NFL Network.
The NFL legend left the ownership group of second-tier English club Birmingham City earlier this month after becoming a minority owner with a 3.3% stake.
Defense attorney Alex Spiro is part of Brady's ownership group and helped negotiate the deal.
Brady had also held a position on the club's advisory board via a partnership with Birmingham's owner, Knighthead Capital Management, headed by his friend and business partner Tom Wagner.
Todd Boehly and fellow co-owner Mark Walter sold their stakes in Chelsea this past September in a deal that gives Clearlake Capital full control of the English Premier League club.
Private equity firm Clearlake, led by Behdad Eghbali and Jose E. Feliciano, previously owned a 61.5% stake in Chelsea, while U.S. businessmen Walter and Boehly each owned 12.83%. Swiss philanthropist Hansjörg Wyss, who also owned a 12.83% stake, remains a partner in the ownership group.
The consortium bought Chelsea for £2.5 billion ($3.3 billion) in 2022 with a further £1.75 billion ($2.3 billion) committed to investment in the club after former owner Roman Abramovich was sanctioned because of alleged ties to Russia President Vladimir Putin following the country's invasion of Ukraine.
The Financial Times reported that Walter and Boehly will receive £950 million ($1.3 billion) for their combined stake in a deal that values the club at £5 billion ($6.7 billion) including debt.
Neither Chelsea nor Clearlake Capital has replied to ESPN's request for comment about Brady's purchase of shares.
Brady purchased a 5% minority stake in the Las Vegas Raiders in 2024 after NFL owners unanimously approved the deal.
ESPN's Adam Schefter and James Olley as well as NFL Network's Ian Rapoport contributed to this report.
author: ESPN

title: 99 problems? Bears DT Simmons says knee injury 'ain't one,' expects to play
summary: Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons said the knee injury that held him to limited participation in practice this week wouldn't keep him from playing Sunday against the Saints.
full_text:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- Chicago Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons dispelled concerns about his availability for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints after a knee injury held him to limited participation in practice.
"Like 99 problems, but this ain't one," he said, referencing his No. 99 jersey and a popular T-shirt that Bears fans created when he was traded to Chicago. "I'll be out there Sunday."
Simmons' remarks came after he missed Tuesday's practice and showed up on the team's injury report as a limited participant on Wednesday (an estimation) and Thursday. He sported a brace on his left knee when he returned to the field Thursday.
"Things happen in this league. It's kind of like when I put the elbow brace on, there was a lot of questions," Simmons said, referring to his 2024 ulnar collateral ligament injury with the Titans. "But I feel fine, practiced today. Practice went great. I've been seeing a lot of things on Twitter about the '99 problems.' That won't be a problem this Sunday."
Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen said he does not believe Simmons' knee injury will impact his availability against the Saints.
"I don't anticipate any issues with him," Allen said.
The Bears sent their 2027 and 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fourth-rounder to Tennessee on Oct. 29 in exchange for the All-Pro defensive tackle. Chicago also received a 2028 fifth-round pick.
Simmons had an immediate impact on the Bears' defense upon his arrival. He logged 87% of defensive snaps in his debut at Seattle, where he tallied six tackles, two tackles for loss, a sack and a defended pass in Chicago's 34-17 win. He followed that performance with another four tackles (one TFL), one sack and a defended pass in the Bears' Week 9 win against the Buccaneers when he played 97% of defensive snaps.
The Bears have allowed 4.5 yards per play with Simmons on the field (in 110 snaps) compared with 11.4 yards per play when he's not in the game (10 snaps). In two games, Simmons has faced a double-team on a team-high 24 pass rushes.
"With him commanding that much attention, it opens up some one-on-one opportunities for some other guys and I think some other guys have benefited from that," Allen said. "I think that's a positive thing that we have. I think the more really good players you have that have the ability to win their matchup -- whether that's a matchup in coverage, a matchup in the run game, a matchup in the passing game -- winning these one-on-one matchups are big in our league.
"Obviously when we can get him in a one-on-one, it's a great thing for us and a lot of times the offense is going to give a lot of attention to him, and so some other guys are going to have to step up."
Bears general manager Ryan Poles described Simmons' addition as "a shot in the arm" for a defense that was forced to work around injury constraints along the defensive line to generate pressure on opposing quarterbacks.
Since Simmons' arrival in Week 8, the Bears' defense has recorded a blitz rate 20 percentage points lower across 69 dropbacks with the defensive tackle on the field, blitzing on 21.7% of those plays compared with 41.7% of the 230 dropbacks with him off the field, according to Next Gen Stats.
Simmons' off-field impact has been felt as strongly as his contributions in games. When asked Thursday whether the Bears' defense needed a leader like Simmons after seeing the response since his arrival, Allen agreed.
"Well, maybe to that extent, yeah," Allen said. "And yet, look, we've always had a group of guys that come in and work and do the things that they're being asked to do to perform at a certain level. I think he just accentuates that."
If Simmons records a sack against the Saints, he will tie the longest streak of his career at three games.
Coming off a Week 10 bye, Chicago is expecting the return of running back Kyle Monangai , who missed five games with turf toe and a thumb injury. Monangai has been a full participant in practice along with wide receiver Luther Burden III , who is out of the concussion protocol, and cornerback Malik Muhammad (toe).
Nickel corner Kyler Gordon is the only player on the 53-man roster who has not practiced this week as he recovers from an injury to his left shoulder sustained in Week 9. Coach Ben Johnson classified Gordon's injury as "day-to-day."
author: Courtney Cronin

title: Cowboys DC Parker says he briefly mulled quitting after losing playcalling role
summary: Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker said he briefly considered leaving the team after informed he was being stripped of playcalling responsibilities.
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- Stripped of his playcalling responsibilities, Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker said he briefly considered leaving the team after being informed of the decision by head coach Brian Schottenheimer.
"Initially in your mind, you're thinking about all the things, and in my opinion, that would've been running from it," Parker said Thursday. "At the end of the day, I've got a job to do, and my job is to be the defensive coordinator of the Dallas Cowboys. Whether that is calling plays on Sunday, obviously that's not the case anymore, but on Monday, on Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday and whatever day we play, there is a focus level that I need to have. There's a contribution that I still have to be able to maintain. That is regardless of feelings and anything else. And I think that our focus is aligned in the building, No. 1, with me and [Mike Pettine], [and] No. 2, with the staff and with the players."
Parker said it would be "hypocritical" of him to leave when he has told players they were going to get less playing time but to stay ready, pointing to a conversation he had with second-year pass rusher Donovan Ezeiruaku a few weeks ago.
"When I saw Easy, he's like, 'Hey, remember what you told me?' because I told him, 'Look, this is changing at the start of the game. This has not changed the second, third, fourth quarter. It doesn't change anything that we expect from you when you go out on that field,'" Parker said. "So if I'm telling Easy that, how can I not tell myself that? And it's not about me. It's about this team. So that's what we're focused on, man. We're focused on winning. We're focused on improvement. Hopefully this is a spark for us to make sure that we get on the right track that we have worked to do, and that's what we're going to continue to work for."
In 10 games with Parker as the playcaller, the Cowboys' defense is last in the league in total yards, rushing yards and third-down defense. Dallas is 30th in points allowed. In last week's loss to the San Francisco 49ers , the Cowboys allowed 584 yards, the most given up in a home game in team history.
"Just overall we haven't executed well," Parker said. "We haven't tackled like we should and like we know we're capable of. We've done it in waves. We have not done it consistently. I think the overall thing would be just the consistency of it. Starting slowly, starting fast and sustainability of those things. So not really to get into the weeds of the exact, every single level of everything call-wise and all those type of things, but I think just overall we weren't consistent enough and that starts with me."
The Cowboys have turned to Mike Pettine to take over playcalling for a defense that ranks 30th or worse in several key categories this season.
Pettine joined the Cowboys as a senior defensive assistant prior to Week 5 because of his previous relationship with Parker. He brought Parker into the NFL with the Green Bay Packers .
Parker said their friendship does not change because of the switch in roles. Parker is still leading the meetings.
"Our process throughout the week on Tuesday with how we plan and game plan was the exact same, walk-throughs, scripting, all those things," Parker said. "I think there's been obviously more collaboration with Pett on some of those things because he's going to be calling it on Sunday. So there's a certain element of input with the playcaller, with certain situations, how things need to come out, communication with the green dots, some of those various topics. Some of those things were altered a little bit, but overall we've had a clean operation."
Parker, who at 34 is the youngest defensive coordinator in team history, called it a "significant" disappointment but views a step back as something that could help him improve.
Schottenheimer said on numerous occasions that he believes Parker has a future with the Cowboys. Does Parker believe that?
"We'll cross that bridge when we get there," he said.
author: Todd Archer

title: New blood test has potential to detect CTE in the living, studies find
summary: A new blood test shows potential to detect advanced stages of chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) in the living, according to two recent published studies.
full_text:
A new blood test shows potential to detect advanced stages of chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) in the living, according to two recent studies published in the medical journal JAMA.
Scientists researching the connection between football and brain damage have long described diagnosing CTE in the living as the holy grail. To date, the disease, which has been linked to repeated blows to the head from football and other contact sports, has been diagnosable only after death.
One study, published Thursday by researchers at Boston University and Banner Health, was based on a small sample of former American football players who donated blood while alive. After those players died, autopsies of their brains determined they had CTE. The researchers then identified a CTE marker by examining the levels of a specific protein in the blood samples.
Michael Alosco, the co-director of clinical research at Boston University's CTE Center and co-senior author of the study, called the test a "game changer" in the ability to diagnose the degenerative brain illness in the living.
"I'm cautiously optimistic that we can really understand this finding and move it forward in the next five years or so," Alosco told ESPN.
However, the Boston University and Banner Health test showed promise only in identifying advanced stages of CTE during life -- not in the early stages.
The severity of CTE increases as it progresses. In the early stages, it often tends to be symptom-free, while patients in advanced stages present with symptoms such as memory loss, confusion, depression, irritability and severe mood swings.
The study released Thursday examined 21 deceased football players: 12 who played professionally, seven who played through college and two who played only through the high school level.
Autopsies showed that most of the former professional players, along with four college players and one high school player, had advanced-stage CTE. The blood tests showed a higher concentration of the identified protein, confirming the diagnosis.
Five players who had both CTE and Alzheimer's disease showed the highest levels of the protein in their blood.
"We are still in the discovery phase and it's a small sample size," Alosco said in a separate statement. "But if future studies validate these findings, this blood test will allow us to detect CTE with a high level of accuracy and open the doors to clinical trials and treatment."
In a separate study published in JAMA last Friday, a research group from the Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis also identified the same blood biomarker. That study was based on 11 cases.
Scientists have been trying for years to detect CTE in the living. In 2017, researchers said they used a brain scan to identify the disease in a former NFL player while he was still alive, and attempts to use scans as a diagnostic tool are ongoing.
So far, no tests or treatments specific to CTE have been approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
While the recent findings are a major milestone, the possibility of a CTE test also raises complicated questions for players at all levels of the game, from pee wee to the pros, and their families. Among the potential issues is whether players, particularly those in the NFL, will want to know if they have the disease while still in the league.
Last summer, ESPN asked more than 30 current and former NFL players about a range of CTE-related topics, including whether they would take a test for CTE if one existed.
"Yeah, I would," Washington Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota told ESPN. "I think because, at the end of the day, it gives insight to the rest of the NFL, to college kids, to high school kids of what we're getting ourselves into. Then yeah, absolutely."
Said Minnesota Vikings safety Joshua Metellus : "I probably wouldn't want [the test] while I'm in the league, because I think it'll change the way I play. But I know there's a lot of guys who are very curious and would like to know."
author: Shwetha Surendran and Mark Fainaru-Wada

title: Titans' Ridley facing misdemeanor assault charge over airport incident
summary: Titans wide receiver Calvin Ridley is facing a misdemeanor assault charge as a result of a Nov. 7 incident at Nashville International Airport.
full_text:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- Titans wide receiver Calvin Ridley is facing a misdemeanor assault charge as a result of a Nov. 7 incident at Nashville International Airport, according to records obtained Thursday from the Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority.
The Class B misdemeanor assault charge involves intentional or knowing physical contact that a reasonable person would consider extremely offensive or provocative. It carries a penalty of up to six months in jail and a fine of up to $500.
Ridley is due in Metropolitan General Sessions Court on Dec. 7.
Ridley gave his account of the incident to the media on Nov. 11, saying he took his truck keys from an airport valet attendant who had refused to give them to him because he didn't have the valet ticket. He said he had shown the attendant multiple forms of identification and a photo as proof of ownership of the truck.
According to Ridley, when he took the keys, the attendant yelled that Ridley had broken his finger.
The Titans said they have been in communication with the Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority.
Ridley signed a four-year, $92 million contract with the Titans in 2024. The veteran receiver has six receptions for 91 yards through seven games this season.
author: Turron Davenport

title: ❤️ Bengals pay tribute to Fiona the hippo after her death
summary: The world-famous hippopotamus passed away Thursday after ingesting a hat that made its way into her enclosure.
full_text:
After news broke Thursday that the Cincinnati Zoo's famous hippo, Fiona, had died, the Queen City's sports teams were quick to pay tribute.
Fiona's death came as a result of health complications following her swallowing of a child's knit cap that had made it into her enclosure. According to zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley, the hat entered Fiona's habitat after it was tossed into the air by a visitor and caught by a ceiling fan that catapulted it through a small opening above the area's viewing windows.
"Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn't fight anymore," Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike said . "She was dearly loved by her Zoo family and countless others around the world. Her loss will be felt deeply by so many."
The 9-year-old Nile hippopotamus rose to fame in 2017, when she was born at the Cincinnati Zoo six weeks premature, requiring around-the-clock care to survive. Survive she did, though, becoming beloved as both she and her story grew.
Each of Cincinnati's three major professional sports teams took to social media after news of Fiona's death broke to honor her legacy as an icon of the city.

Forever an icon.

author: ESPN

title: Our guide to every NFL Week 11 game: Matchup previews, predictions, picks and nuggets
summary: Joe Burrow vs. Jayden Daniels? Fernando Mendoza vs. Bo Nix? There are 12 more games in Week 11, and we have picks, predictions and more for all of them.
full_text:
Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season is here! The Eagles are hosting the Steelers in the Battle of Pennsylvania, and Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins makes his second start against the 49ers in two weeks. The Chargers will face off against the Jets, looking for their second win on a short week, and Raiders rookie Fernando Mendoza will get his second career start when Las Vegas meets Denver. The Jaguars look to keep rolling against the Giants, and the Ravens travel to Carolina.
We're here to get you ready for the action. First, our NFL Nation reporters take you inside the locker room with the best thing they heard this week, and ESPN Research provides a key stat to know. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder makes a bold prediction for each matchup, fantasy analyst Eric Moody shares fantasy football intel and betting analyst Pamela Maldonado hits betting insights for each contest. We also have Football Power Index (FPI) game projections, and Maldonado, Moody and Walder all give us final score picks for every game.
Let's get into the full Week 11 slate, which culminates with a "Monday Night Football" matchup between the Bengals and Commanders on ESPN . (Game times are Sunday unless otherwise noted, and all odds are via DraftKings.)

title: Five offseason additions who are working out well with their new teams -- and five who aren't
summary: Kenneth Walker III and Devin Lloyd look great with their new teams in 2026.
full_text:
Everyone loves the NFL offseason hot stove. Fans get super excited about outside players joining their favorite team, whether through trade or free agency. Those holes on the roster have finally been filled by wily veterans!
Unfortunately, those moves don't always work out. Some players excel in new surroundings, bringing strong production. Others struggle with their new situation, confirming why they were made available in the first place.
Here's a look at five players who are working well with their new teams and five who are not. How are the successful new players helping their teams? Which teams find themselves on the hook for bad contracts? Let's start with a quarterback who has helped two teams this season.
Jump to a section: Moves that have worked out Moves that have not yet worked out
How he got there: Signed a one-year, $11.3 million contract with the Raiders before being traded to the Vikings on Nov. 10 2026 stat to know: 65.0 QBR (10th out of 31 qualifying QBs) Comparable 2025 stat: 47.6 QBR (not enough passes to qualify)
This is a bit of a special case, because Cousins is thriving in his second new city of the season. Or perhaps we should say one new and one old city, because Cousins played for Minnesota from 2018 to 2023.
His performance this season is further proof that it takes a long time to recover from an Achilles tear. Cousins tore his Achilles in 2023 on the last play of his previous stint with the Vikings. He went to Atlanta in 2024 and was completely immobile on plays such as rollouts and play-action fakes. He put up a career-low QBR of 47.0 and lost the starting job to then-rookie Michael Penix Jr . toward the end of the season. In 2025, Cousins came in after Penix was hurt and looked a bit better. He was able to avoid turnovers, but his yards per attempt average dropped from 7.7 in 2024 to 6.4. It resulted in his QBR virtually being the same as it was the previous season.
But Cousins is back to being his old self this season. His yards per attempt is up to 7.4, and his 22 passing touchdowns rank second in the NFL. His sack rate of 3.9% is also the lowest of any starting quarterback.
The Raiders were able to get four wins out of Cousins (one more than they earned all last season) until they were ready to transition to rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza . Then they got an additional third-round pick by trading Cousins to Minnesota. Cousins won his first start with the Vikings in Week 10 and dramatically improved their chances of winning the Super Bowl by taking Minnesota's offense from horrific to slightly above average.
How he got there: Signed a three-year, $43.1 million contract 2026 stat to know: 1.66 rushing yards over expected per attempt (second out of 45 qualifying RBs) Comparable 2025 stat: 0.25 RYOE/attempt (30th out of 51 qualifying RBs)
Do running backs matter? Well, special running backs are only special when they get enough blocking to do great things. Last season, the Chiefs had the blocking but didn't have a back who could fully take advantage. This season, they have two in Walker and rookie Emmett Johnson .
Walker has always been good at breaking tackles, but he's in another universe this season. According to FTN charting , Walker leads the league with a 35.2% avoided tackle rate and is third with 3.14 yards after contact per carry.
The biggest question about Walker in Kansas City was whether he could handle the workload of a clear No. 1 running back after being in a committee in Seattle. Although Walker missed last week with a groin injury , he's on pace for 318 carries, which would easily exceed his previous career high of 228 set as a rookie in 2022.
How he got there: Signed a three-year, $42.4 million contract 2026 stats to know: minus-12.2% DVOA (63rd out of 79 qualifying WRs), 10.8 yards per target Comparable 2025 stats: 45.1% DVOA (first out of 58 qualifying WRs), 6.0 yards per target
Evans had a difficult final season in Tampa Bay. Oft-injured QB Baker Mayfield had a hard time getting Evans the ball in places where the receiver could excel. He hit career lows in yards per reception (12.3) and catch rate (48%). Last year was the first season of his career in which he failed to reach 1,000 receiving yards.
Evans has been refreshed and renewed in San Francisco's powerful offense. His catch rate is up to 69%, which would be the highest of his career. He's also averaging 15.6 yards per reception. He had 23 first downs on 62 targets in 2025; this season, he's up to 25 first downs on only 39 targets so far.
The only problem is the Achilles tendinitis that has sidelined Evans since Week 6. The 49ers are being very careful so they can have Evans back and 100 percent for their playoff run. They are hoping he can return in the next couple of weeks and continue to demonstrate why he was such a good signing.
How he got there: Signed a two-year, $13 million contract (up to $17 million with bonuses) 2026 stat to know: Tied for lead among LBs with 20 defeats Comparable 2025 stat: 15 defeats in 13 games
Williams was a first-team All-Pro for the Jets in 2023 but is still not as well known as his younger brother, Cowboys defensive tackle Quinnen Williams . Quincy had only 12 starts for the Jets last season and turned 30 in August, so it was reasonable to assume that he was at the tail end of his career.

The Browns brought him in on a reasonable contract and stuck him next to Defensive Rookie of the Year Carson Schwesinger , and Williams has been an outstanding playmaker in that role. I keep track of a stat called defeats, which measures defensive splash plays. It combines tackles for loss, turnovers and any play that prevents a third- or fourth-down conversion. Williams has 20 defeats so far this season, tied with the Vikings' Blake Cashman for the lead among all linebackers. (Quinnen leads all players with 24.)
Williams is known for speed and has been excellent in pass coverage, with four passes defensed and 15 pass tackles, which prevented a successful yardage gain despite a reception. Opposing running backs have fewer than 20 receiving yards per game against the Browns.
How he got there: Signed a three-year, $42 million contract 2026 stats to know: 16 defeats, three interceptions, average run tackle at 3.3 yards Comparable 2025 stats: 14 defeats, five interceptions, average run tackle at 4.0 yards
Unlike Williams, Lloyd entered the 2026 season with big expectations. He was one of the NFL's top linebackers last season and signed the largest contract of any free agent off-ball linebacker this past offseason. So far, Lloyd has lived up to that contract.
Entering the season, it was hard to imagine Lloyd getting five interceptions again, but his Week 10 interception already puts him at three. Lloyd already has more defeats than he did last season, too, and he was part of two combined tackles to prevent Saints running back Audric Estime from converting on third-and-short last week. With the NFC South still up for grabs, the Panthers are counting on more big plays from Lloyd to get them back into the postseason.
How he got there: Acquired from the Dolphins along with a 2026 fourth-round pick for 2026 first-, third- and fourth-round picks 2026 stat to know: minus-17.6% receiving DVOA (52nd out of 58 qualifying WRs) Comparable 2025 stat: 11.6% receiving DVOA (19th out of 79 qualifying WRs)
Trading for Waddle was supposed to unlock the Broncos' intermediate passing game and help Bo Nix complete passes over the middle. Instead, Waddle has been victim of Nix's struggles. Right now, Nix ranks 26th in DVOA on passes over the middle and 28th on intermediate passes (10-19 air yards). His numbers in those areas are a little better throwing to Waddle than to other receivers, but they are still not good. Nix is also…
author: Aaron Schatz

title: Eight stadiums, seven countries, four continents: NFL field director has earned a break
summary: Nick Pappas is the man charged with making sure international venues are up to standard to host NFL games.
full_text:
Nick Pappas will soon finally go home.
When the NFL's field director steps on a flight Monday night at Benito Juarez International Airport in Mexico City bound for Atlanta, it'll be the last leg of the longest stretch of travel he's done in his role overseeing the fields for all the league's international games.
Eleven weeks. Nine games. Eight stadiums. Seven fields. Seven countries. Four continents. His first regular-season trip was to Melbourne in September. His last was to Mexico City. In between, Pappas went to Brazil, England, France, Spain and Germany. From the time he left Rio de Janeiro on Sept. 28, the night after the Cowboys-Ravens game, Pappas spent just about two weeks at home with his wife and three kids.
This season -- with an NFL-record nine international games -- was an exhausting stretch for Pappas. He survived on coffee -- lots of it -- and two workouts a day.
"The work, it feels effortless, honestly, at times," Pappas said. "It's obviously, for me, it's being away from my family more than anything. I've got three little kids and a rock star of a wife, so I'm very fortunate to be able to be away and commit my time and put the energy into these games that it deserves and it requires."
And that's just the in-season international travel.
He flies to every international market at least once during the offseason. If the league has been there before, like Munich, London or Madrid, Pappas might go once in an offseason, twice maximum.
But for new cities, such as Rio de Janeiro and Paris this year, he might visit anywhere between six and 12 times over the two years before kickoff. He went to Brazil three times before the game this year. On one of those trips, Pappas flew overnight from Atlanta, landed in the morning, spent about 14 hours at Maracana Stadium and then flew back that night, not even getting a hotel. And because of how far Melbourne is, Pappas went once in December 2024, once over the summer and again in September for the game.
How often he visits a stadium depends on how complex adapting the stadiums to NFL standards will be.
In Melbourne, Pappas was working with a massive field suitable for cricket, rugby and Aussie Rules Football, which made the transition to an NFL field easier than most other venues.
However, the fields had to be extended in Rio de Janeiro and Madrid, where the first couple rows of seats had to be removed, and both required a bit of engineering to shape the surfaces to the exact specifications of the NFL.
Perhaps the biggest challenge for Pappas when it comes to international games is "trying to provide a surface globally that meets our compliance standards first and foremost, but then also meets the preference of our athletes. Preference isn't always captured in compliance."
In an ideal world, Pappas would ship Bermuda grass to every venue that hosts an NFL game. Well, the world isn't ideal. He has to rely on what's available to him either at the stadium or within driving distance, whether that's from a sod farm in Milan that grows the field for the Munich game or the sod farms in Holland or London that he's had to rely upon in the past to fix quick needs.
"We've seen grass get trucked all over the U.S. I mean, the perspective is pretty similar," Pappas said. "It's just there's always challenges when you're going country to country versus state to state, importation from Italy to Germany."
One of the most notable differences Pappas experiences while preparing the international fields is the amount of paint. Grounds crews in foreign countries don't deal with the amount of paint that an NFL field requires.
But that's part of what makes Pappas' job stressful and challenging. He needs to provide a playing surface that is playable and doesn't become a topic of conversation after the game, while looking, aesthetically, like every other NFL field that fans see on TV.
"There's a lot of attention paid to this," said Jeff Miller, the NFL's executive vice president for player health and safety. "Nick's performance is measured in front of the millions of viewers who watch the games. That's not unlike many other aspects of this business. Millions of people are watching the officials. Millions of people are watching the coaches. Millions of people are watching the players. Millions of people are evaluating the league's decision to go play in a particular market, and the field is one of those things.
"So Nick certainly has the mettle to be able to deal with all of that and the expertise and the strength of his convictions to know how to go about doing his job really well."
• How Houston has banded together • Bills defense rolling since bye week • Why are the Colts sticking with Daniel Jones? • Falcons back in a familiar place • Freeling, Hunter top Panthers rookie report
Part of Pappas' responsibilities at the league level is to support all the fields at the 30 NFL stadiums. Each stadium has its own field crew responsible for the daily maintenance, but Pappas oversees compliance and testing and can be a resource for all the grounds crews when various situations arise.
He also handles all of the league events. So, Pappas' season started at the Hall of Fame Game in Canton, Ohio, on Aug. 6 and won't end until Super Bowl LXI in Los Angeles is over. He'll be in Los Angeles for a month before, preparing and maintaining the field for SoFi Stadium's second stint hosting the Super Bowl.
In all, out of the 24 weeks between the week of the Melbourne game and the Super Bowl, Pappas will have been on the road for 15 or 16 of them.
For about seven weeks, Pappas will be home, enjoying time with his kids and wife, relaxing, recovering and getting ready for another grueling stretch.
"His air miles are incredible," said Karl Standley, the head of grounds and surface transitions for Wembley Stadium in London. "Don't know how he does it. I really don't."
author: Josh Weinfuss

title: How Vikings brought Mexico City's elevation to Minnesota
summary: Rather than spending the week in high altitude like Denver, the Vikings trained in a facility at home.
full_text:
EAGAN, Minn. -- The Minnesota Vikings have moved mountains to prepare for their game Sunday night against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City, which sits at an altitude eight times higher than their team headquarters.
Instead of practicing at a higher elevation this week, as the 49ers are doing at the Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, Colorado, the Vikings brought the altitude to them.
About five weeks ago, they constructed a temporary altitude room on the second floor of their training center. Players have been doing weekly cardio workouts in altitude settings as high as 12,000 feet ever since, according to vice president of player health and performance Tyler Williams. The team has also provided access to beet juice, which adds nitrates to the bloodstream and could help circulate oxygen more efficiently, as well as sodium bicarbonate supplements to reduce muscle acidity.
The ideal timeframe for acclimating to extreme altitudes is two weeks, according to Dr. Laura Lewis, the science director of the U.S. Anti-Doping Agency. In other words, neither the Vikings (7-2) nor 49ers (8-1) will be completely adjusted for the conditions they'll encounter Sunday night ( 8:20 p.m. ET, NBC ) at Estadio Azteca, which sits 7,352 feet above sea level -- more than 2,000 feet higher than the most elevated NFL market, Denver at 5,280 feet.
"There's no smoking gun, home run recipe to attack these trips," Williams said. "Every strategy you look at, you slice and dice and find the benefits and the considerations."
After playing back-to-back games in Europe last season, the Vikings were surprised to learn in May that they would have another international game in 2026. Sunday night's game will be the fifth time they have played outside of the United States in the past five seasons. Co-owner Mark Wilf said in training camp that the team did not "seek out" a game in Mexico City, and coach Kevin O'Connell noted the NFL did not provide any advance notice.
Williams led the organization's efforts to craft the travel and preparation plan. The Vikings considered multiple options, including spending the week in a region with higher altitude than in Minnesota, which is anywhere between 850-950 feet above sea level, depending on the precise location. But by late spring, they chose to exchange any additional acclimation benefits for conducting their preparation in their home environment.
They tested some of their plans during an off-site, team-wide workout in Denver prior to the Vikings' Aug. 28 preseason game there. But the decision to remain in Minnesota this week had been based in part on feedback from players who last season spent the week living and practicing in the English countryside, where they were far away from the their usual recovery routines, their personal chefs and bodywork people, and even their own beds.
Williams said he believes "travel fatigue is real" and would have been part of the calculus had the Vikings departed last Sunday's game in Green Bay and spent the week practicing elsewhere.
Said Lewis: "If they aren't going to be able to get that exposure, they're best served making sure that they're in as healthy and rested state as possible before traveling."
In the Vikings' view, altitude is the only substantive difference for a trip to Mexico City compared to what the schedule otherwise would have dictated: a trip to play the 49ers at Levi's Stadium. The flight to Mexico City is about 20 minutes longer, and there is an added benefit of no time change. The Vikings' flight will depart Saturday, as it normally does for Sunday road games, and return immediately after the game.
"If you do go from Green Bay, Wisconsin, to another destination," O'Connell said, "you basically turn that into any other [full] international game. It is an international game. I'm excited to play in Mexico City. I think the fans are going to be phenomenal, but we are playing on Central Time."
The biggest impact of the altitude, Lewis said, will be elevated breathing rates. Oxygen molecules are more spread out, so each breath takes in less oxygen and thus requires the body to breathe more. That increased rate can lead to quicker dehydration. Common practice in those situations, she said, is to expand the time between exertions in a game. In football, that means more substitutions -- something defensive coordinator Brian Flores said he addressed with the defensive staff this week.
"It's certainly something that we're going to have to deal with," Flores said, "but there's always elements that we're dealing with, whether it's cold or rain or things like that. ... That's the environment we're going to be in.
"We'll prepare them to play in that environment, but I'm not going to be silly and say, 'Hey everybody, you got to go in there for 12 straight plays.' We're not doing that. So we'll have rotations. We'll have a plan in place. Inevitably we're going to have to fight through some of that."
Lewis was less convinced that beet juice will make much of a difference, saying she believes the quantities needed for real impact are unrealistic. She said she encourages athletes of all sports to utilize pure oxygen tanks during competition at altitude, which the NFL will provide Sunday on the sidelines in Mexico City.
The Vikings have pushed players to use the sauna at their training facility two or three times per week during this ramp-up period, on Williams' belief that heat stress can expand the body's ability to circulate oxygen. But the centerpiece of their efforts is the altitude room, which Williams said is designed as much to familiarize players for what elevated breathing will feel like as it is to achieve a physiological transformation.
The room contains treadmills, stationary bikes and elliptical trainers, among other equipment, and has room for up to 12 players at a time. By the end of this week, players will have participated in 450 training sessions at altitude since the room was built.
"Even though you're not doing a full practice at altitude," Williams said, "you're trying to gain a lower rate of perceived exertion. So, how your body feels. The more often you're exposed to that, you have a lower rate of perceived exertion.
"You also have a behavioral adaptation. It's how your body responds. How you know how to pace yourself at altitude. How you use breathing strategies in your first exposure compared to your fifth is totally different. It's a learned adaptation."
Receiver Justin Jefferson said "you feel it every time you go in there, for real." But ultimately, linebacker Eric Wilson said players will just have to "thug it out."
"There's a science to it they say," Wilson added, "but we've just got to go out there and ball."

title: What to know to set your lineup: Opportunity knocking for these Titans, Broncos
summary: Adam Rank catches you up on the vital information and insights before you make your toughest lineup decisions.
full_text:
I've never been one to stream quarterbacks. I know that a lot of you live this life, but it isn't for me. It's kind of like people who took Thursday off to play Grand Theft Auto IV ; people are really into that, and I understand the fascination. That's not for me. I grew up playing "Baseball Stars" on the NES.
But this year, I'm into it. Streaming quarterbacks, not GTA (I mean, I'm not Kyler Murray ). This season, in my league of record, I've been forced to stream quarterbacks. Why? I drafted Justin Herbert . And -- you get it -- mistakes were made. We cut bait about eight weeks ago, and I've been living that streaming life ever since.
It's been exciting for sure. I had to sweat out Aaron Rodgers last week, but I'm not making that mistake again. No, I'm taking the old tried-and-true method. I'm playing whomever is going against the Dallas Cowboys . This week, it's Cam Ward . Which is kind of like the same feeling you get when you start popping off about eating a ghost pepper. It sounds like something you could really do until -- you know -- you are actually called to do it.
But I do love Ward this week. He's averaged 22-plus fantasy points over his past three games. Coach Robert Saleh has even publicly stated he's putting Ward through evaluation mode, which is an awfully nice thing for him to do for the next coach of the Tennessee Titans . Kidding! Although, if the Titans ever thought Ward wasn't the guy, I could see the Titans getting rid of everyone. Like with an unruly crowd at closing time, don't try to find the troublemaker -- just kick everyone out. But that's a story for another day. Right now, we're streaming Ward. But here are some other things you need to know as you head into this "Bye-mageddon" Week 11.

title: Last-minute pickups for Week 11: Flournoy, Ayomanor among top candidates
summary: There is no busier bye week than this one. Matt Bowen lists potential options if you need a fill-in.
full_text:
With six teams on bye this week ( Atlanta Falcons , Cleveland Browns , Green Bay Packers , Los Angeles Rams , New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks ), managers likely have some spots to fill in their lineups.
If you need wide receivers, this is a good place for you, as I have six pass catchers (with varying levels of value) to pick from. Based on the matchups and player availability (focusing on those under 50% rostered), it's pretty lean at quarterback and running back, but there are still a couple of options. We'll wrap things up with the tight ends and a D/ST to stream.
Ryan Flournoy , Dallas Cowboys (36.5% rostered; vs. Titans)
In the Week 10 shootout loss to the 49ers, Flournoy had a season-high 19.1 points, catching six of seven targets for 91 yards and a score. Sure, game script impacted his totals, but Flournoy has at least 11 points in five of his past six games, with a touchdown reception in three of them. With a matchup against a Titans defense allowing 42.8 PPG to wide receivers (most in the league), Flournoy should be in lineups as a WR3.
Adonai Mitchell , New York Jets (40.8% rostered; at Chargers)
Mitchell had a breakout game in Week 8 versus the Raiders, scoring 27.2 points, but he has caught only three of 15 targets over the past two games. However, there is opportunity for Mitchell this week as the No. 2 option opposite Garrett Wilson with Omar Cooper Jr . (ankle) questionable for Sunday. If Cooper sits, Mitchell gets a boost in volume and brings big-play upside versus a Chargers defense that allows the seventh-most fantasy points per game to wide receivers.
Elic Ayomanor , Tennessee Titans (9.8% rostered; at Cowboys)
Ayomanor scored a season-high 12.9 points last week against the Jaguars, leading the team with 79 yards receiving while catching five of 10 targets. With Wan'Dale Robinson done for the season, Ayomanor should be in line to see steady volume from quarterback Cam Ward , who has played his best football of the season during the past two games. And managers should be all over the matchup versus a Dallas defense that is allowing the sixth-most fantasy points per game to wide receivers.
Caleb Douglas , Miami Dolphins (33.7% rostered; at Bills)
I wrote about Douglas last week in this spot as a deeper-league flier/big-play target and not much has changed. With backup quarterback Kyle McCord under center last week against the Colts, Douglas caught only three of eight targets, but he finished with 71 yards (10.1 points). Douglas has scored 10 or more points in three of his past four games. He's a WR3 option versus Buffalo on Sunday.
Antonio Williams , Washington Commanders (19% rostered; vs. Bengals)
Williams saw just two targets in the Week 10 win over the Giants, but he caught both for 42 yards, with one going for a touchdown (12.2 points). Williams has posted double-digit points in two of his past three contests, catching 10 of 15 targets during that stretch. He matches up with the Bengals on Monday night, and there is value here if you need a good route runner in the lineup.
Malachi Fields , New York Giants (8.8% rostered; vs. Jaguars)
I'll throw Fields in here as a bye week fill-in versus the Jaguars. He has at least three catches in each of the three games with J.J. McCarthy under center for the Giants. Fields is a 6-foot-4, 222-pound boundary target who can create explosive plays and is an upside play for deeper formats.
Cam Ward, Tennessee Titans (23.8% rostered; at Cowboys) ]/p>
