It's a great matchup Sunday in Dallas for Ward, whose numbers have jumped the past two games. Ward scored a season-high 26.26 points versus the Bengals in Week 8 (before the bye) and followed that up with 19.14 points in the Week 10 loss to Jacksonville. Ward has thrown for multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games (for the first time this season), and his rushing totals are up (two straight games with 39 or more yards rushing). With six teams on a bye this week, Ward should be viewed as a top streaming option.
Aaron Rodgers , Pittsburgh Steelers (37% rostered; at Eagles)
Rodgers' numbers have declined over his past four games (12.4 PPG), but he has thrown multiple touchdowns passes in two of them. Sunday, he'll face a Philly defense that is ninth worst in fantasy versus quarterbacks. Managers will need Rodgers to be throwing in red zone situations. He's a deeper league superflex option.
Kaelon Black , San Francisco 49ers (37.1% rostered; vs. Vikings)
I don't love the matchup versus the Vikings' defensive front, but it's hard to ignore the volume Black is seeing as the No. 2 behind Christian McCaffrey . Black has at least 11 carries in three straight games and 10 or more points (and a touchdown rush) in two. He's a downhill hammer with flex upside in deeper leagues.
Justice Hill , Baltimore Ravens (18% rostered; at Panthers)
Hill will see limited rushing volume behind Derrick Henry , but he has value as a pass-catching flex option. Hill caught five passes from Jacoby Brissett in the Monday night loss to the Chargers, and he has at least three receptions in five straight games. He has a positive matchup Sunday versus the Panthers, who allow the third-most points to running backs.
Chig Okonkwo , Washington Commanders (37.7% rostered; vs. Bengals)
Okonkwo is seeing steady volume from quarterback Jayden Daniels, and he gets a positive matchup on Monday night. Okonkwo has at least six targets (with four or more receptions) in four of his past five games, and he has scored at least 10 points in three of them. He's a solid option this week given the tight ends available.
Michael Mayer , Las Vegas Raiders (22.6% rostered; at Broncos)
Mayer's value is tied to the health of starting tight end Brock Bowers (ankle). If Bowers can't go for Sunday's home matchup versus the Broncos, Mayer elevates as a streaming option. He has four games of double-digit production this season, and while he posted those numbers with Kirk Cousins under center, he will still see volume -- if he's the No. 1 tight end -- from rookie Fernando Mendoza on Sunday. Stay tuned.
Detroit Lions (46.9% rostered; vs. Bucs)
Yes, pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson (knee) is down for the season, but this Lions defense has really changed its identity over the past five games. During that stretch, Detroit has produced at least six fantasy points in every game, with 10 or more in each of the past two. Plus, this unit has at least three sacks and an interception in three straight. And it gets the Bucs at home.
author: Matt Bowen

title: Barnwell debunks a myth: Yes, there are at least 32 starter-level QBs in the NFL at any given time
summary: Finding legit quarterbacks can be tough, and many people think there aren't even enough true QB1s to fill the league's 32 QB1 spots. Is there any validity to that?
full_text:
It has been an absolutely brutal year for quarterback injuries in the NFL. When I wrote about this in September , the 2026 season was already looking as if it could be on the high end for missing signal-callers. And as we hit Week 11, it's almost more difficult to find teams that haven't had to go to their backups than ones who have been able to stick with their starter all season.
Fourteen teams have been unable to play their primary quarterback for more than a quarter of work because of an injury this season. The Bears, Cardinals and Ravens have been forced to turn to their third-string option. As many as seven of the 10 afternoon games Sunday will feature at least one backup quarterback.
Though both the league and its teams are desperate to keep the best quarterbacks healthy, injuries are going to happen. And in just about every case, going from a starter to a backup is going to create problems. Over the past decade -- without factoring in any other information -- teams that got a full game from their starting quarterback and went up against opposition that didn't get a single snap from their preferred starter won nearly 66% of the time.
Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show'
It would be great if teams could turn to a deep pool of backups, but that just isn't the case at quarterback. And there's a phrase that comes up all the time: "There aren't 32 starting-caliber quarterbacks to go around in the NFL." And yes, the reality is that the league rarely, if ever, has 32 quality starters featuring at the same time.
But does that mean that there couldn't be 32 quality starters if they were dispersed around the league's 32 teams? I'm not so sure. There are some gaps in that logic, and it's a topic I've always wanted to explore. The middle of an injury-riddled 2026 season feels like the right time to get there. How many viable starting QBs are typically on NFL rosters at any one time? Is it 20? 30? 40?
I wasn't sure of the answer, but I'm sure we're not considering the question correctly. I'm going to show why that's the case and give my best estimate for how many viable quarterbacks have typically been present on NFL rosters at any one time over the past few decades.
Jump to: Why the argument is flawed True QB1s in a typical season What it means for 2026
The fundamental flaw in the "There aren't 32 starting-caliber quarterbacks" argument is that it evaluates only the 32 quarterbacks who are currently playing in NFL lineups. Even if we ignore injuries and just consider each team's ideal and preferred option heading into 2026, that's still going to leave us with a handful of teams that don't have a quarterback who projects to be even a viable starter, let alone a solid one. At any one time, there are typically going to be at least a couple of replacement-level starters in a starting lineup. By midseason, when injuries have usually hit the league, those concerns feel even more acute.
On the other hand, there are a lot of reasons why the 32 starting quarterbacks in the league at any given time aren't the 32 best options to fill those roles.
Teams aren't as good at identifying the right starting QBs as we'd like to believe. When it comes its quarterbacks, NFL teams are generally meritocratic and able to identify who they should be starting by the end of training camp. But not always.
Some teams are locked into long-term contracts for players and want to give that passer every chance to prove that he's worth his deal. The Browns started Deshaun Watson to open the 2024 season and got historically bad play for seven games before the highly paid veteran tore his Achilles . Jameis Winston isn't a superstar, but the Browns were a much better offense the moment he entered the lineup.
Other teams are operating in the opposite boat and have a young, highly drafted quarterback who isn't very good yet playing ahead of a veteran backup who would be more effective if given the full-time starting role. Also in 2024, the Colts were starting Anthony Richardson Sr . ahead of Joe Flacco for most of the season despite the fact that Flacco had helped lead the Browns to the postseason the previous season. Richardson plays a very different style, but if the goal was just to field the best possible quarterback, Flacco probably should have been the choice.
Teams also just flat-out make evaluation mistakes, even with players they've already seen in their offense. The Vikings chose Kyler Murray , Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer ahead of J.J. McCarthy and then traded their 2024 first-round pick to the Giants, where he has been a much more productive player than any of the signal-callers he had been competing with in camp. I'm sure some of that was a product of not wanting to deal with McCarthy as a third or fourth quarterback, but strictly in terms of on-field performance, the Vikings appear to have chosen the wrong guys.
In the big picture, teams find it even more difficult to identify which quarterback prospects will succeed as they enter the NFL, even when those guys are roughly entering the league within the same tier. In 2018, five QBs came off the board in Round 1. Baker Mayfield , who has been somewhere between a solid starter and a replacement-level passer in his various stops around the league, was the first pick. Sam Darnold , who fits the same mold, was next. Josh Allen , a future Hall of Famer, followed. The Cardinals then chose Josh Rosen , who was out of football after 16 starts, before the Ravens took Lamar Jackson , who will join Allen in Canton one day.
I'll get to later-round picks in a moment, but the idea that the 32 quarterbacks starting around the league at any given time are actually the 32 best quarterbacks in football simply isn't true. And it takes a few seconds to quickly look around the league to see that.
Some teams have no viable quarterback, but others have more than one. There are going to be some QB1s this weekend who either haven't proved themselves to be NFL starters or previously weren't able to perform like one. Players such as Tommy DeVito and Joe Milton probably don't qualify as viable starting quarterbacks for the purposes of the statement we're evaluating, even if they're going to be on the field Sunday. Of course, they're replacing quarterbacks who are hurt in Drake Maye and Jalen Hurts , respectively, who would comfortably fit any definition of a quality starter.
Elsewhere, there are teams that haven't needed to turn to a backup but might have two viable starters. The Bengals have Flacco backing up Joe Burrow . Marcus Mariota has been solid behind Jayden Daniels as an injury replacement in Washington. Joshua Dobbs put together an impressive run with the Vikings in 2023 and hasn't been needed behind Jared Goff in Detroit. Murray has been disappointing in Minnesota, but he was a solid starter for the Cardinals over the past half-decade. Drew Lock has been effective filling in for Darnold in Seattle. And Mac Jones was able to sustain the offense for the 49ers when Brock Purdy was injured last season.
Are all of those guys stars? No. But if the goal was to pick the 32 best quarterbacks in football in 2026, backups such as Flacco, Jones and Mariota would probably be in that conversation ahead of some starters around the NFL, even though they're backing up other high-profile quarterbacks and aren't currently in starting roles. And we've seen each of those backups push teams to the postseason as starters in the past, which would seem to suggest that they would be viable starters again in the right situation.
Some players would be starter-worthy in certain schemes and ineffective in others.
If we were looking for quarterbacks who would excel in every single scheme and situation, regardless of their individual skill set, that number will be very low. That's also true for many other positions, too, though, and we don't talk about scarcity in those spots in the same way. Guard Kevin Dotson was struggling in a Steelers scheme that asked him to move laterally…
author: Bill Barnwell

title: Titans defense crumbling post-Jeffery Simmons, Amani Hooker trades
summary: The moves Tennessee made might have helped the rebuilding process, but it also impacted the current team.
full_text:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- Getting off to a 1-8 start is disappointing in itself, but the way the Tennessee Titans are losing games as of late is even more dispiriting.
Titans coach Robert Saleh is known for his success as a defensive coordinator with the San Francisco 49ers , so it's reasonable to expect Tennessee to be solid on that side of the ball.
Yet the Titans find themselves having lost three consecutive games with the defense giving up at least 400 total yards of offense in each of them. Trading defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears and safety Amani Hooker to the Buffalo Bills took away two of Tennessee's best defensive players in the weeks leading up to the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline might have helped the rebuilding process, but it didn't help the current team.
The Titans gave up 43 points to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8 without Simmons, even though Hooker finished with three interceptions in his final game with the team. The Jacksonville Jaguars dropped 40 points on the Titans the next game out of their Week 9 bye after Hooker was traded.
"I really felt like we were trending towards being a top-10 defense after the Indianapolis game," Saleh said Wednesday. "These last three weeks, it hasn't been good enough, not even close. It has been disappointing, and obviously the objective is to get back to where we were trending a few weeks ago."
The secondary has been one of the biggest contributors to the defensive shortcomings. Blown coverages, poor tackling and simply getting beaten by better players have led to opposing quarterbacks finishing with 300-plus yards passing in each of the past three games.
Cincinnati's passing game featuring Joe Burrow , Ja'Maar Chase and Tee Higgins ' production was video game-like. Burrow threw for 462 yards and five touchdowns. Higgins caught 10 passes for 155 yards and two touchdowns. Chase posted his first 100-yard game (155) of the season on 11 catches, including a touchdown.
Given how elite Cincinnati's offense is, it's understandable that the trio put up numbers. But Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson passed for 308 yards rookie wideout KC Concepcion surprisingly exploded for a career-high 129 receiving yards in Cleveland's 27-24 win against the Titans.
Trevor Lawrence 's 352 passing yards and three touchdowns, along with a career-best 152 receiving yards from Parker Washington , led to the Jaguars handing Tennessee its third loss.
"There's going to be moments where you've got to win a one-on-one [in coverage] if we want to be able to get pressure on the quarterback and do those things," Saleh said.
"That's something that we're not proud of," linebacker Cedric Gray added. "What we can do is just try to step up and figure out what the problems are, what the disconnect is in certain situations and why we're not delivering and making plays when we need to make those plays."
The offense and the defense are going in different directions.
Titans QB Cam Ward and the offense are averaging 27.7 points over the past three games, pushing their season average to 18.6, up from their 14-point average the first six games of the season. That helped spark the recent offensive surge, but it hasn't resulted in wins because the defense has allowed 36.7 points per game over that span, dropping their season average from 21.6 points per game (13th in the league) to 26.6 (27th).
"You can't win allowing 30, 40 points, either one of those," Titans safety Kevin Winston Jr . said. "We want to make sure we limit that to below 20 if we can to give our offense a chance. Our mindset is: if the offense scores 20-plus, we should win. We've got to get that fixed."
Edge defender Jacob Martin has been one of the few bright spots on the defense. Martin has already set a career high with 7.5 sacks in nine games. He has played for Saleh before when they were with the New York Jets in 2022, so there's familiarity. Martin believes the Titans' success on defense comes down to processing things faster.
Saleh decided to make a philosophical shift on offense so Ward would have more command and show that he can be the franchise quarterback the team desperately needs. Martin indicated that perhaps a similar shift should be made to allow the defense to process and play faster.
The losing streak has caused Saleh and the defensive staff to consider if they're "pushing the envelope too much" with the number of checks to get the right call against the right formation to create the right player positioning. That takes a lot of pre-snap thinking and communication, which could be putting the guys in the wrong headspace and keep them from playing the fast, violent style of defense Saleh wants. The coaching staff's solution is to simplify things by delivering the call to the players in a way that allows them to get the call knowing exactly what they're asked to do without worrying what the formation is.
"As a player on the field, it's good getting simplified playcalls or things that have easy answers," Martin said. "Like it's not a whole bunch of one-offs; if they line up here we do this or line up there, and we do that. I think it allows guys to play faster with their feet on the ground and not in the middle of communication while the ball's being snapped. I think it will allow guys to play faster for sure."
The first test will be when the Titans face the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Sunday ( 1 p.m. ET, Fox ). The Cowboys' offense is scoring 28.6 points per game. The road doesn't get easier after Dallas, with visits to Jacksonville (which ranks fourth in the league at 29.9 points per game) and in Week 14 the Detroit Lions , who are tied with Dallas for the fifth-best scoring offense. Buckle up.
author: Turron Davenport

title: Reid's midseason NFL mock draft: 32 prospect landing spots, four QBs and one big trade
summary: Which team could land Drew Mestemaker? Who needs Chris Cole, Ashton Hampton or Jamari Johnson? Jordan Reid projected first-round picks for 2027 -- and a trade.
full_text:
Now that the NFL trade deadline has passed and we're in the second half of the 2026 season , it's a great time to look ahead to the 2027 NFL draft .
Some teams whose playoff hopes are mostly dashed are already fully into the process of evaluating prospects for the draft, which will take place in April in Washington. So why not take our own look at how that draft might turn out?
This latest mock draft factors in a combination of what NFL teams need, my evaluation of production and tape from the 2026 college football season , and conversations I've had with trusted scouts and evaluators. Of course, things will change between now and April -- players will move up and down the board or exit the class entirely by returning to school -- but this is how I see things currently.
The draft order obviously is far from set, so I based this 1-32 on what the order would look like if the season ended today. There have already been six trades in Round 1, and I actually pitched a seventh that could make sense.
How many quarterbacks will make Round 1? Here are my full projections for all 32 first-round picks.
Note: Underclassmen are marked with an asterisk.
Jeremiah Smith , WR, Ohio State*
Smith is the best player in this draft, and as the first wide receiver to go No. 1 since 1996 (Keyshawn Johnson), he would allow the Titans to continue to build around quarterback Cam Ward , the No. 1 pick of the 2025 draft. How special is Smith? He has drawn comparisons to some of the best wideouts of the past quarter century -- including Calvin Johnson, Larry Fitzgerald and Julio Jones -- by NFL scouts.
Smith's 131.7 receiving yards per game ranks second in the FBS, and he continues to thrive despite Ohio State's quarterback issues . Speaking of the Buckeyes, the Titans could reunite Smith with fellow wide receiver Carnell Tate , Tennessee's first pick in 2026. Smith's rare combination of size (6-foot-4 and 225 pounds), speed and power gives him early All-Pro potential and makes him the type of player Ward and the Titans need to further improve their offense.
The Jets have three first-round picks, so I have them sending Nos. 4 and 13, along with a 2028 third-rounder, to the Chargers for the No. 2 selection. New York originally acquired the No. 13 pick in a trade with the Cowboys for defensive tackle Quinnen Williams .
Could this move finally allow the Jets to select their quarterback of the future?
Drew Mestemaker , QB, Oklahoma State*
Mestemaker has progressed from a walk-on who didn't start in high school to my top QB in this class. The Jets have used the past three drafts to establish an offensive base, selecting bookend tackles ( Olu Fashanu and Armand Membou ), wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. and tight end Kenyon Sadiq in Round 1. Along with star wideout Garrett Wilson , they make New York an ideal landing spot for a rookie signal-caller.
Mestemaker excels at pushing the ball down the field, with his 21 completions of 20 or more yards this season ranking eighth in the FBS. His decision-making is inconsistent at times, but Mestemaker is young (he's in his first season as a Power 4 starter) and has the tools to transform the Jets.
Colin Simmons , Edge, Texas*
After drafting 13 players last year, the Dolphins have a foundation of young talent on their roster. Now, Miami needs a star, which Simmons could be on defense. He is arguably the top pass rusher in this class and one of the best in the FBS at generating pressure off the edge. His 10.5 sacks are third most in the country despite him missing two games because of injury . His 20.5% pressure rate ranks fifth in the FBS, and Simmons' powerful hands let him set a violent edge in run defense.
Pairing Simmons with 2024 first-rounder Chop Robinson would give the Dolphins an explosive pass-rush duo for defensive-minded coach Jeff Hafley.
Charlie Becker , WR, Indiana*
The Chargers have been extremely disappointing this season, and their 1-8 start has exposed the need for more talent everywhere. That and the fact that they already have a QB in Justin Herbert are why I had them trade out of No. 2 and add another pick. And we'll use this first pick to get Herbert some help.
Becker is an excellent vertical threat who has 10 touchdowns this season (sixth in the FBS) and can also execute the short to intermediate levels of the route tree. He is tall (6-foot-4) and sure-handed (zero drops on 85 targets this season) with excellent body control and elite hand-eye coordination, allowing him to win in the air on long and contested catch opportunities. Becker would immediately become Herbert's WR1.
Dylan Stewart , Edge, South Carolina*
This season has been a disaster for Philadelphia, but it allows the Eagles to get an elite edge-rushing talent. Stewart is a toolsy and explosive player who has the unique ability to bend around the corner and wreak havoc in the backfield. The 6-foot-5, 250-pounder hasn't had consistent production in college, but his tools and flashes of potential are tantalizing and reminiscent of Brian Burns coming out of Florida State . Stewart will have to answer questions during the predraft process about his production and an in-season suspension , but he's an ideal talent for the Eagles to draft and develop behind Jonathan Greenard , Nolan Smith Jr. and Jalyx Hunt .
Leonard Moore , CB, Notre Dame*
Now that the Jets have traded up to take their quarterback of the future, they could select my No. 1 defensive prospect in this year's class here. Moore's 8.6% target rate is the lowest among all FBS corners this season, and he has allowed only seven completions in eight games. Moore is one of the most consistent cover guys in the country and has the length (6-foot-2, 197 pounds) and ball skills to be a shutdown corner in the NFL. He could start right away at outside corner for New York.
The Cardinals desperately need to add help in the trenches, and Seaton is an upper-tier athlete who is very polished in pass protection. He has allowed only one sack and four pressures this season on 344 pass-blocking snaps. He is more than capable of mirroring and matching edge rushers, though he needs to get stronger and improve his anchor and drive strength. But Seaton would be a plug-and-play starting option at either tackle spot opposite Paris Johnson Jr. , who will be on his fifth-year option in 2027.
With Michael Penix Jr. struggling to find consistency in Year 3, the Falcons could once again be convinced to use the No. 8 pick on a QB -- like they did three years ago with Penix , especially since the Falcons' front office and coach have changed since making that selection. Atlanta has plenty of skill-position talent (RB Bijan Robinson , WR Drake London , TE Kyle Pitts Sr. ) that could enable a young QB to thrive immediately.
Carr is an instinctive passer who consistently has answers and has already been given considerable autonomy in Notre Dame's offense. He doesn't have the high-end traits of some passers in the class (picture a more mobile Kirk Cousins ), but he is polished in many of the skills that are essential to playing the position.
Zereoue Williams , OT, Utah
"I could see him making a rise similar to Kolton Miller " is a text that a scout sent me after watching Williams earlier this season. Miller was drafted No. 15 in 2018 by the Raiders, and Williams could be taken even higher. He is already 24 years old, which is part of why he is receiving some second-round grades from scouts right now. But I'm confident in Williams' tools and ceiling ultimately leading to a big rise; I see a first-round player.
Houston has been trying to fix its offensive line in front of C.J. Stroud for years, and taking Williams at tackle would be a logical follow-up to their selection of guard Keylan Rutledge in the 2026 first round. Williams is one of the best blockers in this class and has upside for more development. He could be the third Utah tackle selected in the first round in the past two drafts.
Ashton Hampton , CB, Clemson*
Hampton is a tough…
author: Jordan Reid

title: Which team will land the No. 1 draft pick? Our look at a five-franchise race
summary: Five teams have at least 5% odds to land the No. 1 pick in 2027, per ESPN's Football Power Index.
full_text:
The race for the No. 1 pick in the 2027 NFL draft is taking shape now that we're 10 weeks into the 2026 season .
Five teams have at least a 5% chance at landing the top pick, according to ESPN's Football Power Index projections. So we called on our experts and reporters to size up each of those bottom-tier franchises at midseason.
NFL analyst Seth Walder used the FPI to make sense of each of the five teams' schedules the rest of the way. Our NFL Nation reporters looked at the biggest positional needs that could be addressed in the first round in April. And NFL draft analyst Jordan Reid spun it forward and suggested one prospect each front office could consider if it landed that top selection.
Let's start with the Dolphins, who currently have the best odds at the No. 1 pick.
Jump to a team: LAC | MIA | NYJ PHI | TEN
FPI chance to earn No. 1 pick: 41.2% FPI chance to earn top-five pick: 93%
What lies ahead in the schedule? Are they favored in any remaining games?
Not only are the Dolphins not favored by the FPI in a single remaining game this season, but the model also makes them at least a field-goal underdog in every game. Their best chances to win are versus the Jets in Week 12 , versus the Chargers in Week 16 and at the Patriots in Week 18 . But because the FPI believes the Dolphins are the worst team in the NFL, they are not likely to win any of those contests. -- Walder
What is their biggest first-round need right now?
The Dolphins have needs across the board, but if we're narrowing down positions that make sense at their projected draft slot, it's edge rusher, quarterback and wide receiver. Chop Robinson has been excellent this season and could use a pass-rush partner to mix in with Josh Uche . However, pairing wide receiver Caleb Douglas in his second year with another receiver or a rookie quarterback is also tempting. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques
Who is the best prospect fit right now for them at No. 1?
Drew Mestemaker , QB, Oklahoma State. Free agent signee Malik Willis hasn't shown any signs of being the long-term answer moving forward, and Miami could use him as a bridge option. Mestemaker is a young and intriguing passer who won't be ready to start from Day 1; 2026 is only his second season as a starter in high school and college combined. Miami already has a productive foundation of youth, but Mestemaker could provide it the QB necessary to continue its rebuild. -- Reid
FPI chance to earn No. 1 pick: 36.9% FPI chance to earn top-five pick: 92.4%
What lies ahead in the schedule? Are they favored in any remaining games?
There are definitely some winnable games available for the Titans: Week 13 versus the Commanders , Week 15 versus the Colts and Week 16 at the Raiders . The FPI favors the Titans only against the Raiders in Week 16 (the model has fairly low confidence in rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza until proven otherwise), but there is a strong chance Tennessee wins at least one of those three games. Still, Tennessee has the second-best chance to earn the No. 1 pick. -- Walder
What is their biggest first-round need right now?
Pass rusher. Sure, Jacob Martin has gotten off to a great start with a career-high 7.5 sacks so far, but there's no guarantee he'll repeat that success next year, and his deal expires after 2027. Getting a running mate opposite Martin would improve the whole defense and give Tennessee an edge rusher to build its defense around in the future. A game-changing pass rusher would also allow coach Robert Saleh to rush with four and drop seven into coverage, which would help a struggling pass defense. -- Turron Davenport
Who is the best prospect fit right now for them at No. 1?
Jeremiah Smith , WR, Ohio State. Even though the Titans have a huge need at edge -- where South Carolina's Dylan Stewart and Texas' Colin Simmons are my top prospects -- it shouldn't be at the expense of taking Smith, the best player in this class. Smith and Titans WR Carnell Tate are very familiar with each other, combining for 2,118 receiving yards and 21 touchdowns at Ohio State in 2025. Quarterback Cam Ward , who still hasn't solidified whether he's the long-term solution under center, has a risk-taking nature that would pair well with Smith's ability to be a three-level threat. -- Reid
FPI chance to earn No. 1 pick: 7.9% FPI chance to earn top-five pick: 68.7%
What lies ahead in the schedule? Are they favored in any remaining games?
Two games stand out as possible victories: Week 13 at the Cardinals and Week 14 versus the Colts . The FPI considers the Eagles as slight underdogs in both of them. I'll throw out one other game to keep an eye on: Week 18 at the Giants . That's because the FPI is pretty bearish on New York, so it thinks the Eagles have a chance, and the Giants could sit their starters if they have the NFC East wrapped up at that point. -- Walder
What is their biggest first-round need right now?
Offensive tackle. The retirement of future Hall of Fame right tackle Lane Johnson created a major need along the offensive front. Rookie Markel Bell , the team's 2026 third-round pick, had a strong summer and took over when Johnson stepped away in early October, but Bell has yet to solidify himself as the right tackle of the future. The Eagles' long run of success is tied directly to their strength along the fronts. They need to invest early and often in the O-line. -- Tim McManus
Who is the best prospect fit right now for them at No. 1? Jeremiah Smith. Right now, there isn't an offensive tackle worthy of a top-five pick. LSU's Jordan Seaton tops my position rankings right now at No. 11. That puts the Eagles in position to take the best player available, which is Smith in this scenario. He would add another outstanding option to an offense that includes RB Saquon Barkley , WR DeVonta Smith and 2026 first-round pick Makai Lemon . At 6-foot-4 and 220 pounds, Smith can glide past defenders or outmuscle them at the catch point. -- Reid

The FPI favors the Jets to beat the Dolphins -- a high-leverage game for AFC East draft capital -- in Week 12 . What is their biggest first-round need right now?
Priority No. 1 is a franchise quarterback. This is their moment. This is why they traded defensive stars Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams in 2025. After four years of Aaron Rodgers , Justin Fields and Geno Smith -- all stopgaps, to varying degrees -- the Jets want to build around a young quarterback who can grow with the talent already in place. -- Rich Cimini

Drew Mestemaker. At 6-foot-4 and 220 pounds, he is a strong-armed passer with plenty of mobility. Mestemaker still needs to become more consistent with his decision-making, but his tools and potential are an ideal fit for the Jets given the offensive personnel they already have in place. -- Reid

title: Behold the Beer Spear: Commanders unveil limited-edition vessel tied to new alternates
summary: The limited-edition collectible vessel can hold 16 ounces of beer, equipped with a gold spear at the end of it.
full_text:
Monday marks the Washington Commanders ' debut of their new alternate uniforms, the "Hail Raiser." The Commanders will be ringing in the all-black threads with a similarly themed concession item: the "Beer Spear."
It's a limited-edition collectible vessel that can hold 16 ounces of beer, equipped with a gold spear at the end of it. Washington already boasts a crab stuffed pretzel at its concession stands. The pretzel is shaped like a crab and is filled with lemon tarragon crab dip topped with garlic butter and grated parmesan cheese.
The beer spear is just another in the list of creative sport-related concession items that deal with beer. Some MLB teams have the "beer bat." title: NFL Week 11 best bets for Sunday's games
summary: Our experts dive into the odds and player props for Week 11 and offer their betting tips and favorite plays.
full_text:
Week 11 of the NFL season features several games where the spread would indicate a mismatch, but this league is full of surprises.
Eight remaining games have teams that are favored by at least six points, and four of them are double-digit favorites. What will that mean for game bets and prop plays? We've looked at it all in hopes of trying to find the best values.
Ben Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Seth Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Matt Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. Also included are fantasy projection creator Mike Clay's top predicted anytime TD scorers.
Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. Let's get into it.
Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change.
Jump to: Solak's plays | Bowen's bets | Walder's props Clay's TD projections
Tampa Bay Buccaneers +6 (-110) at Detroit Lions
It's a good spot here for the Buccaneers, who are coming off of their bye week and are one of the healthiest teams in football. It sounds like quarterback Baker Mayfield will go, but safety Antoine Winfield Jr . (ankle) isn't ready to return to action. Meanwhile, the Lions are coming off a trip to Munich and will be without star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson on a defense that was already absent one key star in Jack Campbell . Center Cade Mays also looks like he's out for this one, and though safety Kerby Joseph might make his long-awaited return, I'm not sure how effective he'll be.
I like this matchup for the Buccaneers' defense. Tampa Bay is elite against the run, and stopping Jahmyr Gibbs is the first priority when facing Detroit. Todd Bowles has also historically had success against Jared Goff . In four games against Bowles' Buccaneers over the last three seasons, Goff averages 0.08 EPA per dropback and an adjusted net yards per attempt of only 6.1. For perspective, Goff is at 0.21 EPA per dropback and 7.6 adjusted net yards per attempt for the season. The Buccaneers have the big defensive line necessary to handle this Lions front and the blitz-heavy approach to disrupt Goff in the pocket.
I expect a low-scoring game that the Bucs try to control with their own rushing attack. This one ends on a field goal attempt.
Minnesota Vikings +3.5 (-118) at San Francisco 49ers
Happy to get the hook here on a Vikings team that might be the best team in football, so long as their quarterback is not actively limiting the offense. Minnesota's defense is so exotic that it's almost worth throwing stats out the window. Brock Purdy is the league's best quarterback against the blitz by expected points and yards per attempt, but what does that really mean against a defense like Minnesota's, which blitzes in unique ways on totally different downs than all other defenses?
FREE to play. Create up to 10 entries and compete for 58 prizes worth $102K. Make Your Picks
The high-flying 49ers offense has struggled with Brian Flores' unit a couple of times -- Minnesota won 22-17 in 2023 against a 5-1 49ers team and again in 2024 in Week 2 by a final score of 23-17. Purdy is accustomed to making quick escapes against lumbering defensive linemen; the blitzers Minnesota sends tend to be better at getting him down. And because Purdy throws with so much anticipation, he's liable for a bad pick against Flores' group as well. He has taken seven sacks and thrown three picks over two games against Minnesota's defense.
If Purdy successfully avoids those big negatives -- which I believe he can -- it's likely because the 49ers have taken a run-heavy approach on offense with a healthy smattering of quick passes. I'm not expecting huge points from San Francisco's side, while the Vikings have the potential for big offensive outputs with Kirk Cousins under center. Remember, Cousins just faced this defense a few weeks ago with the Las Vegas Raiders , and now he gets to port over all his takeaways into an entirely new offense. That feels like a big edge here.
Jahmyr Gibbs rushing yards UNDER 87.5 (-111)
Hello, it's me, the idiot, taking a Gibbs under.
The Buccaneers are the best run defense in football. They're allowing 3.6 yards per carry to opposing running backs and a league-low 65.9 yards per game overall. And the Buccaneers' run-heavy approach on offense should help them limit the number of possessions the Lions get.
Given the shakiness of the Buccaneers' linebackers in coverage, I think we see a bigger day for Gibbs through the air and a quieter day on the ground.
Ashton Jeanty receiving yards OVER 29.5 (-105)
Receiving backs against the Denver Broncos tend to be a good bet, as Denver's heavy dose of man coverage gives dangerous receivers out of the backfield big opportunities in space. The Raiders definitely fit into this category, as Tre Tucker , Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech are not a sufficient enough receiver room to test the Broncos' corners in coverage. Volume in the passing game will be funneled to Brock Bowers , of course, but after him, Jeanty, against linebackers Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad , is the best matchup option the Raiders have.
Running backs are averaging 1.40 yards per route run against the Broncos this season, the seventh-highest rate among all defenses (their 8.8 yards per reception is also seventh). Jeanty saw only four targets in Fernando Mendoza 's first start, which is tied for his season low in a game. I imagine the Raiders will make a priority of getting the ball to the checkdown more frequently in Mendoza's second start, especially given the negative matchup for the wideouts in this one.
Check out the latest Super Bowl odds and major NFL awards futures .
Parker Washington receptions OVER 4.5 (-101)
Since Brian Burns went down with a torn right ACL in Week 3, the New York Giants have the second-highest blitz rate in football (47%). That's good news for Washington, who sees a 35% target rate against the blitz this season, relative to a 26% target rate on non-blitzed dropbacks. And on the season, the Giants run the fifth-highest rate of man coverage. More good news for Washington: He has a 38% target rate against man coverage and a 20% target rate against zone coverage.
In this particular matchup, Washington will be the primary wide receiver option for quarterback Trevor Lawrence , as he lines up most frequently in the slot. Outside cornerbacks Greg Newsome II and Deonte Banks have been a wonderful duo for the Giants, but slot corner Dru Phillips is gettable in space. I waffle on receptions and receiving yards here, as the Lawrence-Washington connections tend to be further down the field, but I think receptions is the safer play.
Chimere Dike receiving yards UNDER 28.5 (-115)
Dike has run 31 and 34 routes in the past two weeks, respectively, with Carnell Tate out with a shoulder injury. But Tate was back at practice Wednesday and Thursday (limited) and could take a huge bite into Dike's snap counts moving forward. Dike averaged only 3.1 routes per game in the seven weeks Tate was healthy.
Wan'Dale Robinson was just placed on injured reserve, but a majority of Robinson's routes were coming from the slot, and Dike's game of straight-line speed doesn't necessarily lend itself to the slot. Dike ran eight routes from the slot last week in Robinson's absence, and backup Xavier Restrepo ran another seven. With Tate back in the starting lineup, it's likely he'll bite into some of those snaps as well.
Even if Dike gets a bigger route share than I'm anticipating, he went over this number only once in the two weeks in which he saw 30-plus routes. As a speed threat, he does more to stretch the field and draw coverage than draw really high-value targets. I'll buy the number now with the assumption Tate plays. And even if Tate doesn't go, I'll have some outs.

title: Burrow odds-on favorite for MVP, Gibbs and JSN in tight race for OPOY
summary: Who are the favorites to win seasonlong honors? Here are the odds for MVP, Rookie of the Year and more.
full_text:
For the first time this season, Cincinnati Bengals QB Joe Burrow is the odds-on favorite to win NFL MVP, improving to -115 from +210 after yet another four-touchdown passing performance. Burrow, who is a significant liability for the award at several sportsbooks, took over the odds lead last week from preseason favorite Josh Allen , who is still in the running at +350. San Francisco 49ers QB Brock Purdy (+425) and Jacksonville Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence (+500) round out the top candidates.
Offensive Player of the Year is becoming a two-man race between Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (+100) and Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba (+125), who are both putting up historical numbers this season. Smith-Njigba seeks to become the first player to repeat as OPOY since Marshall Faulk won three in a row from 1999 to 2001.
Houston Texans defensive end Will Anderson Jr . continues to lead the Defensive Player of the Year odds board at +120, but one of the biggest movers has been linebacker Dallas Turner , who has been a leader for the vaunted Minnesota Vikings defense and shortened from 14-1 to +350 in less than two weeks. Chicago Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and San Francisco 49ers LB Fred Warner are also in the running at +750.
Las Vegas Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza continues to lead the Offensive Rookie of the Year board at +230 after he became the favorite following the trade of Kirk Cousins from Las Vegas to Minnesota. title: Colts release QB Daniel Jones
summary: Colts avoid $10.51 million injury guarantee for 2027 by removing Jones from the roster.
full_text: We predicted that Colts quarterback Daniel Jones will be benched, sooner than later. Technically, he has been. The Colts have announced that Jones has been released. It accelerates a process that would have begun with the Colts benching Jones to avoid having a $10.51 million injury guarantee for 2027 becoming a full guarantee if Jones were to suffer a serious injury over the balance of the season. Jones would have then asked to be released, and the Colts would have likely done it. So the Colts went straight to the final move on the chess board. Jones will, once officially released, go to waivers. If/when (when) he clears waivers, he'll become a free agent. That's the same thing that happened in 2024, after the Giants benched Jones and he asked to be released. He later signed with the Vikings, remaining there for the rest of the season before signing with the Colts in March 2025.

title: Carson Beck dealing with back spasms, Josh Johnson in line to start vs. Chiefs
summary: The Cardinals may have a fourth starting quarterback in four weeks when they play the Chiefs on Sunday.
full_text: The Cardinals may have a fourth starting quarterback in four weeks when they play the Chiefs on Sunday. Rookie Carson Beck is once again dealing with back spasms, which puts veteran backup Josh Johnson in line to start in Week 11. Beck made his regular-season debut last week in the 34-6 loss to the Rams. He was able to practice in full on Wednesday but was listed as limited for Thursday’s session. The rookie QB was previously sidelined with back spasms earlier in the season. “It’s basically just responding to the treatment, see how he feels when he wakes up tomorrow,” head coach Mike LaFleur said in his Friday press conference. LaFleur added that he doesn’t think Beck will be out multiple weeks with the injury, but he’s unsure at this point. “You go with the people who know what they’re doing to treat it. It’s not like this is the first time he’s dealt with it,” LaFleur said. “We’ll see more tomorrow.” If Johnson does start, it will be his first time playing for Arizona in the regular season and add to his long list of clubs. Johnson has appeared in regular-season games for seven teams, including the Jets back in 2021 when LaFleur was the team’s offensive coordinator. “Cool part is, if it is Josh, I’ve called plays for him before and had a really great experience calling plays for him,” LaFleur said. “So, we’ll go shoot our shot and I expect nothing less from our guys.” Still, the instability within Arizona's QBs room is remarkable. In Week 8, Jacoby Brissett made his last start for the club before Gardner Minshew came in and engineered a comeback to send the game to overtime, ultimately beating the Cowboys. Minshew then started Week 9 against Seattle, but suffered a season-ending elbow injury in the loss. Beck made his first start last Sunday and now Johnson is in line to be under center against Kansas City. The Cardinals’ full injury report with game statuses will be released later on Friday.

title: Dan Campbell: Tay Martin's special teams tape was so good, I was shocked we got him
summary: Lions wide receiver Tay Martin has been in the NFL since 2022, and he has only four career catches.
full_text: Lions wide receiver Tay Martin has been in the NFL since 2022, and he has only four career catches. So he's not exactly a household name. But Lions coach Dan Campbell has always been well aware of Martin, and was delighted when he arrived in Detroit this year. That's because Martin isn't only a wide receiver, but also a special teams player. And according to Campbell, he's one of the best special teams players in football, so good a player that Campbell was surprised to learn Martin was available for the Lions to sign in June. "Tay's just a heck of a football player," Campbell said. "I still can't believe that we got him. I'm just shocked, I couldn't believe, seriously I couldn't believe it. His tape last year, his special teams tape. We're fortunate to have him. He's a football player." The 28-year-old Martin spent three years in college at Washington State, then two more at Oklahoma State, before signing with the 49ers as an undrafted free agent. He has also spent time with the Titans and Commanders, and he was the leading receiver for the UFL's Columbus Aviators in the spring. Campbell said Martin is perfectly capable of playing wide receiver in the NFL, and while the Lions haven't used him there much, knowing that he can catch passes when he needs to while also tackling as well as a defensive player in special teams coverage is a huge boost to the Lions. "He's grown as a receiver," Campbell said. "But the special teams production is outstanding. What he's able to bring to us from the receiver position — it's one thing when you get a DB, a safety, a corner, this guy serves that role on special teams, so it kind of buys you a spot, in a good way. He's a stud. Thank goodness we got him."
