title: Shane Steichen on Daniel Jones remaining the starter: "We'll evaluate everything"
summary: Anthony Richardson could finally get a chance to show what he can do.
full_text: As the Colts continue to struggle offensively, they continue to cling to quarterback Daniel Jones. That may not last for long. Asked by reporters after the 26-3 loss to the Texans whether Jones will remain the starter, coach Shane Steichen said, "We'll evaluate everything." The No. 2 quarterback is 2023 top-five pick Anthony Richardson. On Thursday night, he got a garbage-time drive in the fourth quarter. The three-and-out, which started at the Indianapolis 39, consisted of Richardson running for two yards and throwing two incomplete passes. It was Richardson's second appearance of the season; in Week 8, he got a couple of mop-up drives when the Colts trailed the Jaguars, 42-7. At some point, Richardson deserves a real chance to play. How much worse can the Colts' offense be? The Colts were outgained by the Texans, 354 yards to 167. They converted one of 11 third-down tries. Jones completed 12 of 27 passes, for 144 yards, no touchdowns, and an interception. There's a business reason that points to the Colts eventually getting Jones off the field. His contract has a $10.51 million injury guarantee for 2027. It vests in March. They'll inevitably bench Jones to keep him from getting an injury that would keep the Colts from releasing him before the injury guarantee converts to a full guarantee. That's what the Giants did to Jones two years ago. He then requested, and received, his release. The same thing could be happening, sooner rather than later, for Jones in Indianapolis. Which means that he could be available to another team. That possibility highlights the Colts' decision to not trade him for whatever they could get. And maybe they tried. Maybe, in the end, his availability in trade is what helped the Vikings keep the Raiders' asking price for Kirk Cousins to a third-round pick. And maybe, in the end, the Vikings will have a chance to add Jones to the depth chart while showing Carson Wentz the door.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jets improved their special teams coverage by having fullback Andrew Beck handle kickoffs
summary: Only one kickoff has been returned for a touchdown in the NFL this season, and it was allowed by the Jets when kicker Austin McNamara not only failed to make the tackle, but got in the way of his teammates as they tried to run down Raiders return man Dylan Laube.
full_text: Only one kickoff has been returned for a touchdown in the NFL this season, and it was allowed by the Jets when kicker Austin McNamara not only failed to make the tackle, but got in the way of his teammates as they tried to run down Raiders return man Dylan Laube. That got the Jets thinking they needed to improve their kickoff coverage. The solution was taking kickoff duties away from both McNamara, who is the Jets' punter, and Jason Sanders, who is the Jets' field goal kicker. Instead, it's now fullback Andrew Beck, who has been a good special teams player for years in the NFL, who is handling kickoffs. Beck made a tackle last week on what could have been a much longer kickoff return without him, and he said he loves being able to both kick and make the tackle afterward. “It was the whole reason that I’m out there, and I think it proves that it’s beneficial to have me doing it ,” Beck told Newsday . “Instead of just to get some cool pictures, I’m actually out there doing it for a reason.” Jets coach Aaron Glenn said when players have a skill set like Beck, with the ability to both kick and tackle, teams need to take advantage of that. “He’s a unique player that has done a little bit of everything throughout his career,” Glenn said. “We want to utilize that as much as we can.” Beck kicked in high school but not in college, and he didn't think he'd be kicking again in the NFL. Now that he has the job, however, he hopes it increases his value to the team, and bolsters his career. “I think I’ve shown that I can be successful in a couple different positions,” he said. “Hopefully the coaches feel comfortable putting me there.” It's almost unheard of for a player whose primary job isn't punter or kicker to handle kickoffs, although with the dynamic kickoff rule promoting returns, it makes sense for a player who can make tackles to be out there if he's capable of kicking the ball into the landing zone reliably. Saints safety Justin Reid has also kicked off, although he's only done it once this season. If the Jets have success with Beck, it might be something that other teams try — and it might make players who have the unique skill set of being both good kickers and good tacklers more valuable.
author: Michael David Smith

title: NFLPA names 49ers DL Osa Odighizuwa their Community MVP for Week 11
summary: The NFL Players Association announced on Friday that they have named 49ers defensive lineman Osa Odighizuwa as their Community MVP for Week 11.
full_text: ' The NFL Players Association announced on Friday that they have named 49ers defensive lineman Osa Odighizuwa as their Community MVP for Week 11. Odighizuwa, who was also a Community MVP last season, recently held events in Dallas, San Jose and Portland. Odighizuwa's foundation teamed with Progressive Insurance to provide a new car to a veteran in Dallas and Odighizuwa distributed 500 turkeys in the other two cities to local residents. “I appreciate everything the NFLPA does for us as players, and I’m honored to be named the Week 11 NFLPA Community MVP,” Odighizuwa said. “Giving back to Portland, Dallas and the Bay Area means a lot to me because each of those communities has played a part in my journey. I hope this recognition encourages my fellow union members to use their platforms to lift others up in the communities they call home.” The NFLPA will donate $10,000 to Odighizuwa's foundation and he will join the other weekly MVPs in being eligible for the Alan Page Award at the end of the season.
author: Josh Alper

title: The Protect College Sports Act proponents are getting desperate
summary: As the Protect College Sports Act languishes in the lame-duck session of the U.S.
full_text: As the Protect College Sports Act languishes in the lame-duck session of the U.S. House of Representatives, the folks who hope to cure the "chaos" in college sports with an antitrust exemption that will give the NCAA and its members a license to violate the rights of players are getting desperate. The best evidence of this comes from the fact that New York Yankees president Randy Levine, who serves as the vice-chair of President Trump’s Saving College Sports Roundtable, has called out Stephen A. Smith and me for our public opposition to the PCSA. We're being challenged by Levine because we've been vocal about calling the PCSA what it is — a bill that addresses the so-called "chaos" in college sports by reducing the rights that the players have won in recent years by successfully attacking a system that was littered with antitrust violations. The powers-that-be want Congress to wave a magic wand that will allow antitrust violations to occur without consequence. (I won't speak for Stephen A. as to why he opposes the PCSA; I respect the fact that he's willing to take a stand that clearly conflicts with the position of his employer.) Levine made his case against Stephen A. (and Michael J.) in an interview with Charles Gasparino of the New York Post . "One thing that has really annoyed me is the bogus argument put out by agents and their pundits such as Stephen A. Smith of ESPN and Mike Florio of NBC," Levine said, adding that we "continually misrepresent that student athletes have had and will have no voice, and that is untrue." The problem isn't they'll have "no voice" later. It's that they have "no voice" now. The process is being run not by the players but by the NCAA and the schools. The players aren't claiming that there's "chaos"; they benefit from the collapse of decades of antitrust violations flowing from the simple fact that the various schools huddled under the umbrella of the NCAA, which issued strict rules limiting what players can receive in exchange for playing college football. Also, the characterization of me as one of "their pundits" means that Levine believes my opinions aren't the product of my own authentic beliefs but that I'm somehow in the pockets of the agents representing college football players. While that is just plain false, the accusation isn't surprising. We've caught wind of at least one media member who was offered a significant payment for a social-media post supporting the Protect College Sports Act. (I don't know who specifically made the offer, but I know it was made.) Levine called me in September , on the same day that Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas) showed up on ESPN's College GameDay to promote the PCSA. Levine began by basically calling me stupid for not realizing that collective bargaining is an impossibility for college sports. Meanwhile, his November 10, 2026, letter to the entire U.S. House of Representatives explains on page 2 that "there will be nothing to prevent collective bargaining" if the PCSA passes. So if it's stupid for me to think collective bargaining is possible, why would he feel compelled to sell the House on the idea that the PCSA would allow for collective bargaining? Near the bottom of the article, Levine says this: "I've reached out to both of them (Smith and Florio) to debate me on this issue and heard crickets." I didn't recall a specific invitation to debate Levine on the issue. I re-read the text message he sent on September 12, after I posted the article regarding our conversation. (It was actually very friendly.) "Always willing to debate and as I said to you in the beginning of the call I just wanted you to have the facts," he wrote. "Was not trying to change your opinion." I didn't interpret that as an invitation to have a public debate. I thought he meant he's willing to continue to discuss the situation privately. I'm willing to do either, or both. One last point. Gasparino's article concludes by saying, "Reps for Smith and Florio had no immediate comment." Here's my immediate comment: I have reps? I'm easy to find, and I haven't received any request from Gasparino about my position on the PCSA. Which I hope will not exit the House — and which I hope will disappear. You broke it, you fix it. That should be the message to college sports. Congress has far better things to do, starting with figuring out how to avert an AI-triggered apocalypse. Which I wish were an exaggeration.
author: Mike Florio

title: David Montgomery credits the offensive line after his first big game as a Texan
summary: Montgomery totaled 124 yards as the Texans beat the Colts, 26-3.
full_text: The Texans traded for running back David Montgomery this offseason, and through the first 10 weeks of the season, he hadn't contributed much of anything. That changed on Thursday night. Montgomery had 26 carries for 107 yards, plus three catches for 17 yards, as the Texans beat the Colts, 26-3. Montgomery nearly doubled his previous season-high for yardage, and he averaged 4.1 yards per carry after having previously never averaged more than three yards per carry as a Texan. Afterwards, Montgomery gave the credit to the offensive line, which has been subjected to quite a bit of criticism this season. “Everybody on our offense, on the O-line , we should believe now because we can do it as long as we stick together and we stick to fundamentals,” Montgomery said, via the Houston Chronicle . “With them guys up front, they catch a lot of heat. They did a hell of a job.” At 4-6 the Texans still have an uphill battle to make the playoffs. But they traded for Montgomery in the hopes that he could have big games late in the season while they're fighting for a playoff berth, and on Thursday night, Montgomery and the Texans' offensive line did that.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Christian Parker considered not staying with the Cowboys
summary: The Cowboys have removed play-calling duties from defensive coordinator Christian Parker.
full_text: ''' The Cowboys have removed play-calling duties from defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Parker initially considered leaving the team. He decided not to. Parker told reporters on Thursday that he decided to process the "significant" disappointment by remaining in his job, albeit with the most important role taken away. "That would have been running from it," Parker said as to the possibility of resigning. As to whether it will be awkward moving forward, Parker said, "I think it's only awkward if you make it, and we don't have to make it that way." But it will be awkward. The defensive coordinator isn't fully coordinating the defense. And it's not like the situation in Denver, where the head coach assumed the play-calling duties from the coordinator. Parker's biggest responsibilities were given to someone other than the head coach — a consultant who arrived just last month. The cleanest approach for the Cowboys, given the team's obvious lack of confidence in Parker, would have been to fire him. But that would have come with a buyout of the balance of his contract. And owner/G.M. Jerry Jones doesn't like paying coaches to not work. Jones likely hopes Parker will eventually realize that the situation isn't sustainable and (as the lingo goes) "self-select." That avoids the buyout and conclusively ends the inherently awkward situation.
author: Mike Florio

title: C.J. Stroud: I knew what kind of player I could be, amazing to be in this groove
summary: After a rough end to the 2025 season, Texans quarterback C.J.
full_text: After a rough end to the 2025 season, Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud came into the 2026 season needing to show he was capable of the kind of consistent production that would land him a big contract extension from the team. The Texans' overall season hasn't played out as hoped in Houston, but it's not because Stroud has fallen short. He's putting together his best NFL season and it continued with three touchdown passes in Thursday night's win over the Colts. It was Stroud's third straight game with at least three touchdown passes and it's the first time that Stroud has put together a stretch like that since entering the league. "I knew what type of player I could be in this league ," Stroud said, via DJ Bien-Amie of ESPN.com. "And to just get in that groove and have a rhythm, it's been amazing. Honestly, I would be lying to you if I said it didn't feel good." Stroud is one off his career high for touchdowns in a season and on pace for a career high in passing yards as well, which makes him a leading reason for the Texans to hope that they can win enough games to get back to the postseason.
author: Josh Alper

title: Puka Nacua serving suspension while on IR raises an important question
summary: The news that Rams receiver Puka Nacua will serve a three-game suspension while on injured reserve raised plenty of eyebrows, because on the surface it seems very convenient.
full_text: ''' The news that Rams receiver Puka Nacua will serve a three-game suspension while on injured reserve raised plenty of eyebrows, because on the surface it seems very convenient. It seems convenient because it is convenient. More accurately, it's strategic. The suspension is the result of a negotiation between the league and Nacua. In lieu of taking the process to a full-blown hearing before Judge Sue L. Robinson, whose findings of fact ( e.g. , "no violation was committed") cannot be appealed by the NFL to the Commissioner, the two sides reached a compromise. They made a deal. It happens every day in civil and criminal courts throughout the country. Controversies get resolved by negotiation. The mutual uncertainty — one side will win, one side will lose — becomes an outcome that, ideally, both sides don't like but they'll accept. So the league, which may have been concerned that Nacua wouldn't be suspended at all, agreed to a three-game suspension. Given the timing of the deal, the league necessarily agreed to let Nacua serve the suspension while otherwise unable to play. The NFL didn't have to do that. It could have dragged its feet. It could have rolled the dice on the decision to be made by Judge Sue L. Robinson. The league ultimately negotiated, and accepted, a situation that allows Nacua to engineer the process in a way that suspends him at a time when he otherwise wouldn't be playing. The league realizes that many will disagree with the outcome. That's why the initial statement regarding the suspension was followed by an email that said this: "A player’s injury designation does not delay discipline or prevent a suspension from being served. "Consistent with prior cases, the suspension begins when it is imposed. "There is precedent for players serving suspensions while on Reserve/Injured or otherwise unavailable because of injury. This is not a new rule or an exception created for Nacua. "• Daniel Ekuale, Pittsburgh, 2025 season, was suspended five games for a violation of the performance-enhancing substances policy following a season-ending injury. "• Sam Williams, Dallas, 2024 season, was suspended three games for violating the personal conduct policy while already out for the season. "• Mike Woods, Cleveland, 2023, was suspended six games for violating the personal conduct policy while he was out on NFI. "• David Parry, New Orleans, 2018, was suspended four games for violations of the personal conduct and substances of abuse policies while on injured reserve." Indeed, Chiefs receiver Rashee Rice had hoped to serve his Personal Conduct Policy suspension for a street-racing incident during the 2024 season, while he was on injured reserve due to a serious knee injury suffered in Week 4. (That didn't happen, because Rice's lawyers were unable to get the prosecutors to finalize the plea deal until after the 2024 season ended.) Similarly, kicker Justin Tucker served his full 10-game suspension in 2025 while not employed by any NFL team. Here's the philosophical question that the NFL could in theory revisit: Should certain suspensions only be served by a player who is healthy enough to play? The current system allows players to navigate the process in a way that allows suspensions to be served while the player is injured. And, again, the league chose to resolve the Nacua case at a time when he was injured. The league could have insisted on a suspension that begins once he's healthy, as part of the negotiation. Ultimately, the league exercised the discretion that is inherent to the negotiations that ended the case in a way that allowed to be suspended while injured. The league could have refused to settle the case in a way that allowed Nacua to serve a suspension while injured. Some will say the league was doing Nacua (and, in turn, the Rams) a favor. The truth may be that the league had real concerns about losing the case before Judge Sue L. Robinson, and that taking a harder line may have resulted in no suspension at all. Either way, the current system permits it. Moving forward, the league should consider whether — when it comes specifically to the Personal Conduct Policy — it will allow a player to serve a suspension that (while expensive as it relates to the forfeiture of pay) costs the player no playing time.
author: Mike Florio

title: Brock Purdy: Practicing at altitude was the right move, for sure
summary: When the 49ers play the Vikings this weekend, they'll do so at the altitude of Mexico City at Estadio Banorte.
full_text: ' When the 49ers play the Vikings this weekend, they'll do so at the altitude of Mexico City at Estadio Banorte. That's why the team is in Colorado Springs this week to practice at the Air Force Academy to get acclimated. The altitude at Colorado Springs is comparable to that of Mexico City, at over 7,000 feet above sea level. Quarterback Brock Purdy told reporters on Thursday that he appreciates being at altitude this week to prepare. “It’s a real thing. I think it’s been nice to be here, practice and get some workouts in," Purdy said, via transcript from the team. "Even just obviously doing meetings and just living here for a week. It’s been a real thing that we’ve had to adjust to, and I’m glad that we’re here. I think it’s the right move, for sure. Obviously, Mexico City is going to be in a higher elevation than this, but overall, it’s going to be tough for everybody. We’re not living in it year-round or anything like that, so I don’t know. It’s going to be a part of the game for sure." Purdy was on the team the last time the 49ers played in Mexico City back in 2022, so he has some understanding of what awaits him. But that was before Jimmy Garoppolo’s injury put Purdy in line to start. “Obviously, I didn’t play, but just warming up and being there in the game, seeing guys come off the field and seeing them pretty exhausted. It’s a real thing and I think we’re all ready for it,” Purdy said. “For me, I remember those kinds of things, so I’ve just got to be on top of it and prepare for it.” Kickoff between the Vikings and 49ers is set for 8:20 p.m. ET on Sunday night.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Ashton Jeanty's bad season running the ball overshadows his receiving production
summary: Jeanty is second in the NFL in both catches and receiving yards for a running back this season.
full_text: In the time of hot takes, nuanced opinions rarely get much attention, and so in the case of Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty, little has been said about him this season other than that he's a bust. Last year the Raiders took Jeanty with the sixth overall pick in the NFL draft, and this year he's averaging 3.09 yards per carry, worst in the NFL among the 34 running backs with at least 70 carries this season. First running back drafted to last running back in the yards-per-carry rankings? Bust. Case closed. Except it's not that simple. There's no excusing the Raiders' awful rushing offense and Jeanty's role in it, but it's also unfair to talk about Jeanty without acknowledging that he's one of the best receivers out of the backfield in the NFL. Jeanty has 46 catches this season, second only to Cincinnati's Chase Brown among NFL running backs. And Jeanty has 417 receiving yards, second only to San Francisco's Christian McCaffrey. There are a lot of running backs who get praised for what they can contribute in the passing game -- Detroit's Jahmyr Gibbs, Atlanta's Bijan Robinson, Pittsburgh's Jaylen Warren -- and Jeanty has produced more in the passing game than all of them. Jeanty's 17 receiving first downs are tied with McCaffrey for the most of any running back in the NFL this season. Although Jeanty has only one rushing touchdown this season, he has three receiving touchdowns, tied for the second-most among NFL running backs. (Kansas City's Kenneth Walker has four.) On Sunday against the Seahawks, when Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza struggled in his first NFL start, Jeanty was his leading receiver, with four catches for 46 yards. With the Raiders trying to mount a comeback in the fourth quarter, it was Jeanty turning a short pass into a 38-yard gain that got the Raiders into range for the field goal that made it a one-possession game. The Raiders lost, and Jeanty deserves his share of the blame for their inability to do anything on the ground, but the loss would have been worse if not for Jeanty being available as an outlet receiver for Mendoza. Jeanty hasn't been the player the Raiders thought they were getting after he was college football's leading rusher at Boise State. But his contributions to the Raiders' offense are real, even if they're not spectacular.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Geno Smith set for full practice on Friday
summary: Jets quarterback Geno Smith's chances of playing against the Chargers on Sunday are looking good.
full_text: Jets quarterback Geno Smith's chances of playing against the Chargers on Sunday are looking good. Head coach Aaron Glenn said at a Friday morning press conference that Smith is set to practice for the third straight day. Smith injured his ankle in last Sunday's loss to the Bills and has been limited in practice, but Glenn said that he is expected to move up to full participation and that things are moving in the right direction for him to get the start this weekend. Smith has not missed a start this season and has 2,226 yards, 12 touchdowns and three interceptions while completing 67.1 percent of his passes. Any positives from those number have been mitigated by red zone struggles that have kept the Jets out of the end zone since the third quarter of Week 8. Glenn said that wide receivers Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) will not play. Defensive tackle David Onyemata (abdomen) will not be activated from injured reserve.
author: Josh Alper

title: Thursday Night Football: C.J. Stroud, Texans lead Colts 17-3 at halftime
summary: Stroud threw two touchdown passes in the first half.
full_text: ' The Texans are doing what they need to do. Now, can they finish? Four days after blowing a 17-0 lead over the Browns, Houston leads Indianapolis 17-3 at halftime. The Texans outgained the Colts 202 to 125 in the first half but settled for Ka'imi Fairbairn's 27-yard field goal after stalling at the Indianapolis 9 in the closing seconds. C.J. Stroud went 13-of-18 for 134 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. He now ranks third in team history in passing yards, surpassing David Carr (13,391). He has 21 touchdown passes, two short of his career high for a season. Stroud's touchdowns covered 42 yards to Nico Collins and 24 yards to Kayshon Boutte. David Montgomery, who missed the previous four games with a groin injury, has 11 carries for 54 yards. Collins has two catches for 48 yards and a touchdown. The Colts had four plays of over 20 yards, but went 0-for-1 in the red zone, missed two field goals and threw an interception. The Colts scored their only points on Spencer Shrader's 34-yard field goal. But he missed from 56 and had a 62-yarder blocked by Logan Hall with 2:41 remaining in the half. Daniel Jones was only 1-for-5 for 22 yards with an interception in the second quarter. He finished the half 7-of-17 for 109 yards and an interception. Jonathan Taylor has eight carries for 17 yards. Texans offensive tackle Trent Brown was questionable to return with a back injury. He had been alternating with Braden Smith at right tackle, but Smith played most of the half. Brown, though, did return before the half ended. Texans defensive tackle Sheldon Rankins is questionable with an ankle injury.
author: Charean Williams

title: Aidan Hutchinson: That's the last time I go airborne
summary: Lions head coach Dan Campbell said he isn't going to tell players to stop celebrating big plays because of defensive end Aidan Hutchinson's torn ACL, but Hutchinson is going to be making some changes on his own.
full_text: Lions head coach Dan Campbell said he isn't going to tell players to stop celebrating big plays because of defensive end Aidan Hutchinson's torn ACL, but Hutchinson is going to be making some changes on his own. In a post to his Instagram account, Hutchinson made his first public comments since suffering his injury last Sunday. Hutchinson leaped in the air after sacking Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and his knee went out upon landing. Hutchinson wrote that he has "jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me" and that it will "never make sense" why things played out the way that they did. He added that he does know he will come back stronger from the injury and "that's the last time I go airborne." Hutchinson closed the post with a message asking his Lions teammates to "hold down the fort til I’m back." That won't be until 2027, but Hutchinson has shown once already that he can make a full recovery from this kind of injury so there is some light at the end of the tunnel in Detroit.
author: Josh Alper

title: As he did with the Giants, Colts QB Daniel Jones is struggling, right after getting paid
summary: Jones was awful again in Thursday night's loss to the Texans.
full_text: Daniel Jones' career has had some ups, but also plenty of downs, both with the Giants and with the Colts. He has a knack for having his "ups" in contract years, and his "downs" after getting paid. Jones was awful in Thursday night's loss to the Texans, continuing the worst season of his career — which comes after the Colts signed him to a two-year, $88 million contract in the offseason. It's not the first time Jones has performed poorly after getting a big deal. In fact, that's all Jones has done throughout his NFL career. Jones' career started when the Giants made the surprising decision to select him with the sixth overall pick in the 2019 NFL draft. That earned him a four-year, $25.7 million contract, with the Giants having a fifth-year option. Jones didn't live up to expectations on that rookie contract, and was playing some of the worst football of his career when his third season ended early with a neck injury, so the Giants declined his fifth-year option. But Jones then played very well in his fourth year, leading the Giants to a surprise playoff berth and a win in the wild card round. That led the Giants to sign him to a four-year, $160 million contract in 2023, committing more money to him than his fifth-year option would have cost. Jones responded to that with a fifth season in which he played poorly, suffered another neck injury and then suffered a season-ending torn ACL. Jones returned in 2024 but was so bad the Giants first benched him, then cut him. Jones spent the rest of that season on the Vikings' practice squad. In 2025 the Colts signed him to a one-year contract, and he responded by winning a quarterback competition with Anthony Richardson and then playing the best football of his career early in 2025 as the Colts jumped out to an 8-2 start. He started to struggle down the stretch in that season, and then his season was cut short by a torn Achilles tendon, but the Colts were so impressed by his start that they signed him to a two-year, $88 million contract in March. And now, in the first year of that contract, Jones is worse than ever. His 13 interceptions are the most of any quarterback in the NFL this season and already a career-high, with six more games to play. He's paired that with just seven touchdown passes. He still hasn't had a single game this season with more touchdowns than interceptions. His 65.4 passer rating is a career low. His 30.3 QBR is a career low. His 58.4 percent completion rate is a career low. His 5.6 yards per pass average is a career low. Jones was once an effective runner, but his 2.9 yards per carry average is also a career low. Any way you slice it, Jones is worse than ever. He's also more expensive than ever. Whether the Colts keep him or cut him, he's going to have a massive salary cap hit in 2027, the kind of cap hit that will make it that much harder for the Colts to rebuild their roster. If the Colts cut Jones, he may sign another one-year contract with another team. No matter how well he plays, that team would be wise not to give him a lucrative extension.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Bills to retire Andre Reed's No. 83 in 2027
summary: The Bills will be retiring the number of the top wide receiver in franchise history next year.
full_text: ''' The Bills will be retiring the number of the top wide receiver in franchise history next year. Andre Reed piled up more catches, receiving yards and receiving touchdowns than any Bills player while helping the franchise to four straight Super Bowls in the 1990s and the Bills announced that they will be enshrining his No. 83 alongside the numbers of his longtime teammates Jim Kelly, Thurman Thomas and Bruce Smith at some point during the 2027 season. All four players are also in the Pro Football Hall of Fame. "He's one of the main reasons I'm up on that wall ," Kelly said, via the team's website. "He's one of the main reasons I'm in the Pro Football Hall of Fame; it takes both of us. When your quarterback goes in, usually you're probably going to have a receiver or two go in. . . . To have Andre for my whole career was just totally awesome. I thought it should have been done a few years ago, but I'm glad that it's getting done, and I'm glad I'm able to be here and celebrate his going on the wall to join me, Bruce and Thurman." Reed had 941 catches for 13,095 yards and 86 touchdowns over 15 seasons in Buffalo. He was added to the franchise's Wall of Fame in 2006 and voted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2014.
author: Josh Alper

title: Thursday Night Football: Texans beat up on Colts, 26-3
summary: The Texans moved to 4-6 to keep their slim playoff hopes alive.
full_text: '' The Texans did what they needed to do Thursday night to remain sort of, kind of, maybe in the playoff race. Houston beat up on Indianapolis 26-3 to move to 4-6, while the Colts fell to 3-8. The Texans outgained the Colts 355 to 167 as C.J. Stroud threw for 194 yards and three touchdowns, while completing 21 of 27 passes. Stroud’s touchdowns covered 42 yards to Nico Collins, 24 yards to Kayshon Boutte and 13 yards to Marlin Klein. It was Klein's first career touchdown as the rookie entered Thursday with only one catch. Collins caught three passes for 58 yards. Texans running back David Montgomery, who missed four games with a groin injury, had 26 carries for 107 yards in his return. The Texans played without running back Woody Marks, who has a concussion. Will Anderson had a sack of Daniel Jones in the end zone for a safety, increasing his league-leading sack total to 11.5. Jadeveon Clowney also had a sack, and Kamari Lassiter had a pick of Daniel Jones. Jones was 12-of-27 for 144 yards and a pick, and Jonathan Taylor rushed for only 21 yards on 11 carries. Anthony Gould made two catches for 48 yards. The Colts scored their only points on Spencer Shrader’s 34-yard field goal. But he missed from 56 and had a 62-yarder blocked by Logan Hall with 2:41 remaining in the first half.
author: Charean Williams

title: Puka Nacua had surgery on MCL injury, will miss 'a couple of months,' Sean McVay says
summary: Nacua suffered the injury on the final play of the Rams' Week 9 win over the Commanders
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams knew they would be without star wide receiver Puka Nacua for at least four games after he was placed on injured reserve, but now it appears that his absence will extend even longer than that. Head coach Sean McVay said Friday that Nacua had surgery on his MCL and will miss "a couple of months."
Nacua suffered MCL and PCL sprains on the final offensive snap of the team's Week 9 win over the Washington Commanders . He took a handoff on third-and-11 and ran it for a 5-yard gain but was injured on the play. He was placed on injured reserve after the injury, which is apparently more serious than initially appeared, given that it required surgery.
Nacua was also suspended earlier this week for three games for violating the league's personal conduct policy, a suspension he will serve while on IR. The NFL did not disclose the nature of his violation, but it's believed that the suspension is related to his ongoing civil suit, which stems from allegations that he bit a woman and made an antisemitic remark.
The NFL did not know that Nacua had potentially season-ending surgery when it suspended him for three games, according to The Athletic .
Now, the Rams will likely be without Nacua for at least the remainder of the regular season. They're on their bye in Week 11 but return in Week 12 to take on the Green Bay Packers in a Wednesday game the night before Thanksgiving. They'll close out their season with games against the Kansas City Chiefs , San Francisco 49ers , Dallas Cowboys , Seattle Seahawks , Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Seahawks again.

title: In Kansas City, Kenneth Walker III and the run game makes the Chiefs contenders again
summary: One of the league's most explosive running backs has the Chiefs looking like their old Super Bowl-winning selves.
full_text:
Over the last two years, the Kansas City Chiefs had a significant problem: they could not create big plays. In 2024 and 2025, Kansas City generated a gain of 20-plus yards on just 4.8% of its offensive plays, according to Tru Media, a rate that ranked tied for 29th in the NFL .
The Chiefs were once arguably the most explosive offense in the NFL. Between 2018 ( Patrick Mahomes ' first full season as the starter) and 2023, the Chiefs created an explosive play on 7.2% of their offensive plays, second-place and just 0.1% behind the league-leading San Francisco 49ers .
Over the years, defenses started playing the Chiefs much differently in the latter part of the Tyreek Hill era, especially after Hill left the team. They prioritized shutting down explosive passing plays with two-high coverages and daring the Chiefs to march the ball downfield with short passes and runs. And for the most part, the Chiefs were able to do just that.
Kansas City ranked second in the NFL in success rate (50.5%) between 2021 (Hill's final season with the Chiefs) and 2023, according to TruMedia, checking in first in passing success rate despite a lower explosive-play rate and a respectable 13th in rushing success rate. In 2024 and 2025, the Chiefs' success rate dropped to 48.5%, and they dropped to 12th in passing success rate and 14th in rushing success rate. Their inability to create explosive plays on the ground or through the air limited their ability to generate positive gains on shorter plays.
Defenses were particularly unthreatened by Kansas City's ability to run the ball. With a post-injury Isaiah Pacheco and an aging Kareem Hunt in the backfield, the Chiefs simply could not create big plays on the ground, and defenses didn't much care if they wanted to plod along at around three-and-a-half yards per carry. They were, in fact, quite happy to let the Chiefs burn plays on those piddling gains, setting up Patrick Mahomes and the passing game in disadvantageous down-and-distance situations.
Faced with this problem, the Chiefs finally made a significant investment in their running back room, targeting one of the NFL's most explosive backs by signing Kenneth Walker III to a three-year, $43.05 million contract in free agency. Between 2022 and 2025, Walker ranked seventh in the NFL in explosive run rate among the 34 running backs with at least 500 carries, according to TruMedia — and he was 0.3% away from third place on that list.
The investment has paid off beyond the Chiefs' wildest dreams. The Chiefs have soared from dead last in the NFL in explosive run rate in 2024 and 2025 to third in 2026. Between Walker and backup Emmett Johnson , the Chiefs already have more explosive runs by running backs this season than they did in the last two years combined, according to Tru Media. Kansas City has done all that without sacrificing down-to-down efficiency, which was at least a minor concern with Walker.
The Chiefs' rate of negative-yard runs has barely moved this year, while their rates of five-plus-yard runs and explosive runs have, well, exploded. As a result, their yards-per-carry average has jumped from 31st in the league to first, and their EPA per-play average on rushing attempts has jumped from 14th in the league to first.
And it really is largely due to the running backs. The offensive line is creating a bit more yardage before contact, according to TruMedia, but the differential pales in comparison to the difference in yards after contact, and especially in avoided tackle rate.
Walker, in particular, is seemingly able to generate explosive runs out of thin air. He can do it by getting skinny in the hole and then bursting through for a big gain. He's not necessarily known for this, but it shows up all over his tape.
pic.twitter.com/LgHBLBHEoZ
He can do it by pressing the hole and then, when he sees nothing available in the designed gap, bouncing it to the outside and beating oncoming defenders—whether they be linebackers or defensive backs—to the corner and scooting right past them to the end zone. How many times have we seen him do something like this this year?
pic.twitter.com/WtNpaShyGp
Both he and Johnson can spot the cutback lanes when the front side gets clogged up. They have the vision, and especially the quickness, to make a hard stop and cut, or jump from one hole to the next and beat defenders to the spot. We've seen this repeatedly throughout the season.
pic.twitter.com/4hs524epcN
Johnson is also just extremely slippery. You can't get him down with the first tackler. He just shakes the guy in front of him, whether with a juke, a cut, a shrug-off, or something else. And then he makes the second and third guy work to bring him down to the ground as well.
pic.twitter.com/aC8F1LzrGx
And of course, Walker can put all of those things together on one run. He'll bounce it to the outside, shake off a tackler, cut back, break another tackle, and then keep gaining yards. Some of the moves he strings together are almost comical.
pic.twitter.com/Sm6R4ILzwb
These two backs creating yardage on their own have been a massive boon to Kansas City's offense. The Chiefs were 11th in EPA per play across the 2024 and 2025 seasons, and they're fifth so far this year. They're fifth in success rate and first in yards per play, as well.
And that's all true despite the fact that they have been without their starting left tackle all season, have benched one of their guards for disciplinary reasons in two different games, and failed to add any talent to the pass-catching corps until they traded for Josh Downs last week. It's been almost entirely about the run game, and specifically about the guys running the ball.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Aidan Hutchinson speaks out on freak injury celebration: 'That's the last time I go airborne'
summary: Hutchinson tore his ACL while celebrating a sack of New England's Drake Maye
full_text:
Star Detroit Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffered one of the most unfortunate injuries of the NFL season when he tore his ACL while celebrating a sack of New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye early in the Lions' win over the Pats in Munich, Germany.
Hutchinson brought Maye to the ground and then jumped into the air in celebration. He tore his knee when he landed.
Aidan Hutchinson suffered an injury on this play and went to the locker room. (📺 FOX) pic.twitter.com/ysx9NLmNHF
Hutchinson is out for the remainder of the season, dealing a significant blow to the Lions' hopes of making a run through the playoffs. On Thursday, Hutchinson released a statement about the injury, his recovery and his future celebration plans via his Instagram account.
"I honestly can't believe it. I've jumped hundreds of times on a football field and never in a million years did I think this would happen to me," Hutchinson wrote. "But even something like this won't hold me back."
In the wake of the injury, New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo said that he's retiring his backflip celebration because of what happened to Hutchinson. And now, Hutchinson himself says he won't be jumping in the air in celebration anymore, either.
"Two things I know for sure: 1. I always come back stronger," Hutchinson said. "2. That's the last time I go airborne 😁👍"
Hutchinson getting injured while celebrating his sack meant that he joined a sneakily extensive list of players suffering unusually-timed injuries, such as Lamarr Houston , Stephen Tulloch and Bill Gramatica, each of whom also tore their ACL while celebrating a play.
Hutchinson's injury probably won't stop everyone in the league from celebrating in the air, but if it inspires even a few more players to stop going airborne, that'll probably be for the best.
For what it's worth, Lions coach Dan Campbell said that even in the wake of Hutchinson being lost for the season, he won't tell his players to stop celebrating on the field.
"I hate it. I think we all understand what it is, and let's be smart, but no, I'm not gonna say, 'Nobody celebrates anymore,'" Campbell said on 97.1 The Ticket .
Campbell also recalled a story from his own playing days while again stating that he won't tell players to stop celebrating their on-field accomplishments.
"No, I don't believe that. I think what happened speaks for itself," Campbell said. "We're not talking to 8-year-olds here. And I'll give you a story. I remember one time I made a big play, and I freaking pumped my arm up and I'm pretty sure I tore my bicep, but I didn't tell anybody. I was just excited. I just pumped my arm.
"This game is built off of emotion. And if you have to contain yourself after a play is made — I'm not talking about in the moment, in the game, because you gotta keep your head — then you're really becoming something you're not."
Campbell is a firm believer in building the personality of your team. It's clear that he doesn't want to change his team's personality — which has been built in his own image over the years — even in the wake of a devastating injury.

title: Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs laying early foundation for one of the best running back careers ever
summary: Gibbs is only 3.5 years into his NFL career, and he's on a few different record-breaking paces
full_text:
For the first three years of his NFL career, Detroit Lions three-time Pro Bowl running back Jahmyr Gibbs was known as part of one of the NFL's best running back tandems, the "Sonic" in the Lions' "Sonic and Knuckles" duo with David Montgomery . Today, Gibbs is showing that, as a solo act, not only can he can be the NFL's No. 1 back, but he's also laying the early groundwork to become one of the greatest running backs of all time.
Yes, that sounds hyperbolic, but Gibbs' production is at all-time levels through three-and-a-half seasons. On an international stage in Week 10, he erupted for 252 yards from scrimmage (153 rushing yards on 22 carries plus 99 yards on 7 catches), the most in a game by any player this season, and 2 rushing touchdowns in the Lions' 35-10 stomping of the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. An outing like that reshuffles some NFL record boards.
Just halfway through his fourth season, Gibbs passed Pro Football Hall of Famer Terrell Davis (61 touchdowns in his first four seasons) for the most touchdowns in a player's first four seasons in NFL history (62 and counting). Gibbs is also now the first player in NFL history with 1,000 rushing yards (exactly 1,000) and 350 receiving yards (384) in a player's first nine games of a season. With an NFL-best 1,384 yards from scrimmage and a league-high13 scrimmage touchdowns in nine games, Gibbs is on pace for an NFL single-season record: 2,614 yards from scrimmage, which would smash current record holder Chris Johnson's 2,509 from the 2009 season.
All of those feats are jaw-dropping on their own, but together they paint an all-time picture. What is perhaps most amazing about Gibbs is how consistently excellent he is, to the point that the football world is somewhat numb to his greatness. Producing 150-plus rushing yards and a rushing touchdown in a game is outstanding. Six players have produced such a game this season, but five of the six have done so no more than twice. Then there is Gibbs, who has done so four times in Detroit's first nine games, making him just the fourth player in NFL history to do so. The other three are a who's who of Hall of Fame running backs: Jim Brown (1958, 1963), O.J. Simpson (1974, 1975) and Emmitt Smith (1995).
Now, some people might feel Gibbs' historic start to his NFL career is amplified by a talent offensive ecosystem that has a five-time Pro Bowler at quarterback, Jared Goff , a four-time Pro Bowler at wide receiver ( Amon-Ra St. Brown ), a Pro Bowl tight end ( Sam LaPorta ), a four-time Pro Bowl offensive tackle ( Penei Sewell ), and a speedster No. 2 wide receiver ( Jameson Williams ). However, Gibbs and his consistent excellence power everything else in the Motor City team's offense. He ranks seventh in the league in yards before contact per rush (1.57) and eighth in yards after contact per rush (3.5) this season.
Among the 27 players with at least 100 carries in 2026, Gibbs' 29.1% tackles-avoided rate is the second-best in the league, behind only Kenneth Walker III's 32.1% rate. Since Next Gen Stats began tracking explosive runs (runs of 10 or more yards) in 2016, no running back has produced more through the first 10 weeks of a season than Gibbs' 34. Prime Ezekiel Elliott in his rookie year with the Dallas Cowboys in 2016 is the closest player in this span with 29. Gibbs isn't just a cog in the Lions' machine: his juice powers the rest of the machine.
Here's the cherry on top. Not even through his fourth NFL season, Gibbs has more games (two) with 250-plus scrimmage yards and multiple touchdowns in his 58-game career than Barry Sanders, the running back many believe is the best pure runner ever, did in his 10-season, 153-game career.
Week 11 gives Gibbs a chance to deliver an all-time encore performance in a matchup against Pro Bowl defensive tackle Vita Vea and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , the No. 1 run defense in the NFL (79.2 rushing yards per game allowed) this season. Get your popcorn ready as Gibbs continues to build a strong case for being the league's most productive running back ever.
author: Garrett Podell

title: NFL exploring possibility of implementing new travel rules for international games
summary: NFL teams might have to change the way they travel for international games
full_text:
With the NFL's uptick in international games over the last few years, there's no rule requiring a team to arrive in a foreign city by a certain date before a game, but that could change. That could change soon.
The NFL is currently exploring a new travel policy that would require each team to spend a minimum number of nights in an international city. In an interview this week with The Athletic , NFL executive VP of club business Peter O'Reilly confirmed that a change could be coming.
"Currently, we leave those football decisions on when the team arrives in the market to the club," O'Reilly said. "It is something that we'll consider moving forward on: Do we put some minimum nights in a market in there? It's something we'll look at."
It's no surprise the NFL is thinking hard about this topic, especially after what happened in Week 1 during the league's first regular-season game in Australia between the 49ers and the Rams . The 49ers decided to fly out a full week before the game so they could acclimate to the 17-hour time difference. Leaving early also allowed the team to fully immerse themselves in Australian culture.
On the other hand, the Rams infamously didn't arrive until the last minute: They landed in Melbourne at about 7 a.m. ET on Thursday morning , leaving them less than 30 hours until their game with the 49ers kicked off.
The Rams traveled late so that their players wouldn't have to adjust to Australian time, but the plan backfired. The Rams looked slow and tired during a 27-7 loss.
If the NFL does implement a minimum-night rule, it likely won't be anything dramatic. The rule that would make the most sense is having teams arrive at least two nights in advance. For a game in Europe, that would mean a team would have to leave Thursday night to arrive Friday.
That exact travel plan was not only popular this year, but also successful. In fact, teams traveling to Europe went 4-0 this year when arriving on Friday. The Steelers , Texans , Colts , and Jaguars (for their first London game) all arrived Friday morning for their international game, and all four teams won. It's hard to imagine the NFL creating a rule to eliminate something that's working well for teams, so if the league implements a new travel policy, it likely won't be a massive change.
Since international play started in 2007, there are only three instances of a team showing up the day before a game in a city at least five time zones away, and the Rams were involved in two of them. The Rams arrived on Saturday in London for a 35-7 blowout win over the Jaguars in 2025, which is why they likely felt good about arriving the day before the game in Australia this year. The Eagles ended up copying the Rams' strategy for their game in London this year, arriving on Saturday for their matchup against the Jags, which ended up being a dramatic 19-17 loss.
There were a total of nine international games this year, and the final one will be played in Mexico City on Sunday night between the Vikings and the 49ers. If the NFL does implement a new travel policy, it will be interesting to see whether it includes games like this that are geographically closer to the United States. The Vikings are flying down to the game on Saturday because the flight from Minnesota to Mexico City is only about 4.5 hours and there's no time zone change, so it's not necessarily a reason to travel early (The stadium in Mexico City does have an altitude of 7,350 feet, so it could make sense to travel early to get acclimated to that, but the Vikings decided not to go that route ).
Under the current CBA, the NFL is allowed to schedule up to 10 international games for 2027, and if the league hits that number, it will certainly be interesting to see if a new travel policy is in place for next season.

And I'm kind of surprised this number is so cheap relative to what Tony Pollard's done for Tennessee this season. Dallas can't stop anyone and Pollard is the Titans go-to guy in the red zone and at the goal line. He's definitely one of the guys I'd put in a two-touchdown scorer round robin parlay (along with D'Andre Swift and James Cook).
I like the idea of targeting some of these running backs to score TWO touchdowns in these high-spread games as mentioned above. But if Cook doesn't score twice -- and even if he does -- the Bills should theoretically be leaning on their backup running back for part of this game given the spread and the lack of Malik Willis for the Dolphins . It's a long shot so only put a half unit on it, but Davis should absolutely see some reps in this one.

title: Week 11 bold predictions: Fernando Mendoza upsets Broncos, Tony Pollard breaks Cowboys
summary: Plus, Jahmyr Gibbs dominates Tampa Bay's No. 1 run defense
full_text:
Almost anything can happen in the National Football League, and the kickoff to Week 11 of the 2026 season showcased the limits of the league's parity.
In the Houston Texans ' (4-6) 26-3 road win on the road over the torn-down Indianapolis Colts (3-8), three-time Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor went for just 21 yards rushing on 11 carries. It marked an unfathomable 21 consecutive games without 100 yards rushing in a game, the worst drought of his career. Meanwhile, quarterback Daniel Jones just polished off his sixth straight game with an interception, the longest streak by a Colts player since Curtis Painter was filling in for an injured Peyton Manning in 2011.
Meanwhile, Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud threw two of his three touchdown passes for 20-plus air yards after having two combined in his first nine games of the 2026 season. Stroud's seven-game streak of multiple total touchdowns is now the longest in Texans history.
What surprises could occur across the rest of the NFL's Week 11 slate? Let's take a look at five bold predictions.
Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza , the first overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, made his debut as an NFL starting quarterback against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in Week 10. That made Mendoza the first No. 1 overall pick in NFL history to make his first career start against the defending Super Bowl champion, per CBS Sports Research. He held his own, completing 17 of his 29 throws for 143 yards while also adding 22 yards and a rushing touchdown on six carries. Despite being sacked six times, Mendoza and the Raiders only lost by eight points, 21-13.
After adjusting to the pace of the NFL game against the Seahawks, Mendoza and the Raiders will head to Empower Field at Mile High Stadium in Denver and emerge victorious against the Broncos . Denver quarterback Bo Nix doesn't scare any defense, ranking last in the league in air yards per pass attempt (5.6). For whatever reason, he can't or won't pull the trigger on throws down the field. Five-time Pro Bowl Raiders edge rusher Maxx Crosby will do enough to spook Nix while Mendoza helps Las Vegas' offense score just enough points for the 10.5-point underdogs, according to DraftKings Sportsbook, to emerge victorious on Sunday.
Tony Pollard is ascending to new heights at the age of 29 and in the final year of his three-year, $21.75 million contract with the Tennessee Titans . Across his last three games, Pollard has produced 279 yards rushing, 112 yards receiving and six total touchdowns. Even though the Titans had a Week 9 bye, Pollard still ranks in the top 10 in rushing yards, rushing touchdowns, receiving touchdowns and total touchdowns by a running back since Week 7. His five rushing touchdowns are tied for the most in the NFL in this span with Bucky Irving , and his six scrimmage touchdowns in this stretch are tied for the most in the league with Christian McCaffrey .
Pollard now has his sights set on scoring a touchdown in four consecutive games for the first time in his eight-season NFL career. And just in time for his first matchup with the Dallas Cowboys , the team that drafted him in the fourth round of the 2019 NFL Draft and the team he called home for his first five seasons. His homecoming on Sunday at AT&T Stadium will mark Pollard's first career game against the Cowboys, and he'll have a special day against a Dallas defense that is in total disarray after the half-firing of first-time defensive coordinator Christian Parker on Wednesday. Parker retains his title as defensive coordinator, but head coach Brian Schottenheimer stripped him of defensive play-calling duties and gave them to senior assistant Mike Pettine, a 60-year-old who was retired and vacationing in Italy just a few months ago. Pettine last worked as a defensive play-caller in the NFL in 2020, his final season as the defensive coordinator of the Green Bay Packers .
Pollard will join Jahmyr Gibbs (twice this season), Bijan Robinson (Week 3 at the Green Bay Packers) and McCaffrey (Week 10 at the Cowboys) as just the fourth player in the entire league this season with 200-plus scrimmage yards and multiple touchdowns in a game on Sunday against his old friends.
Detroit Lions Pro Bowl running back Jahmyr Gibbs decimated the New England Patriots for 252 yards from scrimmage (153 rushing yards on 22 carries plus 99 yards on seven catches), the most in a game by any player this season. He also added two rushing touchdowns in the Lions' 35-10 stomping of the Patriots in Munich, Germany. What can the league's rushing yards (1,000), scrimmage yards (1,384) and scrimmage touchdowns (13) leader do for Week 11 as an encore against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , the NFL's No. 1 run defense?
The Bucs  are giving up just 79.2 rushing yards per game allowed. But Gibbs will steamroll Buccaneers Pro Bowl defensive tackle Vita Vea and Co. for 120 yards rushing, something that hasn't been done to Tampa Bay since TreVeyon Henderson did so in Week 10 of last season. Do you know who produced the next-most-recent occurrence against the Buccaneers? That's right, it was Gibbs in Week 7 of the 2025 season when he went off for 136 yards rushing and two touchdowns on 17 carries in a 24-9 victory. He'll go over 120 again against the NFL's best run defense on Sunday.
The Miami Dolphins head up north to Buffalo to face the 8-1 Bills , the AFC's No. 1 seed, as 16.5-point underdogs per DraftKings Sportsbook. Essentially, the expectation is for the Dolphins to lose by three scores. It's understandable to see why. Bills quarterback Josh Allen has the most total touchdowns in a player's first 10 seasons (325) despite 2026 being just his ninth NFL season. Allen alone has more career playoff touchdowns (39) than Miami's active roster (38) does in the regular season. The Dolphins active roster's 38 combined career touchdowns are the fewest in the NFL by any team's active roster by nearly 50 touchdowns — the Arizona Cardinals are the next-lowest with 85.
Buffalo is tied for the best record in the NFL along with the San Francisco 49ers at 8-1, while Miami is tied for the worst record at 1-8 with the Titans and the Los Angeles Chargers . However, the Dolphins will lose by only one score on Sunday.
How is this possible? Well, the Bills have outscored their opponents 90-28 in their last three games while facing five backup quarterbacks: Tyler Huntley , Joe Fagnano , Carson Wentz , Max Brosmer and Cade Klubnik . Yes, the Dolphins are starting one too — 2025 sixth-round pick Kyle McCord — with Malik Willis sidelined, but McCord had a decent debut at the Indianapolis Colts in Week 10. He threw for 209 yards, the second most in an NFL debut in Dolphins history, on 17-of-32 passing with a rushing touchdown and one lost fumble. Rookie third-round wide receiver Caleb Douglas ' 367 yards receiving in six games is the most in a player's first six career games in Dolphins history.
No team in the last 20 years has seen a higher rate of their snaps (28.8%) go to rookies than the 2026 Dolphins have. They don't know what they don't know. That's why they're going to lose by just one possession against the mighty Bills in Buffalo in Week 11.
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams returns from a Week 10 bye out for blood after throwing four interceptions in Week 9 against the Buccaneers. That snapped his 36-game streak without multiple interceptions, the fourth-longest streak by a starting quarterback since 1950. Williams will be itching to go deep downfield to wide receivers Luther Burden and Rome Odunze to atone for his sloppy play in the last time out.
Williams' problem is that he is facing one of the best pass-rushing teammate duos in football against the New Orleans Saints . Saints edge rushers Carl Granderson (8.5 sacks, tied for the second most in the NFL) and Chase Young (8.0 sacks, tied for the fourth-most) have combined for 16.5 sacks, tied for the most of any teammate pass rush duo this season along with the…

full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
The NBA season started one month ago today. The first stanza of the campaign brought a great deal of excitement at the top of the league with superstars doing superstar things and most of the projected championship contenders getting off to hot starts. But we also saw injuries, a disappointing first handful of games from Mikal Bridges and an Eastern Conference that is not nearly as dominant as it was supposed to be.
Those are three of the biggest letdowns of the young season . Here's our John Gonzalez on why Bridges might be the greatest dud of any individual player:
Another major disappointment: The Kings . How can a team underperform expectations when those expectations are already about as low as they come? Well, Sacramento sure has found a way. With a 1-13 record and after a puzzling trade, the Kings earned their spot in our ranking of the NBA's most hopeless teams .
The College Football Selection Committee is in love with the SEC . Only one time in three different rankings have the bracket-makers ranked a team from that conference lower than AP Top 25 voters. Whether or not you think it's fair, the numbers largely back it up. In fact, two-loss No. 5 Texas even has a better resume score than undefeated No. 2 Utah ! So maybe the committee is not all that out of line. You can be sure they will have their eyes on these five key matchups in Week 12.
Another important clash is the only top-25 contest of the week: No. 1 Georgia at No. 21 South Carolina . In his Six Pack of picks , our Tom Fornelli explained why the Bulldogs will roll on the road.
Moving away from the SEC, look out for a potential upset in the Big Ten . Nothing is going well for Michigan , but the Wolverines are only small underdogs against unbeaten No. 4 UCLA . These five factors will determine whether the Bruins move one step closer to the CFP or fall for the first time this season.
Here's how to watch the biggest games of Week 12 and our picks for each of them:
This is easily the most lopsided week of the NFL season. The Bills and Chiefs are three-score favorites. The Bears and Broncos are also favored by double digits. The Cowboys , Lions , Jaguars and Bengals are all favored by about a touchdown. You know how these things go, though. One of these favorites is bound to lose. We put a few of them on upset alert , and a handful of our experts are in agreement that the Lions are among the most vulnerable.
First of all, the Buccaneers have just as much to play for as the Lions. Both of them are locked into tightly contested division battles. The motivation will be there for a Tampa Bay team that could somehow sneak into the playoffs even with a losing record. And then there's the Tampa Bay defense, which has forced at least four turnovers in each of its last three games. Our Tyler Sullivan said it would not surprise him if Jared Goff 's interception streak continues.
And even though our Jordan Dajani could not bring himself to pick the upset outright, he does see the Buccaneers keeping this one highly competitive.

full_text:
Week 10 was not quite what we were hoping. After finishing the first half of the season above .500, we went 2-3 last week and are now 25-25 on the season.
And it was agonizing. The Ravens failed to hit their OVER 20.5 points thanks to a drop at the 1-yard line and, later, a game-sealing fumble in Chargers territory. Los Angeles beat Baltimore 23-20. The hook got us. We were looking for 4+ receptions from Colby Parkinson , but he managed only two. And the Seahawks beat the Raiders but didn't pick off Fernando Mendoza .
The wins were good ones. The 49ers covered at the Cowboys , and Josh Downs stepped right in and produced for the Chiefs , going well over the 25+ yard mark we had set for him. Let's not bite the hand that feeds us.
In his Kansas City debut, Josh Downs had four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown ... on eight routes run! In that teeny-tiny sample size, he provided exactly what the Chiefs had hoped: a man-coverage-beating slot presence who adds a little juice downfield, too. He should, at the very least, be able to put up those numbers again against a beatable Cardinals defense.
There simply aren't enough good things to say about the Buccaneers ' defense. It is what's kept them afloat in an underwhelming NFC South; the Tampa Bay offense is scoring just 20.7 points per game, 22nd in the NFL .
With uncertainty regarding Baker Mayfield's status, I just don't see a way for Jalon Daniels and co. to find much success here. The Buccaneers lead the NFL in yards per rush, but the Lions have been solid defending the ground game. The secondary has improved significantly, too, and ball-hawking safety Kerby Joseph is expected back this week. On the other side, the Lions should find some success, even if it's not up to their normal standard. Detroit is averaging 28.6 offensive points per game, the fifth-highest in the NFL, and when not pressured, Jared Goff is absolutely cooking—only Brock Purdy , Trevor Lawrence, and Joe Burrow have a higher expected points added per play. For all the good things Todd Bowles' defense does, it is 28th in pressure rate.
Tony Pollard faces his former team and is on a hot streak, with six touchdowns in his last three games. The Cowboys, meanwhile, have allowed 11 rushing touchdowns to running backs, the fourth-most in the NFL, and five receiving touchdowns to running backs, tied for the most in the league. They just got burnt to a crisp by Christian McCaffrey in the passing game, too. Last week, Pollard caught eight of nine passes for 66 yards and a touchdown.
The Titans ' offense is (obviously) not the 49ers' offense, but it should find enough success to get Pollard into the end zone at least once.
J.J. McCarthy has exceeded all expectations as the Giants starting quarterback after coming in midseason, playing far, far better than he did for any extended time with the Vikings . He has only two interceptions, but he has also had three would-be picks dropped and is one of the luckiest quarterbacks in that category.
Meanwhile, the Jaguars have forced 12 interceptions this year, the third-most in the league, and they just added Jessie Bates III . I anticipate the Jacksonville offense will keep rolling, which will force McCarthy to chase the game all afternoon. That sounds like a recipe for at least one interception for me.
The Bengals are a top-tier Super Bowl contender. There's little doubt about that. The Commanders , meanwhile, are simply trying to hang around in the awful NFC East. I'd be really surprised if Washington finds a way to win this game; Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are simply too good against an up-and-down defense.
It's been a tougher year for Chase Brown , but he's still a workhorse back in an offense that racks up points. He found the end zone twice last week, which should be a positive regression for him. Prior to that, he had just one score on 142 touches. It's worth betting on that continuing for a red-hot offense.

title: Bengals duo could break NFL record that has stood for 31 years: Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins on historic pace
summary: Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins could make NFL history for the red hot Bengals
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- The Cincinnati Bengals offense has been nearly unstoppable this year. Heading into Week 11, Joe Burrow is the MVP favorite and one of the reasons that he's been so successful this year is because he has arguably the top receiving tandem in the league in Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins.
Through the first 10 weeks, there are only seven players in the NFL who have topped 800 receiving yards, and both Bengals players are on that list. Chase ranks fourth in the NFL with 878 receiving yards while Higgins is right behind him with 824 yards, which ranks sixth in the league.
Chase and Higgins are just the fourth receiving duo in NFL history to both hit the 800-yard mark in just nine games (Christian Watson and Matthew Golden have also topped 800 yards this year, but the Packers duo has played 10 games compared to just nine for the Bengals duo).
The two Cincinnati receivers are both on pace to finish with more than 1,500 yards, which is mostly notable because no team has ever had TWO players hit 1,500 yards in the same season. As a matter of fact, it's been 26 years since a duo even came close to hitting that mark.
Back in 2000, Torry Holt finished with 1,635 yards while playing for the "Greatest Show on Turf" Rams and his teammate, Isaac Bruce, finished with 1,471. In 1995, the Lions' receiving tandem of Herman Moore (1,686) and Brent Perriman (1,488) came closer than anyone to having two players on the same team hit 1,500 yards, but Perriman came up 12 yards short. The Lions duo totaled 3,174 yards, which is the NFL record for a receiving tandem. The record has somehow stood for 31 years, even with the league now in a pass-happy era.
This year, Chase is on pace for 1,658 yards while Higgins is on pace for 1,556, which would put them at 3,214, topping Moore and Perriman. During a press conference on Thursday, Chase was asked if it would be meaningful for him and Higgins to become the first duo to top 1,500 yards in the same season, and he didn't hesitate with his answer.
"100%," Chase said. "I'm not pushing for it, but I'm definitely speaking it into existence with me and Tee."
This week, the Bengals get to face a Commanders defense that has given up at least 120 receiving yards to five different players this season, so Chase and/or Higgins could end up having a big game on Monday night.
Burrow is good at spreading the ball around, which is why Chase and Higgins are both succeeding.
Both guys have been hot at different times this season. There was a four-game span starting in Week 4 where Higgins topped 145 yards in three of four games. As for Chase, he's been unstoppable over the Bengals' past three games, catching 32 passes for 527 yards. In terms of NFL history, Jerry Rice is the only player who's had a better three-game span and that happened back in 1995.
One reason the Bengals' star duo is putting up such big numbers is that opposing defenses can't seem to figure out who they should take out of the game.
"What all that going on with me and Tee is just how the coverage works out," Chase said of why one of them always seems to be open. "Maybe a coverage could be sliding to my side the whole time, but then the coverage that's sliding to my side is the look we want or maybe it's the opposite, they're going to my side and it's not open, but Tee's getting a one-on-one on the backside. It's really pick your poison playing with us. And this year, Tee's jumped into more of a bigger role of his play than usually."
Chase and Higgins have both hit 1,000 yards in the same season twice, but that hasn't happened since 2022. Both guys could hit that number before the month of November is over, and if that happens, they'll have their sights set on the historic 1,500-yard mark that no duo has ever hit.
author: John Breech

title: Bills to retire franchise legend Andre Reed's No. 83 during the 2027 season
summary: Reed is Buffalo's career leader in every major receiving category
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills will honor another key member of their iconic 1990s team. The franchise announced on Thursday night that it will retire Hall of Fame receiver Andre Reed's No. 83 during the 2027 season.
Reed, who starred in Buffalo from 1985-99, is the franchise's all-time career leader with 941 catches, 13,095 yards and 86 touchdowns. He had an additional 85 catches for 1,229 yards and nine touchdowns in 17 playoff games.
Reed has joined former teammates Jim Kelly, Bruce Smith and Thurman Thomas as the fourth Bills player in the organization's history to have his jersey number retired.
Kelly, Thomas and Bills owner Terry Pegula surprised Reed with the news.
“There’s no family like your football family.” Some special guests showed up to One Bills Drive to surprise @Andre_Reed83 with the news. @JimKelly1212 | @thurmanthomas pic.twitter.com/LUDGDB0h8c
"Oh man, it's almost like the moment when we all got the call for him going into the Hall of Fame," Thomas said . "We knew that he deserved to be in the Hall of Fame, and it was kind of the same thing. One of the four guys that, when you mention the Bills, his name is always mentioned.
"You saw his work ethic when we were in training camp together for 12 years, like, yeah, that guy is special, and he was a big part of our run to try to win a Super Bowl here. There aren't too many people today that go over the middle as much as Andre Reed did back in the day. He took a lot of punishment, but he was always there for us."
Reed was an integral part of Buffalo's historic run of success during the 1990s. While they didn't win a Super Bowl, Buffalo made history by becoming the first (and last) team to play in four consecutive Super Bowls. Reed caught eight passes for 153 yards in Buffalo's third of four consecutive trips to the big game.
About time. Andre Reed’s number should have already been retired Glad the Bills are finally giving him his due. Best WR in team history pic.twitter.com/FWDroOn6a7 https://t.co/lVC62BJ2hU
Buffalo's run also included the largest come-from-behind win in playoff history. The Bills overcame a 35-3 deficit to defeat the Oilers in the 1992 wild card round. Reed caught three consecutive touchdowns during Buffalo's comeback.
January 3, 1993 ° 1992 AFC WILD CARD ° LARGEST COMEBACK IN #NFL POSTSEASON HISTORY The Oilers take a 35-3 lead over the #Bills early in the third quarter. Buffalo claws all the way back to lead 38-35, but Houston ties it to force overtime. #BillsMafia prevails in OT, 41-38. pic.twitter.com/SrZn6jGsZf
Reed was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2014.
