title: Texans vs. Colts prediction: Houston looks to bounce back on 'TNF' vs. lowly Indy after rough Week 10 loss
summary: Plus, how to watch, what to know and a prediction before the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup
full_text:
In the Week 11 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Houston Texans play host to the division rival Indianapolis Colts .
Houston enters this game coming off a dispiriting loss to the Cleveland Browns that dropped the Texans to just 3-6 on the season and dealt a significant blow to their playoff hopes. The Texans need to start stacking wins, and they need to do it right now if they want to make a run at a back-end postseason spot.
The Colts, meanwhile, snapped a five-game losing streak with a close win over the Miami Dolphins last week. They didn't exactly light the world on fire, though, and have the look of a team that is just playing out the string after their series of trades ahead of the deadline.
Will the Texans bounce back, or will the Colts make it two in a row? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
The Texans defense has been one of the most disappointing units in the league this season. Houston ranks 20th in yards allowed, 18th in points allowed and 22nd in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. The Texans checked in first in yards, second in scoring and third in EPA per play a year ago, and were expected to again field one of the top defenses in the league this season after returning almost all of their key pieces.
Instead, Houston has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks, repeatedly leaking on the back end despite putting pressure on quarterbacks at an above-average rate. Players like Kamari Lassiter have regressed significantly, while Reed Blankenship has been a bust as a free-agent signing.
Luckily for the Texans, they are about to face one of the most inept passing offenses in the NFL . Daniel Jones has been entirely unable to drive the ball in intermediate and deep areas of the field since returning from his Achilles tear, and it has neutered the entire aerial attack. Jones has completed a career-low 59.6% of his passes at a career-low 5.6 yards per attempt, with just seven touchdowns against a league-high 12 interceptions.
The Colts also traded away both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen last week, leaving them with Laquon Treadwell , Ashton Dulin , Anthony Gould and Deion Burks as their main wide receivers. There is not an imposing player in the bunch. The Texans should be able to shut down this passing offense with relative ease -- especially if they can get pressure on Jones, who can no longer evade the rush like he did last season. He's already been sacked more times than he was a year ago despite playing three fewer games.
The Colts have turned the dial down on Jonathan Taylor 's workload in recent weeks, having him split snaps and carries with rookie Seth McGowan , including in the red zone. Taylor played 81.2% of the offensive snaps through the Colts' first six games, according to Pro-Football Reference, but is at just 66.5% of the snaps since then, with McGowan's usage ticking up.
Taylor has also not been as effective this season (career-low 4.2 yards per carry) as in recent years, which isn't surprising given the total lack of a passing game and the Colts' offensive line issues. Those issues should persist on Thursday, with both of Indianapolis' starting tackles out for this game. It's fairly difficult to run on the Texans to begin with (4.0 yards per carry allowed), and it should be even more so with the Colts in their current state.
C.J. Stroud is playing the best ball of his career, including his rookie year. Stroud checks in sixth in the NFL in EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, despite the fact that he's been working with an injured and rotating pass-catcher corps for much of the season.
The Colts are an easy bunch to throw on, checking in 27th in the league in net yards per attempt allowed (which accounts for sack yardage), and they won't have Charvarius Ward in this game and may not have Sauce Gardner , either. Nico Collins should see favorable matchups on the outside and be able to feast all night long. The likes of Tank Dell and Xavier Hutchinson could get in the mix as well, though they tend to rotate more heavily in and out of the lineup and therefore see fewer targets than Collins.
It's also quite easy to run on Indy, which has leaked 4.8 yards per carry on the season, 29th in the NFL. The Texans, though, have been entirely unable to run the ball, with neither David Montgomery (who is set to return from injury on Thursday night) nor Woody Marks (who is out with a concussion) able to establish anything resembling success on the ground. Montgomery was averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry before his injury, and Marks has been at only 3.7 per carry in Monty's absence.
This is likely to be a game where the Texans lean heavily on Stroud to establish a lead, then turn to the ground game to run the clock out, in what should be a relatively easy matchup given the state of the Colts' roster. So long as the Texans keep Stroud well protected early on, that strategy should be plenty successful, even if it doesn't necessarily result in a blowout win because the Texans themselves aren't that explosive of an offense.
I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody.
Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13

title: How Aidan Hutchinson injury could grant Lions a salary cap credit in 2027
summary: The Lions would not be the first team to receive cap relief for an injured player
full_text:
The loss of star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson , who suffered a season-ending torn ACL while celebrating a sack in Week 10, is a brutal blow to the Detroit Lions in their hunt for the NFC North title and beyond. There is a silver lining to the injury, though. Clauses in Hutchinson's contract and the NFL's collective bargaining agreement with the NFL Players Association open the door for the Lions to potentially gain financial flexibility as a result of his looming absence.
In the massive four-year, $180 million contract extension Hutchinson signed in 2025, there is a clause that permits the Lions to purchase insurance policies against his salary, according to the Detroit Free Press .
The contract reportedly states that the Lions are entitled to purchase insurance policies naming them as beneficiaries for up to $60 million in lost salary if Hutchinson cannot play due to injury. For this season specifically, the Lions may insure up to $45 million. That sum includes $15 million of his signing bonus, the full $28.4 million option bonus and his $1.2 million base salary.
It is unknown whether the Lions purchased those policies and, if so, whether they maximized them.
Not only would the Lions earn a prorated amount of Hutchinson's salary as an insurance payment, but the CBA would also allow them to receive salary cap credits in future years to offset the difference between Hutchinson's pay and the insurance proceeds.
Hutchinson's salary and bonuses still count toward the 2026 salary cap, but the Lions could free up millions of dollars in space for 2027 if they purchased sizable insurance policies. According to Over The Cap, Detroit owns the fourth-most cap space this year at $32.9 million and ninth most in 2027 at $62.1 million. Multiple key players, including tight end Sam LaPorta and safety Brian Branch, will reach free agency at the end of this season, so maximizing 2027 cap space would help the Lions re-sign them to larger contracts.
Salary insurance is expensive, and the Lions do not purchase policies for all players. They reportedly did not insure quarterback Jared Goff's contract when he inked an extension in 2024, nor did they insure linebacker Jack Campbell offseason deal. Campbell suffered a severe neck injury in Week 8 , and it is unclear when -- or even if -- he will return to the football field.
Language about salary cap credits for insurance payments first appeared in the CBA in 2006. It took a few years for teams to take advantage of the clause. A CBS Sports report in 2024 found that the New York Giants included an insurance clause in the addendum to Eli Manning's historic 2009 contract extension that made him the highest-paid player in the NFL. And the earliest known instance of a team qualifying for the cap credit came in 2013 when the Green Bay Packers insured $20 million of Aaron Rodgers ' $35 million signing bonus.
The Lions have a history of insuring their largest contracts. They did so in 2017, when they took out a policy on Matthew Stafford's five-year, $135 million extension. Interestingly, they did not do the same when they re-signed Goff. And as of Oct. 2024, Goff's contract was the only one out of the 13 quarterbacks who earned an average of $45 million per year or more that was not insured.
Salary cap credits tied to these insurance policies tend to be more modest than one might think. The policies typically require players to miss a certain number of games before payouts begin. Sometimes there is a deductible associated with the policy. This reduces the total payout and, in turn, the amount of cap relief teams receive from the NFL.
Here are a few examples of cap credits teams received as part of their insurance policies:
Fractured shoulder (11 games)
Torn ACL, strained hamstring (15 games)
Torn wrist ligament (7 games)

title: Rams' Puka Nacua suspended three games, will serve ban during injured reserve stint
summary: The NFL threatened Nacua with potential "banishment" from the league for future violations of the personal conduct policy
full_text:
The NFL issued a three-game suspension to Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua on Thursday for violating the league's personal conduct policy. Nacua's suspension takes effect immediately, and he will be eligible for reinstatement on Monday, December 14, after the Rams' key divisional game against the San Francisco 49ers .
Nacua is set to miss three high-stakes matchups against the Green Bay Packers , Kansas City Chiefs , and 49ers before he is eligible to return on December 20, in Week 15 against the Dallas Cowboys .
The NFL did not publicly disclose the nature of Nacua's personal conduct policy violation. It can be inferred, however, that the suspension is related to his ongoing civil suit, which stems from allegations that he bit a woman and made an antisemitic remark.
The woman filed a temporary restraining order against Nacua in March. The lawsuit also mentioned allegations of gender violence and assault and battery. Nacua's attorney denied the allegations and said this is a "blackmail" attempt from the alleged victim on December 31, 2025.
According to ESPN , the NFL said it communicated to Nacua that "any further violation of the personal conduct policy, including failing to satisfy the conditions of his diversion program, will subject him to additional and more substantial discipline, including banishment from the league."
As unfortunate as the suspension is for Nacua, the timing is convenient. The Rams placed him on injured reserve on November 12 due to his PCL/MCL sprain and turf toe, so he was already set to miss at least four games during his recovery. Players may serve suspensions while on injured reserve, so he will complete the three-game ban during the remainder of his minimum IR stint. While suspended, Nacua will not be allowed in the team facilities, meaning he will not be allowed to rehab his injury with the team until the suspension is over.
Previous instances of players serving suspensions while on injured reserve include Daniel Ekuale (2025), Sam Williams (2024), Mike Woods (2023), and David Parry (2018).
Nacua already missed two games this season due to a hip injury, and the Rams went 1-1 in his absence in Weeks 2 and 3 against the New York Giants and Denver Broncos . Davante Adams stepped up in a big way as the team's No. 1 receiver and racked up 332 yards in those contests. Adams remains in the midst of his recovery from a hamstring injury but could return for the Rams' battle with the Packers, which would put him back at the top of the receiving pecking order.
When he is on the field, Nacua remains a top-flight wide receiver. He averages 102.1 yards per game this year, which is high enough to make him the NFL's all-time leader in receiving yards per game at 96.2 over his career.
Nacua has been a massive piece of the Rams' offensive game plan and saw at least seven targets in each of his first seven games of the year. He amassed a whopping 24 targets in Week 5 against the Buffalo Bills , which were the most by any player in a single game since 2009.
author: Carter Bahns

title: What Cowboys' Christian Parker said about demotion: DC considered leaving, pushed back on decision
summary: Parker mulled departing Dallas after Brian Schottenheimer took defensive play-calling
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- The Dallas Cowboys put first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker in a no-win situation.
Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer left Parker in a bizarre limbo state after stripping him of his defensive play-calling responsibilities and giving them to senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine for the rest of the season. Yet, Schottenheimer is keeping Parker on staff as the defensive coordinator to lead defensive meetings and build the defensive game plan.
Teams regularly fire coordinators in-season, and they also let coordinators fight through adversity. Dallas did a little bit of both with Parker, which is certainly unique. That's why, when addressing the move on Thursday, Parker called his situation "not ideal."
"Not an ideal situation for me personally, but it's what's best for the team at this current point," Parker said. "So that's how we're moving forward. Continuing to prepare and operate in the same way that we've been doing during the week to have the goal of winning on Sunday."
Some coaches in Parker's shoes would have walked out the door after being essentially neutered professionally. Parker said he considered it as an option, yet he chose to stay.
"I think you can always choose to do that, right? Yeah, exactly," Parker said. "[But] we didn't even get to the point of discussing that. I think initially it's going to stink, right? So initially in your mind, you're thinking about all the things and in my opinion, that would've been running from it.
"And at the end of the day, I got a job to do, and my job is to be the defensive coordinator of the Dallas Cowboys. Whether that is calling plays on Sunday, obviously that's not the case anymore, but on ... whatever day we play, there is a focus level that I need to have. There's a contribution that I still have to be able to maintain. That is regardless of feelings and anything else."
Parker, who at 34 is the youngest defensive coordinator in Cowboys history, made it clear that he lobbied hard with Schottenheimer to remain the DC with full responsibilities. But he said, "At the end of the day, that was a decision that was made."
That decision came after another loss in Week 11 when Dallas allowed the 49ers to rack up 584 total yards, the most allowed in a Cowboys' home game in franchise history. In the aftermath of another frustrating defensive effort, the Cowboys now have the NFL's worst total defense (393.8 total yards per game allowed), run defense (154.1 rushing yards per game allowed), third down defense (48.8% third down conversion rate allowed) and the worst defense in terms of defensive expected points added (EPA) per play (-0.13).
Parker confirmed everything Schottenheimer announced on Wednesday about his duties remaining the same during the week going forward, outside of play-calling responsibilities. What has also remained the same in Dallas over the years is the defense's inability to play sound football.
Per CBS Sports Research , the Cowboys are the only team in NFL history to allow 27-plus points per game in three consecutive seasons with a different defensive coordinator each year: Mike Zimmer (2024), Matt Eberflus (2025) and now Parker (2026). Nothing has stuck, which likely has more to do with Jones' roster-building and decision to trade away All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers .
Schottenheimer saying Parker has a "very bright future here as our defensive coordinator" comes off as if he's talking about a first-round-pick quarterback he has to bench because the speed of the game is too fast. Schottenheimer disagreed that he is "benching" Parker, but Parker himself drew some parallels with his players in that regard.
He pulled 2025 second-round pick edge rusher Donovan Ezeiruaku from the starting lineup in Week 6, and Parker said it would be hypocritical for him to not have the same mature, steady attitude as a player when dealing with a similar demotion.
"Yesterday when I saw Eze, he's like, 'Hey, remember what you told me?'" Parker said. "Because I told him, 'Look, this is changing at the start of the game. This has not changed the second, third, fourth quarter. It doesn't change anything that we expect from you when you go out on that field.'
"So if I'm telling Eze that, how can I not tell myself that? And it's not about me, it's about this team."
The timing for Parker is unfortunate because Dallas' next two games provided him a chance to rebound against the 1-8 Tennessee Titans and the 2-7 Philadelphia Eagles . However, Parker doesn't see his situation that way.
"There's never a right time for anything like this. So our focus is forward. It doesn't matter who we're playing."
Speaking of looking forward, Parker's future in Dallas is very unclear at the moment. Does he expect to return to the Cowboys as their defensive coordinator in 2027, like Schottenheimer said he believed he could?
"We'll cross that bridge when we get there," Parker said.

title: Robert Kraft, Bill Belichick advance in Pro Football HoF selection process after last year's snub
summary: The two were snubbed in last year's vote
full_text:
Former New England Patriots head coach Bill Belichick and Patriots owner Robert Kraft have advanced in the Pro Football Hall of Fame's Class of 2027 selection process, per The Hall. They advanced following votes by the Coach and Contributor subcommittee.
Kraft and Belichick were up for a gold jacket last year but were not selected in the final round, to the surprise of many .
To make the Pro Football Hall of Fame, candidates need approval from at least 80% of the full Selection Committee after additional rounds of voting at the annual selection meeting in early 2027, ahead of Super Bowl LXI.
There will be a total of 15 candidates — 13 players yet to be determined, one coach (Belichick) and one contributor (Kraft) — considered. The selection process involves reducing the list to 10 candidates, then to seven. From there, selectors can vote for six of the seven, and any candidate who reaches that 80% mark will be elected in the Class of 2027.  Between three and seven new members will be selected, per the bylaws.
The other four nominees to reach the final vote in the coach category were Tom Coughlin, Mike Holmgren, Dan Reeves and Mike Shanahan. The other nominees to reach the final vote in the contributor category this year were Ralph Hay, Virginia McCaskey, Doug Williams and John Wooten.
The Pro Football Hall of Fame's Class of 2027 will be announced at NFL Honors in Los Angeles in February. Members will be enshrined in Canton in August.
Kraft became the principal owner of the Patriots in 1994, buying the team for $172 million, and was integral not only to the team's dynasty but also to keeping the team in Massachusetts.
Kraft and Belichick worked together for decades, bringing unprecedented success to New England in the form of six Super Bowl rings. It all started when Kraft hired Belichick, who at the time had an offer from the New York Jets , as head coach in 1999.
During his time with the Patriots, Belichick had a 266-121 record, with a resume that included 17 AFC East titles, 13 AFC Championship Game appearances, and nine Super Bowl appearances.
Things between the two didn't end perfectly, with rumors of tension and disagreements. The Patriots struggled immediately after quarterback Tom Brady left in 2020, and eventually the team and Belichick parted ways in 2023.
While the relationship may not have ended on great terms, Kraft still speaks highly of his former HC, calling him the "greatest coach of all time." When Belichick was not selected to the Hall of Fame in the last go-around, Kraft said he should've been a unanimous selection.
"Whatever perceptions may exist about any personal differences between Bill and me, I strongly believe Bill Belichick's record and body of work speak for themselves," Kraft said at the time, via the Associated Press . "As head coach of the New England Patriots for more than two decades, he set the standard for on-field excellence, preparation, and sustained success in the free agency and salary cap era of the National Football League. He is the greatest coach of all time and he unequivocally deserves to be a unanimous first-ballot Pro Football Hall of Famer."
Brady also spoke out after Belichick was not elected, saying , "If he's not a first-ballot Hall of Famer, there's really no coach that should ever be a first-ballot Hall of Famer, which is completely ridiculous because people deserve it. He's incredible."
Belichick is currently the coach at North Carolina.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Revisiting the Chiefs' 2026 NFL Draft: Was Kansas City justified in trading up for Mansoor Delane?
summary: Trading up for Mansoor Delane has paid off in the secondary, but Peter Woods' slow start and an ignored wide receiver room leave lingering questions about Kansas City's first-round approach
full_text:
The Kansas City Chiefs made significant changes to their offense by moving on from offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and spending big on running back Kenneth Walker III , but the sheer volume of moves on defense was more impressive. On the heels of an uncharacteristic 6-11 season, the franchise bid farewell to a trio of defensive starters and even more depth.
The Chiefs were flush with draft capital after trading cornerback Trent McDuffie to Los Angeles. The team utilized its newfound wealth to revamp the defense. How are those decisions maturing halfway through the regular season?
Kansas City traded away All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie and allowed cornerback Jaylen Watson to walk in free agency. Leadership decided to reallocate financial resources elsewhere and invest in the position through the draft. After acquiring Nohl Williams in the third round of the 2025 NFL Draft , the Chiefs traded up from No. 9 overall to No. 6 overall, in exchange for third- and fifth-round picks, for the right to select Delane.
When available, Delane has been excellent. He operates with supreme awareness of his surroundings and plays aggressively downhill in run support. The LSU product is not afraid to be physical at the line of scrimmage or through the route. He has the top-end speed to stay in-phase when covering crossing routes, but has been known to allow receivers behind him.
Delane has missed three games this season due to injury. TruMedia credits him with 234 yards and 1 touchdown allowed on 15 receptions.
If the Chiefs hadn't traded up, would another team have picked him sooner? Teams generally have an inkling of another team's interest when making such a move. The Commanders and Saints sat ahead of Kansas City before the trade. Odds are good Washington would have taken Ohio State linebacker Sonny Styles Jr., but the Saints were the real mystery. New Orleans lost Alontae Taylor in free agency and Kool-Aid McKinstry's play had been frustrating, to say the least. They ultimately selected Arizona State wide receiver Jordyn Tyson before signing veteran cornerback Martin Emerson shortly after the draft.
Although it was a relatively steep price to pay for a cornerback, Kansas City was convinced about the player and thought he might no longer be available if they waited; the reasoning was sound. Those resources could have helped address the team's wide receiver problem. Notre Dame's Malachi Fields was literally taken with the third-round pick Cleveland received, and Caleb Douglas was taken one pick later.
Kansas City would then select Clemson defensive tackle Peter Woods at 29th overall. Defensive tackle is a position the Chiefs had been linked to throughout the pre-draft process, so it did not come as a surprise when they elected to address it. Were they too rigid in their approach rather than adapting as the first round progressed?
As established quarterbacks advance into the latter stages of their careers, teams often prioritize other roster needs rather than helping them. Green Bay's track record of not drafting wide receivers in the first round ran parallel to Aaron Rodgers ' career, for example. Any offensive deficiency can be masked by Patrick Mahomes ' performance or Andy Reid's play-calling; that is how the franchise has operated.
Until this off-season's signing of Walker, notable skill position changes included the trade of Tyreek Hill and the signings of Hollywood Brown or DeAndre Hopkins . Neither was a particular needle-mover.
If the Chiefs had been more open-minded, would Washington wide receiver Denzel Boston or Indiana wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr . have impacted this year's team more? Hindsight is 20-20, but it would be difficult to debate that argument.
Among 31 rookies with 50+ pass-rushing snaps this season, Woods ranks second-to-last in pressure rate (2.2%), according to TruMedia. He also has not been credited with a defensive run stuff.
Delane looks like a high-quality long-term starter. Cornerback is an incredibly volatile position year-over-year, and only a small number can maintain a level of excellence in the NFL . Too often, people see a high number of interceptions and equate that to coverage ability; some of the worst contracts in the league have been doled out as a result of that flawed way of thinking.
The conversation is particularly interesting regarding Kansas City because the franchise has traded away Marcus Peters , L'Jarius Sneed and McDuffie over the years. Will Delane spend his entire career with the Chiefs or become a trade chip down the road?
Regarding Woods, he does not turn 22 until March, so it is too early to definitively say what his career will look like. However, he has yet to prove how he will win as a pass rusher in the NFL, and his run defense has hardly been better. The players who initially struggle to contribute rarely develop into difference-makers.
If Woods eventually occupies the role Chris Jones has held for a decade, the team may salvage value, but early returns have been disappointing.
author: Josh Edwards

title: Ravens send Marlon Humphrey home after his controversial comments, sit him for Week 11 game
summary: The decision comes after the cornerback faced backlash, including criticism from the city's mayor, for claiming on his podcast that Baltimore is 'best at making criminals'
full_text:
Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey was sent home by the team on Thursday and will not be active when the Ravens take on the Carolina Panthers in Charlotte this Sunday, head coach Jesse Minter told reporters.
Minter said this is just a one-game deactivation, and that the conversations they are having are "very personal and private," and "need to remain that [way] for the good of the team and the organization."
"This is a team thing, in my opinion. With what's transpired, and look, he's going to be dealing with this a lot more probably than the rest of the team ... This is about the team and putting us in the best position to be successful..."
Coach Minter on Marlon Humphrey pic.twitter.com/zI2xoYoOfD
Humphrey found himself in hot water after saying that the city of Baltimore is best at making "criminals" during a recent taping of his podcast.
"What is Baltimore best at making? They're best at making criminals," Humphrey said on "The Marlon Humphrey Show" Tuesday. He then added, "Yeah, no, that's obviously going to get cut out."
Humphrey attempted to retract his insult to the city of Baltimore on Wednesday.
"I apologize for some comments on my podcast I had yesterday to the city of Baltimore," Humphrey said Wednesday, via The Baltimore Sun . "As you guys know, I've been here my whole career. I've spent a lot of offseasons here, welcomed a son here, and I'm an investor in the city, investor in different parts of the state. Obviously, I do know the effect that words have, and I'd just like to apologize for those comments."
Despite Humphrey's apology, this had already become a major story. Even Baltimore mayor Brandon Scott issued a scathing statement on the matter.
"While we acknowledge Marlon's apology, a verbal apology is not enough," Scott said in a statement, via The Baltimore Sun , on Wednesday. "Baltimore is a city full of young Black boys who look to the Ravens as a beacon of light in their lives and to have someone that looks like them who wears a Baltimore Ravens jersey relegate them to becoming criminals cuts deeper. I wonder how he would feel if prominent Baltimoreans used their platforms to imply that Baltimore once produced great defensive backs, but we have recently lost our way.
"They wouldn't do that because our team and city are supposed to be united as one. Baltimore versus the world. I invite Marlon to sit down with me and some Baltimoreans who have re-entered into our community and are now preventing others from making the mistakes they made."
Humphrey has recorded 40 tackles, nine passes defensed and two forced fumbles in 10 games played this season. The 30-year-old corner is in the final season of a five-year, $97.5 million contract and his $26.3 million cap hit in 2026 leads all NFL cornerbacks, according to Over The Cap.
Humphrey is a four-time Pro Bowler and two-time First Team All-Pro, but as pointed out by Mayor Scott, his play has dipped. Humphrey's 507 yards allowed in man coverage are the fourth-most in the NFL, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. This season, he is allowing a career-high 9.5 yards per target and the second-highest passer rating against in his 10-year career, at 94.4, per Next Gen Stats.
In Humphrey's place this week, Minter said Chidobe Awuzie and TJ Tampa will see an increase in their snap counts.
"He's very remorseful. I think he really understands that words mean a lot, especially to people in this city, and when you say something like that, it's not a reflection of our team and our organization and how we want to operate," Minter said on Thursday.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Vikings have a secret weapon to fight altitude heading into showdown with 49ers in Mexico City
summary: Minnesota transformed part of its facility to help the team adjust to the altitude it will face in Mexico City
full_text:
When the Minnesota Vikings head to Mexico City this week, they'll face multiple challenges, including one they've never really dealt with: altitude.
The Vikings' showdown with the 49ers on Sunday night will take place at Estadio Azteca, which sits at an elevation of just over 7,350 feet. To put that in perspective, that's more than 2,000 feet higher than the altitude in Denver, which has the highest elevation of any NFL city at 5,280 feet.
To get acclimated to the altitude, the 49ers are spending their week of practice in Colorado Springs , where the elevation is over 6,600 feet. On the Vikings' end, they've spent the week at their normal practice facility, but they do have a secret weapon that will help them acclimate to the high elevation: The team has been using what is essentially an altitude chamber for the past few weeks.
Rather than leaving Minnesota to train at altitude before Sunday night’s game in Mexico City, the Vikings built an altitude chamber in Eagan, where players can get familiar with the effects of working in thinner air before Sunday’s game at 7,200 feet (photos courtesy of the… pic.twitter.com/b9FWMF3KxJ
The room is full of exercise equipment — like stationary bikes and treadmills — and it lets players simulate training at altitudes up to 12,000 feet. So while they aren't fully practicing in those conditions, they are working out and, they hope, slowly getting their bodies ready.
The Vikings did give some thought to relocating for the week, but in the end, the team didn't want to take the players out of their normal routine, according to Vikings Vice President of Player Health and Performance, Tyler Williams.
"As much as they enjoy prime-time games, they love that Sunday-to-Sunday weekly rhythm, and there's so many things now that players take in on nutrition and body work and all their recovery processes and what they do to prepare," Williams said, via the Vikings official website . "They like their Mondays being their Mondays. We're rhythm-and-process-habit people. And so, knowing that we can reduce [those variables] by staying here, that went into the equation."
When you're at a higher elevation, each breath takes in fewer oxygen molecules, which is why athletes get winded faster when playing at these altitudes. That science is why the Vikings felt the addition of the chamber was necessary.
"A couple things that [it] looks to achieve: Even though you're not doing a full practice at altitude, you're trying to gain a lower rate of perceived exertion," Williams said.
Was fascinating to hear #Vikings VP of health & performance Tyler Williams speak about preparing the team for Sunday's game in Mexico City at an altitude of 7,352 feet. Process includes this temporary altitude room at TCO. Players have spent time in there going back many weeks. pic.twitter.com/9t12eM5l1d
The Vikings installed the chamber more than five weeks ago, and since then, the players have been taking advantage of it in the facility.
"I'd say to date, we have close to 450 sessions accumulated in there," Williams said. "Nearly our whole roster has done five-plus sessions and nearly our whole roster has [experienced] 12,000 feet, which is great."
The team's goal is simple: The Vikings want every player on the roster to be at least somewhat acclimated to the altitude once they land in Mexico City.
"The more often you're exposed to that, you have a lower rate of perceived exertion," Williams said. "You also have a behavioral adaptation — how your body responds to [altitude]; how you know how to pace yourself at altitude; how you know how to breathe and use breathing strategies in your first exposure compared to your fifth is totally different. It's a learned adaptation."
If you're wondering whether the players like the chamber, the answer seems to be yes, at least according to Justin Jefferson .
"It's been really good," Jefferson said of the chamber this week . "It's good to have that feel and to kind of get acclimated to that feeling of being in that altitude. For the past four or five weeks we've been training in there, trying to get our lungs acclimated to taking that. It's different for sure. It's different than what we're really used to, but I feel like we're ready, and they got us well prepared to play fast and play freely and not really [be] thinking about all the extra stuff that goes into it.
Although this should help the Vikings, they won't be quite as acclimated as San Francisco. With the 49ers spending the week in Colorado, they'll be eating, sleeping and practicing at the higher altitude 24 hours a day, which should fully acclimate their body. On the other hand, the Vikings are only using the chamber for workouts — they're not practicing in it — so it's not quite the same as being fully immersed in a higher altitude like the 49ers.
According to scientific research , it generally takes one to three days to fully adjust to a higher altitude, but the Vikings won't have that time since they'll be arriving in Mexico City on Saturday. The Vikings are clearly hoping that the altitude chamber will help them adjust just enough to pull out a win in this huge NFC showdown.
author: John Breech

title: Pick Six: Biggest storylines and noteworthy predictions heading into NFL's Week 11
summary: Here's everything you need to know about the NFL for Nov. 19
full_text:
Hello football friends, and welcome to the Thursday edition of the Pick Six newsletter!
For your football fill tonight, you have two options: You can suffer through the Colts-Texans game, or you can watch the new "Madden" movie. Sure, that movie only has a 20% score on Rotten Tomatoes , but that's from the critics, and as we all know, movie critics are snooty. Going into Thursday, the Texans will be missing several key players on defense, including Danielle Hunter (hamstring) and Azeez Al-Shaair , who was placed on injured reserve this week due to a groin injury. On the upside, the Texans should be getting David Montgomery back on the field. The running back hasn't played since suffering a groin injury in Week 4.
With that in mind, here's one reason why each team should feel confident going into the game:
You can get a full preview of the game from Jared Dubin by clicking here .
If you're thinking about betting on the game, here are a couple of props.
If you're wondering how my props are doing this year, I'm 14-24 (7-12 on kicker props and 7-12 on all other props). It's gotten ugly, but not as ugly as the Colts' season.
And now, it's time for some picks.
Jared Dubin's pick: Texans 23-13 over Colts John Breech's pick: Texans 24-17 over Colts Jordan Dajani's pick: Texans 27-14 over Colts Tyler Sullivan's pick: Texans 30-17 over Colts Prisco's pick: Texans 30-27 over Colts

Last week, Sullivan, Dajani and I finished in a tie by going 11-3 with our picks and if that's any indication of what's going to happen this week, then you can probably go ahead and ignore the predictions from Dubin and Prisco.
Anyway, if you're new here, here's how things work: I'll give you one Week 11 pick from each writer and then direct you to the rest of their picks for the week. That way, if you like their pick, you can click over and check out all their Week 11 predictions; if you hate it, you can ignore the rest and move on with your life.
For more Week 11 NFL picks , you can check out our CBSSports.com picks page here .
Every week during the NFL season, we rank all 32 starting quarterbacks, and heading into Week 10, we had a new player on top: Joe Burrow. He remains there for Week 11 as well.
The QB ranking here is handled by Garrett Podell, who breaks down every possible QB stat to figure out who should be on top, and since Burrow leads the NFL in nearly every conceivable stat, it was an easy decision.
Here's a short explanation from Garrett of how his QB ranking works: "These rankings are fluid and designed to tell the story of each starting quarterback's respective rise and/or fall throughout the season." Basically, this ranking isn't based on what any QB has done in the past. It's only based on what they've done this year.
After 10 weeks of action, let's check out the top three names on the list, plus the QB who's ranked dead last:
1. Joe Burrow, Bengals. Burrow is on a historic heater: He is the first player in NFL history with a 70-plus completion percentage and four-plus total touchdowns in five consecutive games. Burrow, Peyton Manning (2004, 2013) and Tom Brady (2007) are the only players in NFL history with 20-plus passing touchdowns in a five-game span. Burrow also leads the NFL in completion percentage (74.7%), passing yards per game (310.6), passing touchdowns (27) and passer rating (117.7). He is the undisputed No. 1 entering Week 11. 2. Brock Purdy , 49ers. Purdy continues to produce no matter who is or isn't on the field for the San Francisco 49ers. Purdy leads the league in passing yards per attempt (9.0) and expected points added (EPA) per dropback (0.34) while ranking second in completion percentage (70.1%) and passer rating (115.2). He is tied for third in the NFL in passing touchdowns (21) and No. 2 in yards per pass attempt (8.8). Lawrence also ranks third in the league in passer rating (112.8) and EPA per dropback (0.23) for the 7-2 Jaguars. ... 32. Carson Beck , Cardinals . Beck looked like a rookie making his NFL debut against Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett in a 34-6 Arizona Cardinals defeat. Unfortunately for him, it doesn't get much easier against Steve Spagnuolo's aggressive Chiefs defense in Week 11.
Garrett ranked every starting QB in the NFL, and if you want to see his full list, you can do that here .

2. Colts coach Shane Steichen. Steichen is a lame-duck coach now that his GM is gone, and he has fewer tools to work with than he did during the 2-7 start to the year. A difficult road ahead spells trouble. Do not forget, too, that the win they just pulled off came at home by a mere two points against a lowly Dolphins team that was without its starting quarterback. Two months from now, the Colts might look back at that win as their last of the season.
3. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer. Offense will never be a problem for Brian Schottenheimer, but the defensive woes that plagued his first season and a half with the Cowboys just keep getting worse. At some point, Jerry Jones has to decide he cannot put up with the inexplicable lapses on that side of the…
author: John Breech

title: The 49ers' Fountain of Youth: Can the NFL's oldest and most injured team win the Super Bowl?
summary: The 49ers have defied the odds en route to a record-setting star, but can they keep it up?
full_text:
It's time to call off the search, Ponce de León, the San Francisco 49ers have struck gold once again. They've found the Fountain of Youth.
Sometimes all we can do is turn to an old legend to explain how a bunch of geriatrics subdued Father Time and a substation (theory) up to this point. They've raced out to an 8-1 start despite having the oldest (28.4 average age) and most injured (19.7 player games missed due to injury per game) team in the National Football League.
As the 49ers prepare for one of the biggest games of the year vs. the Vikings in Mexico City on Sunday ( between scheme gods Kyle Shanahan and Brian Flores ), I'm marveling at just how incredible they've been at the midway point.
Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy are in their bag, and Christian McCaffrey is still one of the league's best weapons at age 30, even after a season with 450 touches.
George Kittle is cooking at age 33, less than a year removed from a torn Achilles. Trent Williams (age 38) is still trucking upfield, leading convoys. Purdy-to-Mike-Evans (age 33) was the league's best combo until Evans got hurt. Deebo Samuel (age 30) has even turned back the clock.
Nobody is using the peanut punch like Fred Warner, who just turned 30 on Thursday. Nick Bosa (age 29) is working his way back into form after his calf injury (and last year's torn ACL). It won't be long before trade deadline acquisitions Keenan Allen (34) and DeForest Buckner (32) get in on the act, too.
It's incredible when you consider the injury history of some of those guys. I'm just going to assume doctors replaced some of those broken bones and torn ligaments with some 'Terminator' stuff because they are straight-up bots.
The old guard has stunningly remained intact up to this point. The same can't be said about the rest of the team. The 49ers' entire WR core and defensive line have been wiped out. At one point, the 49ers' top six wideouts entering the year were out: Mike Evans, Ricky Pearsall, De'Zhaun Stribling, Deebo Samuel, Christian Kirk and Demarcus Robinson.
Injuries ravaged the d-line with Nick Bosa, Mykel Williams, Alfred Collins, C.J. West and Gracen Halton out at different times. Kyle Juszczyk, Mike Evans and Dre Greenlaw have notably missed action as well.
It's not shocking to see the 49ers playing well, especially given how they persevered last year, but they are taking it to a completely different level this season.
This is the most decorated offense on paper in NFL history. The 49ers have the most combined Pro Bowl selections (48) on offense by any team in NFL history. It's an embarrassment of riches, but it doesn't always translate. San Francisco is certainly cashing in, though, with one of the most efficient offenses in modern history.
They have the highest success rate (55.2%) of any offense in a season this century. Meaning, they keep their offense on schedule, ahead of the chains, better than any unit ever recorded. Overall, they have the most efficient unit, in terms of EPA per play (0.19), since the 2018 Chiefs, when Patrick Mahomes threw for 50 touchdown passes. San Francisco is scoring touchdowns at the third-highest rate (39% of drives) since 2000, behind the 2007 Patriots (who went 16-0 with MVP Tom Brady tossing 50 touchdowns) and the 2020 Packers (with MVP Aaron Rodgers, who had 48 touchdowns and five interceptions).
Brock Purdy has the highest EPA per dropback (0.34) since Lamar Jackson in 2019, his unanimous MVP year.
Amazingly, they are in the company of legends despite having the oldest offense, weighted by playing time, since at least 2010 (30.0).
And the most stunning part is how they are doing it. It's crazy to see their old core look like they are still in their primes. Deebo Samuel was clocked at his fastest speed in two years (20.39 MPH) when he took this hook-and-ladder 80 yards to the house. He made another house call at 19.96 MPH in Dallas last week.
HOOK-AND-LADDER TD 🤯 Deebo Samuel traveled a total distance of 110.35 yards and reached a max speed of 20.39 MPH on this 80-yard touchdown, per @NextGenStats @AZvsSF on FOX/FOX One Stream on #NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/88dsZtSZum
Christian McCaffrey turned Jerry World into a track meet with a 66-yard TD reception to ice the game, where he was clocked at 20.29 MPH. That was his fastest speed in over three years and faster than any Jahmyr Gibbs play this year.
Christian McCaffrey reached 20.29 MPH on this play. That's his fourth-fastest speed since joining the 49ers and his top speed in a game since Week 14 of 2023. pic.twitter.com/TJnSOYzRw3
Perhaps the most shocking was George Kittle getting clocked at his fastest speed in seven years earlier this season vs. Denver, nine months removed from his Achilles injury.
George Kittle reached 19.84 mph on this play, per Next Gen Stats. That's the same speed as Xavier Worthy's 41-yard TD today. It doesn't make sense for a player fresh off an Achilles injury to hit these kinda speeds so soon. He's a freak. pic.twitter.com/NPYVdpKeaD
See what I'm saying?! They have literally found the Fountain of Youth. They account for five of the longest touchdowns by 30+ year olds this year. Last week, they became the first team ever with three 50-yard scores in a game from 30+ year olds and the first team, regardless of age, with three 65-yard scores since the 2000 "greatest show on turf" Rams.
Longest TD Scored by Age 30+ players this year Deebo Samuel                80 yards   (49ers) Christian McCaffrey      74 yards   (49ers) Deebo Samuel                70 yards   (49ers) Christian McCaffrey     66 yards   (49ers) George Kittle                   56 yards   (49ers)
They are going to obliterate old man records. The 49ers have 30 touchdowns from 30+ year olds this season, putting them on pace for 56! The record is 36 by the 1994 49ers and 2002 Raiders.
They are on pace for 5,028 scrimmage yards from 30-somethings. The only team with 4,000 was the 2002 Raiders (5,016), who were anchored by Jerry Rice and Tim Brown.
The 49ers are responsible for 22% of the league's touchdowns from 30-plus year olds, and no other team has more than 13.
They have 555 yards worth of touchdowns from 30-plus-year-olds. No other team has cracked 500 this year, from all players! It's just silly.
If you weighted their age by scrimmage yards only, the only squad in league history older than this 49ers team is the aforementioned early-2000s Raiders.
It goes beyond age and scoring. I can confidently say we have never seen a team quite like the 49ers, at least in modern times.
As mentioned off the top, the 49ers are the oldest and most injured team in the league this year.
I looked at every team since 2010, using data from SportRadar, to dive a little deeper.
That's 544 team seasons in that span. The 2026 49ers have the sixth-most games missed due to injury (19.7 per game) and the third-oldest (28.4) roster among those 544 teams. That is why, in the illustration below comparing age and injuries, the 49ers are light years away from all other teams in that span.
They are the only team of the 544 to rank top among the top three in a season in each of the following: Win percentage, oldest team, and most injured team.
Those numbers are madness. They defy logic, right? Teams aren't supposed to be this good when they are this old and injured. So can they sustain it and win their first Super Bowl since the 1994 season?
General manager John Lynch addressed the age concerns last week on KNBR's morning show, "Murph & Markus".
"I don't think that's a conscious thing. We're not saying, 'Let's go find every old guy.' I've talked about it a lot, and we really feel [this]," Lynch said. "We think it's a good mix because we have those vets, and it's skewed a little bit. Our long snapper [Jon Weeks] is 40 years old. I don't worry about that. He snaps the football and that's tough to do, and he does it very well. Weeks, Trent Williams, I'll take that. [Williams] defies age and the things. I do think there's some level of, 35 is the new 30.
"These guys are…

title: Patriots offensive lineman had possible tell that tipped off Seahawks in Super Bowl, other teams
summary: Moses' hand placement may have given away whether the Patriots were passing or running on any given snap
full_text:
During the New England Patriots ' Super Bowl loss to the Seattle Seahawks last season, the Seattle defense dominated the New England offense up front. It was a huge part of the game. The Seahawks registered six sacks on Drake Maye , and the Patriots' offensive line allowed 25 total pressures on 57 dropbacks — a 43.8% pressure rate, according to Pro Football Focus.
And it's possible that the player who actually allowed the fewest pressures among that group — right tackle Morgan Moses was actually the culprit.
Former NFL analytics staffer Ryan Paganetti analyzed hundreds of Patriots offensive snaps and found a tell in Moses' stance that tipped opposing defenses off to whether each play would be a pass or a run. When Moses lined up with his hands clasped together on his knee while the Patriots were in shotgun, New England passed 90% of the time, Paganetti noted. And when Moses lined up with his hands apart, the Patriots ran the ball 78% of the time.
Paganetti notes Moses had this tell during much of last year and during the Super Bowl, and infers it may have continued for part of this season. He said he was planning on posting about the tell before Week 1, but "a player on another team encouraged [him] to hold it because they wanted to use it themselves against New England."
Did this offensive lineman’s stance tell help decide the Super Bowl? I classified every Patriots early down snap for the whole season entering the Super Bowl (situations where they could plausibly run or pass) and found a glaring tendency from right tackle Morgan Moses.… pic.twitter.com/sziGDRWxau
The reason this is particularly notable is that Seahawks defensive back Devon Witherspoon claimed after the Super Bowl that the Seahawks did have a tell on the Patriots' offensive linemen coming into the game.
"I knew what was going on," Witherspoon told SiriusXM NFL Radio at the time. "We had a good tell on what they like to do and how they like to play and how they were going to attack us."
Witherspoon specifically noted the offensive linemen were the ones who had the tell.
"We had a tell on their guards and their tackles; how they like to set, they're going to overset on certain rushes," Witherspoon said after the Super Bowl. "They're going to fall for certain moves any time a group of guys get after them, and today I think we did that."
It's possible that other teams noticed this trend and have used it against Moses, who has not had his best year in 2026.
This season, Moses' 13.9% pressure rate allowed is the fourth-highest among all offensive linemen with at least 100 pass-blocking snaps, according to NFL.com's Next Gen Stats. Moses has done okay in terms of quick pressure rate (2.6%) and sack rate (1.1%), where his numbers are in line with the rest of his career, but the high total pressure rate could be due, at least in part, to opposing defensive lines getting a hint as to whether a particular play will be a pass or a run.
Paganetti is a reliable source for nuggets like this. He spent several years working with NFL teams in analytics and game management, including for the Eagles, Jaguars, and Raiders. He spent the 2025 season with Las Vegas, which faced the Patriots in Week 1 of the 2025 season.
Paganetti said he noticed this tell from Moses before that game, and the Raiders used it in route to a 20-13 upset over the eventual AFC Champions. Earlier this season, Paganetti also discovered a distracting video board tactic New England used against opposing kickers under Bill Belichick . Because of that discovery, the NFL eventually changed the rules for what teams can put on their video boards during field goals.

title: Are Woody Marks and David Montgomery playing tonight? Texans' rushing attack short-handed vs. Colts
summary: Both of Houston's two RBs are on the injury report ahead of the Week 11 matchup against Indy
full_text:
The Houston Texans and Indianapolis Colts kick off Week 11 in the NFL on Thursday Night Football. The Colts stole the first matchup vs. Houston this season in Week 3, 19-17, but have lost five out of their last six games to fall to 3-7. As for the Texans, their playoff hopes are also dwindling at 3-6.
Injuries are once again a major factor heading into Thursday night. Both of the Texans' top two running backs, Woody Marks and David Montgomery, are listed on the Week 11 injury report, and both have different outlooks.
Marks has officially been ruled out for this week after he suffered a concussion against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday. He's the Texans' leading rusher this season, with 391 yards and two touchdowns over nine games. Marks did not practice at all this week, and he was expected to miss this matchup, given that it comes on a short week. We'll see if he can clear concussion protocol for Houston's Week 12 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens next Sunday.
As for Montgomery, he is set to play in his first game since Week 5 back on Oct. 11. He was listed as a full participant in practice all week with his groin injury, and carries no game designation into Thursday. The former Lion has rushed for 138 yards and two touchdowns this season. He had a productive season opener against the Buffalo Bills , rushing for 60 yards and two touchdowns and catching three passes for 19 yards and another touchdown, but his production fell off a cliff by Week 2.
Now, Montgomery has a chance to rebound against a flailing opponent that boasts the fourth-worst run defense in the NFL, allowing 131.1 rushing yards per game. He will likely share duties with Emari Demercado , who rushed for 16 yards on seven carries against Cleveland four days ago.
The Colts also have a few notable names on their final injury report, including cornerbacks Charvarius Ward and Sauce Gardner . Ward has already been ruled out with a knee injury, while Gardner is questionable with a calf injury despite missing all of practice.
Let's take a look at the final injury reports for both teams.

title: Cardinals RB James Conner’s injury update
summary: Okay, right up front. The update on James Conner’s injury is: there isn’t an update. So, back to what you were doing. It is our opinion that Conner deserves to be discussed, and basically, that’s all this article is going to do. And no, nobody here at ROTB gets paid by the article. Which, come […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 14: Running back James Conner #6 of the Arizona Cardinals runs the ball against the Carolina Panthers during the fourth quarter at State Farm Stadium on September 14, 2025 in Glendale, Arizona. The Cardinals defeated the Panthers 27-22. (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Okay, right up front. The update on James Conner’s injury is: there isn’t an update. So, back to what you were doing. It is our opinion that Conner deserves to be discussed, and basically, that’s all this article is going to do. And no, nobody here at ROTB gets paid by the article. Which, come to think about it, might bring more funds to their writers, right? RELATED: CARDINALS’ FANS EXCITED TO SEE BECK IN ACTION The only reason this is coming up is that Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur was asked about Conner’s rehab and injury status after practice this week. So, here is what was said. Conner remains out. He is still on IR. He is not practicing, so nothing new to divulge. He did do a bit of work during training camp, but nothing strenuous. During those camp days, LaFleur did mention about Conner being able to return to perform, but that never materialized. This is what LaFleur stated after Wednesday’s practice session: “It was not a good injury. James has earned the right to know how he is feeling and go about his process.” Conner went down last season in Week 3 against the San Francisco 49ers. At the time, Arizona was 2-0-0. They lost a 16-15 heartbreaker to the Niners in the final minute. #AZCardinals come out for James Conner, who leaves on a cart. Conner is the team’s emotional bellwether. They are going to have to overcome that now. pic.twitter.com/rhenfurYyP — Darren Urban (@Cardschatter) September 21, 2025 Conner had a horrific injury to his right ankle that required surgery. The cart was summoned after he went down and the entire stadium was deafly quiet. The loss of Conner opened up the door for youngster Trey Benson, who was injured the very next week and is also currently on Cardinals’ IR. For the remainder of the season, the Cardinals used backups and practice squad guys as their primary runners. Meanwhile, Conner is still considered to return at some point. Just when is the big unknown and nobody seems to have an idea when. There are rumors that his rehab isn’t going as planned, or that the injury was a lot worse than originally projected. Did something go wrong? LaFleur answered that question with: “I don’t know if it did go awry. I know he’s not available to (interview), but I’d rather have him answer that.” Right now, the media doesn’t have access to Conner. Nobody is saying if he is ready to get to the point of “return to perform” which is not the same as “ready to return to practice.” Medically, his injury is called a “pedal ankle dislocation.” His right foot/ankle was bent sideways and then he was rolled up and trapped as the tackle was being made. At first, it was thought to be a foot injury, but later it was deemed more serious and surgery was scheduled. In March, Conner agreed to have his contract renegotiated in order to remain with the team. He was set to earn $6.39 million this season with a $9.83 million cap hit. In order for the Cardinals to not release him for cap savings, the final year of his contract was revised. Now, his deal is for one-year at $3 million with $2.1 guaranteed. Not too shabby if he doesn’t see the field this year. But both Conner and the coaching staff are anxious to get him bad into the huddle. After this year, he becomes a free agent. Consider that Conner is 31 years old, and coming off a significant ankle injury. Running backs must be able to cut on a dime, so will the healing process bring him back to normal, or will there be some sort of residual effects? And what about his speed? Being able to shift into another gear once he pops to the second level? All of these are legitimate concerns. There isn’t a single doubt that the fanbase loves Conner, or that his leadership in the locker room is sorely missed. We get that. Also consider that Conner is a bruising back. Both Tyler Allgeier and rookie Jeremiyah Love have a similar style, so could Conner become the odd-man out once he returns? Remember the Cardinals didn’t spend the third overall draft pick on a running back and then not let him dance. That is – if Conner returns.

title: What the Falcons need in 2027, based on 10 games in 2026
summary: Help. You can make the reasonable case that the Falcons need a bit of everything and I wouldn’t argue with you, given the state of the team. There’s nine straight losing seasons underway, the team is 3-7 with three straight losses and five losses in their last six games, and the clear limitations were showing […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - NOVEMBER 15: Atlanta wide receiver Jahan Dotson (4) runs with the ball after a reception during the NFL game between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Atlanta Falcons on November 15, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Help. You can make the reasonable case that the Falcons need a bit of everything and I wouldn’t argue with you, given the state of the team. There’s nine straight losing seasons underway, the team is 3-7 with three straight losses and five losses in their last six games, and the clear limitations were showing up long before the Falcons traded away Jessie Bates and Ryan Neuzil. You’ll likely see this roster entering 2027 with a third of the roster turned over and five-to-seven new starters, if I was to throw a dart in the here and now. But where is that help most needed, and what are the Falcons likely to invest in the spring? Based on what we’ve seen to this point and what we know about this team’s priorities, here’s my best guess. An offensive line overhaul Yeeting Ryan Neuzil to Baltimore was a sign that the Falcons were sellers, yes, but also a clear signal that Neuzil was not in their plans for 2027 as the starting center. Given that Jake Matthews is older and Jawaan Taylor is both on a one-year deal and has struggled with penalties and run blocking, the overhaul is likely to involve at least two and possibly three positions. Ideally the Falcons would not have to change out both tackles in one year, though they have Mike Jerrell, Ethan Onianwa, and Cameron Williams as potential in-house options with youth; the options at center are nonexistent. Levin may be fine the rest of the way and would likely be back in 2027 as a backup to the new center, but Atlanta’s not going to settle for a 30-plus year old journeyman at the position. Tackle is a bit less straightforward, but Taylor is out. His pass protection has been better than his run blocking by a mile, but Taylor has not been a standout and is up to a team-high seven penalties, a fair number of which have been concentrated in the red zone. This team will almost certainly want to replace him with a young, long-term option, with a new draft pick likely to go up against the likes of Onianwa for 2027. Matthews is where things get interesting. Ideally, you’re not turning over the majority of your line in a single offseason, but while Matthews has been better than Taylor across the board, his run blocking has been uninspiring and he’s got six penalties of his own. The team would be on the hook for a $20.5 million cap hit in 2027 and another $12 million in 2028 if they cut him without a post-June 1 designation, at which point they’d instead be on the hook for $8.5 million in 2027 and 2028; either way they’ll also have $3.5 million on the books in 2029. This team needs to decide if Matthews’ slow decline is slow enough that they can keep their ironman left tackle for another season, or if they need to make a major change after well over a decade. Regardless of their choice there, you’ll have at least two new starters sandwiched around the team’s two highly-paid, largely excellent guards. One era of Falcons football defined by Dwayne Ledford’s coaching and preferences is drawing to a close. Safety help Xavier Watts is going to be one of the team’s starters a year from now, even if his second season has been decidedly lackluster compared to his first. The other spot is very much up for grabs, however. With Jessie Bates traded, DeMarcco Hellams has currently stepped in and played well in his initial game, but he’s not the caliber of playmaker and lacks the range Bates brought to the position. The Falcons are more likely to view him as a very good backup heading into 2027 than a potential starter, which means they’ll want to invest in another player. The compelling veteran options in free agency are all older, with Bates, Kevin Byard, and Jeremy Chinn among the best options clocking in at 29 or older; Jaquan Brisker is probably the guy I’m most interested in and he’ll be 28. Brian Branch is beyond intriguing but is not likely because of his injury history and the level of investment the Lions have in him. The likelier move? A draft pick invested in the position, with Hellams and Sydney Brown as insurance. The Falcons have made a concerted effort over the past three drafts to get younger on defense at every level, and there are some legitimately interesting players in this class from Georgia’s KJ Bolden to Watts’ former teammate Brauntae Johnson. Reinforcements at outside linebacker Cameron Thomas, James Pearce Jr., and Jalon Walker is a good starting point for this group. It is definitely not enough, however. The Falcons like to rotate and have had to be unusually reliant on Thomas for major snaps, mostly because he’s their lone consistently healthy and effective player in the group. Pearce is off to a slow start two games off of his eight game suspension, and the team has to have in the back of their mind that after his suspension, arrest, and negotiated diversion program for stalking and attacking Rickea Jackson, any further legal issues may jeopardize his future in the league. Walker, meanwhile, should be great but will be returning from a major injury that has cost him the entire 2026 season. They need depth and insurance, which they can find affordably as they did with Za’Darius Smith, Samson Ebukam, Charles Snowden, and even Thomas, but I’d argue there’s a need for another high-upside or well-proven starter here given how John Timu and Jeff Ulbrich like to rotate this group. They’ll have the money to do something audacious like chase Andrew Van Ginkel—they’re not going to do that, but they’ll have the money—but K’Lavon Chaisson, Uchenna Nowsu, and Tuli Tuipulotu would all raise the floor and ceiling of this group. A team that likes fresh legs could also invest a draft pick or two in service of making this group even younger. Wide receiver Jahan Dotson would be an incredible third receiver in this offense as a vertical threat who can shake defenders with his speed over the middle; he’s done a good enough job without major target volume as the team’s outside threat opposite Drake London that I have zero complaints about that signing. Perhaps a healthy Zachariah Branch in year two takes enough of a step forward that he takes on a major role, giving Atlanta real speed and better bang for their buck in 11 personnel. Would be, perhaps, if, etc. Atlanta needs another high-end receiver in this group pretty badly to allow them to use Dotson and Branch more creatively and take more pressure off London, who has been carrying this group since he got here. London’s consistent excellence has masked the fact that the Falcons have been relying on guys who would not be starting for many teams and/or are one year wonders in Atlanta, i.e. Darnell Mooney and Ray-Ray McCloud. Without a huge step forward from Branch, there is just not enough here for the Falcons to enjoy a high-level passing game without elite quarterback play they’re unlikely to get in 2027. Tight end This is a little more speculative, but it fits with the team’s needs and what we know about their coaching staff. Kyle Pitts has had a disappointing season against expectations, and this team could be looking for a second pass-catching tight end to pair with him. Last year’s Browns led the NFL in 12 personnel usage under Kevin Stefanski and Tommy Rees, but this year’s Falcons team is 9th with a much lower usage rate. That’s primarily because Charlie Woerner and Nick Muse are not huge receiving threats, to say the least, and Kyle Pitts and Austin Hooper are merely adequate blocking options; last year’s Browns could bring Harold Fannin Jr. and David Njoku to bear as legitimate pass catching weapons. It would not surprise me at all to see the Falcons prioritize a late day two or early day three tight end who can address that…

title: Ravens bench CB Marlon Humphrey over comments about Baltimore
summary: The Baltimore Ravens have sent cornerback Marlon Humphrey home from the team facility and benched him for Sunday’s matchup against the Carolina Panthers, head coach Jesse Minter announced on Thursday. Humphrey, 30, drew swift and widespread condemnation on Wednesday for saying on his podcast that Baltimore was “best at making criminals.” He apologized for his […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 01: Marlon Humphrey #44 of the Baltimore Ravens warms up on the field prior to a game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens have sent cornerback Marlon Humphrey home from the team facility and benched him for Sunday’s matchup against the Carolina Panthers, head coach Jesse Minter announced on Thursday. Humphrey, 30, drew swift and widespread condemnation on Wednesday for saying on his podcast that Baltimore was “best at making criminals.” He apologized for his comments at his locker that afternoon: I would like to apologize for some comments on my podcast I had to the city of Baltimore. As you guys know, I’ve been here my whole career. Spent lots of offseasons here. Welcomed a son here and I’m an investor in the city. And obviously, I do know the effect that words have and just like to apologize for those comments. Many, including Baltimore mayor Brandon Scott, felt that his words were inadequate. “While we acknowledge Marlon’s apology, a verbal apology is not enough,” Scott said in a statement. “Baltimore is a city full of young Black boys who look to the Ravens as a beacon of light in their lives and to have someone that looks like them who wears a Baltimore Ravens jersey relegate them to becoming criminals cuts deeper.” Scott then threw some shade at Humphrey’s on-field struggles in recent years before inviting him to back his words with action. “I wonder how [Humphrey] would feel if prominent Baltimoreans used their platforms to imply that Baltimore once produced great defensive backs but we have recently lost our way,” Scott continued. “They wouldn’t do that because our team and city are supposed to be united as one. Baltimore versus the world. I invite Marlon to sit down with me and some Baltimoreans who have re-entered into our community and are now preventing others from making the mistakes they made.” Scott said on Monday ( via Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun ) that Humphrey had reached out to him to accept his invitation to meet. It is worth noting that Humphrey’s comment played into a historical stereotype about Baltimore that is no longer accurate. The city has seen significant decreases in crime (especially violent crime) under Scott in recent years, in some cases ahead of the national average. Humphrey’s current teammates largely declined to comment. Linebacker Roquan Smith said that Minter informed the Ravens’ leadership council with “conviction” of his decision to bench Humphrey. Both Smith and left tackle Ronnie Stanley insisted that the incident had not become a distraction for the struggling team. Humphrey is no stranger to off-field antics, but his comments about his team’s home city crossed a clear line within and without the organization. “In this day and age, I think it’s important for these guys to understand that, yes, you have freedom of speech,” defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver said. “You can say what it is you want to say, on your phone, on your platform, whatever that is. But that doesn’t give you freedom of consequence.” However, Minter’s phrasing – that Humphrey will be deactivated vs. the Panthers – indicates that the veteran corner will still receive his weekly salary of roughly $850k for Sunday’s game. The Ravens likely took that route to avoid any kind of dispute regarding a team suspension, as Humphrey’s actions may not rise to the level of “conduct detrimental to the team.” Minter already started including Chidobe Awuzie and T.J. Tampa in their cornerback rotation in recent weeks. Both will be in line for more playing time on Sunday with Humphrey sidelined. Tampa, a 2024 fourth-round pick, could be a potential starter in 2027, so he should see more snaps even after Humphrey returns.

title: Ravens film study: Mike Green’s second-year leap continues
summary: The Baltimore Ravens came up just short against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football, resulting in their fifth consecutive loss. Despite the defeat, two players on opposite sides of the ball delivered noteworthy performances. Mike Green continued to showcase his development as a pass rusher in Year 2, while Chuma Edoga provided stability […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 16: Mike Green #15 of the Baltimore Ravens celebrates after sacking Justin Herbert #10 of the Los Angeles Chargers during the fourth quarter of the game at M&T Bank Stadium on November 16, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens came up just short against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football, resulting in their fifth consecutive loss. Despite the defeat, two players on opposite sides of the ball delivered noteworthy performances. Mike Green continued to showcase his development as a pass rusher in Year 2, while Chuma Edoga provided stability along the offensive line after stepping in for injured first-round pick Vega Ioane. OLB Mike Green 45 snaps | 20 run defense | 22 pass rush | 3 coverage | 4 pressures | 2 sacks Mike Green continued his impressive sophomore campaign against the Chargers, finishing with two sacks, four pressures and a tackle for loss. The 2025 second-round pick now leads the Ravens in sacks and has made significant developmental strides in Year 2, particularly with his inside counter moves and improved physicality against the run. His expanding pass-rush arsenal has made him a more complete edge defender and a consistent presence along Baltimore’s defensive front. On one rep, Green split two offensive blockers and penetrated the backfield to record a tackle for loss, showcasing his improved ability to defeat blocks against the run. On another, he attacked the inside shoulder of the offensive tackle with a hesitation-spin move, working back toward the quarterback to secure a sack. Mike Green leap this year has been real Inside counter and run defense have been a big asset for him pic.twitter.com/lJ7lwji2nF — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) November 18, 2026 Green’s development of effective inside counters has complemented his already-dangerous outside speed rush, forcing offensive tackles to respect multiple avenues of attack. He’s also become noticeably more physical at the point of attack, displaying improved strength and willingness to engage blockers. Green’s continued emergence provides Baltimore with a building block along its defensive front, both for the remainder of this season and beyond. With Tavius Robinson approaching free agency, Green’s development becomes even more important to the Ravens’ long-term outlook at edge rusher. His ability to consistently generate pressure while becoming a more reliable run defender suggests that Baltimore has a potential cornerstone at the position for years to come. RG Chuma Edoga 33 snaps | 25 pass blocking | 8 run blocking | 0 pressures allowed Chuma Edoga stepped in at right guard following Vega Ioane’s shoulder injury and delivered an impressive performance despite being elevated to the active roster just this week. The veteran journeyman provided some much-needed stability along the interior, allowing zero pressures across 25 pass-blocking snaps while flashing functional strength, fluid hips and the ability to operate effectively in space. Chuma Edoga kicked some ass pic.twitter.com/DMrvVgmLhd — Yuri (@Yuri_Ravens) November 18, 2026 On one rep, Edoga pulled across the formation and flattened a Chargers defensive end, clearing a running lane for Derrick Henry. On another, he seamlessly passed off a stunt with Cam Jurgens, displaying excellent awareness and hand-fighting technique to neutralize the looping defender. Edoga showed a strong anchor in pass protection, playing with good leverage and enough sand in his pants to absorb contact without surrendering ground. Edoga’s performance gives Baltimore a valuable insurance policy along the interior offensive line should Ioane miss additional time. He could also provide an alternative at left guard if the Ravens elect to make a change from John Simpson, although that appears unlikely. Regardless, Edoga demonstrated that he can provide quality snaps when called upon, giving Baltimore some much-needed depth down the stretch.
