title: Familiar faces, different sidelines for Bills vs. Dolphins
summary: The Buffalo Bills and Miami Dolphins have been seeing each other twice a year since 1966, and over those 60 years, both teams have had their turn making life miserable for the other.  In the early years, Miami dominated the rivalry, winning championships and making trips to the Super Bowl. Then came the Jim Kelly-Dan […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills and Miami Dolphins have been seeing each other twice a year since 1966, and over those 60 years, both teams have had their turn making life miserable for the other. In the early years, Miami dominated the rivalry, winning championships and making trips to the Super Bowl. Then came the Jim Kelly-Dan Marino era, when two future Hall of Fame quarterbacks battled for AFC supremacy. Kelly and the Bills made four consecutive Super Bowl appearances while Marino never returned after his lone trip following the 1984 season. These days, the rivalry belongs mostly to Buffalo. Since Josh Allen arrived in Western New York in 2018, he’s gone 14–3 against Miami, including a playoff victory. The Dolphins have managed to sneak in three wins — just enough to make Allen and the rest of Bills Mafia angry before the next meeting. But the Dolphins coming to Buffalo this week look very different from the team that challenged the Bills’ hold on the AFC East just a couple of seasons ago. Tua Tagovailoa, Tyreek Hill, and Jaylen Waddle are gone. So are Minkah Fitzpatrick and Bradley Chubb, who now wears a Bills uniform. De’Von Achane is still in Miami but sidelined with an injury. And with starting quarterback Malik Willis also on injured reserve, Kyle McCord is preparing for just his second NFL start. Miami may have a new look, but that doesn’t mean everyone on its sideline is unfamiliar with Buffalo. Several members of Jeff Hafley’s coaching staff have faced the Bills in previous stops around the league, while others have crossed paths with the coaches now leading Buffalo. For this week’s Time Capsule, we’re looking beyond the players to revisit some of those coaching connections, the games they’ve been part of, and the history they’re bringing into Sunday’s matchup. _____________________________________________________________________________ Jim Leonhard vs. Kevin Patullo Buffalo defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard and Miami passing game coordinator Kevin Patullo have already been on opposite sidelines, and their last meeting didn’t end particularly well for Patullo. In October 2025, Leonhard was Denver’s assistant head coach and defensive passing game coordinator, while Patullo was running Philadelphia’s offense. The Eagles entered the game undefeated and looked ready to stay that way, building a 17–3 lead early in the third quarter. But Denver’s defense kept Philadelphia off the scoreboard for the remainder of the afternoon, giving the Broncos’ offense time to mount a comeback. Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts completed 23 of 38 passes for 280 yards and two touchdowns, but Denver sacked him six times. The Eagles managed just 45 rushing yards and converted only two of 11 third-down attempts. After scoring on their opening possession of the second half, they never reached the end zone again. Denver scored 18 unanswered points in the fourth quarter to win 21–17, handing Philadelphia its first loss of the season. Patullo has some history with Buffalo, too. He spent three seasons with the Bills from 2010–12 before eventually landing in Philadelphia, where he was part of two victories over Josh Allen. The first came in November 2023, when Allen accounted for 420 yards and four touchdowns, only to watch Jalen Hurts score the winning touchdown in overtime. Philadelphia also edged Buffalo 13–12 in December 2025, despite struggling offensively throughout the afternoon. Now Patullo will be helping Miami offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik prepare for Leonhard’s defense. _____________________________________________________________________________ Joe Brady vs. Bobby Slowik Buffalo head coach Joe Brady and Miami offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik were on opposite sidelines in October 2024, when Brady was running the Bills’ offense and Slowik was calling plays for the Houston Texans. It was an afternoon Allen and the Bills would probably prefer to forget. Houston jumped out to a 20–3 lead behind quarterback C.J. Stroud, who finished with 331 passing yards and a touchdown. Meanwhile, Allen struggled through one of the least productive passing performances of his career, completing just nine of 30 attempts for 131 yards. Buffalo eventually fought its way back, tying the game at 20 in the fourth quarter. But with the score still tied and less than a minute remaining, the Bills took possession deep in their own territory and threw three consecutive incompletions. Houston got the ball back with enough time to set up Ka’imi Fairbairn’s 59-yard field goal as time expired, giving the Texans a 23–20 victory. Now Brady is Buffalo’s head coach, and Slowik is running Miami’s offense. Will Brady’s experience against Slowik in Houston give him something useful to share with defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard as the Bills prepare for Sunday’s matchup? _____________________________________________________________________________ Pete Carmichael Jr. vs. Joe Barry Buffalo offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael Jr. and Miami senior defensive assistant and run game coordinator Joe Barry have faced each other twice as coordinators, with each coming away with a win. Both meetings came when Carmichael was running the New Orleans Saints’ offense and Barry was Green Bay’s defensive coordinator. The first was in September 2021, when New Orleans handed Green Bay a 38–3 loss. Jameis Winston threw five touchdown passes, despite finishing with just 148 passing yards. The Saints scored on five of their first seven possessions, while Barry’s defense struggled to find an answer for Carmichael’s offense. The second meeting, in September 2023, went much differently. New Orleans led 17–0 at halftime, but quarterback Derek Carr left the game with a shoulder injury in the third quarter. That put Winston back under center against Barry’s defense, but there would be no repeat of his five-touchdown performance. This time Barry had an answer for Winston, and the Saints failed to score again. Green Bay put up 18 points in the fourth quarter to win 18–17. Barry figured out how to stop Winston the second time around, but he’ll have a different challenge Sunday. Carmichael now has Josh Allen running his offense, while Barry is working with a young Miami defense that has been surprisingly effective despite its inexperience. Whether that group can slow down Allen is another question — one we will get an answer to on Sunday. _____________________________________________________________________________ Familiar Faces There may be plenty of familiar names and shared history between these coaching staffs, but none of that will matter much once the ball is kicked off Sunday. By the end of the afternoon, they’ll have another game to add to their résumés — the only question is how that entry will read.
author: Rachel Auberger

title: On hidden talents, even the Miami Dolphins have one
summary: We’ve all gotten the same advice at some point in our lives, likely pre-kindergarten. “If you can’t say something nice, don’t say anything at all.” I’ve also pointed out how embedded it is in my personality to never take an opponent lightly. That’s why for years I’ve been accused of writing articles about doom and […]
full_text: We’ve all gotten the same advice at some point in our lives, likely pre-kindergarten. “If you can’t say something nice, don’t say anything at all.” I’ve also pointed out how embedded it is in my personality to never take an opponent lightly. That’s why for years I’ve been accused of writing articles about doom and gloom takes on how bad teams are to be feared. So here’s my latest one of those. Combining all the above, I decided to play off another cliche, that everyone has a hidden talent. It’s true, even the Miami Dolphins have one and my last article declared them the worst team we’ll face this season. The Dolphins’ Hidden Talent is: Interceptions Now let’s be clear. Hidden talent is not the same thing as “best at.” The Dolphins are not the best team in the league in getting interceptions. They’re not even second best. They’re seventh. Which is still in the “good” realm according to my rule of four. Which I keep referencing but no one seems to ask about it so either you’re not reading my articles at all, or I’ve already explained things so well that my rule of four is super well known in football circles. I’m optimistic it’s the second thing, but here’s a test. If you’re actually reading this, prove it by donating precisely $542.13 to the “Skare Would Really Like to Buy His Dream Car Foundation.” It has to be that exact amount so I know you’re reading. Oh right, football things. The Dolphin have seven interceptions so far this year and their rate (that seventh best I mentioned) sits at 2.88% of passes thrown their way. Rookie Michael Taaffe leads the team with three. Here’s a video of all seven with a few thoughts afterward. pic.twitter.com/x3bagzh1Ru — Kuebiko (@Kuebiko_Kami) November 19, 2026 It might look easy to write off most of these as bad throws and I want to be clear that most are indeed bad throws or at least errant enough where there’s no good shot for the receiver to snag it. I’ve been watching interceptions for quite some time now and I want to be even more clear, that’s the most common type of interception. The skill is seizing the opportunity when it comes your way and the Dolphins’ defensive backs have been doing just that. There’s even a couple in there that are pretty much all anticipation. Is this another “Skare is doing some click bait to pretend the Dolphins are scary” article? Nah. Miami is a bad team this year. Really bad. The Buffalo Bills should be embarrassed if they lose to Miami. Short of a team wide diarrhea-bug I won’t be accepting any excuses to the contrary. If the Dolphins manage an interception, heck maybe even two, don’t be too shocked. It just isn’t likely to help them all that much.

title: Buffalo Bills record watch: Josh Allen, James Cook chase history
summary: We’re going to need a fresh pencil, a good eraser, and maybe a little more room in the record book. Josh Allen keeps giving us names to cross out and new numbers to write in their place.  Allen moved past Peyton Manning on the NFL’s all-time touchdown list and tied Eric Dickerson on the career […]
full_text: We’re going to need a fresh pencil, a good eraser, and maybe a little more room in the record book. Josh Allen keeps giving us names to cross out and new numbers to write in their place. Allen moved past Peyton Manning on the NFL’s all-time touchdown list and tied Eric Dickerson on the career rushing touchdown list. And while we’ve been keeping a close eye on both of those records for weeks, seeing Allen check them off in the same game gave us a little extra work to do. Of course, we’re not complaining. Crossing names off our lists and moving Allen up a few spots is pretty much the whole point of this exercise. Besides, he’s not the only one keeping us busy. There are still plenty of records within reach for the Bills, and with another week of football ahead, it’s time to see which pages we might need to rewrite next. With another week in the books and a new set of milestones within reach, here’s where things stand heading into Week 11. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 1 — Sure Things Josh Allen moves into the NFL’s top 50 in career passing yards This one shouldn’t take long. Josh Allen needs just 20 passing yards against Miami to move past Hall of Fame quarterback Kurt Warner (32,344) and into the NFL’s all-time top 50. Allen enters Week 11 with 32,325 career passing yards, so we’re probably looking at a first-quarter update to the record book. And there’s a good chance he won’t stop there. Cam Newton sits just ahead of Warner with 32,382 career passing yards. Allen needs 58 yards to pass both quarterbacks and move up another spot on the leaderboard. Unless something goes very wrong against Miami, Allen should be leapfrogging a couple of NFL legends before halftime. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 2 — A Good Bet Josh Allen moves up the NFL’s all-time rushing touchdown list Allen didn’t waste any time making changes to this list last week. With two rushing touchdowns against the Jets, he reached 90 for his career, tying Eric Dickerson and Curtis Martin on the NFL’s all-time rushing touchdown list. Now he’s just one away from moving up again. Another rushing touchdown against Miami would put Allen at 91, moving him past Dickerson and Martin and into a tie with Jerome Bettis and Franco Harris for 12th all-time. Not bad company for a quarterback. Josh Allen climbs the all-time passing touchdown list Allen has another opportunity to move up the NFL’s passing touchdown leaderboard this week, and he won’t need a career day to do it. He enters Week 11 with 233 career passing touchdowns, just one behind Donovan McNabb (234). One touchdown pass would tie McNabb for 38th all-time, while two would move Allen ahead of him. Three would bring Allen to 236, tying George Blanda for 37th. We’re not saying Allen is going to throw three touchdown passes against Miami. But we’re not not saying it, either. James Cook takes sole possession of second place For eight straight games, James Cook has rushed for at least 75 yards and scored a touchdown. That’s a pretty impressive streak on its own, but it gets even better when we look at where it puts him in NFL history. Cook is currently tied with John Riggins, George Rogers, and LaDainian Tomlinson for the second-longest streak in league history. If he reaches both marks again against Miami, he could put those names behind his. And then there’s Terry Allen, who holds the NFL record at 10 straight games. We’re not quite there yet, but Cook could be knocking on that door before November is over. Greg Rousseau sets a new career high At this point, Greg Rousseau’s name might as well have a permanent spot in this chapter. We’ve been waiting a few weeks to move his single-season sack record from the watch list to the history books, but that ninth sack is proving a little stubborn. Rousseau enters Week 11 with eight sacks, matching his previous career high. One more against Miami would give him a new personal best, and we’d finally get to retire this particular entry. But don’t worry, Groot. We’ve got another spot for you later in the record book. You’re not getting out of here that easily. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 3 — Not Impossible Bills defense closes in on a franchise record The Bills’ defense has gone 33 consecutive opponent drives without allowing a touchdown. That’s a lot of possessions ending without six points on the scoreboard, and it’s the longest such streak for Buffalo since 1999. That 1999 defense put together 38 straight drives without surrendering a touchdown, leaving this year’s group just five away from matching the franchise mark. Six more would give the current defense the record outright. Of course, if the Bills are going to break a franchise record, why stop at 39? They’ve already kept three straight opponents out of the end zone for a full four quarters. What’s one more? Dawson Knox moves up the Bills’ receiving touchdown list Dawson Knox is becoming another familiar face in our weekly record watch. We’ve been waiting for him to move up the Bills’ receiving touchdown leaderboard for a few weeks now, and we’re still holding his place. Knox enters Week 11 with 28 career receiving touchdowns, tied with Stevie Johnson and Gabe Davis. One more would move him past both former Bills receivers and into a tie with Jerry Butler at 29. Two touchdowns against Miami would put him at 30 and move him ahead of Butler, too. We’ve already made room for Knox a little higher on the list. Now we just need him to give us a reason to write his name there. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 4 — Superhuman Josh Allen chases Jim Kelly’s franchise passing touchdown record We’ve already got Allen moving up the NFL’s all-time passing touchdown list in Chapter 2, but this is where things get a little crazy. Allen needs four touchdown passes against Miami to tie Jim Kelly’s franchise record of 237, or five to break it. Six would also tie Len Dawson (239) on the NFL’s all-time list. Five touchdown passes in one afternoon? That’s asking a lot, even of Josh Allen. But we’ve seen him do some pretty ridiculous things on a football field, so we’re not ruling anything out – and that’s the point of this Superhuman chapter anyway, isn’t it? Greg Rousseau chases Mario Williams on the Bills’ sack list Remember when we told Groot he wasn’t getting out of our record book that easily? Well, here we are. Rousseau enters Week 11 with 40 career sacks, sitting three behind Mario Williams (43) on the Bills’ all-time list. A three-sack game is a pretty tall order, even for Rousseau. But if he’s going to pick a week to finally break that single-season personal best we’ve been tracking, he might as well make it one that sends us scrambling to update two chapters at once. _____________________________________________________________________________ One more for the record book Some of these milestones could be checked off before halftime Sunday. Others might keep us reaching for that pencil for another week or two. Either way, there’s no shortage of history within reach for Buffalo. And while we’ve been keeping track of what individual players are accomplishing, there’s one more number worth watching. A win over Miami would give the Bills their first 9–1 start since 1991. That’s a pretty good reminder that, for all the individual records being chased, the most important number on Sunday will still be the one in the win column. Let’s hope we’re adding another one.

title: Houston Texans vs. Indianapolis Colts ‘TNF’ Week 11 fan discussion

full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - OCTOBER 08: Ryan Fitzpatrick on set of the TNF on Prime pregame show prior to an NFL football game between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on October 8, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Look what we have here, Rumblers: It’s a primetime matchup between a pair of AFC teams. Though we’ve had a couple this season and more frequently of late, AFC vs. AFC is about as rare as a Barbary lion these days. The trouble here is that this is a terrible matchup, featuring teams that are decidedly anything other than apex hunters. That the NFL can still sell this product to anyone is an incredible feat. Yet football fans continue lining up to see awful teams take on each other. It’s not that this one is without some interest, which is due to a few star players among both Houston and Indianapolis. The issue is that as Buffalo Bills fans, you’re settling in to watch the 3-6 Texans take on the 3-7 Colts. Those two teams are a combined 6-13 — which, if you’ve done the math, is less total wins than the 8-1 Bills have on the season. Neither of these teams was supposed to flop this season, though the writing was on the wall for Indianapolis. But Houston? It’s been an epic collapse for the Texans in 2026. A once-mighty defense has proven feckless far too often this season, which has some saying that head coach DeMeco Ryans could be warming the very seat he sits on in Houston. Fair or not, the NFL is a production-based industry. If you’re like me, the game will be on simply because it helps fill the room a bit this evening. You may also share my passion for the Thursday Night Football crew, and their pre-/postgame coverage. If nothing else, there’s also the chances to see the Texans in their Nike Rivals uniforms — and yes, they sure did again steal the Oilers’ vibe. Are you looking for a reason to root on one team over the other here? What you favor depends on who to cheer on to victory. A Houston win helps Buffalo’s strength of schedule/strength of victory, which matters most for NFL teams with postseason hopes on life support. Instead, you may prefer seeing the Colts win simply so it “harms” the slotting of 2027 first-round pick they sent to the New York Jets. With that, here’s your open thread for Week 11 of Thursday Night Football . Maybe this one also turns into a decent game, like a few suspect snooze-fests in primetime before it. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

title: Buffalo Bills Week 11 Power Rankings: Do power rankings matter heading into a divisional game?
summary: Despite a convincing win over the New York Jets, national analysts remain divided on whether Buffalo deserves the NFL’s top spot. The Buffalo Bills walked out of MetLife Stadium with a 31-12 victory over the New York Jets, but apparently a 19-point divisional win isn’t enough to impress everyone. Heading into Week 11, Buffalo remains […]
full_text: Despite a convincing win over the New York Jets, national analysts remain divided on whether Buffalo deserves the NFL’s top spot. The Buffalo Bills walked out of MetLife Stadium with a 31-12 victory over the New York Jets, but apparently a 19-point divisional win isn’t enough to impress everyone. Heading into Week 11, Buffalo remains firmly entrenched among the NFL’s elite, with four of our eight tracked national outlets ranking the Bills No. 1 and the remaining four placing them at No. 2. Interestingly, two outlets moved Buffalo in opposite directions following Sunday’s victory. ESPN dropped the Bills from first to second, while Sports Illustrated bumped them from third to second. The result? Buffalo’s average ranking remained exactly where it was last week: 1.50 . While national analysts might disagree about which team deserves the top spot, there’s little disagreement that the Bills belong in the conversation. Buffalo Bills Week 11 Power Rankings ESPN drops Buffalo despite another convincing victory Perhaps the most interesting development this week came from ESPN, which moved Buffalo from No. 1 to No. 2 following its victory over New York. It’s not as though the Bills struggled to put points on the board. Buffalo scored 31 points, generated 389 yards of offense, and kept the Jets out of the end zone entirely. Was it a flawless performance? Absolutely not. The Bills converted just two of their 10 third-down opportunities, and the defense allowed New York to sustain several extended possessions. However, Buffalo also produced three second-half touchdown drives totaling just seven plays and 2:49 of possession. James Cook rushed for 157 yards, including a 74-yard touchdown, while DJ Moore contributed 90 receiving yards and a score. Buffalo found ways to win comfortably without needing everything to go perfectly. Power rankings aren’t simply about the previous week’s final score. Analysts consider the overall body of work, strength of opponents, and how teams stack up against other contenders. Still, dropping a team after a 19-point divisional victory certainly raises some eyebrows. USA Today FINALLY showing Buffalo some respect Now here’s an outlet we’ve been watching closely. USA Today hasn’t exactly been Buffalo’s biggest supporter throughout the season. In fact, the Bills sat at No. 9 entering Week 8 before beginning a steady climb. The Bills moved from No. 9 to No. 6 entering Week 9, then made an impressive four-spot jump from No. 6 to No. 2 heading into Week 10. FINALLY, some respect! Following Buffalo’s victory over the Jets, USA Today kept the Bills at No. 2 for Week 11. While USA Today isn’t quite ready to crown the Bills the NFL’s best team, the steady climb suggests Buffalo has done enough to change the perception of its overall performance. And considering how long we’ve been watching USA Today rank Buffalo lower than several other national outlets, seeing the Bills maintain their place near the top is certainly worth acknowledging. Miami Dolphins: A very different power rankings conversation While Buffalo continues battling for the top spot in the national rankings, its next opponent finds itself at the opposite end of the conversation. The Miami Dolphins enter Week 11 with considerably less confidence from national analysts. USA Today dropped Miami five positions, from No. 27 to No. 32, while FOX Sports also placed the Dolphins last in its rankings. ESPN, NFL.com, and CBS Sports each ranked Miami No. 30. It’s a striking contrast between two AFC East rivals heading into their Week 11 matchup. Buffalo is receiving serious consideration as the best team in football. Miami is being evaluated among the league’s worst. However, divisional games have a way of making power rankings feel irrelevant once the ball is kicked off. The Bills cannot afford to overlook Miami simply because national analysts have little confidence in the Dolphins’ current trajectory. The Bills remain among the NFL’s elite Buffalo has an opportunity to continue building momentum, and another convincing divisional victory would only strengthen its case among the NFL’s top contenders. The biggest remaining question isn’t whether Buffalo belongs among the NFL’s elite. The national rankings have largely settled that debate. It’s whether the Bills can continue proving they deserve to be considered the very best. With the struggling Dolphins coming to Buffalo, the Bills have another opportunity to make their case.

title: Parker Brothers Tailgate Menu for the Buffalo Bills 2026 season
summary: Tailgating has become synonymous with the Buffalo Bills and their passionately loyal fanbase, football fans from every walk of life who routinely show up exuding energy regardless of the location of the game or the temperature outside to fervently support their team. And I’m writing the Parker Brothers Tailgate menu because I’ve been friends with […]
full_text: Tailgating has become synonymous with the Buffalo Bills and their passionately loyal fanbase, football fans from every walk of life who routinely show up exuding energy regardless of the location of the game or the temperature outside to fervently support their team. And I’m writing the Parker Brothers Tailgate menu because I’ve been friends with Rory and Ray since Kindergarten and have remained close friends with these brothers through a lot with the Bills over the years. It’s a bond that has always extended beyond Bills tailgates, but as we’ve gotten older, the Bills tailgates have become our central meeting ground, a guaranteed place to reconvene every fall and winter. And I sincerely cherish the yearly regathering with these two. I’m sure you know the exact feeling of camaraderie with your tailgating group. What started as a nano-tailgate with a deep fryer for wings and fries has gradually morphed into a full-scale tailgating operation, often feeding 50-plus patrons thanks to multiple flat tops, cooking apparatuses, and condiments galore. I cannot recommend the Parker Brothers Tailgate enough. And here is their menu for the 2026 Bills season. (Rory and Ray will be situated in the new “white” lot — behind Prohibition 2020 — for the 2026 campaign, and they welcome you to join them.) Week 2 – September 17: Detroit Lions, 8:15pm — Birria tacos This was a new menu item in 2025, and it went over like gangbusters. And who hasn’t experienced the birria taco craze at their local Mexican restaurant or taqueria? Well the Parkers are bringing that succulent experience to the grand opening of the new Highmark Stadium. Slow-cooked, marinated beef, melted Oaxacan cheese, and a consomé that knocks your socks off the moment you take your first bite. Birria tacos will hit the spot on a momentous evening in Orchard Park with weather that should still feel like summer… before literal and figurative fireworks inside the new stadium. Week 3 – September 27: Los Angeles Chargers — No tailgate (wedding in Lake George) For the first time I can remember, Rory and Ray will not be at a Bills tailgate, working tirelessly to feed the masses before unwinding while watching their Bills play. Family wedding in the Adirondacks will keep them away for this one, but trust me, they’ll be back with more energy than ever after their own bye week. Week 4 – October 4: New England Patriots, 1pm — Stingers What wings are to Buffalo, stinger subs are to the Parkers tailgate. Well, stingers and garbage plates. Every year, the stinger tailgate attracts more friends and random passers-by than any other because of the Parkers’ attention to detail with their stinger construction. Thick chicken fingers, dipped in country sweet sauce, combined with perfectly cooked shredded beef, with any combination of lettuce, cheese, onions, banana peppers, and mayo on a fresh sub roll that can be toasted if you’d like (highly recommend it). All ahead of a colossal showdown with the defending AFC champs in the House That Josh Built. Week 8 – November 1: Baltimore Ravens, 1pm — Surprise, Surprise Despite the pestering of my Parker Brothers sources, this tailgate remains a mystery. All I could manage to coax from said source was this, and it’s awesomely cryptic, it’s actually making me hungry right now: “This tailgate has never been done before, maybe never again,” and “I’ll go out on a limb and say no one has ever tried it ever.” ….as if you needed more encouragement to get to Bills-Ravens. Week 11 – November 22: Miami Dolphins, 1pm — Turkey 2 Ways Have you ever had deep-fried turkey? If the answer is no, this is one glorious sliver of life you have yet to experience. The Parkers call this Turkey 2 Ways because you can get a few slices of classically cooked Thanksgiving turkey. And if that’s your jam, I respect that. I recommend a taste of the Parkers deep-fried version that of course features a crunchy exterior and impossibly juicy meat as the focal point around mashed potatoes, corn, and everything else you’ll eventually eat on Thanksgiving with your family. Week 12 – November 26: Kansas City Chiefs, 8:20pm — Cheesesteaks Why aren’t the Parkers doing a Thanksgiving tailgate on Thanksgiving night? Well, they figured the tryptophan would probably be overwhelming at this stage of Thanksgiving, so they’re venturing away from all the food you’ve likely eaten in the hours leading up to this perennial enormous regular-season battle between the Bills and Chiefs. And the Parkers Cheesesteaks could hold their own on any corner on the streets of Philadelphia. Trust me. Ask for extra cheese. Thank me later. Week 15 – December 19: Chicago Bears — Italian beef A cousin of the Cheesesteaks, I actually slightly prefer the Italian beef — my last name should be a dead giveaway I’d have this take. Of course, this menu item from Rory and Ray is a nod to one of Chicago’s most revered culinary offerings, which just so happens to be the city’s version of the beef on weck. The spicy giardiniera — finely diced peppers, carrots, celery — elevate this sandwich into the stratosphere. And the warm, seasoned roast beef will warm your insides ahead of this super-fun AFC-NFC showdown between two of the best improvisational quarterbacks in the NFL. Week 18 – January 10: New York Jets, TBD — Smash burgers I adore smash burgers, and every time I eat one, I wonder… how and why were we not always eating burgers this way… two patties, pressed thin, with ample amounts of melted cheese to hold them together? And the Parkers have perfected the on-site smash burger… Ray is normally on the flat-top, precisely flattening each patty before loading with cheese. Rory’s responsibilities come in the made-to-order building of your burger. And he will walk you through the process once your patties are ready to be assembled between two buns. Because the Parkers have gotten so good with the presentation — and taste — of their smash burgers, this is an exquisite cap to the Bills 2026 regular season at this tailgate. Playoffs — TBD Among the menu items the Parkers have done in the past that would be possible during a Bills playoff run: Garbage Plates (unequivocally my favorite, thanks in large part to Mrs. Parker’s meat sauce) Hibachi (a gigantic undertaking but Michelin-star worthy) Burritos (made to your exact specifications, Chipotle-style) Breakfast (bacon, sausage, eggs, all sizzling on the griddle) Deep-fried everything (bring anything you want, the Parkers will deep fry right in front of your eyes) Spaghetti and meatballs (I never knew I needed this Italian classic before a football game, until I went to a Parker Tailgate) What is your tailgate scene like? Are you already planned out with specific menu items? Leave a comment explaining everything in detail!

title: Buffalo Bills Week 11 rooting interests
summary: The Buffalo Bills are 8-1.  I really don’t need to say anything more than that, do I?  But since I know someone is going to try to argue, let’s get a few things out of the way.  Don’t come at me with the number of backup quarterbacks the Bills have faced. How about we talk […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills are 8-1. I really don’t need to say anything more than that, do I? But since I know someone is going to try to argue, let’s get a few things out of the way. Don’t come at me with the number of backup quarterbacks the Bills have faced. How about we talk about the fact that those quarterback changes have forced Buffalo’s defense to adjust its game plan in the middle of a game? And don’t come at me with strength of victory, either. A lot of those teams looked pretty strong on paper when the schedule came out. Joe Brady has had his team ready to play week after week. Some wins have been fun. Some have been downright ugly. But every single one of them counts exactly the same in the standings. The Buffalo Bills are 8-1. They have the AFC East all but locked up at the midway point of the season, and they’re sitting in the AFC’s No. 1 seed. Is there still plenty of work to do? Absolutely. Do they control their own destiny? Yes. We know all of that. But we also know that somewhere along the way, the Bills might have a bad day. And there are other teams whose wins — or losses — can give Buffalo a little breathing room if that happens. So, let’s see who we’re rooting for — and against — this week. _____________________________________________________________________________ AFC standings at the start of Week 11 Buffalo Bills (8-1) Kansas City Chiefs (7-2) Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2) Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) Denver Broncos (7-2) Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) Cleveland Browns (6-4) New England Patriots (5-5) Las Vegas Raiders (4-6) Baltimore Ravens (4-6) Houston Texans (3-6) Indianapolis Colts (3-7) New York Jets (2-8) Los Angeles Chargers (1-8) Miami Dolphins (1-8) Tennessee Titans (1-8) ____________________________________________________________________________ AFC East Miami Dolphins at Buffalo Bills Rooting for: Buffalo Bills Go Bills! Buffalo gets its first shot at Miami this season, and a win would do more than keep the Bills sitting atop the AFC standings. It would also give them their second division win in as many weeks and put a little more distance between them and the Patriots. With New England enjoying its bye week, the Bills have a chance to turn their current three-game advantage in the win column into four. That’s a pretty nice opportunity heading into Thanksgiving. New York Jets at Los Angeles Chargers Rooting for: New York Jets I know. I know. We’re rooting for the Jets? But hear me out. At 2-8, New York isn’t much of a threat to Buffalo in the AFC East. What the Jets are in contention for, however, is a very high pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. And every loss helps their chances of getting one. So, as much as we’d normally enjoy watching the Jets lose, maybe it’s time they started winning a few games. At this point in the season, with their record, a New York win is really a loss for the Jets. _____________________________________________________________________________ Rest of the AFC Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans Rooting for: Houston Texans We’re going with Houston here for strength of victory (SOV). The Bills beat the Texans earlier this season, so every Houston win makes that victory a little more valuable if Buffalo finds itself needing a tiebreaker down the road. But there’s a consolation prize if Indianapolis wins. Remember, the Colts traded their 2027 first-round draft pick to the Jets. Every Indianapolis win makes that pick a little less valuable for New York. So, we’re rooting for Houston, but we’re not going to be too upset if Indianapolis pulls this one off. Baltimore Ravens at Carolina Panthers Rooting for: Baltimore Ravens The Ravens aren’t exactly breathing down Buffalo’s neck in the AFC standings, so we’re not going to worry too much about giving them another win. Plus, the Bills hold the tiebreaker if they did randomly start a comeback tour. Buffalo already beat Baltimore this season, which means a Ravens victory helps the Bills’ strength of victory. And if Buffalo ends up tied with Kansas City, Denver, or another AFC contender for playoff seeding, we’ll be glad we rooted for the Ravens this week. Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys Rooting for: Tennessee Titans This one is all about the 2027 NFL Draft. Tennessee currently holds the No. 1 overall pick, and we’d love to see the Titans win enough games to give that spot up. But there’s a catch. The Jets acquired a 2027 first-round pick from Dallas in last year’s Quinnen Williams trade. The Cowboys had two first-round picks, their own and Green Bay’s, and the Jets get whichever one is higher. That means losses by either Dallas or Green Bay could make New York’s pick more valuable. So, we’re sticking with Tennessee here, hoping the Titans can win their way out of the top draft spot. But if Dallas wins, at least there’s a consolation prize. Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs Rooting for: Arizona Cardinals This one shouldn’t require much thought. Kansas City is just one game behind Buffalo in the AFC standings, and the Chiefs aren’t going to make the race for the No. 1 seed any easier. An Arizona win would give Kansas City its third loss and provide Buffalo with a little more breathing room at the top of the conference. And with the Bills and Chiefs set to meet in Week 12, a little help from Arizona this week could keep a Thanksgiving letup from becoming a letdown. Pittsburgh Steelers at Philadelphia Eagles Rooting for: Philadelphia Eagles Pittsburgh is still very much in the AFC playoff picture, and at 6-3, the Steelers are close enough to Buffalo that another loss would be welcome. The Eagles are in the NFC, so Philadelphia winning doesn’t create any additional competition for Buffalo in the conference standings. Easy enough. Fly, Eagles, fly. Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos Rooting for: Las Vegas Raiders Denver is another one of those 7-2 teams sitting just behind Buffalo in the AFC standings. A Broncos loss would give the Bills a little more separation from another potential challenger for the No. 1 seed. And there’s a bonus here. Buffalo already beat Las Vegas this season, so a Raiders win would improve the Bills’ strength of victory. Denver, meanwhile, only factors into strength of schedule at this point. A Denver loss and a boost to Buffalo’s SOV? We’ll take both, please. Jacksonville Jaguars at New York Giants Rooting for: New York Giants Jacksonville is right there with Kansas City and Denver at 7-2, which makes this another opportunity for Buffalo to put some distance between itself and the competition. The Giants have their own problems in the NFC, but none of those are Buffalo’s concern. A New York win would hand Jacksonville its third loss and help the Bills hold on to the AFC’s top spot. Cincinnati Bengals at Washington Commanders Rooting for: Washington Commanders Cincinnati is another 7-2 team chasing Buffalo, and potentially the hottest team in the league right now. We’d certainly appreciate the Commanders cooling the Bengals down. At this point, every loss handed to one of those teams sitting just behind the Bills is another little bit of insurance in the race for the No. 1 seed. And the road to the Super Bowl running through Orchard Park has a nice ring to it. _____________________________________________________________________________ NFC Rooting Interests Chicago Bears over New Orleans Saints – Strength of schedule (SOS) Detroit Lions over Tampa Bay Buccaneers – Strength of victory (SOV) Minnesota Vikings over San Francisco 49ers – Strength of victory (SOV) Games that don’t move the needle for Buffalo: None this week. Every NFC-only matchup has at least some impact on Buffalo’s SOS or SOV. _____________________________________________________________________________ Teams on Bye New England Patriots, Atlanta Falcons, Cleveland Browns, Green Bay Packers, Los Angeles Rams, Seattle Seahawks _____________________________________________________________________________ Bills Mafia has plenty of teams to root for this week, but the most…

full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 15: Jalen Coker #18 of the Carolina Panthers warms up before a game against the New Orleans Saints at Caesars Superdome on November 15, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone. The Panthers season is well on its way as they still control their own destiny. Thanksgiving is around the corner and I’m happy football is still meaningful at this juncture. Let’s dive right into all your questions! RealityDan: So question… according to a quick google search, the Panthers have two “return from IR designations”. One seems to be locked in for Horn, do we use the other one on Thomas Incoom or do we hold onto it and loose Incoom for the rest of the season? I believe you are correct in that Jaycee Horn is earmarked for one of those designations, unless they decide it isn’t worth bringing him back. I don’t know what his injury situation looks like since he didn’t get surgery and is rehabbing it instead, so it is definitely possible he doesn’t come back at all. For the last spot, I suspect at this point in the season they will still hold one. Remember, they only have to be in injured/reserve for 4 weeks to qualify for that designation. We still have 8 games left, so lots of runway. schrodingersblackcat: Brian, what was your favorite part of the game on Sunday? Beating the Saints in NO? Chuba going into full-on superhero mode? Our recovering DEF showing up and looking like they’re could soon become more-than-respectable? Freeling and Hunter showing us signs that they’re the future of this franchise? The 15 minute mindless turducken conversation that let you completely switch off and dissociate just long enough to forget how boring the first half was? Which aspect of this victory isn’t being celebrated enough? Also: Brad Idzik gets a visit from the Ghost of Offensive Drives Past. What does the ghost show and tell him? I don’t care how ugly the victory is, a win against the Saints in New Orleans will always be a massive plus in my book. Carolina also hasn’t beaten the Saints in two whole seasons, so we’ll take it. I would also say seeing the defense play hard and fast. They are certainly still motivated which gives me hope this team could still make the playoffs and be somewhat competitive, at least in the wild card. I would imagine the ghost shows him that having Bryce Young take the easy throws is sometimes the right call. I know that many have detracted from the win on Sunday since Bryce was hitting Chuba Hubbard out of the backfield, but Brad Idzik’s offense is definitely taking a lot more shots down field. WHICH IS GOOD! But some weeks, you just got to take what the defense is giving you rather than pushing the ball down the field when it isn’t as necessary. The NFL now knows Carolina isn’t going to hesitate to throw the deep balls, that does open things up in the short game in itself. @WTMealey: What NFC wildcard contender playoff teams do you think we can beat? At least have a decent chance even if we’re not favored. I think even with our current losing record the goal is a playoff W. That would look like progress. I’d say the Lions and Packers are teams the Panthers can beat. They already beat the Lions and I think the Packers game goes a bit differently in round two. I’d also go with the Rams and Seahawks, just because the Rams aren’t a dream team and I think they played Seattle well enough last season that they could make a jump. I’m not expecting the playoffs right now but if they do make it, I think there’s a real chance they could win at home against some of these teams. TXPanther: What should be my 3rd side choice for our Thanksgiving order? We are going with Mashed Sweet Potatoes and Fire Roasted Brussels Sprouts. The last option comes down to Mac & Cheese, Green Bean Casserole, or Mashed Potatoes with poblano mushroom sauce. There’s a cornbread stuffing option but we didn’t like it last year. I’m very partial to Green Bean Casserole, though it was one of my favorite recipes growing up that had a lot more fixings in it that I think most recipes have as a standard. Mashed Potatoes with that mushroom sauce sound very good as well though. If I were coming to your Thanksgiving I’d be excited to try them. TXPanther: How many penalties/penalty yards will the Panthers have this week? 25 yards on 2 penalties, this is the get right game. Book it, you heard it here first. Brazilian Panther: Give us three players you want to see resigned and other three dudes you want to see released or traded at the end of the season Brian. The list to bring back is pretty easy for me, OT Ikem Ekwonu, CB Mike Jackson, and TE Tommy Tremble. I think the Panthers are in a much better situation if the first two are healthy this season, and bringing back Jackson allows them to play a slower game with upgrading the cornerback situation. And Tommy Tremble just deserves it with how far along he has come. He’s an important piece in the passing game now and has always been an important piece in the run blocking attack. Based on your question I assume we’re not talking about players that are simply going to be free agents in 2027. I’m going to preface this question by saying I almost never vote for players to lose their jobs. But, if I had to pick, I think you need to let OG Robert Hunt go, DT Terk Wharton go, and maybe QB Kenny Pickett. For the first two, it would be purely for cap reasons as compared to performance. But I wouldn’t be upset if they both stay. As for Pickett, I think his ceiling is fairly capped if he ever needs to come in for a long period. I’d bring in another veteran with higher upside or see what you really have in Haynes King. Bull123: just took a quick look at tampas schedule…notwithstanding lions this week, they have chargers, ravens, saints twice, falcons, rams and us they can easily be 9-8…i see no path for us without beating them on the Monday night game are they the hurdle? After the beating they put on the Panthers, not only do I think they need to beat them to push any tie-breakers, but I think the Panthers have to beat them to prove they deserve to be in the wild card. Every season teams have bad games, but that was a fundamental beating you need to really bounce back from in game 2. Irishboy: Brian, I thought the Panther’s offense was completely out of sink most of the game against the Saints. While I thought this could be a get right game for them, only for Chuba, we would have been in trouble. I know the saints have a decent front 7, but their secondary wasn’t. As I am someone you wouldn’t have a strong grasp on schematics, why was our offense basically bad? As schrodingersblackcat pointed out in the comments, the Saints did play a lot of man against the Panthers, and that has generally been their formula playing against the Dave Canales/Brad Idzik offense. While I love Jalen Coker and Tetairoa McMillan, both guys just aren’t as strong against man coverage because they aren’t the fastest guys. Both can win jump balls and 50/50 passes for sure, but in man they are more likely to have a guy in their hip pocket which forces tighter window throws. I think this is why losing Chris Brazzell for the season was a bigger deal than people realize, the offense just doesn’t have that speed option that can beat the breaks off a guy who just wants to run with them. Couple that with Idzik trying to push the ball down the field more and the margin for error is just much lower. All in my opinion, but I’ve seen several analysts this week share the same sentiment. schrodingersblackcat: Who was the best James Bond, and why was it Sean Connery? Sean Connery is a strong one. I have more of a connection to Daniel Craig but that was because Connery was a bit before my time. I will say, my out of left field answer, Patrick Gibson as a young James Bond in the First Light video…

title: Panthers vs Ravens: Matchups to watch
summary: The Carolina Panthers notched a key divisional win over the New Orleans Saints last Sunday. They sit alone at the top of the NFC South with a one game advantage over both the Saints and Bucs. Both of those teams have very difficult road games against NFC North foes. Meanwhile the Panthers are playing host […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 30: Mike Jackson #2 of the Carolina Panthers celebrates after an interception return touchdown against the Los Angeles Rams during the first quarter at Bank of America Stadium on November 30, 2025 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Grant Halverson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers notched a key divisional win over the New Orleans Saints last Sunday. They sit alone at the top of the NFC South with a one game advantage over both the Saints and Bucs. Both of those teams have very difficult road games against NFC North foes. Meanwhile the Panthers are playing host to the Baltimore Ravens, who are having a season from hell and just loss to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers. It was the Ravens’ fifth straight loss. And now they’re embroiled in controversy because their starting cornerback said his own team’s city was “ best at making criminals. ” He’s been suspended for those comments and won’t be playing on Sunday. It’s a great spot for the Panthers to create some space and the teams that are chasing them. There are some spots where they can really take advantage and help themselves get that much needed win. Derrick Brown, Lee Hunter, and Bobby Brown vs Cam Jurgens The Ravens made a desperate trade for former Eagles center Cam Jurgens as they were ravaged by injuries at that spot over the course of the season. They apparently hadn’t noticed that Jurgens had been struggling, and he has done little to alleviate the problems they had at that position. PFF currently ranks him 34th out of the 35 qualifying centers, and he’s bottom five as both a run blocker and pass blocker. Lee Hunter hasn’t been getting a lot of snaps, but he’s made some huge plays when he’s on the field. This is a matchup he can take dominate when he’s on the field and the rest of the line can take advantage of play to play. Mike Jackson vs Zay Flowers Jackson looks poised to make his return to the lineup, and he’s walking into a tough spot. Zay Flowers is probably one of the more underrated receivers in the league. He’s remarkably shifty and can turn any catch into a huge play. He’s been credited with nine big plays this season, by far the most on the team. He’s about the only explosive play threat on the offense right now. Keeping him under wraps and forcing Jacoby Brissett to sustain long drives is a recipe for this defense to succeed. Rasheed Walker vs Trey Hendrickson The Ravens suspiciously backed out of a trade for Maxx Crosby over the offseason and then conveniently able to sign Hendrickson to a free agent contract like the very next day. It hasn’t paid off so far. He’s been decent at winning as a pass rusher, but it hasn’t translated into sacks, and sacks are pretty much all you pay him to do. Walker has had his fair of struggles at left tackle this season, and he’s going to be the primary adversary for Hendrickson in this game. The Panthers need him to just hold up in the passing game, hopefully with some help. And they’ll need him to move Hendrickson in the running game to give Chuba Hubbard space to work. The Ravens vs the fourth quarter Last week, it was the Saints vs the first quarter. They didn’t score any points in the entire first half, so it was a decisive win for the first quarter. The Ravens have a problem with the other end of games. Dating back to the end of the John Harbaugh era, the Ravens have blown more fourth quarter leads than anyone. Firing Harbaugh has done nothing to fix that. They’ve already blown two double digit leads in the fourth quarter this season. The Panthers just need to hang around, and they’ll have a really good shot to make hay late if they need to.
author: Jonathan DeLong

title: Panthers vs Ravens: Jaelan Phillips, Mike Jackson among storylines to watch
summary: The Panthers managed to get out of New Orleans last week with a win, which snapped a 3 game losing skid and once again placed them atop the NFC South with a one and a half game lead. While their division is widely criticized for its inability to post a winning record or just win […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - DECEMBER 21: Mike Evans #13 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers catches a touchdown against Mike Jackson #2 of the Carolina Panthers in the first quarter of a game at Bank of America Stadium on December 21, 2025 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Panthers managed to get out of New Orleans last week with a win, which snapped a 3 game losing skid and once again placed them atop the NFC South with a one and a half game lead. While their division is widely criticized for its inability to post a winning record or just win games in general, any team in the division could get hot and win a few games to take the lead. The Panthers have the Ravens, and the newly traded for QB Jacoby Brissett, on deck this week. And while its a winnable game, the Panthers have made many of their games difficult this season with penalties and mistakes. So this is by no means a gimme game, and there’s a lot the Panthers have to both continue to progress in and make right for them to have any realistic possibility at both the playoffs themselves and any chance of actually making any waves short of a first round exit. Don’t get me wrong, I know this Panthers team has had a ton of adversity injury wise and game script wise, but you can only handle those things as they come and to your best to overcome them. Let’s dive in to some important storylines for this week. Offense: Re-connect with the wide receivers The Panthers started the year with many pundits wondering if the combination of WRs Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker being one of the best combos in the league. They have since not proven they are, and this is coming from someone who very much believes in them both. T Mac continues to play at the level you’d expect, but with6 targets and only 4 catches against the Broncos for 56 yards and a TD, and only 3 catches on 7 targets against the Saints last week, that’s not quite good enough. For Jalen Coker, he caught 4 passes on 6 targets for 29 yards against the Broncos and didn’t log a single catch on 4 targets against the Saints. These two were (for the most part) the catalyst behind the Panthers having one of the more productive passing attacks in the NFL to start the season, specifically on throws down the field. Coker’s unfortunately missed a couple that could have been big, but the reality is close doesn’t count in the NFL. And trust me when I say this, I know it isn’t necessarily their fault. The offensive line was battered and bruised, Bryce Young hasn’t been consistent ever since the losing skid had started, and Brad Idzik likely needs to make adjustments as the offensive coordinator now that defenses have more of a read on what the Panthers passing attack is trying to do. But winning games by basically feeding Chuba Hubbard every touch and the two tight ends in Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller around him is not going to be a sustainable formula. The Panthers employed the run-pass option at times this year, mostly with T Mac, to diversify their offense. Jalen Coker tends to be most effective when he’s gotten a few catches early on in games. This might be the time to try and get these two DAWGS involved early. They also may have to lean on these guys since both Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble are dealing with knee injuries that kept them out of practice Wednesday. Defense: Aggression is working The Panthers have basically simplified their defense since Todd Wash took over for Ejiro Evero, who is hanging out on Sean Payton’s couch in Denver somewhere I’m sure. While making a whole defensive transition in the middle of a season will have its own growing pains, mainly in the form of penalties, I am seeing the vision with what Wash is trying to accomplish. Jaelan Phillips won NFC defensive player of the week, Derrick Brown was productive, Lee Hunter continues to excel in limited snaps, and the Panthers cornerbacks being more aggressive and in the face of the Saints offense paid huge dividends. They are going to face more polished offenses as the season goes on, but this formula seems to be working. And it starts with stopping the run. They held the Broncos to 75 yards rushing by their running backs, and 24 yards by the Saints as QB Tyler Shough led the team with 25 yards, more than their running backs combined. This week could be a major test because this Ravens team should lean on Derrick Henry out of the backfield. I say “should”, because despite Brissett making his first start for the team, they threw the ball 49 times in a game where they were down by 10 points at worst throughout. Regardless, putting pressure on this offense with aggression in both aspects of football should help them win this game. Hopefully the offense can capitalize on more short yardage fields this time if they generate turnovers. Bonus storyline: More reinforcements The Panthers are most likely getting CB Mike Jackson back this week from injury, after losing both Mike and Jaycee Horn a few weeks ago. The Panthers have mostly operated on a skeleton crew, especially after Will Lee III got injured himself. It looks like they’ll get one of their top corners back this week, and he excelled at times last season when he needed to be the CB1 in the absence of Horn due to injury/suspension. They also signed Marco Wilson to the active roster, who showed out when needed in his last three games called upon as an active roster escalation from the practice squad. But in theory, if Mike Jackson can play and Will Lee doesn’t suffer any setbacks, they’ll have two of their top three CBs healthy for this week. On the offensive side, Carolina is still waiting to fully clear OL Brady Christensen, but he would be a very important piece for an offensive line that is thin. He would start anywhere if they needed him to due to injury at this point. And Luke Fortner hasn’t been good at center, so they could even opt to make a switch with Christensen playing center, he’s done that in the past and been more than passible. What are you looking for this week, Panthers fans?

full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 19: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears passes the ball during the second half of the NFL football game against the New Orleans Saints at Solider Field on October 19, 2025 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the initial spread dropped for the Chicago Bears and the New Orleans Saints, I thought, that’s a really big number . Four days ago, the 7-2 Bears opened as a 9.5-point favorite over the 3-6 Saints; it then climbed to 10.5 later that evening. It’s currently up to 11.5 (at the time I’m writing this), according to FanDuel Sportsbook , but the more I look at this matchup, the more I think the Bears will easily cover. The Bears are coming off their bye week, so they’ll be well rested and ready to make another statement. I’m not saying get ready for a 59-point explosion like Week 1, but a 50-burger wouldn’t surprise me. The running game has been criticized lately, but did you realize it still ranks number 1 in attempts and is 4th in yards per game? The Bears have a top-10 offense by most metrics while the Saints have a bottom-10 defense. On the flip side, New Orleans’ offense has been bottom-10, while the surprising Bears have been top-10 on defense. And that’s with Jeffery Simmons only being a Bear for two games. Chicago’s offense is what everyone thinks of when discussing how well-timed their bye week was, but the defense also gets a chance to self-scout and figure out how best to play off Simmons. I like the Bears’ offense starting strong on Sunday, their defense getting a few turnovers, and them winning 38 to 17. So give me all these Bears overs: Caleb Williams’ passing yards (245.5), Caleb passing touchdowns (2.5), Rome Odunze receiving yards (45.5), and D’Andre Swift rushing/receiving yards (82.5). title: Chicago Bears-New Orleans Saints: Keys to a Chicago victory
summary: Chicago Bears football is back! After all those primetime games, not having the Bears in action made the bye week feel longer than usual. Now the Bears kickoff a very tough, but important stretch of football. The Saints and Dolphins stand as the only two losing teams on their remaining slate. And they still have […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - OCTOBER 19: Carl Granderson #96 of the New Orleans Saints tackles Kyle Monangai #25 of the Chicago Bears during the first half on October 19, 2025 at Soldier Field in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Melissa Tamez/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Chicago Bears football is back! After all those primetime games, not having the Bears in action made the bye week feel longer than usual. Now the Bears kickoff a very tough, but important stretch of football. The Saints and Dolphins stand as the only two losing teams on their remaining slate. And they still have to face the gauntlet of the NFC North four more times. It starts with the Saints, though. And while their record is not good, it’s the NFL. Chicago is in no position to overlook an opponent. The Saints have talent. They’ve been in most of their games this season. In fact, all but two of their games have been decided by one score or less. So it’s no walk in the park. Our crew breaks down what it will take for Chicago to get the win on Sunday. Sam: This is the worst defense the Bears have faced in a month. However, they have a formidable pass-rushing duo in Chase Young and Chad Granderson. If the Bears slow them down, they will be able to get back to the run game we saw earlier this season. That will set up play action. For the defense, the Saints look like they’ll be without their starting RT and C. That should give the advantage to Montez Sweat and Jeffery Simmons. Get pressure on Tyler Shough, cover Chris Olave and there isn’t much else the Saints have been able to do well this season. Josh: Chicago just needs to stay out of its own way. Caleb needs to play clean ball, the running game needs to stay on schedule, and the front four need to apply enough pressure that the weak secondary is never stressed. Mongo Peanut: The Bears need to neutralize a sneaky good pass-rush by New Orleans by leaning back into their running attack. I expect them to pound the rock repeatedly and set up several downfield shots. Additionally, if they can erase Olave on the other side, this should be a fairly straightforward victory. Jacob: The Bears need to go back to their roots with Kyle Monangai healthy and pound the rock. Their offense has been very good each of the last few weeks, but we really see this offense operate at its best when it gets to dominate the time of possession and wear down the opposing defense with a steady dose of Monangai and D’Andre Swift. The Saints have struggled in run support this year, and as good as their edge rushers have been, their interior defensive line leaves a lot to be desired. Gary: The Saints are one of the handful of teams I have watched very closely this year due in large part to my grading of Tyler Shough. It’s a team that really doesn’t have much an identity, outside of their Edges getting to the QB. Tyler Shough leads the team in rushing, and after watching him for 10 weeks he struggles with attacking the entire field, with throws over the middle coming few and far in-between. I will consider it a big failure if the Bears don’t cover the spread against the Saints, the skill level gap between each team is a canyon, so in those scenarios if the Bears take care of the football, they will be 8-2.

title: Bears’ Caleb Williams Focused on Bouncing Back After Four-Interception Game
summary: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams’ four-interception performance against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 9 was uncharacteristic of the ball security he had displayed throughout his NFL career. The bigger question now is how Williams responds to that performance and bounces back over the remainder of the season. That will be especially important as the […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 8: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears prepares in the tunnel before the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Soldier Field on November 8, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams’ four-interception performance against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 9 was uncharacteristic of the ball security he had displayed throughout his NFL career. The bigger question now is how Williams responds to that performance and bounces back over the remainder of the season. That will be especially important as the Bears enter the second half of the season with a challenging stretch of games remaining on their schedule. Williams described two of the interceptions as “funky” and acknowledged that one was a bad decision, but the four-interception performance was still frustrating for the Bears quarterback, with his biggest disappointment stemming from feeling like he had let his teammates down. “The biggest thing is, the frustration comes from the feeling of, for me, personally, I always don’t want to let my teammates down,” Williams said. “That’s always big for me, and in those situations, I feel like did. That’s the frustrating part that lingers.” Even after throwing four interceptions, Williams still led the Bears on a late-game drive that put them in position to win, setting up the field goal that sealed the game. That ability to respond is something that Bears offensive coordinator Press Taylor has seen Williams demonstrate time and again, particularly in high-pressure situations. His history of delivering in critical moments has given the coaching staff confidence in how he handles adversity and moves forward from difficult performances. “That’s something that’s been his thing, you know, late in last year, you think of the late game plays he’s able to make,” Taylor said. “He’s demonstrated that over and over, so as you see it over and over and continue to reveal itself, then you’re going to trust him more and more with that type of situations. And every game is really a learning opportunity for all of us to learn how everybody responds to certain situations.” Caleb Williams is ready to respond after his four-interception game, Press Taylor says. pic.twitter.com/5ollz0dC2E — 104.3 The Score (@thescorechicago) November 19, 2026 Even with the four interceptions against Tampa Bay, Williams’ career interception rate remains unmatched in NFL history among quarterbacks with 1,000 or more pass attempts. It’s a testament to the level of ball security he has maintained throughout his young NFL career, and why one rough performance doesn’t change the bigger picture. Even after throwing four interceptions in his last game, Caleb Williams still has the lowest interception percentage in NFL history among QBs with at least 1,000 pass attempts. #Bears — Adam Hoge (@AdamHoge) November 19, 2026 With the bye week giving him time to step away from the field, Williams has shifted his focus from the frustration of the performance toward what he can learn from it and apply moving forward. “I’ve moved on from it,” Williams said. “It’s more of a, how can I get better? What can I be better at? Just finding ways to be more consistent.” That starts with turning the page and shifting the focus to the New Orleans Saints. The Bears have remained committed to taking the season one game at a time, with the goal of going 1-0 each week rather than looking too far ahead. For Williams, that means applying what he learned against Tampa Bay while keeping his attention on the opportunity in front of him.

title: Week 11 game preview: Chicago Bears vs. New Orleans Saints
summary: The Chicago Bears are back to business following the bye week. To kick off the back half of their season, they host the New Orleans Saints. While the Saints haven’t looked great in their past few games, this is the NFL, and no opponent should be taken lightly. And Chicago shouldn’t be resting on their […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 08: Chris Olave #12 of the New Orleans Saints runs the ball during an NFL football game against the Cleveland Browns at Cesars Superdome on November 8, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears are back to business following the bye week. To kick off the back half of their season, they host the New Orleans Saints. While the Saints haven’t looked great in their past few games, this is the NFL, and no opponent should be taken lightly. And Chicago shouldn’t be resting on their laurels. In their last game, they needed a field goal at the end of regulation to win. Plus, the end of their season is filled with playoff teams and their division opponents. They can’t afford to trip up against the bad teams on the schedule. Let’s get into this matchup and see what it will take for the Bears to get a win against the New Orleans Saints Sunday. New Orleans Saints SB Nation site: Canal Street Chronicles Record: 3-6, third in the NFC South Last week: 20-17 loss to the Carolina Panthers Game day, time, TV: Sunday, noon CT, FOX Spread: Bears -11.5 Bears all-time record against: 16-18 (including 2-1 postseason) Historical meetings: In week 9 of the 1991 season, the 5-2 Bears went to New Orleans to face the 7-0 Saints. Saints QB Bobby Herbert hit Floyd Turner for a 65-yard score in the first quarter. The Bears added just two Kevin Butler field goals while the Saints tacked on a field goal of their own before halftime. In the second half, Brad Muster rushed for Chicago’s first touchdown of the day. The Saints struck back with Turner again, scoring on a pass from Herbert. But Jim Harbaugh shook off what had been a bad day to that point and hit Wendell Davis for 27 yards and Neal Anderson for 6 yards, before finding Tom Waddle for a 12-yard score 59 seconds left. The Bears won 20-17. Harbaugh was 5 of 22 for 61 yards, one TD and two interceptions. Three of his five completions were on the final drive of the game. Last meeting: The Bears and Saints met in week seven last year. Spencer Rattler started the game for New Orleans. On their first drive of the game, he was sacked and fumbled, setting up a Jake Moody field goal. Neither team could get much going, as New Orleans punted, Caleb Williams was intercepted and the Saints missed a field goal. Following the miss, the Bears drove but had to settle for another field goal. But then, Rattler threw a pick to Nashon Wright, setting up D’Andre Swift for a touchdown four plays later. Kyle Monangai scored on the next Chicago drive and the Bears were in business. Rattler rallied to finish the first half with a touchdown to Chris Olave, finding him for a 57-yard completion before hitting him for the 21-yard score. Rattler again found Olave on the Saints’ opening second-half drive for another touchdown. But the Bears scored two more field goals and Rattler threw two more interceptions. The Bears won 26-14. Injury report: The Saints listed nine players on their Wednesday injury report. Did not participate CB Martin Emerson Jr. (concussion) T Taliese Fuaga (knee) Alvin Kamara (NIR – rest) C Erik McCoy (biceps) S Justin Reid (NIR – rest) T Asim Richards (knee) LB Pete Werner (hamstring) Limited participation CB Decamerion Richardson (thigh) WR Jordyn Tyson (chest) Offense: The Saints offense ranks 15th in points and 22nd in yards. Their passing offense ranks 16th and their rushing offense ranks 27th. Tyler Shough (66.8 cmp. pct./2,173 yds./15 TD/7 INT) is still developing, but has overall been solid and played well for New Orleans. He’s led two fourth-quarter comebacks and had two game-winning drives. Lately though, he’s been reluctant to throw downfield. Kellen Moore’s offense has Shough targeting Chris Olave (59 rec./764 yds./2 TD), Devaughn Vele (37/379/3) and TE Juwan Johnson (30/317/4). Alvin Kamara (28/160/2) remains a featured part of the offense. First-round pick WR Jordyn Tyson (15/110/0) could return from injury and brings high hopes with him. TE Noah Fant (12/96/3) is a red zone target. On the ground, it’s not been very pretty. Kendre Miller (57 att./159 yds./2 TD) is the leader in carries. Alvin Kamara (49/161/3) is the leader in touchdowns. Shough (40/187/2) is the leader in yards. Travis Etienne (38/142/0) just returned from injury. As a team their 3.6 yards per attempt ranks 29th in the league and their 811 yards is 27th. Defense: The Saints defense ranks 25th in points and 29th in yards allowed. Their passing defense ranks 21st and their rushing defense ranks 27th. While those numbers aren’t impressive, they do have a solid pass rush. DEs Carl Granderson (8.5 sk/10 QB hits/7 TFL/36 tkls) and Chase Young (8 sk/15 QB hits/5 TFL/19 tkls/4 PD/1 FF) are both in the top-10 for sacks on the year. LBs Pete Werner (70 tkls/2 sk/2 PD/4 TFL/4 QB hits) and Kaden Eliss (56 tkls/10 QB hits/6 TFL/2 sk/2 PD) lead the team in tackles. Behind them, Justin Reid (46 tkls/2 TFL), Jonas Sanker (52 tkls/1 FR/4 PD/1 TFL) Julian Blackmon (43 tkl/2 PD/2 INT) and Martin Emerson (21 tkls/4 PD/2 INT) are making plays in the secondary. Kool-Aid McKinstry (35 tkls/6 PD), Quincy Riley (21 tkls/5 PD) and Jonas Sanker (52 tkls/4 PD/1 FR) have all made plays at times, too. Key matchups: The Bears have a lot of advantages here. The Saints’ run defense should allow D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai to get going and set up those play-action shots. Looking at the injury report, New Orleans could be without two key defenders in Werner and Emerson. Emerson had started three straight games after notching two interceptions against the Giants. On the offensive side, the Saints could be without two OL in center Erik McCoy and RT Taliese Fuaga. Tyler Shough has shown regression in recent weeks, bailing on clean pockets or at the slightest sign of pressure. The Bears can get him uncomfortable. If they can cover Chris Olave, the Saints don’t have much else in terms of game-breakers. Key stats The Saints rank 27th in third-down defense, allowing opponents to convert 45.1 percent. The Bears rank fourth in third-down offense. New Orleans has allowed 30 rushing touchdowns, which is the third-most in the league. The Saints are seventh in blitz percentage but 29th in pressure percentage. They have the 12th most sacks in the league, with 26. The Saints are tied for the fourth-fewest takeaways on defense with nine.
