title: 3 keys to a Cincinnati Bengals victory against the Washington Commanders
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals will take their version of the greatest show on Earth to Washington in Week 11 against the Commanders in primetime, playing them on Monday Night Football. Washington is 3-5-1 this season, but coming off a crucial win against the AFC East division-leading New York Giants on Thursday Night Football last week. The […]
full_text: Joe Burrow is questionable to return with a wrist injury. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Cincinnati Bengals will take their version of the greatest show on Earth to Washington in Week 11 against the Commanders in primetime, playing them on Monday Night Football. Washington is 3-5-1 this season, but coming off a crucial win against the AFC East division-leading New York Giants on Thursday Night Football last week. The Bengals are coming off a primetime victory of their own, defeating the Pittsburgh Steelers 38-18 at Paycor Stadium on Sunday Night Football. The win improved the Bengals to 7-2 on the season, and they currently have a one-game lead over those Steelers for first place in the AFC North. Let’s take a look at 3 keys to the Cincinnati Bengals continuing their winning streak this week. Keep Jayden Daniels In Check Jayden Daniels is completing a respectable 64.8% of his passes so far during the 2026 season. He has 10 passing touchdowns to 2 interceptions in the 7 games he has played this year. Daniels has an additional 280 rushing yards on the season. Even more so than those numbers, the Bengals likely remember what Jayden was able to do against them in primetime football back in 2024. Daniels completed 21 of 23 passes for over 250 passing yards, 2 passing touchdowns, and an additional 39 rushing yards with a touchdown on the ground. He helped Washington pull off the victory 38-33 that night in Cincinnati. While Daniels is a dangerous player, it is important to note that this is a completely different defense than the one he faced back in 2024. While this defense hasn’t been dominant, they certainly have shown a lot more than what we saw in 2024 and 2025. They are also coming off two really good performances against Atlanta and Pittsburgh. This won’t be an easy game for Cincinnati, but they do have a defense that we should have much more faith in than we did back in 2024. The talent is substantially different, and they have started to play some really complementary football at all three levels of the defense. Be You Offensively There is no reason to change up what is working. Let Joe Burrow do what Joe Burrow does best, and that is throwing the football all over the field with surgical precision. Coming off of a 400-yard and 4-touchdown passing performance, the Bengals should just keep on throwing the football. There will be times to take deeper shots down the field, but the most impressive part of what Burrow is doing is just how patient he has become. He isn’t putting the ball in harm’s way; he is settling for the check-down passes when necessary, and is allowing the running backs to catch passes as an extension of the run game. When you have a quarterback that is playing at an MVP level, you have to let him cook. That is fully what I expect to see again this week in a primetime matchup against the Commanders’ defense. The Commanders have the 31st-ranked passing defense this year. They are allowing 244.8 passing yards per game. Joe Burrow. Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins, and the rest of the Bengals offense should be in for a big night. Take Care Of The Football About the only way teams currently have a chance to beat the Bengals is if they decide to beat themselves. When they lose the turnover battle, they will have a chance to lose the game. We saw that against Pittsburgh and Jacksonville early in the season this year. We also saw them get pushed to overtime when they had 4 turnovers against the Tennessee Titans. If they take care of the football, they should win this game in Washington this week. If not, they will be in for a closer contest than they hope for, and potentially an upset loss on the road. Sometimes, it really is that simple.

title: Bengals Film Room: Amarius Mims is the best right tackle in the NFL
summary: Amarius Mims is finally getting the national recognition he so rightfully deserves this season. Mims has been playing at an All-Pro level at right tackle for the Cincinnati Bengals. Often left on an island, Mims has allowed just 6 total pressures the entire season. Allowing just 6 pressures is the lowest of any right tackle in […]
full_text: Amarius Mims is finally getting the national recognition he so rightfully deserves this season. Mims has been playing at an All-Pro level at right tackle for the Cincinnati Bengals . Often left on an island, Mims has allowed just 6 total pressures the entire season. Allowing just 6 pressures is the lowest of any right tackle in the league that has played at least 50% of their team’s required snaps. The only tackle in the league with a lower number is Denver left tackle Garrett Bolles. Mims also has 40 more pass-blocking snaps than Bolles has taken on the season. No matter the numbers you want to look at, Mims has been the most dominant right tackle, if not overall tackle in the NFL this year. I guess we should get the one pressure he allowed out of the way. He gave up a pressure to Jack Sawyer against Pittsburgh, the only one he allowed all game. That was on 47 total pass-blocking snaps. Mims has allowed just 2 pressures in his last 200 pass-blocking snaps played. On the pressure to Sawyer, it appears he thought he would have help on the inside by Dalton Risner, but he could not get over quickly enough. Either way, Burrow was able to escape the pressure and avoid a negative play. I guess Mims is at least human, allowing this one whole pressure lol pic.twitter.com/5hbvjoVhVx — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 17, 2026 Beyond that, Mims was his usual dominating self again in primetime against the Steelers. He and the rest of the Bengals offense set the tone early against Pittsburgh. Mims escorted Watt up the field away from Burrow, Brown picked up the blitz, and Gesicki made a tough catch over the middle of the field. Setting a tone right away. Chase Brown with the blitz pickup, Mims showing Watt he isn’t getting near Burrow yet again against him, and Gesicki hanging on to the ball while absorbing the big hit. pic.twitter.com/diD19pbmY6 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 16, 2026 Mims really has kept TJ Watt in check this season. To be honest, he kept him in check last year too. His performances against Watt last year is what had me believing he was going to take the leap into being an All-Pro talent this season, and that is exactly what has happened. Mims had TJ Watt in hell all night long, not letting him get any kind of pressure on Joe Burrow. Amarius “ Bye Week” Mims Might as well be on your bye week going against him as the guys on the postgame show said last night 🤣🤣 pic.twitter.com/PmprZsk0RD — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 17, 2026 Maybe it doesn’t mean a lot to most of you, but I loved that Mims was willing to give a little extra shove to Watt when he started to show his frustration later in the game. The Steelers love to be the more physical team, and set the tone for what type of game you will be playing against them. That wasn’t the case this week, as Mims and the rest of the Bengals team were the tone-setters. Watt gave him a little extra shove so he gave him one back 😳 https://t.co/mR4TpiVTZW pic.twitter.com/GtdjqeruCr — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 17, 2026 There is still a lot of season left to be played, but Amarius Mims should be an obvious selection for All-Pro if he continues playing at the level he has all season. I think it is safe to say that TJ Watt would agree with that being the case. Amarius Mims vs. Pittsburgh Steelers All-Pro Amarius Mims with another great performance pic.twitter.com/4VnmyCgxFu — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) November 17, 2026

title: Bengals vs. Commanders odds, expert picks, and our prediction for Week 11 matchup
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have been one of the hottest teams in the NFL and are tied with a handful of teams with a five-game win streak. That culminated in an absolute whooping of the Pittsburgh Steelers at home on Sunday Night Football that wasn’t even as close as the 20-point win made it seem. Now […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals have been one of the hottest teams in the NFL and are tied with a handful of teams with a five-game win streak. That culminated in an absolute whooping of the Pittsburgh Steelers at home on Sunday Night Football that wasn’t even as close as the 20-point win made it seem. Now they are taking their show on the road to play the Washington Commanders in their house on Monday Night Football. Joe Burrow is 0-2 so far in his career against the Commanders, but that comes with some pretty big caveats. The first loss was the game in which he injured his knee midway through the game as a rookie. The other loss came in an absolute monster of a shootout where the Bengals defense did not stop the Commanders or Jayden Daniels a single time in 2024, with the game ending 38-33. That would not be the first time Burrow would helm a losing team despite putting up more than 30 points over the next few seasons. These teams are drastically different as the Cincinnati defense has had a major overhaul, and Washington is far from the team it was during Daniels’ rookie season. There is no doubt Daniels is a talented quarterback, but the Commanders themselves seem to be a very average to below-average team that needs a combination of home run hits on offense and a handful of turnovers to spark a win. Meanwhile, Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins are giving their best impressions of the Colts’ offense during Peyton Manning’s heyday by trusting their quarterback to put up points with his top weapons over a balanced attack. That has led to four straight games of four touchdowns for Burrow, which ties a record set by Manning. The real x-factor here will be the Bengals defense. Will the version we have seen since the Madrid game against the Atlanta Falcons show up that has been able to contain opposing offenses that tried to test their linebackers and safeties? Or will the young players at those positions allow a few too many big plays? Here is how the oddsmakers and experts feel about the game. Odds The Bengals are currently 6.5-point road favorites against the Commanders, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . It really is a fairly big deal when a road team gets almost a touchdown advantage over a home team. It clearly shows that there is a step between where these two teams are currently at. The point total is set at 53.5 is the second highest of the week. That is fair because even when this team has faced teams like the Tennessee Titans, they have given up opportunities to score. Expert picks 10 of ESPN’s 11 experts are going with the Bengals CBS Sports has all seven experts taking Cincinnati to win All five of NFL.com’s experts are expecting the Bengals to extend their win streak to six games NFL Pick Watch — which takes into account picks from across the web — has Cincinnati receiving 99% of the picks for this game. Cincy Jungle Pick I think this team has really turned a corner as far as this defense is concerned. The young linebacker duo of Demetrius Knight and Barrett Carter have grown enough to prove to be a competent — maybe not the most consistent — duo. That is the level of play this defense needs when the defensive line led by Boye Mafe and Dexter Lawrence is able to get penetration. We will have to see how well they contain Daniels, who can really cause some damage by extending plays with his legs. All of that more or less will determine how much the Commanders lose by. Washington has no way of slowing down or throwing off this offense. The Bengals are getting into at least the 30s. Can the Commanders keep pace? Final Score: Bengals 45, Commanders 25 Who Dey! title: Bengals News: Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins eyeing NFL history
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are having a very historic passing attack. Joe Burrow has been firing on all cylinders, and Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are both on pace to finish with over 1,000 receiving yards. The duo has both cracked 800 receiving yards through only nine games. That means the Bengals have two receivers on […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are having a very historic passing attack. Joe Burrow has been firing on all cylinders, and Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are both on pace to finish with over 1,000 receiving yards. The duo has both cracked 800 receiving yards through only nine games. That means the Bengals have two receivers on pace to have over 1,500 receiving yards. A feat that no team has ever accomplished, but that two have gotten very close to . Back in 2000, Torry Holt finished with 1,635 yards while playing for the “Greatest Show on Turf” Rams and his teammate, Isaac Bruce, finished with 1,471. In 1995, the Lions’ receiving tandem of Herman Moore (1,686) and Brent Perriman (1,488) came closer than anyone to having two players on the same team hit 1,500 yards, but Perriman came up 12 yards short. The Lions duo totaled 3,174 yards, which is the NFL record for a receiving tandem. The record has somehow stood for 31 years, even with the league now in a pass-happy era. It is important to note that both of those teams did that during a 16-game regular season. So if Chase and Higgins want to make this an even more impressive feat, they will do it within 16 games. However, being the first to accomplish it even with 17 games is still noteworthy. Bengals news Quick Hits | Jonathan Allen Returns With An Old Move And A New Team That Could Be His Best Yet; Ja’Marr Chase Stacks Another New Number: Nine Allen was the most underrated move of the offseason. He may not be Dexter Lawrence, but he is a quality veteran defensive tackle who can still get it done not only against the run but as a pass rusher. The team adding Boye Mafe, Dexter Lawrence and Allen this offseason helped put its defensive line rotation over the top as one of the best in the league after being one of the worst the year prior. Quick Hits | Dalton Risner Day-To-Day After Missing Practice; Short and Sweet One player who probably didn’t get the credit they deserved after Sunday night’s win was Jalen Rivers. He played practically the whole game after Risner had to exit knee injury. Offensive line coach Scott Peters did a hell of a job turning Rivers around after he looked horrendous the last time we saw him play. Kudos for those folks. Bengals QB Joe Burrow dealing with illness before Week 11 It is still Thursday, so there is plenty of time for this to pass. It could still be a Michael Jordan Flu game loading (mostly joking). It is definitely something to monitor as we get closer to the game, though. NFL News Colts-Texans on ‘Thursday Night Football’: What We Learned from Houston’s 26-3 win I am seeing a lot of hype for CJ Stroud, and he had a good game, but the Colts defense has been one of the worst this season. I don’t think this makes me think any more or less highly of Stroud. He is certainly winning the bet on himself against the Texans front office, though. Ravens CB Marlon Humphrey sent home, won’t play vs. Panthers after Baltimore comments Things are not going well in Baltimore. Humphrey is making headlines more for his podcast than his play on the field. This team has a major identity crisis, and it certainly feels like head coach Jesse Minter is trying desperately right the ship after public outcry caught up to the comments and not because of the comments themselves. Bill Belichick, Robert Kraft advance in election process for Pro Football Hall of Fame It is still the biggest failing of the Hall of Fame voting process that Belichick was not a first-ballot Hall of Famer. Fans in Cincinnati have known the process has been hugely flawed for a long time, but everyone got a big example of it last season.

title: Browns history: Where are they now? interview with S Thom Darden
summary: The Cleveland Browns are one of those teams that have had their fair share of really good defensive units. Folks kinda expect that from this franchise – even today. And the list of great Cleveland defenders is pretty lengthy. Somewhere, safety Thom Darden fits nicely on that list as a member of the defensive backfield. […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns are one of those teams that have had their fair share of really good defensive units. Folks kinda expect that from this franchise – even today. And the list of great Cleveland defenders is pretty lengthy. Somewhere, safety Thom Darden fits nicely on that list as a member of the defensive backfield. Darden is an Ohio guy. He grew up in Sandusky and attended Sandusky High School. In 1965, they were Ohio State champions in football. The school is known for its football tradition and is the fifth winningest program in the state. RELATED: DT JERRY SHERK INTERVIEW But Darden’s interest in football was situated in third place early on. His love was basketball, but his athletic greatness was on the diamond playing baseball. He was even scouted by the hometown Cleveland Indians. Coming out of high school playing safety, cornerback, and middle linebacker, Darden was recruited by many Big 10 colleges, with Ohio State and Michigan leading the list. He gave Ohio State the first shot at recruiting him to play football, but ultimately signed with Michigan, where he was part of head coach Bo Schembechler’s first recruiting class. Darden would go on to become a First Team All-American (UPI), Second Team All-American (AP), First Team All-Big 10 as a junior, and First Team All-Big 10 in his senior season. He played in 33 college games with 218 tackles, 11 tackles for loss, 11 interceptions, three touchdowns, and 13 pass defenses. He also ran back 42 punts. In his final two seasons at Michigan, Darden’s teams only lost three games, including a Rose Bowl defeat when the 8-3-0 Stanford Indians upset Michigan 13-12. Darden was also part of two Big 10 conference titles. After his Michigan career, he played in the 1971 Coaches All-America Game in Lubbock, Texas, an All-Star contest. He was voted the game’s MVP. In April, he was drafted by the Browns in the first round with the 18 th overall selection . Darden grew up a Browns fan. Before reporting to training camp, Darden participated in the Chicago Charities College All-Star Game on July 28, 1972, against the Super Bowl champs, the Dallas Cowboys. In his first NFL training camp, Darden was with a defensive backfield that the year before had started Clarence Scott and Ben Davis at cornerbacks, and Walt Sumner and Mike Howell at the safety positions. Darden had a great rookie training camp and was an immediate starter for the Browns at strong safety when they switched Sumner to free safety. Darden started all 14 regular season games in 1972. He received votes for the “NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year.” In the 1975 preseason, he suffered a knee injury and missed the entire season. In all, Darden played 10 years, all with Cleveland. He was voted to the Pro Bowl in 1978 and was named Second Team All-Pro in 1976, 1978, and 1979. In his Pro Bowl year, he was the “NFL Interceptions Leader” with 10 for 200 yards. Both stats led the league. Darden still has three Browns team records: Most career interceptions – 45, most interceptions in a single season – 10, and most interception return yards – 820. He last played with Cleveland in 1981. Since that time, hundreds of defensive backs have come and gone. That’s 45 years his team records have stood. Today, Darden lives in Cedar Rapids, Iowa. He and his wife Melissa have raised six children. #Browns honoring Thom Darden, Dick Ambrose at halftime. Both inducted into the team’s Legends program. pic.twitter.com/qQgZvrUcIR — Scott Patsko (@ScottPatsko) September 18, 2016 Darden was inducted into the: Sandusky High School Athletic Hall of Fame (1991) Cleveland Browns Legends Program (2016) Northwest Ohio Sports Weekly Top-10 Athletes in Erie County History Dawgs By Nature staff writer Barry Shuck was able to interview Darden and find out what his trick is with getting so many interceptions, if he grew up a Browns fan, and why the heck did he choose Michigan over Ohio State?!? Shuck: You were a standout basketball and baseball player at Sandusky High School. Why did you pursue football at the college level instead of these other sports? Darden: My first love was basketball. I loved it and started playing in the 10 th grade. I played baseball since I was seven until I was 18 years of age. My high school was considered one of the better programs in the State of Ohio. With football, in my sophomore year, we were Number 1 in the state, and Number 3 my junior year and Number 5 in my senior year. We had a good foundation. If you were any kind of athlete, your goal was to get a college scholarship. My father told me if I wanted to go to college, I better figure it out how to pay for it. So, I had to get a scholarship because I didn’t have any money. My best way of going to a prominent school was through football because our program was well liked across the State of Ohio. We had good coaches. Shuck: What is the story about you almost signing with the Cleveland Indians? Darden: You have done your research. I was a pretty good pitcher, a left-hander. And played first base. And left handers were rare back then. I played on our legion team which you had to be 16 or 17. My coach said that this guy was coming in from the Indians and wanted to see about two or three of us on the team. And when I got up to bat, the scout brought his own pitcher and told him to throw low and inside on me. I couldn’t hit the low and inside pitch. I think that’s what kept me from being signed by the Indians. So, the Indians never offered me a contract and I never heard another word from them. I was a senior in high school and decided to go to Michigan and play football instead of baseball. Shuck: Did you grow up a Browns fan? Darden: I definitely grew up a Browns fan. Loved Jim Brown. After Otto Graham, I remember when they got Milt Plum and then sent him to Detroit. Frank Ryan and Gary Collins. Paul Warfield. All great players. And all players that a young man would admire and want to root for. Plus, they won all the time. Warfield ended up being my roommate when he came back that second time to Cleveland. Shuck: You had plenty of college offers coming out of high school. I am perplexed. You had the opportunity to go to Ohio State. Why choose Michigan? Darden: You want the full version? Going into my senior year at high school, I played safety and also cornerback. But our middle linebacker broke his arm, and because I knew how to hit, they wanted me to move to his position. I was about 173 pounds in probably the second-best conference in the State of Ohio. So, when I got recruited the coaches had to tell these schools that I was really a defensive back. Woody Hayes of Ohio State told me they had this position that they wanted me to play – it’s a hybrid position. And it was a weakside linebacker/safety type position. It was still in the 4-3, but the outside linebacker played off the line. My father later became a minister, and Woody came by himself and started talking about football. He sat in our living room. And then he started talking about war. He would congregate war and football. When he would start doing that, he got excited. And then he started frothing at the mouth. And then he started cussing. When he left, my father, said, “You’re not going there.” So, with Michigan, Bo Schembechler didn’t come until January. A gentleman, soft spoken, and my mother fell in love with him. As parents, you want your son to be somewhere safe and can flourish and be taken care of. You’re sending your boy off and he’s not going to be down the road and you want him to be taken care of at just 17 years old. As a teenager, you don’t know what’s going on in life. And I signed with Michigan, but Ohio State went first. title: Grading the Browns defense: New faces, similar results at the bye week
summary: Going into the 2026 season, the Cleveland Browns defense was undergoing some changes that were seen as major from the outside. Reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett was traded to the Los Angeles Rams, and defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz chose to leave the team after being passed up for the head coaching job. […]
full_text: Going into the 2026 season, the Cleveland Browns defense was undergoing some changes that were seen as major from the outside. Reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett was traded to the Los Angeles Rams , and defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz chose to leave the team after being passed up for the head coaching job. In the Myles Garrett trade, the team received defensive end Jared Verse from the Rams (who won defensive rookie of the year in 2024 and is a two-time Pro Bowler), who isn’t necessarily the same caliber player as Garrett but has shown signs of being a really good edge rusher while in LA. The Browns hired Atlanta Falcons passing game coordinator Mike Rutenberg to be their defensive coordinator. Analysts and fans were concerned about the defense taking a step back after losing Garrett and Schwartz, but it appears that the defense is doing just fine. Just like we did with the offense earlier this week , it is time to size up the Browns defense at the bye week and give it a grade. What has changed? Outside of losing Garrett and Schwartz, not much. After losing linebacker Devin Bush in free agency, the team replaced him with linebacker Quincy Williams. Cornerback Martin Emerson also left, but outside of those minor subtractions, the team has essentially returned most of their group from last season. Defensive tackle Mason Graham has emerged as the best player on the defensive line. Linebacker Carson Schwesinger might be a top 10 linebacker in this league, maybe even Top 5. Extending cornerback Denzel Ward and safety Grant Delpit were no-brainers. Ward, who is playing at a top-5 level, will likely be an All-Pro this season, and Delpit has been one of the more underrated safeties in the league. After being acquired in a trade with the Jacksonville Jaguars last season, cornerback Tyson Campbell has fit in well in his second full year with the team. When Schwartz wasn’t retained as the defensive coordinator, many wondered how the scheme would look. Rutenberg, also known as Rudy, decided to not change the scheme but instead tweak it. Schwartz’s defenses weren’t complex in terms of how the scheme looked. Not much creativity in terms of mixing up the coverages and disguising looks. Schwartz also failed to make the necessary adjustments, and his defenses were easy to decipher against better offensive minds. Rutenberg has made tweaks to the scheme but is still keeping the core principles that made the Browns defense elite last season. Browns defense pre-bye (last season) 5th in EPA/per play 3rd in Defensive Success Rate 15th in Defensive Dropback EPA/per play 14th in Defensive Dropback Success Rate 2nd in Defensive Rush EPA/per play 1st in Defensive Rush Success Rate Browns defense pre-bye (2026 season) 10th in EPA/per play 8th in Defensive Success Rate 9th in Defensive Dropback EPA/per play 4th in Defensive Dropback success rate 26th in Defensive Rush EPA/per play 17th in Defensive Rush Success rate Overall, going from a top 5 defense to a top 10 is not that bad. One of the more surprising stats is how the team is still top 10 in pressures despite losing Garrett. It speaks volumes as to how talented their defensive line is. Players such as defensive end Isaiah McGuire and tackles Adin Huntington and Maliek Collins have contributed to the pressure. For all the talk about how versatile the Browns' defense has become under DC Mike Rutenberg, they still look downright special when they just lock up man-to-man and dare teams to beat them. — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) November 15, 2026 In terms of the play on the back end, the Browns play man coverage more than anyone in the league, and they are really good at it. Rookie safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has started to stand out, and it’s not long before he becomes a full-time starter because of how well he’s played. Defensive coverages weeks 1-10 via @FantasyPtsData pic.twitter.com/kHyr8wIvIn — Football Insights 📊 (@fball_insights) November 17, 2026 Slot corner was considered a weakness going into the season, but cornerback Myles Harden might have fixed it. Harden has shown his effectiveness on blitz packages, but his coverage is what stands out. Harden had a rough training camp, but he was able to bounce back and show his contributions at a high level. Teams will regularly throw in his direction, but that is a testament to Ward and Campbell more than anything else. What Needs to Improve? The run defense . It’s not a major concern, but the run defense has taken a step back from last season. As good as the Browns defensive line is, they lack someone big along the interior. Cleveland’s defensive line is small but quick in terms of their get-off, but against teams that run trap/wham run concepts, they are susceptible to giving up chunk yards. The tackling also needs to improve, but some of the tackling woes can be due to the team’s attacking style they play. In terms of who needs to improve from a player standpoint, it’s Jared Verse. Verse hasn’t had the season he’s wanted, but he has to find a way to convert pressures into sacks. Last Sunday against the Texans, Verse played one of his best games as a Brown, but it can only get better if he builds off that performance. Browns DE Jared Verse registered season-high marks in pressures (5) and pressure rate (17.9%) against the Texans. — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) November 16, 2026 It's no secret Jared Verse has had a disappointing season, but Sunday was arguably his best game of the season and as impressive as Tyson Campbell's interception was on this play, Verse made it happen. Gets around Aireontae Ersery and pressures Stroud into a rushed throw. If he… pic.twitter.com/7r91tBqlIK — 𝚂𝚙𝚎𝚗𝚌𝚎𝚛 𝙶𝚎𝚛𝚖𝚊𝚗 (@Spencito_) November 18, 2026 Grade Despite losing Garrett, the Browns defense is still a top 10 unit in the league. Rutenberg has been an upgrade over Schwartz. The team is still missing that alpha in the defensive end room, but overall, for a unit that many people thought would fall off, the fact that this unit has been top-10 has been a surprise, but not to those who pay close attention. title: Browns: Offense has opportunity to put up points after the bye
summary: The Cleveland Browns’ offense has been an adventure through the first 10 games of the 2026 NFL season. While the Browns are enjoying their bye week with a 6-4 record that has them currently occupying the final playoff position in the AFC, those six wins have been anything but easy. Thanks to a slow-starting offense […]
full_text: (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns’ offense has been an adventure through the first 10 games of the 2026 NFL season. While the Browns are enjoying their bye week with a 6-4 record that has them currently occupying the final playoff position in the AFC, those six wins have been anything but easy. Thanks to a slow-starting offense – the Browns are ranked No. 31 in first-quarter points with an average of 1.3 points per game – Cleveland has been forced to pull off fourth-quarter comebacks in all six of their wins. (And missed out on a seventh win because quarterback Deshaun Watson was out against New Orleans with a concussion.) While the Browns are bad in the first quarter, they turn into a different team in the fourth as they are averaging 7.4 fourth-quarter points per game, good for a respectable ranking of No. 12 in the league. And Watson’s numbers mirror those figures as his Total EPA in the first quarter of games this season is -36.65, while it is 2.8 in the fourth quarter. Put everything together, and the Browns are averaging 18.8 points per game, just a shade under the 20.4 points per game they averaged over the past six seasons. They also have a point differential of minus-32, making Cleveland the only team with a winning record and a negative point differential. That is not exactly surprising, as the Browns have played eight games decided by five points or less mixed in with two blowout losses. But if they want to stay in the playoff race over the final weeks of the season, they will likely need to start scoring a bit more. The good news is the final seven games present a group of teams – outside of the Cincinnati Bengals and New York Giants – who are giving up a lot of points. Let’s run through the teams the Browns will be facing to see where they currently rank in points allowed per game: Week 12 vs. Las Vegas: 21.4 points per game, ranked No. 31 Week 13 & 18 vs. Cincinnati: 21.4 points per game, ranked No. 10 Week 14 vs. Atlanta: 25.8 points per game, ranked No. 23 Week 15 vs. New York Giants: 21.8 points per game, ranked No. 11 (tied) Week 16 vs. Baltimore: 25.9 points per game, ranked No. 24 Week 17 vs. Indianapolis: 27.1 points per game, ranked No. 29 The Browns have struggled to score points all season, and while that makes for exciting games, it does not exactly instill confidence in the offense. But with some weaker defenses coming on the schedule, Cleveland’s offense has an opportunity to find its groove and help keep the team’s playoff hopes alive. title: Week 11 Browns NFL Power Rankings: A new season-high for Cleveland
summary: It is Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Cleveland Browns are feeling great with a record of 6-4 and currently on their bye week. Overall, the Browns went up by 3.0 spots from week-to-week to have an overall ranking of 13.7. The Browns are feeling good right now, and this is their […]
full_text: (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Cleveland Browns are feeling great with a record of 6-4 and currently on their bye week. Overall, the Browns went up by 3.0 spots from week-to-week to have an overall ranking of 13.7 . The Browns are feeling good right now, and this is their highest ranking of the season as they enter the bye. Let’s hope they come out strong out of the bye, as they’ll be featured on Sunday Night Football. Here is a summary of how the Cleveland Browns are viewed across mainstream media outlets in NFL Power Rankings heading into Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season. CBS Sports – No. 14 (up 3 spots) If the playoffs started today, they would be in the postseason. Can you believe it? Deshaun Watson is playing good football. ESPN – No. 14 (up 2 spots) Non-QB MVP at midseason: CB Denzel Ward The Browns’ defense hasn’t taken a big step back without two-time Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett or former coordinator Jim Schwartz, and Ward is a big reason. Cleveland is still playing the highest rate of man coverage in the NFL, and Ward’s ability to shut down half the field gives coordinator Mike Rutenberg the confidence to use that man-heavy approach. Ward leads the Browns with three interceptions and is allowing 3.8 yards per target, the third fewest among corners with at least 30 targets, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. NFL.com – No. 12 (up 7 spots) I’m admittedly a skeptic when it comes to these Browns, but Sunday started to change my tune. Cleveland got walloped in the mouth by the Texans early and had every reason to fold, yet the Browns did the opposite, regrouping defensively and punching back offensively to overcome the deficit and close with yet another game-winning touchdown drive late in the fourth quarter. Their shift toward playing aggressive, sticky coverage and a sudden jump in athleticism and mobility from Deshaun Watson (I know, I can’t believe I’m writing this, either) have made me think this team might actually be able to keep this strange run of success going. Sporting News – No. 14 (up 2 spots) Deshaun Watson is up to delivering all six Browns wins with fourth-quarter comebacks and game-winning drives and the latest came against his former team, the Texans. The numbers still aren’t pretty, but Watson is locked into the bottom line for Todd Monken. Yahoo Sports – No. 14 (up 4 spots) One developing story is what to do with Deshaun Watson. Those who log quarterback wins will say he is 6-3 this season. That’s misguided, but many people follow that logic. Watson is 20th in adjusted EPA per play and he has a middling 89.1 passer rating. That’s 20th among quarterbacks with at least 100 attempts. The Browns have had some fun comeback wins and it will be interesting to see if Cleveland overreacts to that and extends Watson, whose contract has been one of the worst in the NFL. Certainly, the Browns would rather not have to come back and win every game, as they’ve been doing. “I wish collectively him and I together would play better early and coach better early and we didn’t have to get to this,” Browns head coach Todd Monken said, via the team’s transcripts. “And it’s not just been them. It’s been our team, last week the same way.” Bleacher Report – No. 14 (up 2 spots) The resiliency now found within the Cleveland Browns roster is something to behold. After decades in which Cleveland found creative ways to lose on a near-weekly basis, the current roster features exciting young talent seemingly unburdened by the franchise’s struggles. Obviously, there’s a reason why the saying “The Browns is the Browns” exists. Now, Cleveland is finding ways to win even when the odds are stacked against the team. For example, the Houston Texans led 17-0 at halftime. Once again, the Browns defense made life difficult on its opponent and provided an opportunity for the Deshaun Watson-led offense to chip away at the deficit before making big plays down the stretch. The 1980 Browns were known as the Kardiac Kids. Forty-six years later, Cleveland is recapturing the magic that was once seen just off the shore of Lake Erie. USA Today – No. 14 (up 1 spot) Their average margin of victory − 3.2 points. Their average margin of defeat − 12.8 points. But that’s playoff-caliber in the world of the 14-team postseason field. Little did anyone know that the Browns rookies would be a part of a season that has started out special with a 6-4 record heading into their bye week. Much of the […]
full_text: Prior to the 2026 NFL season, almost everyone believed that the Cleveland Browns hit another home run with their 2026 NFL draft class . Little did anyone know that the Browns rookies would be a part of a season that has started out special with a 6-4 record heading into their bye week . Much of the excitement has been around WRs KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston , for good reason, but safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren , OT Spencer Fano, and guard Austin Barber have also had very good seasons to help Cleveland’s record. In many ways, the rookie class is meeting or exceeding expectations , which is pretty impressive given what many thought before the year. That includes PFF grades , with McNeil Warren topping the list of Browns rookies and second overall, with an 86.7 grade: Like Wheatley, McNeil-Warren played a career-high snap count in the Browns’ most recent game, seeing 67 plays in the win over the Houston Texans . It was a game that saw him finish with a 77.6 PFF grade that was the second-highest of his career, and best in a game where he has played more than 30 snaps. On the season, McNeil-Warren has recorded eight tackles resulting in a defensive stop, and all eight have come over the past five games. Fano is next on the list, seventh overall, with Barber noted as the next highest-graded offensive lineman, but outside the Top 15. Concepcion didn’t make the Top 15, but Boston was graded 12th among rookies at 69: After setting a career high with 98 receiving yards in Week 9, Boston was targeted just once from 42 snaps as a receiver in the Browns’ win over the Houston Texans on Sunday. He still leads all rookie receivers with 523 yards but has been held below 1.00 yards per route run in four of his past five games. What surprises you most about this Browns draft class? title: Cowboys vs Titans: 3 causes for concern in Week 11
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are back in action Sunday afternoon, hosting their second of three straight home games as they welcome the Tennessee Titans to town. While the Titans enter the matchup with a 1-8 record, nothing the Cowboys have shown this season suggests this will be an easy game. With that thought in mind, here […]
full_text: Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are back in action Sunday afternoon, hosting their second of three straight home games as they welcome the Tennessee Titans to town. While the Titans enter the matchup with a 1-8 record, nothing the Cowboys have shown this season suggests this will be an easy game. With that thought in mind, here are three causes for concern in Sunday’s matchup. 1) Cam Ward Flashing His Potential Former number one overall pick Cam Ward’s NFL career has not gotten off to the best start. Ward showed some flashes during his rookie year but struggled with consistency. Playing behind arguably the league’s worst offensive line, Ward was sacked a league-high 55 times during his first season. Despite some of the struggles he endured last season, expectations were high for the Miami product entering year two. Most of Ward’s second year in the league hasn’t been much better than his first. This season, the 24-year-old has thrown just eight touchdown passes in nine games to go with a disappointing 53.3 QBR. While Ward and the Titans as a whole have not had an ideal season, to say the least, the past two weeks have been much better on the offensive side of the ball. Tennessee’s signal-caller has been the main reason why, as the talented young quarterback has played arguably his best two games of the year in back-to-back weeks. Over the course of the last two weeks, Ward is second in the NFL in completion percentage (70.9) to go with four touchdown passes and a very impressive 98.9 Passer Rating. While the Titans have not won either of these contests, their offense has not been the reason why, as they have recorded 325 or more yards in each matchup. With Ward playing as well as we’ve seen him since he entered the league, the Cowboys need to be on high alert and not let the young quarterback get into a rhythm on Sunday afternoon. 2) Titans’ Defense Takeaway Surge Like the Cowboys, the Titans have been one of the worst defenses in football this season. Tennessee has given up the sixth-most points (239) in the league, allowing at least 26 points in four of their last five matchups. While the Titans have not done much well on defense this season, since Week 6 they have been one of the better defenses in the league at taking the football away from their opponent. Tennessee’s defense has 10 takeaways in their last four matchups, including two or more in three straight games from Week 6 through Week 8. The one win the Titans recorded this season came in Week 6 when they recorded three takeaways in a 26-20 win over the Indianapolis Colts. One positive for Dallas is that four of those 10 takeaways came via safety Amani Hooker. The 28-year-old, who was without a doubt the top takeaway threat on the Titans’ defense, was traded to the Buffalo Bills before the trade deadline two weeks ago. Taking care of the football is going to be paramount for the Cowboys on Sunday. The Titans have plenty of defensive weaknesses they should be able to exploit, but if they don’t protect the ball, Tennessee could make it a long day for Dallas’ offense. 3) Internal Defensive Chaos As is usually the case, there is a bit of chaos surrounding the Cowboys. Earlier this week, Dallas made the decision to take play-calling duties away from first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker, giving the job to 60-year-old Mike Pettine. With how bad Dallas’ defense has been, giving play-calling duties to Pettine, the veteran coach was brought in a few weeks back to be a defensive consultant; this should not come as a surprise, but the decision has stirred up some internal drama. Parker himself admitted he contemplated leaving the organization altogether after the decision was made, while Dallas’ star defender Quinnen Williams refused to answer questions on the matter this week. It’s been quite the week in Dallas, and the Cowboys’ issues on defense seem to be extending off the field as well. It will be very interesting to see if the events of this week have any impact on the field this weekend.

title: Cowboys vs. Titans: Matchups to watch in Week 11
summary: This Week 11 matchup between the Dallas Cowboys (4-6) and the Tennessee Titans (1-8) is an interesting one. Both teams have struggled this season. The Cowboys are still somehow in playoff contention thanks to a suspect NFC East, while the Titans currently hold the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. The Cowboys […]
full_text: Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images | Getty Images This Week 11 matchup between the Dallas Cowboys (4-6) and the Tennessee Titans (1-8) is an interesting one. Both teams have struggled this season. The Cowboys are still somehow in playoff contention thanks to a suspect NFC East, while the Titans currently hold the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. The Cowboys are clearly the more talented team, but you wouldn’t know it by the way they’ve continued to disappoint at nearly every turn thus far this season. Because of that you can’t quite count out the Titans pulling off the upset. The best way for the Cowboys to secure another “W” just to win certain matchups, which we’ve listed below. Cowboys’ defense vs. Titans RB Tony Pollard Christian McCaffrey absolutely shredded the Cowboys defense last week and you can bet Tony Pollard is hoping to do the same against his former team both on the ground and through the air. He’s currently on a hot streak over the last three games averaging 130 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns per game. On the ground he’s averaging 93 rushing yards per game and 4.8 yards per carry. Considering the Cowboys are allowing 154.1 rushing yards per game and 5.2 yards per carry, there’s a good chance Pollard’s hot streak continues. DT Quinnen Williams vs. Titans OL If there is someone playing better than Quinnen Williams is over the past month or so, it’s by a slim margin. No. 92 has been a one-man wrecking crew on what is arguably the worst defense in the entire league. He’s playing like the All-Pro he is, and is the one bright spot for the Cowboys putrid defense thus far this season. He should once again wreak havoc against the Titans interior offensive line in Week 11. We fully expect him to make some game-changing plays as both the run and pass defender, possibly adding a couple more QB sacks to his total. Cowboys’ aerial attack vs. Titans secondary This is one of those strength versus weakness matchups that should heavily favor the Cowboys. Allowing 266.9 passing yards per game, the Titans defense currently ranks dead last in the category. On the flipside, the Cowboys are averaging 265.5 passing yards per game, which currently ranks third overall in the NFL. With CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens both capable of dropping in 100+ yard receiving game at any moment, and with Ryan Flournoy coming up clutch lately, the Dak Prescott led aerial attack should feast this week.

title: Cowboys offensive line versus the Titans defensive line
summary: The Dallas Cowboys will be back in action on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans. They need to win in the trenches on offense to carry the day, as they can’t rely on the struggling defense. Here’s how it looks. Trench Dashboard Here are the Cowboys offensive line metrics for the 2026 season so far.  Pass […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys will be back in action on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans. They need to win in the trenches on offense to carry the day, as they can’t rely on the struggling defense. Here’s how it looks. Trench Dashboard Here are the Cowboys offensive line metrics for the 2026 season so far. Pass Block Win Rate – 55% (8th) Run Block Win Rate – 71% (27th) Pressure rate allowed – 33% (18th) Sacks allowed – 15 (5th) Last three-week trend: Steady protection, not elite The Pressure Point Every opponent will look at the Cowboys offensive line and ask, where can we break it? Here’s what to watch for. PRESSURE POINT: Jacob Martin has become Tennessee’s main problem off the edge The Titans no longer have Jeffery Simmons after they traded the four-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle to Chicago at the end of October. The player Dallas now has to locate is Jacob Martin. Martin leads Tennessee with 7.5 sacks and has 31 total pressures, 17th among qualifying edge defenders. He added another sack and three quarterback pressures against Jacksonville last week. That is impressive production for a Titans defense that has only 21 sacks as a team. Martin wins largely with speed. At 242 pounds, he wants to get an offensive tackle moving backwards and then attack the quarterback before the blocker can establish his position. Dallas handled a much more intimidating group of individual pass rushers against San Francisco, so there is no reason to panic. But Martin cannot be the player who turns a favorable matchup into a difficult afternoon. PRESSURE POINT: How quickly does T.J. Bass settle in? This is probably Tennessee’s first place to attack. Tyler Booker had become one of the Cowboys’ most reliable offensive linemen. Before the 49ers game, his pressure rate allowed was just 4.6%, fifth-lowest among NFL right guards, now due to a high ankle sprain, T.J. Bass steps into his position. Bass has already started this season when Tyler Smith was injured, so Dallas is not putting an inexperienced player onto the field. Schottenheimer specifically praised his versatility after Booker went down, but Tennessee should test him immediately. John Franklin-Myers is the Titans’ best remaining interior defensive lineman and led their defensive front with three pressures against Jacksonville. Expect Tennessee to move Franklin-Myers around and see whether it can create confusion between Bass, Cooper Beebe and Steele. WHERE TO ATTACK Every defensive line has a weakness, here are the Titans soft spots and where the Cowboys offensive line should attack. GREEN LIGHT: Run directly at Jacob Martin Martin is Tennessee’s best pass-rush threat, so make him do something else and take him out the game. PFF gives Martin a 47.1 run-defense grade, ranking 105th among 111 qualifying edge defenders.That creates an obvious opportunity. Whenever Martin is on the field, Dallas should make him defend Javonte Williams rather than allowing him to simply chase Dak Prescott. If Martin has spent two quarters fighting through run blocks, he cannot attack every passing snap with the same freedom. The best way of slowing down Tennessee’s leading pass rusher might be making him tackle Williams. GREEN LIGHT: Trust five-man protection The Titans do not rely heavily on blitzing. As it stands, Tennessee’s blitz rate sits at 26%, that places them among the least aggressive blitzing teams in football and that means Dallas should see plenty of four-man rushes. The offense should therefore trust the offensive line and not leave an extra blocker beside the tackles unless Martin begins consistently winning. If Guyton, Smith, Beebe, Bass and Steele can handle Tennessee’s four rushers, Dallas can put more receivers into routes. That should be particularly valuable against a Titans defense allowing 267 passing yards per game, worst in the NFL. THE CHAOS REPORT Here’s the Tennessee Titans defensive trends for this season at the defensive line. Sack Total – 21 (21st) Pass Rush Win Rate – 43% (28th) Run Stop Win Rate – 30% (11th) QB Pressure Rate – 22% (30th) Last three-week trend: Front is struggling Matchup of the week T.J. Bass vs. John Franklin-Myers Tyler Booker’s injury makes this the matchup to watch. Bass enters the starting lineup at right guard and immediately faces Tennessee’s most dependable interior defensive lineman. Franklin-Myers can line up in several positions across the front, but expect Robert Saleh to find opportunities to place him across from Bass. Best Route to Success The Titans run defense has allowed 137 yards per game over the last four weeks, their most productive pass rusher is one of PFF’s lowest-graded edge defenders against the run. Dallas should know exactly what to do, run Javonte Williams like a madman. Use play-action after the linebackers start creeping toward the line, then trust the offensive line when Tennessee rushes four. San Francisco presented Dallas with one of the most talented defensive fronts in football and Prescott still went down only once on more than 50 pass attempts. Tennessee should be a much easier challenge. Injury Updates: Tyler Booker suffered a high ankle sprain against San Francisco and is expected to miss time. John Franklin-Myers played last week after dealing with a back issue and had been a full participant in practice before the Jacksonville game. Other than that their defensive line has no new injuries, their issues, however, show up a lot in their linebacker corps. So keep watch on that this week in practice reports.

title: The Cowboys handled the Christian Parker situation poorly
summary: Its been a frustrating season for the Dallas Cowboys as they sit at 4-6. More specifically, after years of bad defenses, the hope was that things would turn around in 2026, but they haven’t. Under defensive coordinator Christian Parker in his first season in the role, the Cowboys are just as bad, if not worse, […]
full_text: Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images | Getty Images Its been a frustrating season for the Dallas Cowboys as they sit at 4-6. More specifically, after years of bad defenses, the hope was that things would turn around in 2026, but they haven’t. Under defensive coordinator Christian Parker in his first season in the role, the Cowboys are just as bad, if not worse, than they were defensively under Matt Eberflus in 2025, which was the worst defense in team history. There’s no doubt that something had to change in order for the Cowboys’ defense to improve, and team owner Jerry Jones and head coach Brian Schottenheimer mentioned on Monday that conversions were being had in that regard. Dallas made a decision on Wednesday that sent shock waves through their fan base and around the NFL. They took away play-calling duties from Parker , and now senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine will call the plays. Pettine brings a ton of experience as his career in the league started back in 2002 with the Baltimore Ravens. He’s been a defensive coordinator for the New York Jets, Buffalo Bills, and the Green Bay Packers. He had success with all three in that role, especially with the Jets when he had four consecutive top 10 defenses. This makes the possibility of this move working out favorable, but there are things about it that raise eyebrows. Parker was given his first job in the NFL by Pettine in 2019 with the Packers as a defensive quality control coach. It made sense that Parker reached out to Pettine in the spring about a consultant role (which he declined), and once again in the fall when it was clear that the Cowboys’ defense wasn’t performing the way that everyone had hoped. The Cowboys then brought him in to assist Parker, and while that’s understandable, it also kind of pulled the rug from under him as a first time play-caller. The Cowboys have now played 10 games, and already Parker, who again is calling plays for the first time, has now essentially been demoted. What makes it worse is that Dallas is still letting him keep the defensive coordinator title, but Pettine is now the man that will make all the calls on game day. Keeping that title on him but taking away a huge part of his responsibility is humiliating. Parker has support from his players like rookie safety Caleb Downs and veteran defensive tackle Kenny Clark. While that’s good, the fact that Dallas is making Parker face these men everyday while knowing how he’s been embarrassed is just bad business. Also, who do the players report to now? Parker or Pettine? The organization would have been better off just firing Parker and going their separate ways. Nobody is saying that this is the case, but stripping Parker of play-calling duties and giving them to Pettine after a month makes it seem like the move to bring him in wasn’t to help, but rather take his job. The Cowboys praised the hiring of Parker all offseason long, yet they only gave him two months before publicly shaming him in a sense. This is his first time doing this, and it was always going to be a process, but the Cowboys didn’t give him the necessary time to grow into the role. Going back to Eberflus, his unit was atrocious last year. Again, it was the worst in Cowboys’ history up until this season. However, he was never stripped of his duties to call plays, so why do that to Parker? Especially when it’s his first time as a defensive coordinator and play caller. This is just a bad look for the organization starting with the aforementioned Jones, but also Schottenheimer. As bad as the defense has been, Dallas has struggled to consistently be good offensively as well despite being ranked highly in certain categories. The case can be made that the Cowboys would have won games against the Baltimore Ravens and Arizona Cardinals had the play calling on offense been better situationally, which falls on Schottenheimer since he calls the plays. So, why hasn’t he relinquished his duties as a play caller? Or better yet, why hasn’t there been conversations about it like with Parker? Schottenheimer is the one that brought Parker in. If he doesn’t feel like Parker can do his job, which is pretty much what he’s saying by taking away play-calling duties, then just fire him. This is just bad business on his part, and it also looks that way on Jones and the organization for allowing it. The bottom line is, the while situation is a terrible look for the Cowboys, and it speaks volumes as to why they’ve been a laughing stock around the league for quite some time.
