title: Cowboys point/counterpoint: Setting goals for the rest of the season
summary: While the Dallas Cowboys are far from eliminated as the potential winner of the NFC East, it really doesn’t feel like they have much of a chance. They are 4-6 with seven games to go. To eventually win the East, they would have to really change the direction they have been heading. So what do […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images While the Dallas Cowboys are far from eliminated as the potential winner of the NFC East, it really doesn’t feel like they have much of a chance. They are 4-6 with seven games to go. To eventually win the East, they would have to really change the direction they have been heading. So what do they face now? And what do they need to accomplish so we no longer feel like this season is just circling the drain? Our Tom Ryle and Sean Martin offer their ideas. Tom – Well, the obvious thing is that they need to win games, but that is the obvious goal each and every time the team takes the field. Clearly, a loss to the 1-8 Titans would be a horrible sign. It is hardly beyond the realm of possibility, sadly. To me, this is about more than simply getting a W against a hapless team. They have to look in control and capable of playing a strong game from start to finish. But then comes a much more important goal: They need to string wins together. And their next game against the badly depleted Philadelphia Eagles is arguably the last really favorable chance for that this year. This is important. Under Brian Schottenheimer this year, the Cowboys have yet to accomplish back to back wins. There just seems to be a true lack of confidence on the team. Putting two together could go a long way to creating some. And if we are going to keep talking about getting to the playoffs as the NFCE representative, it would also get them to .500 and keep them in striking range of the current division leading New York Giants. Then we can see what they can do against some stiffer competition down the stretch. Sean – The Titans have certainly been in a lot of games this season, Tony Pollard has had some monstrous games out of the backfield, and will have to love what he saw from his former team’s defense against Christian McCaffrey, and they have yet another defensive minded head coach to scheme against Schottenheimer and try to have the upper hand. Plus, the Cowboys have played two other games against the AFC South, narrowly escaping with a win at the Houston Texans, and beating the Colts in a fashion that set us up for exactly what we saw in the latest loss. So yes Tom, getting out of this game with a win is a solid enough goal, and one might even go as far as saying controlling it for four quarters like we’d want to see is a sign of progress to play the first complete game of the season. But, it’s not a win against a conference opponent not in the NFC East , something Schotty is still searching for. How do you have any playoff viability if you can’t beat anyone good in your own conference? It’s not in any way a win against a quality opponent, and it has absolutely just as much of a chance to be forgotten about as every other win this season against those Texans, Colts, Commanders, and Eagles. The Cowboys are playing so poorly they have a chance to sweep the Eagles for the first time since 2021, winning their second game of the week next week in order to do so, and still have it all be a footnote. I guess if you want to circle back on one of these wins with the context we now have through ten weeks, beating a Commanders team that went on to beat the Giants team the Cowboys are still chasing at home is a decent result. But nobody will forget that Jayden Daniels was knocked out of the game, and nobody is getting away with moving the goalposts a country mile for this season along with that. From potential playoff contenders to happy to be in the mix with the… 5-3-1 Giants? I’m not buying it, and oh by the way the most glaring and obvious thing the Giants do better than the Cowboys to start having instant success is coach better under their new leadership. Tom – Maybe that’s another way to look at things. The Cowboys need to prove they can show they are a viable NFL franchise, one that can play a full sixty minutes and close out games. Those elements have been lacking all season, even in some of their wins. The team is so up and down, even from play to play. They will have a strong defensive stop on one play, maybe a sack or a run stuff, then give up a big gainer – usually, it seems, on third and long. And the offense is not exempt. They will have several good plays, then a couple of dropped passes or a breakdown in the blocking scheme, and Bryan Anger or Brandon Aurbrey will have to come out. And if things weren’t bad enough, Aubrey is showing signs of having the yips, missing kicks we used to take for granted. And that’s one other way to consider it. This team just does not have one thing it can consistently hang its hat on. Even Dak Prescott will have several bad reps in a row and things will stall. There isn’t one fatal flaw on this team. There are a collection of things that are making it so hard to keep up with their competition. I don’t know how they can start to heal these wounds, but it would certainly be nice to see at least one thing get cleared up. That just might be the real goal for them. Oddly, the news of Christian Parker being forced to surrender play-calling duties to Mike Pettine is, for me, encouraging. At least it shows the owner sees the problem and is willing to do something. (Yeah, I don’t think this was Schotty’s call.) Sean – For fans with one eye toward the offseason already, the only good news about what you said is that the team is putting themselves in a position where getting help for any position group in the offseason would be seen as a good move. The bad news is we know how this always goes. The Cowboys will have to prioritize one thing or the other, meaning they sell us on already being stable at some other position to do this, and then that very thing holds them back on gamedays. Dak Prescott starting a streak with this Titans game of not only playing well but winning would be great, but by season’s end if they still aren’t a playoff team, we’ll have to do it all over again in year 12 for Dak and hope for a third straight year of good health from him. The defense needs an answer for how not to waste Quinnen Williams and Joey Porter Jr. right now, but nobody has those answers. I do also like the idea of Pettine having more overall control now, to run this defense through the front seven where the denser nucleus of talent has shown itself. Not just Williams playing like a game wrecker, but Shemar James and even Caleb Downs as a box player too. This is almost surely more stable ground to build something around than Christian Parker’s preferred position groups, cornerback and safety, where the injuries have been rampant for years. Still, I can’t recall a time where both the present and the future feels so shaky for the Cowboys, or trust in the leadership that can get an organization through shaky times is so low. After all, Pettine has only been here since October, and now he’s calling plays? I don’t know if we’re even grasping how much of a structural failure it takes to get to that point in any season. Maybe they’ll still win the NFC East and find the faintest something to hang their hat on? Who knows. One thing I do know is that it’s Brawl of the Wild week as Montana State hosts Montana in one of the best rivalries in college football, and I can’t wait for that! Here’s hoping it’s not just a fun Saturday but a successful Sunday for our Cowboys as well, Tom. Thanks for chatting.
author: Sean Martin

title: Christian Parker considered leaving the Dallas Cowboys
summary: Thursday had to be difficult for Christian Parker. The Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator, the one who no longer calls defensive plays as of Wednesday, took to the podium for his standard weekly press conference. Obviously the issue of this week and the adjustments made in it came up. First things first, Parker stated the obvious […]
full_text: Tom Fox/The Dallas Morning News via Getty Images Thursday had to be difficult for Christian Parker. The Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator, the one who no longer calls defensive plays as of Wednesday, took to the podium for his standard weekly press conference. Obviously the issue of this week and the adjustments made in it came up. First things first, Parker stated the obvious in that this is not an ideal outcome for him. Cowboys DC Christian Parker said he did push back to Brian Schottenheimer when he was informed of the decision to strip him of play-calling. Obviously, the decision was still made. “Not an ideal situation for me, personally.” — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) November 19, 2026 It goes without saying that this is the case. In many ways what Parker is experiencing is a demotion. It suggests that his future at his job is one that is very much in doubt. That would make anyone feel uncomfortable. Regarding Parker’s future, the Cowboys have been pushing a bit of an idea that he could wind up along the lines of someone like Sean Payton. The Denver Broncos head coach is, as are others, a success story told of someone getting play-calling duties taken away early in their career and going on to find success. Why couldn’t that be Parker? It might be, but it is hard to see how that can be the case for him with this team specifically. What’s more is that judging by his comments Parker doesn’t exactly sound like someone who is strongly consider a future possibility in Dallas anyway. Christian Parker when asked if he sees a future here as the defensive coordinator in Dallas: “cross that bridge when we get there.” #DallasCowboys pic.twitter.com/nRGx6lKBzS — Jeff Kolb (@JeffKolbFOX4) November 19, 2026 Perhaps Parker will leave the Cowboys after this season. That bridge truly will be crossed at that time as he noted. But according to Parker he considered taking it on immediately. He noted that he thought about leaving the team as a result of this decision. Christian Parker said he considered not remaining with the Cowboys, but, “in my opinion that would have been running from it.” Called a “significant,” personal disappointment and said the new arrangement is “only awkward if you make it that way.” — Todd Archer (@toddarcher) November 19, 2026 This is just this author’s opinion, but I can’t see how Parker would consider leaving the Cowboys at large, publicly confess to it on top of that, and do so if he did not believe his future with the team was already sealed, in that he won’t be a part of the team’s future. The other point in all of this is why does Parker have to speak? He is obviously the defensive coordinator in title. The Cowboys are pushing that he is still very important. But who needed this? The argument to that is, fairly in my opinion, that Parker should be afforded an opportunity to tell his side of the story. Maybe that’s what this was. Assuming that’s the case then there is no need for him to speak next week on behalf of what Mike Pettine is or isn’t doing. But the Cowboys are the Cowboys so we will see.
author: RJ Ochoa

title: No Bull Perspective: The Importance of Riley Moss
summary: I’m honestly surprised at how many comments I’ve seen since Riley Moss’ extension that are casting shade on Moss, the extension, or Moss’ play. I think the biggest obstacle to understanding this extension and player comes from how hard it is to understand the role of cornerbacks in the NFL. So let’s start there. Cornerback […]
full_text: I’m honestly surprised at how many comments I’ve seen since Riley Moss’ extension that are casting shade on Moss, the extension, or Moss’ play. I think the biggest obstacle to understanding this extension and player comes from how hard it is to understand the role of cornerbacks in the NFL. So let’s start there. Cornerback differences There is a lot of variance you can have in the cornerback position. Are they boundary corners or nickel corners? Do they play man-to-man or zone primarily? Are they better playing off or press? Each of these things is a big deal in how a player fits in an NFL defense. I’m not going to break down each nuance, but let’s talk about what Riley Moss is from this set of questions. Moss is a boundary corner. He plays on the outside of the defensive backfield, typically either manned up on a receiver or dropping into a deep zone if the call is cover-3 or quarters. Moss excels at playing man-to-man coverage. He has no problems handling zone coverage when asked to, though. Moss can use either technique, but is excellent at press man. This last piece is what makes him so important to the defense that Vance Joseph calls. Why Moss helps make the defense hum It isn’t just that Riley Moss is a better-quality player than Kris Abrams-Drane or Jahdae Barron. It is that he has no limitations on the outside. Joseph can do anything he wants with his defense when he has All-Pro Patrick Surtain II on one side and Riley Moss on the other. Joseph can call cover-0 (requiring man coverage across the table while he blitzes from wherever he wants). He can run their typical match zone coverages. He can give safety help to a tough tight end assignment that Ja’Quan McMillian or another defensive back has. He can ask Moss to fall back into cover-3 and know Riley will handle that side of the field deep with no issues. Defensive limitations If you look back over the last game against Carolina, the pass defense looked pretty suspect. Moss could only play 17 snaps into the game, leaving with an injury in the middle of the 2nd quarter. Kris Abrams-Drane was out as well. That left Barron filling in with two depth safeties on the back end as well. It’s hard to tell given the television angles, but the Broncos’ defense after Moss left was VERY different than what we’re used to seeing on the field. They ran a lot of zone coverages throughout the game (wisely). There were too many players on the field who do not have the skill sets to play the normal aggressive press and match coverages that Joseph likes to mix in. Heck, one of the big plays happened in the deep right zone that Surtain had and he was a solid step late getting there. Just having Moss out there at least would have let them man the outside and let the safeties support the middle of the field. Final Thoughts This team is so blessed to have the three starting cornerbacks they have today. This is the most stacked the team has been at corner since the No Fly Zone. Riley Moss is a huge part of how the defense can play aggressive mix-and-match schemes to keep offenses guessing. The flexibility we have in coverage is what has made this defense hum in the past couple of years, and it is going to be the key to how successful it is in the back half of the season. Congratulations, Riley. You hopefully don’t pay much attention to the peanut gallery, but know that there are many of us out here who appreciate what you mean to this defense and locker room.
author: sadaraine

title: Broncos vs Raiders 5 questions: How is Raider Nation feeling about Fernando Mendoza?
summary: The Fernando Mendoza era is officially underway in Las Vegas. The rookie quarterback made his first career NFL start for the Las Vegas Raiders against the Seattle Seahawks. Now he gets a taste of the historic rivalry against the Denver Broncos this Sunday. For the first time in close to two decades, it appears that […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 15: Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders looks to pass against the Seattle Seahawks in the second quarter at Allegiant Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Seahawks defeated the Raiders 21-13. (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Fernando Mendoza era is officially underway in Las Vegas. The rookie quarterback made his first career NFL start for the Las Vegas Raiders against the Seattle Seahawks. Now he gets a taste of the historic rivalry against the Denver Broncos this Sunday. For the first time in close to two decades, it appears that there is legitimate excitement over the future of the Raiders. But is that really the case? To get some answers, we go “behind enemy lines” with Matt Holder from Silver and Black Pride . MHR: After a great start to the season, why have the Raiders dropped off in the last month? What is the thinking on the season, is there playoff discussion? Matt : Ultimately, Las Vegas’ 3-0 start proved to be fool’s gold. The Raiders were expected to beat the Dolphins, but no one really saw the Chargers being as bad as they are, and the Saints have been a big disappointment this year. Those three teams have a combined record of 5-22 and are currently slated to pick second, third, and 11th in the draft, according to Tankathon . The only real tangible difference between the start of the season and the last month is that the defense was doing a better job of creating turnovers, with nine turnovers in the first three weeks and seven in the last seven. For good measure, the one win in the last seven weeks was against the 2-8 Jets, who hold the fourth pick in the draft. That being said, Vegas is a team that had the No. 1 pick last April, an “award” for finishing in last place. So, the Raiders are making progress by separating themselves from the bottom of the league, and this was always supposed to be year one of a two-year rebuild. Technically, they’re still in the Wild Card hunt, but they aren’t a legitimate postseason contender until they can beat another team in that category. MHR: How are fans feeling about the start of the Fernando Mendoza era in Las Vegas? What was there to like about his first game? What needs to be seen against Denver? Matt : Raider Nation is pretty excited to see what Mendoza can do for the rest of the year. A lot of people were sad to see Kirk Cousins go because he certainly gave the Raiders a better chance to win than a rookie quarterback, given how well Cousins has been playing this year. However, the rest of the team just wasn’t ready to compete for a playoff spot, so it was time to pivot to the long-term plan and give Mendoza reps. The No. 1 pick did a good job of protecting the football, using his athleticism to scramble or run the ball, and was good at getting through his reads to find his checkdowns last week. A lot of that may seem trivial, but going up against the Seahawks’ defense with mad scientist Mike Macdonald calling the plays is probably the worst draw a rookie quarterback can have in his first start. Moving forward, I’d like to see Mendoza be more aggressive pushing the ball down the field — he missed a few opportunities last week — and show a better feel for pressure. The latter was the biggest issue last week, as he took six sacks, and that will be a point of emphasis against the Broncos’ pass rush this Sunday. If anyone is interested/curious, I wrote an article breaking down a few plays that I felt told the story of Mendoza’s starting debut, good and bad. MHR: Where are fans on the excitement level for the franchise right now? Is there hope for the team’s future and direction? Matt : Losing six of the last seven games has definitely put a damper on the mood within the fanbase. A big part of people’s frustration is that a lot of general manager John Spytek’s draft picks and free-agent signings aren’t yielding high returns on the organization’s investments right now. However, we’ve only seen one game from this past year’s top pick, and there are a few offseason additions who are making an impact, like safety Treydan Stukes, linebacker Nakobe Dean, and guard Trey Zuhn III, to name a few. So, there’s definitely a good amount of optimism surrounding the future of the Raiders, but how much definitely depends on who you ask. MHR: What do the Raiders need to do defensively and offensively to get a win? Matt : Defensively, they have to get pressure from someone other than Maxx Crosby. Bo Nix has been one of the worst quarterbacks in the NFL under pressure this season, but the Raiders don’t have a respectable pass rusher outside of Crosby. That’s led to opponents sliding the protection to him and/or double teaming/chip blocking him throughout the game, essentially forcing someone else to beat them. No. 2 edge rusher Malcolm Koonce was answering the call in the first five games of the year, but that was primarily against backup-quality tackles. The competition level rose over the last five weeks, and Koonce’s numbers have gone way down. And don’t even ask me about the defensive tackles; they’re terrible. Offensively, it goes back to what I brought up a couple of questions ago: protect Mendoza. I’ve given up on the offense’s ability to run the ball because the answers in that department will have to be solved in the offseason. Rookie quarterback or not, the Raiders are a passing offense. The problem is that Mendoza doesn’t have a good feel for pressure; that was one of his biggest weaknesses as a prospect. So, the offensive line has to be at their best to keep him upright, which, of course, is easier said than done with Nik Bonitto and Zach Allen on the other side of the trenches. MHR: How does this game unfold on Sunday? What is your prediction? Matt : As crazy as it sounds, I actually think Mendoza can have a decent game and take a step forward in Denver. He was good at making week-to-week adjustments in college, and as good as the Broncos’ defense is, they do rank 27th in yards allowed per game (355.0). Of course, Brock Bowers’ status is a big factor, and that’s up in the air at the time of writing, but I think the Raiders will be able to move the ball. However, I have zero confidence in the defense. They’ve been a total mess on that side of the ball, to the point where I can’t trust them enough to pull off a 9.5-point upset. However, I’m willing to take the points and say Vegas will cover: 31-24 Broncos.
author: Ian St. Clair

title: Why extending Riley Moss was a smart decision for the Denver Broncos
summary: The Denver Broncos continued their tradition of rewarding their homegrown talent. Yesterday, news broke that the Broncos had agreed to terms with fourth-year cornerback Riley Moss on a four-year contract worth $67 million. As of now, the guarantees have not been made available. However, the average annual value makes him the NFL’s 23rd highest paid […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - SEPTEMBER 20: Cornerback Riley Moss (21) of the Denver Broncos celebrates his interception of quarterback Trevor Lawrence (16) of the Jacksonville Jaguars during the second half a 20-13 win on Sunday, Sept. 20, 2026, at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colo. (Photo by Timothy Hurst/MediaNews Group/The Denver Post via Getty Images) | Denver Post via Getty Images The Denver Broncos continued their tradition of rewarding their homegrown talent. Yesterday, news broke that the Broncos had agreed to terms with fourth-year cornerback Riley Moss on a four-year contract worth $67 million. As of now, the guarantees have not been made available. However, the average annual value makes him the NFL’s 23rd highest paid corner. In my opinion, that’s quite the bargain. This summer, I asked Broncos Country who they felt deserved extension priority —Moss or Ja’Quan McMillian. I was under the impression that Denver would have to just choose one. It was a close battle, but Moss came ahead with 56-percent of the votes. Flash forward to recent memory and fans seemed to have changed their tune. A little over a month ago, Scotty Payne wrote an article and put a poll up on Mile High Report’s X account asking the same question. The result? McMillian in a landslide with 94-percent of the votes. Would I love for McMillian to come back too? Absolutely. He has been an underrated playmaker in their secondary and has a penchant for big plays in crunch time. It appears Denver will revisit negotiations after the season, but I have a feeling the Broncos’ standout nickelback may test the open market. Though I’d like to offer some thoughts on why extending Moss was a good decision. Vance Joseph needs that boundary corner opposite of Patrick Surtain II to hold his own in man coverage The Broncos’ defense under Vance Joseph is known for their aggressive man-to-man coverage assignments. This season due to injuries in the secondary, they have utilized more zone coverage than prior years. However, their man numbers are still higher compared to many teams in the NFL. In fact, I’d argue that Joseph would like to be running more man than he has this season. Every team uses a mixture of both, but the difference compared to past season is notable. With a healthy Moss and Surtain, I expect Denver’s man coverage numbers to go up quite significantly in the second half of the season. The main critique on Moss has been those pesky pass interference penalties. That’s fair. However, I’d just say it’s also a part of the process considering how often he is targeted and tasked with man-to-man assignments. Last year, Moss was targeted an astounding 118 times. However, he allowed just a 58-percent completion rate and had the most pass breakups of any corner in the league. This season, the targets have been significantly less. The former Iowa prospect has been thrown at only 35 times. Through eight games, Moss has allowed 18 receptions for 223 yards. That’s only a 51.4 completion percentage allowed—certainly one of the best marks in the NFL for any defensive back. Even with those penalties, he has proven to be a great player for Denver. If Ja’Quan McMillian moves on, they already have an in-house replacement Only time will tell if the Broncos can come to terms with McMillian too. As I wrote in my article this summer, I felt that they would likely only choose one for cap purposes. Truth be told, they have the cap flexibility to accommodate a deal. Additionally, there are also various contracts that may be moved on to bolster their salary cap space. However, I question whether or not General Manager George Paton and the rest of the Broncos’ brass would want to invest such a monumental number of guarantees at the cornerback position. McMillian will likely get a lucrative deal in free agency and have no shortage of suitors. In the event he embarks on greener pastures, the Broncos do have his replacement already in house. That’s second-year cornerback Jahdae Barron. The former Jim Thorpe Award winner was a versatile defender for the Texas Longhorns. Barron played just about every spot imaginable in their secondary. His cross-training across the backend of the defense has continued into the pros in Joseph’s scheme. While many fans have already written him off as a potential bust due to lack of playing time, I still remain confident he has the ability to contribute at a high level. He seems like a more natural fit on the inside anyway. I’m not sure Barron had the length or athleticism to routinely hold his own in press and go head-to-head against bigger wide receivers in man coverage. It’s also important to note that Kris Abrams-Draine will be a free agent at the end of the 2027 season. Abrams-Draine has primarily been a boundary backup for Denver in his first three seasons. He has played well when the opportunity presented itself. Quite frankly, I think he is a starting caliber player and there is a chance he could wind up receiving a nice free agent deal a few years down the line. With Moss extended, that’s a little bit less of a worry at the boundary position moving forward, though they will still have to find depth at some point in time beyond the ‘27 season.
author: Christopher Hart

title: Scouting the Enemy: Las Vegas Raiders
summary: The Denver Broncos battle the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. It’s a big division rivalry matchup for Broncos who are coming off their bye week. After starting their season 3-0, the Raiders have dropped six of their las seven games and are 4-6 on the season. Here is a deeper look at their Week 11 […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 15: Brock Bowers #89 and Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders wait to be introduced before a game against the Seattle Seahawks at Allegiant Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Seahawks defeated the Raiders 21-13. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos battle the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. It’s a big division rivalry matchup for Broncos who are coming off their bye week. After starting their season 3-0, the Raiders have dropped six of their las seven games and are 4-6 on the season. Here is a deeper look at their Week 11 opponent. 2025 Las Vegas Raiders Regular Season Review The Pete Carroll experiment in Las Vegas lasted just one season. The Raiders finished dead last in the AFC West with a 3-14 record. After his dismissal, the Raiders hired Klint Kubiak to be their next Head Coach. 2026 Las Vegas Raiders Offseason Additions and Departures After a disappointing ’25 season, the Raiders embarked on a tremendous overhaul this offseason. Both their offense and defense were awful. They added a handful of players on offense early on in free agency including center Tyler Linderbaum and wide receiver Jalen Nailor. On defense, they overhauled their linebacking corps bringing in former Georgia Bulldog teammates Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker to man the middle of their defense. They also added edge rushers Kwity Paye and Malcolm Koonce to bolster their pass rush. Additionally, the Raiders traded for former Buffalo Bills defensive back Taron Johnson to shore up their secondary. Head Coach Klint Kubiak and General Manager John Spytek were busy this past April making ten selections in the 2026 NFL Draft . Quarterback Fernando Mendoza, taken with the top pick, is poised to start his second career game with the Broncos. The Raiders found two starters on Day 2 with defensive back Treydan Stukes and offensive lineman Trey Zuhn. On Day 2, they made high upside picks with cornerback Jermod McCoy and running back Mike Washington Jr. who have seen a decent amount of reps this season. Offensive X-Factor: Quarterback Fernando Mendzoa Tight end Brock Bowers was going to get the nod here. However, Bowers injured his ankle against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 10. While the ankle injury won’t land him on injured reserve, Head Coach Klint Kubiak stated he will be day-to-day and did classify it as significant. With that in mind, I’ll turn to rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza as their offensive X-Factor for the game. Last week against the Seahawks, Mendoza made his first start of his NFL. He struggled and completed just 17 his 29 pass attempts for only 143 yards. However, he did get his first career touchdown with 10-yard quarterback draw in the first quarter of the matchup. The Raiders’ offensive line had just allowed 11 sacks all season before the Seahawks game, but their defense was able to drop Mendoza for six sacks. This is a game where Denver’s defensive front seven needs to play at a high level. I consider it a favorable matchup for Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph and his players. If they can rattle the rookie signal caller and force him into bad decisions, I really like their chances on Sunday. Defensive X-Factor: Edge rusher Maxx Crosby For a moment earlier in the spring, Broncos Country was elated with the news that premier edge rusher Maxx Crosby would be heading out of the division to join the Baltimore Ravens. However, much like the Daiyan Henley trade, the deal was nixed due to a failed physical. So now, he is back for his eighth season with the Raiders. At 29-years-old, Crosby has cemented himself as one of the league’s best defenders. He has earned five-straight Pro-Bowl designations and has been a two-time All-Pro dating back to the 2021 season. In ten games this season, Crosby has 34 tackles, 9 tackles for loss, 21 quarterback hits, and 5 sacks. During the bye and earlier this week, Head Coach Sean Payton emphasized that blocking up front, whether it’s against the run or the pass, is one of the huge things Denver’s offense needs to accomplish to finally hit their stride in the second half of the season. Going up against Crosby will be a big challenge for them. We will see if the offensive line is up to the task. How the Broncos can achieve a victory over the Raiders ICYMI: Yesterday, I wrote how the Broncos can achieve their eighth victory of the season over the Raiders. Overall, I feel confident about Denver’s chances. The extra week of preparation should help them out, plus going up against a rookie quarterback in his second start should help matters. I believe the Broncos will achieve a decisive double-digit victory over the Raiders. Hart’s Prediction: Broncos 30, Raiders 16.
author: Christopher Hart

title: Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph praises Riley Moss for his resilience and toughness
summary: The Denver Broncos have become one of the best franchises in the National Football League when it comes to rewarding their players who perform well. Since the Walton-Penner Family Ownership Group took over several seasons ago, the Broncos have doled out nearly a dozen large contracts to assemble a championship caliber roster. Yesterday, fourth-year cornerback […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - JANUARY 4: Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph of the Denver Broncos roams the sidelines during the first quarter against the Los Angeles Chargers at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Sunday, January 4, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images The Denver Broncos have become one of the best franchises in the National Football League when it comes to rewarding their players who perform well. Since the Walton-Penner Family Ownership Group took over several seasons ago, the Broncos have doled out nearly a dozen large contracts to assemble a championship caliber roster. Yesterday, fourth-year cornerback Riley Moss became the most recent player to earn a lucrative multi-year contract extension. While no particulars on guarantees have been provided, the known terms are a four-year deal worth up to $67 million dollars. That’s a shade below $17 million annually, and several million less on average than many thought he would garner on the open market. Yesterday after practice and the news about the extension, Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph met with the media and was asked about the importance of getting the deal done. “It’s special. I think it speaks to the Walton-Penner Family Ownership, the GM, and the Head Coach. That’s the program. That’s the plan here to draft, develop and retain. It’s working to obviously maintain and get better each year. That’s the key to this league. Keep your own and find them early and pay them,” stated Joseph. The Broncos moved up in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft to select Moss out of Iowa. As a rookie, it was mostly a learning season for the former Hawkeyes standout. He appeared in 14 games, but most of his action was as a core special teams’ player. He only had 23 defensive snaps that season. Over the next two years, Moss would be a 31-game starter for the Broncos opposite of All-Pro cornerback Patrick Surtain II. Between the 2024 and 2025 seasons, he would log over 1,900 defensive snaps and proved himself to be an important piece in Joseph’s talented secondary. “I’ll start with this; he’s always been very athletic. He’s competitive. To play opposite of Pat Surtain II, that’s a tough job. Outside of Bo Nix on gameday, it’s probably Riley,” Joseph remarked stating who likely has the hardest assignment on a week-to-week basis. In his third season as a starter, Moss has missed some time, but he is performing very well—allowing 223 yards in coverage on 18 catches. Opposing quarterbacks aren’t having much success targeting him at all, completing just 51-percent of passes that go in his direction. Those are all career bests for him. “No one understands his gameday because Pat’s out there at left corner, and they never look at Pat. They do sometimes, but mostly they don’t. They’re trying to find Riley. So that’s a tough job. He’s the perfect personality for that job. Most corners wouldn’t have the resolve to kind of over, and over again just take 12 targets a game, and two penalties here and there,” added Joseph. Speaking of penalties, that’s one area Broncos Country has been right to criticize Moss for the past two years. He had fourteen defensive pass interference calls in 24’ and ‘25. However, things are markedly different in 2026. To date, he has just two of those on the season. That’s significant progress. When the time came yesterday afternoon, Moss answered a handful of questions for reporters. He was extremely grateful for the extension and had high praise for his coaches, teammates, and ownership. There is no doubt the talented cornerback has had his fair share of ups and downs throughout his career. Nevertheless, he has proven to be a gritty player who can overcome the obstacles that have come his way. He gave credit to his upbringing for this ability to do such things. “I think the biggest thing is it’s how I was raised with my parents. The biggest thing was they let me fail so I would be able to figure out how to become successful through that, through that adversity. It’s the reason I am who I am today. It’s a hard job, but it’s a rewarding job and I love it.”

title: Broncos aim to hit their stride at just the right time
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! The Denver Broncos are in a good spot. They sit at 7-2 coming out of the bye week after a gauntlet of a schedule to start the season. They’re in the hunt for the AFC West title, the top seed, and home-field advantage in the AFC playoffs. The key now is […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos reacts after a touchdown by Jonah Coleman during the fourth quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. The Broncos defeated the Chiefs 28-24. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! The Denver Broncos are in a good spot. They sit at 7-2 coming out of the bye week after a gauntlet of a schedule to start the season. They’re in the hunt for the AFC West title, the top seed, and home-field advantage in the AFC playoffs. The key now is to not let up or lose momentum. “I think collectively, we just finished a team meeting talking about the improvement in certain areas where we feel like we’re going to have to be better at in this, call it, second half of the season,” Broncos head coach Sean Payton said to the media earlier this week. “Specifically, I mentioned this last week, we need to block better on offense, and we need to be in the right place. I thought we did an average job against Carolina, and I think that’s an area of focus relative to more consistency in our run game. Then there were some third-down, fourth-down-and-longs defensively that was an Achilles’ heel for us a year ago, and the other day became one. Those are just a few things.” Broncos quarterback Bo Nix wouldn’t call it a sense of urgency, more refreshed and a second wind. The bye week allows the body to get a break and the mind to turn off. “I think there is something to that,” Nix said to the media this week. “The first part of the season is really tough coming out of the gate after training camp, so you get to the bye, and that is always a point to regroup and go from there. I think we’ve put ourselves in a spot to now make the push and really get going. There is an element to the peak of the season. “We’re almost to that point and almost to the end in December and January, where the games get really important. Not that they weren’t already, but those have playoff implications, and then you run into the playoffs. You want to be confident going into those. Right now is the stretch as a team that we can’t let off, and really continue to press.” For Nix and Denver, it’s about peaking at the right time, and that’s the end of the season. As Nix often says, you don’t want to peak too early or in the early part of the season. That means the Broncos must carry over the momentum from the bye and improve from week to week. “In the NFL, there are so many weeks that you have to put your head down and just keep working,” Nix said to the media. “One week could look completely different, and one week doesn’t tell the story for the next week. For me, it’s a marathon and not a sprint. You can’t wear yourself out early. You don’t want to peak too soon. “It’s just sort of the game within the game of the season. It’s finding ways to get better so that when that moment comes, and the playoffs are here and when you have to win the football game, you’re not going home early because you missed out on your peak. Coming off the bye, we feel fresh, we feel good, and ready for this next stretch.” Broncos links

title: Not extending Ja’Quan McMillian would be a mistake
summary: The news breaking of the $67M contract extension for cornerback Riley Moss was well-received by most fans. As it should, he’s been the primary focus of targets with Pat Surtain II opposite him and he has held up as well as any number one guy on any defense. He probably could have gotten close to […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 8: Ja'quan McMillian #29 of the Denver Broncos reacts during the fourth quarter against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on November 8, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The news breaking of the $67M contract extension for cornerback Riley Moss was well-received by most fans. As it should, he’s been the primary focus of targets with Pat Surtain II opposite him and he has held up as well as any number one guy on any defense. He probably could have gotten close to $20M a year and Denver got him for $16.75. A very good deal. That said, it would still be a mistake for the Denver Broncos to let fellow cornerback Ja’Quan McMillian walk in free agency. McMillian is just a playmaker and you cannot put a price tag on that or find any easy replacement. They will have same issue if/when Marvin Mims Jr. walks, although he has been a bit quiet this year so far on the playmaker side of things. We asked fans a month ago who they felt the Broncos should keep if they only kept one and the vote was quite literally one-sided: The funny part about that is even those of us who voted McMillian would also love to see Riley Moss around too. He has been a very good outside cornerback, but McMillian has made the big plays in key moments. Those monster plays stick with you when you think about who has made a bigger impact. Hopefully Denver finds a way to keep both and gets McMillian locked down long-term ahead of free agency next year . Broncos daily recap Broncos vs. Raiders: 3 Things to Watch in Week 11 The Denver Broncos host the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Here are three storylines I’ll be watching closely in their Week 11 matchup. How the Denver Broncos can beat the Las Vegas Raiders In order for the Denver Broncos to defeat the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, here are three things they need to accomplish. Broncos looking to start second half of season on a high note The Denver Broncos are back to business this week and will host the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Despite a 4-6 record, Head Coach Sean Payton knows they’ll be a tough team to beat. Potent quotables Sean Payton On if he can tell what the bye week did for the team physically “It’s hard to tell. I think you never can control obviously your bye. I’m sure there are a handful of players that may not have been able to play had we have played last Sunday that will have a chance of playing this Sunday. I thought we had good work. It was a good full practice longer than two weeks ago. Yes, it went well.” On if he knows Raiders Head Coach Klint Kubiak “I know his father [former Broncos Head Coach Gary Kubiak]. I know he was here. [He’s] one of the guys I spent a lot of time with. I have a ton of respect for their family and what he’s doing. There are a lot of ties just to that organization. I think already you can see it on tape what they’re wanting to build and the early success this year. You go through Kansas City, Seattle, Buffalo, these are all teams that are in the thick of it, and they played all those teams to one-score games.” On if the Raiders’ offense has changed with a new starting quarterback “There’s a system they believe in though, and you still saw it in the game they played last week. So they’re going to do a good job with the run game, the play-action off of it. Fortunately we’ve had a week at least to see tape on the new quarterback. You have to defend the offense and then obviously the people in it.” On what he likes about what the team is doing right now “It’s a little bit more than halfway in the season, and there’s a lot that still needs to be done. I feel the same way about our team. We knew going in there was a challenge to the start of the season based on the opponents. You get so micro-focused on just the next game and the things that these guys do well. They return kicks well. They punt it well. They force fumbles better than anyone in the league. They’re really good offensively, red zone. They’ll possess the ball if you allow them to. They do a really good job of the time of possession. The takeaways have been noticeable. I don’t know if that answers your question, but rarely do you really take a bigger picture look. You’re aware of where your team’s at, but then you’re also very mindful of the things that we need to continue to improve on.” On how the offensive line can block better “There are times in a game where there are going to be some looks that are tougher looks. There were some opportunities against Carolina where we could have been a little bit better, a little cleaner.” On how taking the whole bye week off benefits the team and his conversations with Chiefs Head Coach Andy Reid about it “Remember it wasn’t like we split the atom when he gave me that answer. It’s a long season. I think guys get away mentally, and physically, the guys that were or currently are injured are here. It’s good to have everyone back.” On Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza’s first start last week “It’s a tough start obviously when you play the Super Bowl champion. I remember his college tape well. All of us that would go through the draft process. Obviously he’s a winner. The things I see really are just from afar, but you see the quick release and all the things you’re looking for in that position. I’ve heard nothing but great things from people that have been around him.” On if the evaluation of quarterbacks in the draft process is the same when there’s not need at that position “It is. We’re not going to have a private workout, so maybe to some degree it isn’t also. Fair question. I just remember what it was the year [QB] Bo [Nix] came out. The tape evaluation, the grades, the reading of the player, that’s very much the same, the time you spent. You don’t really try to hurry through position groups. You really try to put grades and discuss players, and you have plenty of time to do that.” On if the notion that rookie quarterbacks struggle in their first few starts is overblown “There have been great debuts. You could go back and find an argument probably for a lot of [players], and a lot of it may be circumstantial relative to the surrounding cast. This clearly is a different team than we’ve played the last couple of years. That’s the part where you see [Head Coach] Klint [Kubiak]’s imprint, the people that are there coaching from top down.” On TE Caleb Lohner returning to practice “It’s good to get him out here. He’s worked his tail off. Today was his first practice. He was making a lot of strides, and that setback was unfortunate, but he has that spirit, that will. You never felt like he lost interest. So it was good to see him moving around.” On if WR Courtland Sutton’s ability to win a release in the short red zone has improved since he arrived “It’s a strength of his. He’s real good at the line. His size, he uses his hands well. I think it’s something that for him, being in the paint, if you will, as a power player is something that he excels at.” On if he looks for the ability to release when grading receivers before the draft “I think you’re looking for stop start, you’re looking for transition. I like bigger receivers in our league period. That doesn’t mean entirely, but the target radius and all those things are quarterback friendly with him.” On if Lions DE Aidan Hutchinson’s injury during a celebration is a teaching moment “I’m kind of with [Lions Head Coach] Dan [Campbell]. I saw the final comments. We’re teachers and we’re constantly… But we’re going to walk out of the doors, and there’ve been a lot of celebrations. I’m kind of with Dan there where it’s unfortunate. Two good players got hurt on the same play, and I think that there are a lot of other things that I would put on tape on a Friday, Saturday that are [teaching moments]. That, I wouldn’t put that on.” On if he takes pride in watching a former player and coach like Lions Head Coach Dan Campbell handle adversity “Yes, absolutely.…

title: Broncos are expected to revisit contract talks with CB Ja’Quan McMillian during the offseason
summary: According to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the Denver Broncos are expected to revisit extension talks with slot corner Ja’Quan McMillian at the end of the season. Klis notes that McMillian remains on the Broncos’ radar after they signed Riley Moss to a four-year extension today and engaged with his reps during the bye week, but […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Ja'Quan McMillian #29 of the Denver Broncos reacts during the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Empower Field At Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Andrew Wevers/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the Denver Broncos are expected to revisit extension talks with slot corner Ja’Quan McMillian at the end of the season. Klis notes that McMillian remains on the Broncos’ radar after they signed Riley Moss to a four-year extension today and engaged with his reps during the bye week , but all remaining talks will be on hold until the offseason. Per source, the Broncos engaged with nickel back Ja'Quan McMillian as well as Riley Moss on contract extensions over the bye week. McMillian remains very much on the Broncos radar and expectation is team will revisit extension talks after the year while he also eyes open market. — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) November 19, 2026 Both Moss and McMillian entered the season as pending free agents, and the narrative was that the team would have to decide which of the two to sign to an extension. Now that Moss has signed his four-year extension, it would appear that McMillian might be the odd man out here. I say this because the Broncos have former first-round pick Jahdae Barron on the roster, and he profiles best as a slot corner. He has played outside primarily when given playing time, but with McMillian healthy and performing as a top slot corner in the NFL, Barron hasn’t played much at slot during his time in the NFL. It would make sense for the Broncos to pay Moss, which they did, let McMillian walk in free agency, and allow their first-round investment to take over at slot. Sounds great on paper; however, Barron has struggled a bit during his short career and likely would be a step back from McMillian in the slot. So, if they do go that route, I would anticipate the team adding some depth and potentially some competition for Barron this offseason. We all know George Paton loves drafting corners, and I would not be shocked if he did it again this coming draft. With that said, it should be a no-brainer to sign Ja’Quan McMillian to an extension. He is arguably the top slot corner in the NFL and has made multiple impact plays for the Broncos during his time as a starter, including his clutch interception of Bills quarterback Josh Allen in the Divisional Round of the playoffs. If you can find a way to retain a talent like that, you do it. In the Broncos’ defense, this current regime has not let many talented players leave. They have signed multiple key players to extensions, but they did let veteran pass rusher John Franklin-Myers leave via free agency last season. Will they do the same with McMillian this offseason? My take is that he is likely gone. We all thought they had to pick one or the other, and now that Moss is signed, it appears that they have made their decision. Also, how often do they let a key free agent go unsigned heading into the offseason in which they become a free agent? I am sure they will have talks, but unless McMillian signs a team-friendly deal, I have a hard time seeing him re-signed at this point. The reality is that McMillian would be a top free agent on the market and would likely get himself a well-earned big-money, multi-year contract. We also have to factor in responsible team building. You have signed Pat Surtain II and now Riley Moss to multi-year contract extensions and spent a first-round pick on Jahdae Barron. Signing McMillian to an extension, with Barron still on the roster, would be a lot of money tied up in one positional group and would continue to keep Barron buried on the depth chart. Now, you could argue he hasn’t shown enough to be handed the job, which is very fair, but that’s a decision the Broncos will have to make. This will be a conversation and topic that we will revisit at the end of the season. For now, I think it is trending towards McMillian leaving, but I hope that I am wrong. Time will tell, and in the meantime, McMillian will continue to be a playmaking slot corner for the Broncos for the remainder of the season.

title: Broncos sign CB Riley Moss to a four-year contract extension worth $67 million
summary: According to NFL insider Tom Pelissero, the Denver Broncos are finalizing a four-year contract extension with cornerback Riley Moss. It is a four-year deal worth up to $67 million dollars as the Broncos lock up one of their key starters in their secondary. The story heading into the season was: which player would the Broncos […]
full_text: SEATTLE, CO - OCTOBER 15: Riley Moss #21 of the Denver Broncos runs out of the tunnel prior to an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Seattle, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to NFL insider Tom Pelissero, the Denver Broncos are finalizing a four-year contract extension with cornerback Riley Moss. It is a four-year deal worth up to $67 million dollars as the Broncos lock up one of their key starters in their secondary. The Broncos are finalizing a contact extension with CB Riley Moss for four years and $67 million, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports . Another key piece of the Denver defense is locked in for the long haul on a deal negotiated by Kyle Strongin of @RangeSportsRMP — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 19, 2026 The story heading into the season was: which player would the Broncos re-sign? Cornerback Riley Moss, whom the Broncos spent a 3rd-round pick on, or cornerback Ja’Quan McMillian, a former undrafted free agent this coaching staff inherited? Well, at least for now, it appears Moss is their choice. He signed a four-year extension, which makes him the 23rd highest-paid cornerback in the league right now. While many wanted the team to re-sign Ja’Quan McMillian, and honestly, they may still, Moss is worthy of this extension. He has one of the hardest jobs in the NFL, which is playing opposite star cornerback Pat Surtain II. Teams avoid going after Surtain II, which means more targets go Moss’s way. Yes, he has had some struggles, and the refs, for whatever reason, love to call phantom penalties on him, but he has been a key part of the success of the Broncos’ secondary these past few years. Now, both he and Surtain II are locked up and will keep their secondary strong for the foreseeable future. Now, all eyes go to star slot corner Ja’Quan McMillian. He remains a pending free agent next season, and the narrative always was that the Broncos will likely have to pick between him and Moss. Well, Moss has an extension, so was the decision made? Perhaps, but there is some room for optimism, in my opinion. Slot corners are typically cheaper than outside corners, and the struggles of Jahdae Barron recently could have the Broncos wanting to bring back both. With that said, you do have Jahdae Barron, a former first-round pick who profiles as a slot corner and someone who many assumed would take McMillian’s job when he was drafted. Could they still have faith in their first-round investment and risk letting McMillian walk? We’ll see. At the very least, the Broncos have Pat Surtain II and Riley Moss locked up for the foreseeable future, and that should keep the Denver Broncos’ secondary strong moving forward. We will just have to see what this Moss extensions means for Ja’Quan McMiillian and his future with the team.

title: Before the Roar: Previewing Detroit Lions vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers
summary: With their trip across the pond now in the rearview mirror, the Detroit Lions are fresh off of their 35-10 win over the New England Patriots in Germany and looking to keep their winning ways rolling in Week 11 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Despite their 3-6 record, Tampa Bay is firmly in the NFC […]
full_text: With their trip across the pond now in the rearview mirror, the Detroit Lions are fresh off of their 35-10 win over the New England Patriots in Germany and looking to keep their winning ways rolling in Week 11 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Despite their 3-6 record, Tampa Bay is firmly in the NFC South hunt, and their stingy defense is one of the biggest reasons why. To break down the defense and everything else ahead of the game, Meko Scott and I are back with another episode of, “ Before the Roar .” We start out with a Buccaneers’ quarterback situation that seems like it’s a fluid one as the week progresses. Initially, it seemed like quarterback Baker Mayfield was a bit of a longshot to play against the Lions, especially considering the moves Tampa Bay made when they signed free agent quarterback Cooper Rush, and elevated Easton Stick to the active roster from the practice squad. However, in a recent interview, Mayfield made it seem as though he would be playing if he can get cleared by Tampa Bay’s medical staff. Ultimately, whoever ends up at quarterback really won’t change the Lions’ gameplan all that much. It all is going to hinge on Detroit’s ability to stop the Buccaneers’ running game. On the opposite side of the ball, the Buccaneers’ defense is arguably the best in the NFL. From front-seven players like rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter and veteran nose tackle Vita Vea, to a secondary that includes the likes of Zyon McCollum and Antoine Winfield Jr, it’s easy to see why this defense is so effective against just about anything that opposing offenses throw at them. You can watch the entire preview podcast right here . If you haven’t already done so, please be sure to like the video and subscribe to the Pride of Detroit YouTube channel.

title: Detroit Lions name a new captain on defense
summary: As first reported by Justin Rogers and confirmed by coach Dan Campbell on Friday, the Detroit Lions have a new defensive captain. Veteran safety Chuck Clark was given the honors earlier this week, after the Lions had lost two defensive captains to injury over the past three weeks: Jack Campbell (neck), Aidan Hutchinson (knee). “It […]
full_text: Nov 8, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Detroit Lions safety Chuck Clark (36) runs with the ball after an interception during the second half against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As first reported by Justin Rogers and confirmed by coach Dan Campbell on Friday, the Detroit Lions have a new defensive captain. Veteran safety Chuck Clark was given the honors earlier this week, after the Lions had lost two defensive captains to injury over the past three weeks: Jack Campbell (neck), Aidan Hutchinson (knee). “It felt like the right thing to do,” Campbell said. “We obviously lost a couple of our captains. He’s really just filled the void as the season has gone on. Type of guy he is, it just speaks for itself. And he’s just grown inside this locker room, he’s a great teammate, and he’s just got leadership qualities through the room. Communication is outstanding. His production has gone up as the season’s gone up. Everybody’s got a lot of faith in Chuck. He’s just kinda one of those bell-cow guys for us right now. So he earned that, so proud of him.” Clark is in his 10th NFL season and first with the Lions. Campbell noted that they knew about Clark’s leadership qualities before they signed him to a one-year, $1.5 million deal this offseason, but you never know for sure until he’s actually in the building. Thus far, he’s lived up to his reputation. “You get around him and you see it first hand. There’s nothing fake about it. He’s just real,” Campbell said. “He’s one of those guys that people gravitate to him. He’s just got it. He’s a great communicator, same guy every day, very consistent, smart, grinder. He’s everything you really want in that type of role.” In addition to his leadership, Clark has become an important part of the gameday lineup. He’s been a steadying force in Detroit’s ever-shifting secondary, logging more defensive snaps (540) than anyone else on the team. And while his role may soon decrease with the return of Brian Branch a few weeks ago and Kerby Joseph this week, Campbell noted that they want to still use all of their safeties, Clark included. “Everybody’ got a role. We’re trying to use everybody that we can in that defensive room. So all those safeties? We want to use them,” Campbell said. “There’s a role for all of those guys. And now you get Kerby back in the fold. So we’ve got a couple of things that we can do here and have flexibility to do.”

title: NFL predictions: 4 keys to a Lions victory over the Buccaneers in Week 11
summary: The Detroit Lions (7-2) and Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) will face off at Ford Field in Detroit in a Week 11 showdown. The Lions and Bucs have faced each other four times in the last three seasons, and these two teams know each other almost as well as their head coaches. “Tampa Bay Bucs, competitive, […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - OCTOBER 20: Amon-Ra St. Brown #14 of the Detroit Lions scores a touchdown in the first quarter against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field on October 20, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Detroit Lions (7-2) and Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) will face off at Ford Field in Detroit in a Week 11 showdown. The Lions and Bucs have faced each other four times in the last three seasons, and these two teams know each other almost as well as their head coaches. “Tampa Bay Bucs, competitive, physical unit,” Lions coach Dan Campbell said of the Bucs. “Known (Buccaneers Head Coach) Todd Bowles a long time. Obviously have got a ton of respect for him and what he’s about. And this defense is playing outstanding football. And offensively, they’re committed to the run game, time of possession. They’re trying to force you into making errors. And really, the last three games, they played some pretty good football.” This week’s prediction preview is sponsored by the folks at FanDuel Sportsbook , who currently have the Lions listed at +2000 to win this year’s Super Bowl and are currently 6.5-point favorites in Week 11 . Let’s take a closer look at this matchup and predict how the Lions will beat the Bucs in this week’s Honolulu Blueprint. Buc s base scheme For a detailed look at the opposing scheme, check out our complementary breakdown piece: Lions Week 11 preview: Breaking down the Bucs’ offensive and defensive schemes . Prediction 1: Lions continue to feed 14 Germany was a storybook celebration of Amon-Ra St. Brown. The Lions All-Pro receiver may have made only four receptions, but he chewed up 98 yards, and both touchdown receptions were epic. As fantastic as Germany was for St. Brown, it’s not his only source of energy; he has a history of repeating big-game success against specific opponents. For example, St. Brown always shows up big when the Lions play the Bills, but after Buffalo, he’s consistently had the most success against the Buccaneers. Over four games, St. Brown’s per-game averages include: 9.25 receptions, 101.5 receiving yards, and .75 touchdowns: 2025: 6 receptions, 86 yards, 1 touchdown 2024: 11 receptions, 119 yards 2023 (Playoffs): 8 receptions, 77 yards, 1 TD 2023: 12 receptions, 124 yards, 1 TD The Bucs run a tight bump-and-run press at the line of scrimmage, and they operate out of zone coverage on nearly 85% of defensive snaps. St. Brown excels at beating press with his precision route running, quickness, and strength, and he’s often quarterback Jared Goff’s first read because the All-Pro receiver is elite at finding soft spots in the zone. Add in the fact that the Bucs blitz nearly 44% of the time (second most in the NFL), and St. Brown will often set up behind the linebackers, secure catches in volume, and churn out yards after the catch (YAC). This is the fifth time in four years St. Brown has faced this defense, so he should have a strong feel for its weaknesses in zone. Feed the hot hand. Prediction 2: Gibbs attacks edges on the ground and through the air Prediction No. 1 last week was to attack the edges of the Patriots’ defensive line, and it played out to perfection. This week, I am calling for it again, not only because it’s working, but it’s also worked in the past against this defense. Here’s a look at Gibbs numbers from the last four games against the Bucs, noting that he was injured and inactive in the first meeting, and splitting touches with David Montgomery in the other three games: 2025: 17 rushes, 136 yards (8.0 ypc), 2 TDs — 3 receptions, 82 yards 2024: 13 rushes, 84 yards (6.5 ypc), 0 TDs — 7 receptions, 22 yards 2023 (P): 9 rushes, 74 yards (8.2 ypc), 1 TD — 4 receptions, 40 yards 2023: Inactive Three things stand out when looking at those statistics: 1) the rushing yards per carry numbers are gaudy; 2) the Lions aren’t afraid to find Gibbs through the air, as it can be highly productive and effective in slowing down the Bucs’ blitz; and 3) if this is what he produced in a part-time role, can he exceed these numbers? It would be a lofty expectation for Gibbs to maintain this level of success, especially since the Bucs allow only 79.1 rushing yards per game (best in the NFL), 3.5 yards per carry (3rd best), -0.13 EPA on runs against them (3rd), and a 38.3% rushing success rate (4th). However, if we look back at the last five weeks (four games for the Bucs), Tampa Bay’s run defense numbers have been closer to average than elite: 87 rushing yards per game, 3.87 ypc (10th), -0.05 EPA on runs against (18th), and a 42.2% success rate (19th) allowed. Over that same time period, the Lions have won five straight games, and Gibbs is averaging 99.2 yards per game (best in the NFL)—eclipsing 100 rushing yards in four of the last five games—, 5.28 yards per carry (5th), -0.02 EPA (9th), and a 43.6% success rate (10th). The Bucs run defense is formidable, but they’ve been slightly vulnerable lately, and with the odds-on favorite for Offensive Player of the Year honors in your backfield (according to FanDuel Sportsbook ), you need to get the ball into his hands. Prediction 3: Lions load the box to stop the run The Bucs rushing attack is one of the best in the NFL, and it’s carried the team through some rough patches. Statistically, they rank No. 1 in the NFL in rushing yards per game (163.9), rushing yards per play (5.0), explosive rushing plays over the last four games (16.1%), and 20+ yard runs (11). While some of those stats may be skewed by the “monsoon” game, where the Bucs attempted only three passes and ran the ball 56 times for 324 yards, they’re still in the top 5 in most rushing categories even without that anomaly. The Bucs deploy a two-headed rushing attack with Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell, but Irving is the starter and Tampa Bay will often ride his hot hand. Here’s Next Gen Stats with more on Irving: “Bucky Irving enters Week 11 of 2026 with 825 rushing yards, 5th in the NFL, including two games with 150-plus rushing yards (tied for 2nd in the NFL, trailing only Jahmyr Gibbs with four). Irving has recorded seven scrimmage touchdowns since Week 5, tied for 2nd in the NFL behind only McCaffrey (9). His 91.7 rushing yards per game in 2026 would rank as the second-most in a single season in Buccaneers history, trailing only James Wilder’s 96.5 rush yards per game in 1984.” The Bucs use a blend of blocking schemes, including outside zone, inside zone, and counter, but they lean most on “gap” concepts. According to Next Gen Stats, the Bucs utilize a gap blocking scheme on “29.7% of their designed carries (5th highest rate) and on these runs have recorded a league-leading 415 rushing yards,” with Irving accounting for over half that production (230 yards). However, as Next Gen also points out, the Lions have done well against gap concepts this season, allowing only 3.3 yards per carry (6th fewest) and just one touchdown this season from this scheme. Overall, the Lions’ run defense has been steady and is improving as the season rolls on. They’re 5th in the NFL in yards allowed per game (90.4), No. 1 in preventing yards after contact, and in their last four games, they’ve allowed a rushing success rate of only 33.8% (3rd best). This is a real strength-on-strength matchup, according to Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard: “They’re the number one rush offense in the League and we’re one of the top premier run defenses in the League. […] They don’t hide it, and we don’t hide the way we play. So it’s a beautiful thing. It’s a beautiful challenge, and we’re looking forward to it.” With the Bucs passing offense struggling (they’re bottom-five in most statistical categories) and the rushing attack being their biggest weapon, look for the Lions to load the box—potentially utilizing three safety sets following the return of Kerby Joseph—and lean on players like Brian Branch to live near the line of scrimmage and try to slow down Irving and the Bucs ‘ run game.…

title: What game are you most looking forward to in Week 11?
summary: With the calendar inching its way toward Thanksgiving, December football in the NFL is just around the corner. And with it, many division and playoff races begin to really heat up. As for the NFC North, things may be warmer than any other division in football. The Detroit Lions hold possession of first place as […]
full_text: With the calendar inching its way toward Thanksgiving, December football in the NFL is just around the corner. And with it, many division and playoff races begin to really heat up. As for the NFC North, things may be warmer than any other division in football. The Detroit Lions hold possession of first place as we head into Week 11, with the Minnesota Vikings and Chicago Bears right behind them, each with seven wins of their own. Even the fourth-place Green Bay Packers have six wins. For Detroit, they will host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field this Sunday. Despite their 3-6 record on the year, Tampa Bay is firmly in the NFC South race and only one game behind the division-leading Carolina Panthers. Overall, Week 11 is a bit light in terms of games where both teams have playoff aspirations, but there are still plenty of games with intriguing storylines. That brings us to today’s question of the day— Which Week 11 game are you most looking forward to? My answer: It feels like the obvious choice to me, but I am going with “Sunday Night Football” featuring the Minnesota Vikings and the San Francisco 49ers. The 49ers have been one of the best teams in the league for most of the year, while Minnesota is hoping they found the cure to their offensive struggles with the return of veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins. With a win, San Francisco would give themselves a nice inside-track towards the number one overall seed in the NFC, while the Vikings would love to keep pace with a Detroit team that is hoping to extend their winning streak to six against Tampa Bay. What about you? Are you going with the heavyweight fight in the NFC in primetime, or do you have another game in mind that you want to keep an eye on? Let us know in the comments below.
