title: Jalen Pitre’s return brings more than big hits to Houston’s defense
summary: The Houston Texans nickel corner Jalen Pitre returned after a month on the sidelines after recovering from a shoulder injury against the Tennessee Titans. His presence was immediately felt on the field and on Twitter. His first game back was by far his best performance of the season with six solo tackles and two tackles […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - NOVEMBER 8: Houston Texans safety Jalen Pitre (5) hits Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Tre Harris (9) during an NFL game between the Houston Texans and the Los Angeles Chargers on November 8, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. (Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Houston Texans nickel corner Jalen Pitre returned after a month on the sidelines after recovering from a shoulder injury against the Tennessee Titans. His presence was immediately felt on the field and on Twitter. His first game back was by far his best performance of the season with six solo tackles and two tackles for loss. He followed up that performance with another six tackles and a tackle for loss against the Cleveland Browns. Houston’s defense struggled with Pitre absent from the lineup. Rookie Kamari Ramsey and veteran special teamer Tremon Smith stood in for the sixth year defensive back and struggled to make the impact that Pitre brought to the defense. Speaking of impact, Pitre absolutely laid the boom on this critical third and goal play. Safe to say… Jalen Pitre is back. 📺: @NFLonCBS pic.twitter.com/9hVTl4IrRv — Houston Texans (@HoustonTexans) November 8, 2026 His ability to recognize play concepts, break on the ball, and utterly destroy professional athletes was a missed attribute over the past several weeks. Pitre has also been brought on corner blitzes more this season as a wrinkle to diversify an otherwise stale offense. It has worked on occasion, but is more of a reflection of his impact on the defense. While Pitre was a part of the defense during the four-straight losses, but he was far from the problem during those contests. What Pitre provides is the ability to play nickel coverage without sacrificing anything in the run game. As the Chargers found out, the screen game is a hazard when Pitre is on the field. It makes every receiver vulnerable to getting their factory reset button hit. Pitre’s ability to play close to the line of scrimmage also alleviates Houston’s corners from needing to do so. Kamari Lassiter and Derek Stingley Jr. have struggled this season, particularly in press man coverage. Their run stopping duties compels them to play closer to the line of scrimmage than they want to, which has resulted in them getting burned on crossing routes. Neither corner is particularly fast. Houston played a young, gritty, and impressive Cleveland Browns offense on Sunday. He guarded Jerry Jeudy and rookie KC Concepcion Jr.. The Browns offense are lead by dual rookie first-round wide receivers Conception and Denzel Boston. Conception’s placement in the slot and more slender frame were a signature matchup for Pitre, who excels in the slot and against smaller receivers. Pitre more than held his own, even though it wasn’t enough for the defense to stop Deshaun Watson down the stretch. Next up, Houston takes on the Indianapolis Colts, who sold their entire wide receiver room before the trade deadline. The Colts WR depth chart is headlined by Laquon Treadwell, Ashton Dulin, and Anthony Gould. Most likely, Pitre will cover Tyler Warren who is the best remaining threat in their offense. Warren is struggling in his second season with the Colts compared to his breakout performance his rookie year. He still leads the team with 40 receptions and 276 yards… and is still on the roster. With Azeez Al-Shaair on the injured reserve, Pitre will be tasked with covering Warren down the field. Whether this season is lost or not, Pitre’s presence on the defense will give this team hope.

title: Houston Texans vs Indianapolis Colts: Predictions
summary: Here we have 2 teams both racing for the basement – the 3-7 Indianapolis Colts and the 3-6 Houston Texans. The Colts traded away most of their key players to start a rebuild, while the Texans trotted out a failed offensive scheme and altered the winning defensive scheme from 2025. 1 team wants to lose, […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 17: C.J. Stroud #7 of the Houston Texans runs withe ball during the second half against the Indianapolis Colts at NRG Stadium on September 17, 2023 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Bob Levey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here we have 2 teams both racing for the basement – the 3-7 Indianapolis Colts and the 3-6 Houston Texans. The Colts traded away most of their key players to start a rebuild, while the Texans trotted out a failed offensive scheme and altered the winning defensive scheme from 2025. 1 team wants to lose, the other wants to win – but loses anyway. The baby horses currently lead the all-time series, 33-15-1 thanks in great part to the Peyton Manning/Marvin Harrison Sr. years. However, Houston has won 5 of past 6, thanks to the Colts no longer showing interest in winning football. On paper, as of this writing, the Texans should absolutely dominate this game – and very well may. H-Town QB C.J. Stroud is having an MVP season. The Houston wide receiver corps is one of the best in the league – including the son of the aforementioned Harrison Sr.. Their run game ran away when Joe Mixon suffered the mystery of the ages injury in 2024, but Stroud has still managed to find ways to complete 201 passes for 2462 yards, 19 touchdowns and only 3 INTs. The offensive line remains offensive, mostly, but has had just enough get-in-the-way-ness to give Stroud time to throw. Currently, the Texans passing attack is 4th overall. Texans are huge home favorites this week. 👀 The Colts took the first matchup 19-17. pic.twitter.com/wFLRC8NoQz — Caesars Sportsbook (@CaesarsSports) November 18, 2026 Defensively, Houston has the horsepower to compete at an elite level, but due to off-coverage, injuries and what looks to be confusion with the gameplan, they’re currently ranked 20th. Some believe it’s a little too much “read your own press coverage”, others blame coaching and play calling. In some ways it seems a desire to change up from last season to keep opponents guessing has taken this defense away from what they do best. If you’re great at zigging, but decide to zag all the time cause you think your opponent is expecting the zig, then you need to be ok with ignoring your own strengths… We won’t talk about the special teams… #ulcerinducing Meanwhile, over in the baby horse stable, the Colts are clearly trotting down the rebuild trail. So far in 2026 Indy has: A new owner who has taken direct control over the coaching staff An interim general manager (after firing their previous one late last month) Quenton Nelson: Traded to the Seattle Seahawks. DeForest Buckner: Traded to the San Francisco 49ers. Josh Downs: Traded to the Kansas City Chiefs. Keenan Allen: Traded to the San Francisco 49ers. And managed to win 1 game since all these team-affecting moves. Their current goal seems to be the #1 draft pick, if the Los Angeles Chargers don’t beat them to it. Colts vs Texans predictions: In true Houston Texans fashion, the Texans will beat an opponent who doesn’t want to win. Just as they did to the aforementioned Chargers. The 2026 brand of Texans football doesn’t defeat winning teams (exception: the Jacksonville Jaguars cause, #Glitter). They do, however, lose the battle to not win – meaning when an opponent wants to lose, they freely allow H-Town to go to town on them. Which will happen again tonight. Stroud will look like an MVP candidate on a national stage. The Colts will show all their dysfunction. And the talking heads will ignore the apparent incoming mutiny on Kirby Drive. Indianapolis Colts 13 Houston Texans 38 Those with a superficial knowledge of the Texans will beat the drum that they still have a shot at the playoffs, and how they’ve fixed their issues. Until the following week when they lose against the Baltimore Ravens at the end of the month. Meanwhile, those who do lift the hood and look beyond the check engine light glaring on this franchise’s dashboard will see a different prediction: The end game pot is on the stove, simmering away. Chances are tonight will turn the burn down just long enough to have a nice Thanksgiving.
author: Mike Bullock

title: BREAKING: Indianapolis Colts Cut Starting Quarterback Daniel Jones
summary: This is not April Fools day and yes the Colts have officially announced this move: Daniel Jones’ play this season has been less than inspiring, having posted more than half a season of, frankly, replacement level play. Last night against the Houston Texans Jones went 12 for 27 (44%) for 144 yards 0 touchdowns and […]
full_text: This is not April Fools day and yes the Colts have officially announced this move: Per Shane Steichen, we have released QB Daniel Jones. pic.twitter.com/jdGAZqj9ZI — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) November 20, 2026 Daniel Jones’ play this season has been less than inspiring, having posted more than half a season of, frankly, replacement level play. Last night against the Houston Texans Jones went 12 for 27 (44%) for 144 yards 0 touchdowns and 1 interception. He was also sacked twice, once in the endzone for a safety. On the season he is completing 58.4% of his throws, has thrown for 1974 yards (179.5 per game), 7 touchdowns and 13 interceptions. His 13 interceptions currently lead the NFL. In the past several weeks questions have intensified surrounding Jones’ status as the starting quarterback, with head coach Shane Steichen changing his tune three weeks ago from “Daniel Jones is our starter” to “He’s our starter, right now” and finally to “We will evaluate everything”. In the past Steichen has seemed unwilling to criticize Jones publicly the way he has other quarterbacks in the past, that also changed last night telling reporters that Jones needed to do some things and just play better. Now this. Jones ends his Colts career with a career win-loss record of 11-13. His legacy here will be the same as just one of the many faces Indianapolis has brought in following Andrew Luck’s sudden retirement. Jones’ start in 2025 was amongst the most fun and most successful stretch of games the Colts had played in nearly a decade, but following a broken tibia and torn Achilles, Jones play, nor the team around him were able to find the magic that carried them through the first half of 2025. Thus far we do not know what led to Jones’ release, it is a drastic leap from benching a starting quarterback after week 11 to outright cutting him from the team, but here we are. It is easy to speculate, however, that Steichen informed Jones that he was being benched and Jones instead asked for his release. A move Jones has pulled before when the same scenario played out when his time with the New York Giants came to an end. This is speculation but it seems, at this time, to be the most likely scenario given what we know. By making this move now, the team will save money against their cap, but not as much as had they waited until post June 1, 2027: Colts Cap Space added by releasing Jones now: 2026: +$5m 2027: +$11.6m 2028: +$26.4m Doesn’t save as much 2027 cap as waiting for post June 1st cut in 2027, but gives the Colts the added cap for the start of Free Agency rather than the post June 1st wave of FA. https://t.co/aKEkrEq2tU — Jay Robins (@TheJayRobins) November 20, 2026 This isn’t something the team would have done under normal circumstances. Never in my life have I ever seen a player react this way, multiple times, to a demotion but Daniel Jones seems to be the first. Stay tuned as this story develops and the rest of this lost season plays out.

title: The Colts should “evaluate” Shane Steichen
summary: “We’ll evaluate everything.” Have you heard that before? It’s becoming a canned phrase and mantra for Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen. The most recent example comes after the Colts were ripped apart by the Houston Texans on Thursday Night Football. That’s a smart move, Shane. Maybe the Colts organization needs to do the same […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 19: Head coach Shane Steichen of the Indianapolis Colts looks on against the Houston Texans during the fourth quarter of the game at Reliant Stadium on November 19, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images “We’ll evaluate everything.” Have you heard that before? It’s becoming a canned phrase and mantra for Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen. The most recent example comes after the Colts were ripped apart by the Houston Texans on Thursday Night Football. That’s a smart move, Shane. Maybe the Colts organization needs to do the same for you too. The Colts sit at 3-8 on the year, and Steichen’s overall record is 28-34. The man who was brought in due to his success with Jalen Hurts and the Philadelphia offense was unable to mold Anthony Richardson in the same fashion or create results. Zero postseason appearances and a 7-25 record when the opponent is over .500 make the case why he needs to be heavily scrutinized. It is wise to consider benching Daniel Jones. Does it get better? Maybe not. That’s on Chris Ballard and Steichen, however. Steichen had a choice between the two men at quarterback. Not that his options were necessarily glowing, but he picked Jones to be his guy. From the onset, it looked like a stroke of genius. Now, it looks disastrous. He can evaluate all he wants. The Colts organization should do the same. It isn’t just Steichen, but it starts there. Based on the last four years of data, the case can be made that a change in leadership is needed. Evaluating is normally a good thing. What can trip one up is the timing. Shane Steichen’s “evaluation” of Daniel Jones and the quarterback position might be too little, too late to save his job. Steichen’s time with the franchise might be drawing to a close, but the Colts organization will live on. Their time for evaluation is now. It starts with the head coach.

title: Colts surrender 26 unanswered points as Daniel Jones benched in blowout road loss to Texans
summary: Houston, the problem here is the Indianapolis Colts offense is broken and has not reached the end zone in 17 consecutive drives. In their final primetime appearance on Thursday Night Football, the Colts surrendered 26 unanswered points in a 26-3 blowout loss to the rival Houston Texans. Outside of the opening drive, there was nothing […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 19: Nico Collins #12 of the Houston Texans catches a 42 yard touchdown pass against Indianapolis Colts cornerback Justin Walley during the first quarter of the game at Reliant Stadium on November 19, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Houston, the problem here is the Indianapolis Colts offense is broken and has not reached the end zone in 17 consecutive drives. In their final primetime appearance on Thursday Night Football, the Colts surrendered 26 unanswered points in a 26-3 blowout loss to the rival Houston Texans. Outside of the opening drive, there was nothing left from this depleted offensive unit. Backup quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. relieved Daniel Jones for the final eight minutes of regulation. Richardson trucked Texans’ linebacker Jake Hansen on his first snap for a minimal two yards, then nearly delivered Houston an interception before another anticlimactic three-and-out ended his night. The Colts were poised to establish an early offensive rhythm after rookie Seth McGowan returned the opening kickoff to the 40. Jones found receiver Ashton Dulin wide open on a sit route against Houston’s zone coverage, allowing the speedster to bounce outside and race to the sideline for 25 yards. McGowan followed with a tough run up the middle for eight yards, then Jonathan Taylor was patient enough to let a hole develop and surge forward to move the chains. Texans’ defensive tackle Logan Hall blew up McGowan’s next run in the backfield, then Jones was forced to throw the ball away on third down. The Colts settled for an early chip shot as kicker Spencer Shrader connected on a 34-yard field goal to give Indianapolis its lone lead. The Texans opened with a promising drive, but a forced pass ricocheted into an early break for the Colts. C.J. Stroud’s throw bounced off the helmet of rookie safety AJ Haulcy before it tipped off Cam Bynum’s hands and back into Haulcy’s grasp for his first career interception. AJ HAULCY!!! 📺 Prime pic.twitter.com/tbGSSROK37 — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) November 20, 2026 Indianapolis could not have asked for a better start as Jones recognized the underneath coverage, went through his progressions and fired a dart down the sideline to receiver Quez Watkins for a 26-yard completion to march right back into Houston territory. The drive stalled after a dropped pass by Taylor was followed by a pass deflection from Hansen, then All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson chased down Jones and forced him to get rid of it out of bounds. The Colts intended to settle for a kick near midfield, but Shrader’s 56-yarder was shanked wide left. Despite taking a hit to his right bicep from Colts’ defensive back Kapena Gushiken, Stroud stepped up into the pocket and launched a missile down the right sideline to receiver Nico Collins, who elevated over cornerback Justin Walley to haul in a 42-yard touchdown and put Houston ahead 7-3 late in the first frame. The Colts’ next possession unraveled inside of Texans’ territory after receiver Anthony Gould took a bubble pass through a hole on the field side for 31 yards. Jones’ next pass would have been picked off if Texans cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. weren’t out of bounds. On the first play of the second quarter, Jones tossed up a meatball sub into double coverage to avoid the sack and was picked off by cornerback Kamari Lassiter over rookie Deion Burks. Jones finished 12-for-27 for 144 pass yards and one interception, the sixth straight game he’s thrown an interception. Shane Steichen has continued to rely on the eighth-year veteran, despite leading the NFL with 15 turnovers and never finishing a single game with more touchdowns than turnovers this season. The Texans mounted a pair of long drives in the second quarter as Stroud shared the wealth with five different pass-catchers. Facing third-and-2 from just outside the red zone, Stroud delivered a perfect post to Kayshon Boutte near the goal line. Boutte rose over cornerback Kenneth Harris to secure the contested 24-yard touchdown catch, extending Houston’s lead to 14-3 midway through the second quarter. The Texans were able to capitalize on a choice to send Shrader out for a 62-yard field goal attempt, which was blocked by Hall to seize possession inside Colts territory. Houston leaned on its run game to drain most of the remaining clock before settling for a 27-yard chip shot from Ka’imi Fairbairn to take a 17-3 lead into halftime. The stampede found some life to start the second half as defensive tackle Adetomiwa Adebawore rushed past the left guard to corral Stroud from behind and secure his team-high fifth sack this season, sending Houston behind the sticks. Houston would avenge the hit on Stroud after a precision punt pinned Indianapolis inside its own 5-yard-line as Anderson rushed inside of right tackle Matt Goncalves to sack Jones in the end zone for a safety. Tomi time. 💥 📺Prime pic.twitter.com/PNQEQjK2zn — Indianapolis Colts (@Colts) November 20, 2026 The Texans took advantage of the short field as Stroud connected with Tank Dell on three consecutive throws for a combined 27 yards to breach the red zone. Houston’s offensive line gave Stroud a full seven seconds to scramble outside of the pocket, find tight end Marlin Klein near the pylon for a 13-yard TD that capped off a 12-play drive to seal the first home win for Houston. The Colts could never get their rushing attack in any rhythm, held to just 38 rushing yards on 17 attempts. The rookies continued to impress on the defensive side as C.J. Allen led the game with 16 tackles, while Haulcy forced the takeaway to terminate Houston’s opening drive. Indianapolis (3-8) enters its bye week for Thanksgiving, with 10 days to prepare to host the New York Giants (5-3-1) at Lucas Oil Stadium on Nov. 29.

title: Struggling Colts should start Anthony Richardson Sr. at QB the rest of the 2026 campaign
summary: The consensus among Indianapolis Colts fans seems to be that this current rendition of Daniel Jones should no longer be the starting quarterback for the franchise. After leading the Colts to an 8-2 start last year, at the helm of a historically elite offense at the time, the wheels have quickly come off for Jones […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 15: Anthony Richardson Sr. #5 of the Indianapolis Colts looks on against the Miami Dolphins during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The consensus among Indianapolis Colts fans seems to be that this current rendition of Daniel Jones should no longer be the starting quarterback for the franchise. After leading the Colts to an 8-2 start last year, at the helm of a historically elite offense at the time, the wheels have quickly come off for Jones and the franchise. Cracks of vulnerability were beginning to show even before Jones suffered critical injuries late last season, including a fractured fibula and season-ending torn Achilles. Most notably, opposing defenses began to blitz Jones at a higher rate, and started having a greater deal of success. Jones continues to be pass pressured at a high rate , and while there may be some expected physical limitations, still working his way back less than a year removed from the torn Achilles, Jones’ regression doesn’t appear to be all physical—as his mental processing and decision-making in-game has also relapsed. He much more closely resembles the turnover prone former failed franchise quarterback hopeful for the New York Giants, than the breakout Pro Bowler that Colts fans saw firsthand for the first half of the 2025 campaign. Embattled Colts head coach Shane Steichen values the much maligned Jones’ continued leadership, preparation, and understanding of the offense, but his on-the-field production so far this season for the 3-7 Colts stinks: Completion rate: 59.6 (28th) Passing yards: 1,830 (19th) Yards Per Attempt: 5.6 (31st) Yards Per Catch: 9.5 (29th) Interceptions: 12 (1st most) Sacks: 25 (6th most) EPA per play: -0.173 (30th) ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler recently reported that Steichen sticking with Jones , despite his continued struggles, may speak more to the lack of viable quarterback options behind him: Colts head coach Shane Steichen’s loyalty to Daniel Jones might be less about Jones’ poor performance and more about the options behind him. As it was told to me, Steichen simply is not motivated to play Anthony Richardson Sr., the 2023 fourth overall pick who fell out of favor after a strong start to his rookie year. Richardson and No. 3 quarterback Riley Leonard did not have strong training camps in the Colts’ view, and it seems that has carried over. Richardson, a 2027 free agent, badly needs a fresh start elsewhere but appears poised for spot duty in Indy at some point this year, given the team’s 3-7 record and its trading away of four key players before the deadline. But I just don’t see Steichen benching Jones right now unless absolutely necessary. That being said, if Steichen doesn’t believe that Richardson can even supplant this clearly spiraling version of Jones, then what was the point of even keeping him on as the primary backup? They should’ve just moved him. Furthermore, even if Richardson Sr. didn’t have a particularly strong 2026 training camp, neither did Jones in 2025 Colts training camp when he won the starting job from Richardson Sr. and was named the new starter just weeks before the regular season started. If anything, Richardson Sr. was arguably the stronger on-the-field performer in 2025 camp, whereas Jones won the job because of his off the field study and practice habits, and mental understanding of Steichen’s offense. I’m not saying Richardson Sr. is going to be the savior either, but at the very least, he could potentially provide this stalling passing offense a much needed spark, especially with his big arm and willingness to throw the ball downfield—which at the very least, is more exciting offense than the “Charlie Checkdown” Jones we’ve seen. For a team on a short week missing its two starting offensive tackles, and facing Houston Texans All-Pro pass rusher Will Anderson Jr. on Thursday night, Richardson Sr. could also provide much needed mobility and escapability in the passing pocket, while making the Colts ground game more dynamic and versatile, and harder to defend and predict for the opposing defense. Coming off the Achilles, this current version of Jones hasn’t looked nearly as explosive or comfortable running with the football, so Richardson Sr.‘s improved mobility would be a significant upgrade in that regard. I’m just having a tough time with this one because Jones starting for the 2026 Colts has clearly run its course, and it’s hard to see how starting Richardson Sr. could be any worse. The status quo at QB isn’t working. At the very least too, it provides the Colts, who are clearly going nowhere fast, one last extended look at the 24-year-old Richardson Sr., to see if he’s made any significant jumps in passing accuracy and progression of reads, and safely close the chapter on his time here—should he falter again.

I just want him to hopefully feel a little bit better as we go.” Limited RB LeQuint Allen Jr. (hamstring) DT Matt Dickerson (neck) S Antonio Johnson (ankle) WR Jakobi Meyers (ankle) RB Chris Rodriguez Jr. (hand) DE Jalen McLeod (groin) C Jonah Monheim (ankle) DE Danny Striggow (concussion) DE Travon Walker (rib) Full participation DE BJ Green II (forearm): Green practiced fully again after doing so all of last week. title: Jaguars vs Giants key matchups: Bates with tough debut assignment
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars head to MetLife Stadium on Sunday looking to extend their winning streak to four games when they take on the New York Giants. Liam Coen’s team has moved to 7-2 following three consecutive victories, while the 5-3-1 Giants will provide another significant test as Jacksonville looks to maintain its position at the […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 11: Jessie Bates III #0 of Jacksonville Jaguars warms up during an NFL football practice at the Miller Electric Center on November 11, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars head to MetLife Stadium on Sunday looking to extend their winning streak to four games when they take on the New York Giants. Liam Coen’s team has moved to 7-2 following three consecutive victories, while the 5-3-1 Giants will provide another significant test as Jacksonville looks to maintain its position at the top of the AFC South. The Jaguars have been productive on both sides of the ball, averaging just under 30 points per game through nine contests. There are several intriguing individual battles to watch this weekend, but these three could have a particularly significant influence on the outcome. Bhayshul Tuten vs. the Giants’ run defense Tuten TD and the team celly 😂 JAXvsTEN on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/EaTKrPwprj — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Bhayshul Tuten has established himself as a major part of Jacksonville’s offensive identity in his second NFL season. The 2025 fourth-round selection has taken on an increasingly important workload, recording 609 rushing yards and five touchdowns on 148 carries through nine games. He has also contributed 18 receptions for 206 yards and three receiving touchdowns. Tuten has been particularly productive over Jacksonville’s last three games, rushing for 221 yards and three touchdowns. His 104-yard performance against Indianapolis in Week 8 was backed up with another 88 yards in last Sunday’s victory over Tennessee . The 26 carries he received against the Titans also demonstrated the confidence the coaching staff has in him as the lead back. The Giants have been relatively vulnerable against the run, allowing 1,094 rushing yards through nine games. That works out at 121.6 yards per contest, with opposing runners averaging 4.5 yards per carry. New York will need to improve that production if it is to prevent Tuten from controlling the tempo of the game. There is an injury consideration, too. Tuten appeared on the Wednesday injury report with an ankle/foot issue and was limited in practice. His availability and workload are worth monitoring as the week progresses, particularly given the importance of his role in Jacksonville’s offense. But if he’s good to go, the Jags’ could and should ride him to victory. Malik Nabers vs. Jessie Bates III and the Jaguars’ secondary "Just go cut it loose, let it rip, go be you. Go be who got you here." Coach Coen on Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis' first game as Jaguars. pic.twitter.com/IDfBIXsau1 — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) November 18, 2026 Malik Nabers remains the Giants’ most dangerous receiving weapon. Through nine games, the wide receiver has caught 58 passes for 692 yards and two touchdowns, making him a central part of New York’s passing attack. Containing Nabers will be a significant challenge for a Jacksonville secondary that has made a habit of creating turnovers. The Jaguars have recorded 12 interceptions this season, ranking third in the NFL, while their +9 turnover differential leads the league. They have shown an ability to turn defensive opportunities into possessions for Trevor Lawrence and the offense. The addition of Jessie Bates III gives Jacksonville another experienced playmaker in the secondary. However, this will be an important first outing for the safety in a Jaguars uniform. Bates and fellow newcomer Jordan Davis were rested for the Week 10 game against Tennessee after joining a team that had already taken its bye week, meaning Sunday should mark Bates’ Jacksonville debut. It would be misleading to frame this as a simple man-to-man matchup: Bates is a safety rather than a cornerback who will necessarily follow Nabers around the field. His positioning, communication and ability to provide help over the top could nevertheless be crucial in limiting the receiver’s opportunities for explosive plays. If the Jaguars can force New York into uncomfortable passing situations and make Nabers work for every reception, they will have a good chance of continuing their impressive turnover production. Jonah Monheim vs. the Giants’ Pass Rush "I've got all the confidence in the world in him." Trevor Lawrence on Jonah Monheim stepping up. pic.twitter.com/Vf764iKy5d — Jacksonville Jaguars (@Jaguars) November 15, 2026 Jacksonville’s offensive line faces a difficult assignment following the loss of starting center Robert Hainsey. Hainsey sustained a knee injury during the victory over Tennessee and has been ruled out for Sunday’s game, leaving Jonah Monheim to take over at center. Monheim is a second-year player who was selected by Jacksonville in the seventh round of the 2025 NFL Draft. He has already made two career starts, but Sunday’s contest will be his first start of the 2026 season. He replaced Hainsey late in the Tennessee game and will now be responsible for helping organise the protection against a dangerous New York defensive front. The Giants have recorded 28 sacks through nine games, with rookie linebacker Arvell Reese leading the way individually with 4.5. Reese was particularly disruptive in the Week 9 victory over Philadelphia, recording three sacks and forcing a fumble. New York’s ability to generate pressure from different areas of the defense makes this a challenging first start of the season for Monheim. Jacksonville has allowed just 14 sacks through nine games, a strong record that it will be keen to maintain. Trevor Lawrence has thrown for 2,284 yards and 21 touchdowns, and giving him time to operate will be essential if the Jaguars are to exploit New York’s defense. Monheim will have to communicate effectively with the rest of the offensive line, identify pressure and help keep Reese and the Giants’ pass rush away from Lawrence. Considering his lowly draft selection and rookie status, he was a pleasant surprise when asked to step in last year. If Jacksonville can maintain its protection standards despite the change at center, it will give its offense a much better chance of controlling the game.

title: Chiefs-Cardinals Week 11 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride
summary: It’s time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs host the Arizona Cardinals, our writers predicted the final score and result. Arizona has found nothing but tough times in 2026. They have moved on from wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. — once considered a generational draft […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs host the Arizona Cardinals , our writers predicted the final score and result. Arizona has found nothing but tough times in 2026. They have moved on from wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. — once considered a generational draft prospect. Then, they saw their top wide receiver Michael Wilson lost for the season due to a neck injury. After trading away Week 1 starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett, the Cardinals have entrusted the offense to rookie Carson Beck — although he is dealing with back spasms and may hand the reins to veteran Josh Johnson . FanDuel Sportsbook currently lists the Chiefs as massive 15.5-point home favorites. After the Chiefs comfortably won their Week 10 game against the Atlanta Falcons , the Cardinals were on the wrong side of a 34-6 home blowout against the Los Angeles Rams . This will be Arizona’s first regular season trip to Arrowhead Stadium since 2018 — when a quarterback named Patrick Mahomes made his 11th career start. We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) The version of the Chiefs we saw in the second half both against the Falcons and the New York Jets the week before could hang 50 on Arizona if they wanted to. With a Thursday showdown with the Buffalo Bills looming, however, the bigger priority will be to shorten the game and minimize injury risk. I think the Chiefs will build a game plan around Emmett Johnson that prioritizes a moving clock. A low number of total possessions will keep this one from getting completely out of hand. Chiefs 24, Cardinals 9 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) On Sunday, the Chiefs need to come in and quickly take care of business against the Cardinals, with much larger games on the horizon. Despite the Cardinals’ tight end Trey McBride being outstanding, the Chiefs defense should not have any issues handling the Cardinals’ offense. I would look for Steve Spagnuolo to dial up the pressure early and often to try to force turnovers. The Chiefs are coming off a monster offensive showing against the Atlanta Falcons, but they could be down the entire right side of their offensive line with Trey Smith and Jaylon Moore both not practicing on Wednesday. Kenneth Walker will likely sit as well, giving Emmet Johnson the green light for another big day against the league’s 28th-ranked run defense. Get in, get out, stay healthy. Chiefs 27, Cardinals 6 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) I’ve got the Chiefs beating the Cardinals because I trust Mahomes and Andy Reid to find answers if the offense starts slow. And if Steve Spagnuolo gets Arizona into third-and-long and can turn Chris Jones loose, I don’t see the Cardinals putting up enough points to keep up. Chiefs 38, Cardinals 13 Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) The Chiefs should take care of business against Arizona, and with a Thanksgiving trip to Buffalo approaching, this is a game they need to control early. The Cardinals are tied for 31st in points allowed, while Kansas City has scored at least 30 in five of its seven wins. What I’ve liked about the Chiefs lately is that they’ve finished off struggling opponents instead of letting them hang around. I expect that to continue Sunday, with Steve Spagnuolo disguising coverages and creating problems for Arizona’s offense with whoever is playing quarterback. I expect Kansas City to give Kenneth Walker III another week to recover, leaving Emmett Johnson with another opportunity to carry the load after his impressive first start. The ideal outcome is building a comfortable lead by the third quarter and giving the starters some rest before the short turnaround to Buffalo. The Chiefs still have to earn that opportunity, but this is a matchup they should control on both sides of the ball. I expect another convincing win. Chiefs 31, Cardinals 13 Matt Stagner ( @stagdsp ) This Chiefs vs Cardinals matchup could’ve been interesting. Arizona has the top TE in the game, and has recently drafted generational prospects at WR and RB. But, alas, injuries and issues have led the Cards to only 3 wins this season– and number 4 may have to wait. It’s a matchup of a Chiefs offense that’s rediscovered the deep pass and the run game vs a Cards defense that can’t stop either one. Look for a big game from more than one Chiefs receiver this week, and I’d choosing Emmett on whatever gambling site you like. Expect multiple sacks and turnovers from the defense this week before they head into tougher games in the coming weeks. Chiefs 42, Cardinals 17 Dakota Watson ( @D_Watson56 ) I see this as the last of the “warm-up series” before the brutal stretch beginning on Thanksgiving. The Chiefs have to take care of business on Sunday. My only real concern is tight end Trey McBride feasting in the middle of the field against the Chiefs’ defense. I have no qualms with giving Travis Kelce and Kenneth Walker a week of low volume or rest going into the clash against the Bills. I’m confident in this one. Chiefs 31, Cardinals 14 Rocky Magana ( @RockyMagana ) The Chiefs are only -15.5 favorites in this game. If it’s one thing we know about Kansas City, it’s that they roll bad teams. And make no mistake: the Arizona Cardinals are horrible. Here is a little test for you: see if you can name 4 starters on the Cardinals who are currently healthy. Could you do it? Did you name more than five? If so, you’re a football sicko who needs to go outside and touch grass. This team’s depth chart reads like a football video game where they didn’t get the NFLPA naming rights to the players. The Chiefs are going to stomp another bird team for a second straight week. Chiefs 35, Cardinals 10 Nate Christensen The Cardinals had some competitive moments to start the year, but they’re more injured now and turned to rookie quarterback Carson Beck for the remainder of the year (until back spasms this week; it may be veteran journeyman Josh Johnson starting on Sunday). The early returns on that have been poor, and I expect that to continue. I expect a pretty conservative game from the Chiefs to keep guys healthy and not show too much before Thursday’s game vs the Bills, but the Cardinals won’t be able to do enough to keep up. Chiefs 23, Cardinals 9 Ron Kopp Jr. ( @RonOnChiefs ) This feels like the least-competitive game of the Chiefs’ season — and that was before reports surfaced that the Cardinals are likely starting veteran journeyman Josh Johnson at quarterback; he signed with the team less than two weeks ago. I see Kansas City coasting to victory in eerily similar fashion as the last two weeks. title: Kingdom Keys: 3 Keys to a Chiefs victory over the Cardinals in Week 11
summary: Kansas City hosts the injury-depleted Arizona Cardinals on Sunday in what should be another very winnable game. The Chiefs are 7-2 and tied with the Denver Broncos atop the AFC West, one game behind the Buffalo Bills in the race for the AFC’s No. 1 seed. Arizona is 3-7, has lost consecutive games, and is […]
full_text: (Photo by Peter Aiken/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kansas City hosts the injury-depleted Arizona Cardinals on Sunday in what should be another very winnable game. The Chiefs are 7-2 and tied with the Denver Broncos atop the AFC West, one game behind the Buffalo Bills in the race for the AFC’s No. 1 seed. Arizona is 3-7, has lost consecutive games, and is coming off a 34-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams . After Sunday, Kansas City begins a five-game stretch against Buffalo, the Los Angeles Rams , Cincinnati , New England and San Francisco. The first three games of that stretch will be on the road, beginning with a Thanksgiving night matchup against the Bills just four days after the Cardinals game. The Chiefs cannot afford to overlook Arizona, but they should use this matchup to prepare themselves for what is coming. Here are three Kingdom Keys to a Chiefs victory. Offensive key: Keep building chemistry with the wide receivers. Kansas City’s wide receivers delivered their best collective performance of the season against Atlanta. Rashee Rice, Josh Downs, Cyrus Allen, and Andrew Armstrong combined for 12 receptions, 222 yards and three touchdowns. Rice led the group with five catches for 82 yards, while Downs caught four passes for 53 yards and a touchdown in his Chiefs debut. Allen and Armstrong also delivered explosive touchdown receptions of 39 and 43 yards, respectively. The receivers accounted for nearly 64% of Patrick Mahomes’ 348 passing yards and three of his five touchdown passes. That production must become the start of a trend rather than a one-game explosion. Downs had only two full practices with Mahomes before the Atlanta game. Sunday offers another chance to build that connection while continuing to define roles for Rice, Allen and Armstrong. It would also be encouraging to get Worthy involved after he went without a reception on three targets against the Falcons. Arizona presents an ideal matchup for that continued growth. The Cardinals have allowed 22 passing touchdowns — tied for the second-most in the NFL — and are surrendering 28.9 points per game. The Chiefs will need their receivers during the upcoming stretch against several playoff contenders. Buffalo, Los Angeles, Cincinnati, New England and San Francisco will all have defensive plans designed to slow Kansas City’s running game and force the receivers to win their matchups. Another combined 150-yard performance from the wide-receiver room would qualify as a successful afternoon. More importantly, Kansas City needs the group to keep building timing and trust with Mahomes before the schedule’s difficulty increases. Defensive key: Force Carson Beck into multiple turnovers The Chiefs’ defense has been one of the league’s best at keeping opponents out of the end zone. Kansas City is allowing only 17.3 points per game, third-best in the NFL, and has surrendered just 13 touchdowns through nine games. The defense has also generated 13 takeaways and owns a plus-six turnover differential. This week should provide an opportunity to add to that total. Arizona traded Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans in October and dealt veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore before the trade deadline. Starting quarterback Gardner Minshew II, rookie running back Jeremiyah Love and wide receivers Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne are among the Cardinals currently on injured reserve. Arizona has 16 players on injury lists, tied for the most in the league. Trey McBride remains a dangerous target at tight end, but Arizona’s offense is otherwise relying heavily on inexperienced players and reserves. Rookie quarterback Carson Beck will make his second NFL start after struggling against the Rams. Beck completed 11 of 18 passes for 108 yards, threw two interceptions, lost a fumble and was sacked five times. Arizona finished with only 123 total yards and failed to convert any of its six third-down opportunities. Steve Spagnuolo should disguise coverages, change the picture after the snap and force Beck to process quickly. Pressure will be important, but the defensive backs must also capitalize when the rookie puts the football in danger. The Chiefs forced two turnovers against Atlanta. Reaching that number again should be the defensive benchmark against Arizona. X-factor: Win early and protect the roster The X-factor is not simply winning the game. It is winning efficiently enough to protect the roster for what comes next. Kansas City already has several important players dealing with injuries. Kenneth Walker III missed the Atlanta game with a groin injury, while Trey Smith remains in the concussion protocol and Jaylon Moore is working through an ankle injury. Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice have also appeared on the injury report, although each practiced fully on Wednesday. The Chiefs cannot control whether every player avoids injury, but they can reduce unnecessary exposure by taking command of the game early. Kansas City should aim to establish a three-score advantage by the middle of the third quarter. That would give Andy Reid an opportunity to reduce the workloads of Mahomes, Kelce, Rice, Chris Jones and other important veterans during the second half. This is particularly important because the Chiefs will have only four days to prepare for Buffalo. After that Thanksgiving matchup, they will remain on the road to face the Rams the following Thursday and Cincinnati 10 days later. The Chiefs cannot let Arizona hang around into the fourth quarter. A comfortable lead would allow them to rest starters, give younger players valuable snaps and begin shifting their attention toward the most demanding portion of their schedule. The bottom line The Cardinals’ record and depleted roster make this a game Kansas City should control, but its importance extends beyond one victory. The Chiefs need another strong showing from their wide receivers as they continue building chemistry for the upcoming gauntlet. Defensively, they should exploit an inexperienced quarterback and force at least two turnovers. Most importantly, Kansas City needs to build an early lead and get its most valuable players off the field once the result is secure. If the Chiefs accomplish those three things, they should improve to 8-2 while entering their Thanksgiving showdown with Buffalo healthy, confident and still positioned to compete for the AFC’s No. 1 seed.

full_text: On Sunday, the (7-2) Kansas City Chiefs are back at Arrowhead taking on the (3-7) Arizona Cardinals . Let’s see how the game plays out in Madden NFL 2 7. Note: Madden simulation is 7-2 this season, predicting the outcome. STOP! If you want to watch the simulation without spoilers, start this video — or if you can’t see it, click here . First quarter The Chiefs’ opening drive stalled after Walter Nolen III sacked Patrick Mahomes. Kansas City went three-and-out and punted the ball to Arizona. The Cardinals managed just five yards on their opening possession before punting it right back to the Chiefs. Emmett Johnson helped Kansas City get a first down, but the drive stalled, forcing another Matt Araiza punt. Midway through the quarter, linebacker Nick Bolton exited the game with an injury. Arizona also managed to pick up a first down behind running back Tyler Allgeier, but the drive went nowhere, forcing another punt. The Chiefs punted. The Cardinals punted. Zaven Collins sacked Mahomes to close out the quarter. End of first quarter: Chiefs 0, Cardinals 0 Second quarter Kai’Trel Clark intercepted Mahomes to open the quarter, giving the Cardinals possession at the Chiefs’ 36-yard line. Arizona capitalized on the turnover as kicker Chad Ryland drilled a 34-yard field goal to open the scoring in Kansas City. Emmett Johnson responded with a 16-yard run, moving the Chiefs to the Cardinals’ 36-yard line. Nolen III would once again get to Mahomes, recording another sack on a crucial third down. Despite some trouble with the snap, Harrison Butker connected on a 53-yard field goal to tie the game. On the Cardinals’ next possession, Chris Jones blew up the middle of the offensive line to sack Carson Beck and force a third-and-long situation. However, Arizona converted as Beck found Trey McBride on a dig route to move the chains. Chamari Conner got in on the sack action on the following set of downs, forcing the Cardinals to punt. With under two minutes remaining in the half, the Chiefs’ offense finally started clicking. Mahomes connected with Rashee Rice and Jalen Royals to help Kansas City pick up multiple first downs. At the Cardinals’ 14-yard line, Mahomes found Josh Downs, who was making his Arrowhead debut. Downs caught a designed pass on the right side of the field and found himself untouched as he crossed the goal line for the game’s first touchdown. Khyiris Tonga recorded a sack on Beck to close out the half. End of second quarter: Chiefs 10, Cardinals 3 Third quarter George Karlaftis opened the second half with a sack on Beck, forcing another Cardinals punt. Mahomes connected with Downs for a 13-yard gain to get the Chiefs to the Cardinals’ 34-yard line. However, Max Melton intercepted a pass intended for Downs, ending the Chiefs’ scoring opportunity. Welcome back, Nick Bolton! The linebacker came flying in like a heat-seeking missile to sack Beck on third down, forcing yet another Cardinals punt. On third-and-10 at the Cardinals’ 22-yard line, Mahomes rolled out to his right and found Travis Kelce running toward the end zone. Kelce made a defender miss and crossed the goal line for a touchdown, giving Kansas City a two-possession lead. End of third quarter: Chiefs 17, Cardinals 3 Fourth quarter For the sixth time today, Carson Beck was brought down for a sack. Chris Jones got to the quarterback for his second sack of the afternoon. The Chiefs then marched down the field, methodically draining the clock to under three minutes. Butker capped off the drive with a 44-yard field goal to put Kansas City up by three scores. The Cardinals quickly turned the ball over on downs, giving possession back to Kansas City. Final score: Chiefs 20, Cardinals 3 Notable stats Patrick Mahomes: 26 for 38 passing, 262 yards, 2 touchdowns, 2 interceptions Emmett Johnson: 10 rushing attempts, 42 yards, 5 receptions, 45 yards Rashee Rice: 7 receptions, 77 yards. Travis Kelce: 5 receptions, 49 yards, 1 touchdown. Jalen Royals: 5 receptions, 50 yards. Josh Downs: 4 receptions, 41 yards, 1 touchdown Chris Jones: 2 sacks George Karlaftis: 1 sack Khyiris Tonga: 1 sack Chamarri Conner: 1 sack Nick Bolton: 1 sack Carson Beck: 5 for 18 passing, 34 yards. Tyler Allgeier: 8 rushing attempts, 47 yards, Tyler McBride: 3 receptions, 31 yards. Walter Nolen III: 1.5 sacks Zaven Collins: 1 sack Kei’Trel Clark: 1 interception Max Melton: 1 interception Next week, the Chiefs are back on the road for Thursday Night Football, taking on the Buffalo Bills . Until then, we will see how it plays out inside the EA Universe.

title: Have the Chiefs finally fixed their pass rush?
summary: Sometimes we make defense more complicated than it needs to be. In the modern game, much of an effective defensive unit depends on its ability to get after the quarterback. Look at the top of the leaderboard this year for proof: The (7-2) Minnesota Vikings and the defending champion Seattle Seahawks lead the league in […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) Sometimes we make defense more complicated than it needs to be. In the modern game, much of an effective defensive unit depends on its ability to get after the quarterback. Look at the top of the leaderboard this year for proof: The (7-2) Minnesota Vikings and the defending champion Seattle Seahawks lead the league in pressure rate. The top two defenses in points per drive allowed? You guessed it, the Vikings and the Seahawks. Get after the quarterback, and you’re more likely to get consistent stops. Fail to do so, and it could be a long day. That’s the case for just about every defense in the league. Except the 2026 Kansas City Chiefs , apparently. The Chiefs have been a rare exception to this rule for much of the season. Kansas City currently ranks 26th in sacks, 27th in QB hits, and 29th in pressure rate, according to Pro Football Reference . But, somehow, they miraculously rank 5th in the league in points per drive allowed. It doesn’t really make sense. For much of the season, it’s felt like smoke and mirrors. Some of it can surely be explained by the schedule. Let’s be honest, the Chiefs haven’t exactly faced a murderer’s row of opposing offenses. The Chiefs have made do with a prototypical ‘bend-don’t-break’ defensive approach for much of the season. But the tide seems to be turning over the past couple of weeks. The Chiefs are bending less. The pass rush is getting home more. It’s incredibly rare to win as often as the Chiefs did early this season with the kind of pass rush they were producing. In fact, only seven other teams in the past 15 years won at least 5 of their first 7 games while allowing 9 or fewer sacks in those seven games. The others were the 2025 49ers, the 2020 Titans, the 2018 Patriots, the 2016 Raiders, the 2015 Falcons, the 2014 Cardinals and the 2014 Cowboys. Those teams finished the season ranked 32nd, 30th, 30th, 32nd, 32nd, 24th and 28th in the league, respectively, for sacks in those individual seasons. That’s not exactly a great omen for the 2026 Chiefs. They’ve been trying their darndest the past couple of weeks to buck the trend. Kansas City produced just nine sacks over their first seven games, but they’ve followed that up with an eight-sack outburst over the past two weeks. In fact, if you look at sack yardage lost by the opposition, the Chiefs have pushed their opponents back more (58 yards) over the past two weeks than they did in their first seven weeks combined (39 yards). What’s changed? Well, a combination of everything. For one, edge rusher George Karlaftis has taken his game to an entirely different level. He’s been earning pressures the entire season, but he’s finally converting those pressures into sacks. Karlaftis had 18 pressures and two sacks in his first seven games of the regular season, and he’s 8 pressures and 3.5 sacks over the past two. Part of what’s helped Karlaftis take that step is those around him winning one-on-one battles. Second-year defensive lineman Ashton Gillotte is probably the first name worth mentioning. He produced just two pressures and one sack in his first seven games, according to Pro Football Reference . He has doubled those numbers over the past two games with 2 sacks and 4 pressures. Chris Jones also finally looks like himself again. The future Hall of Famer tallied just three hurries and 0.5 sacks in his first 7 games of the regular season. He’s added 2.5 sacks and 3 pressures over the past couple of weeks. The results are hard to ignore. The Chiefs produced 8 sacks in a 2-game stretch for the first time since December of 2024. It’s worth noting this is a feat the Chiefs accomplished at some point in the 2019, 2022, 2023 and 2024 seasons. They reached the Super Bowl in each of those four years. Could history be repeating itself? Time will tell. This pass rush has been underwhelming far more often than it’s been great this season. But the past two weeks were legitimate signs of life. The Jets and Falcons aren’t great teams, but their offensive lines aren’t awful. Brandon Thorn of Establish the Run is as respected as any offensive line analyst covering the game, and he currently has the Jets ranked as his 12th-best offensive line in the league. He has the Falcons at 19th. Not world beaters, but this wasn’t the Chiefs taking advantage of the early-season Packers MASH unit offensive line. This weekend should set up well for another dominant performance by the Chiefs’ D-Line. The Cardinals’ quarterbacks have been sacked 8 times over the past two weeks. Thorn ranks their offensive line as the third worst in the league. This could be yet another get-right game for the defensive side of the ball before things start to get real. What lies ahead will dictate the Chiefs’ postseason seeding. The Bills (4th), Rams (14th), Bengals (5th), and 49ers (3rd) all have top-half-of-the-league offensive lines, according to Thorn. The Chiefs’ defensive line will have its work cut out for them. The past two weeks have been encouraging. There’s still work to be done. Pressure has been building on this defense to get after the quarterback. It’s nice to see them finally applying some of that pressure to the opposition.

The latest Kansas City Chiefs news ‘Bring Him Back to the Chiefs,’ ‘Chicago Should Be All Over This’ — NFL Fans React As 2-Time Super Bowl Champion Hits Waivers After Getting Released | Pro Football Network Chiefs Fans Want Justin Reid Back in Kansas City The Saints released Reid on Nov. 19, according to Jordan Schultz, with Louisiana Sports’ Ross Jackson independently confirming the move. His departure followed a reduction in playing time in recent weeks. One fan skipped the recruiting presentation altogether. “Bring him back to the Chiefs!”the fan wrote. NFL just gave the Kansas City Chiefs an early Christmas gift during the toughest 3-game stretch of their 2026 schedule | A to Z Sports Multiple reports confirm the league is suspending Rams WR Puka Nacua for three games for violating the personal conduct policy. The violation stems from an altercation during which Nacua allegedly bit a woman and made an antisemitic remark. The suspension is effective immediately, while Nacua remains on injured reserve. He’s eligible for reinstatement on Monday, Dec. 14. The Chiefs face the Rams on Thursday, Dec. 3, which ensures that even if Nacua is healthy, he won’t play in that game. There’s no risk of the suspension being reduced through appeal either. Chiefs, Kansas officials float polarizing PSL blueprint in new stadium documents | The Kansas City Star The new documents, which the authority approved Wednesday, suggest that the team is at least considering selling personal seat licenses, or PSLs, a polarizing pay-to-buy system in which fans purchase licenses for seats in order to later buy season tickets. Under the agreements released this week, the revenue generated from any PSL fees would help the Chiefs pay for construction of the new multibillion-dollar domed stadium and count toward the team’s 40% commitment. The remaining 60% would come from public funds, including supercharged bonds from the state of Kansas. The documents mark the first public revelation that the team is evaluating imposing the fees on fans to help pay for the new stadium — though in previous fan surveys, they have included questions to season-ticket holders about PSLs. Revisiting the Chiefs’ 2026 NFL Draft: Was Kansas City justified in trading up for Mansoor Delane? | CBS Sports Long-term outlook Delane looks like a high-quality long-term starter. Cornerback is an incredibly volatile position year-over-year, and only a small number can maintain a level of excellence in the NFL. Too often, people see a high number of interceptions and equate that to coverage ability; some of the worst contracts in the league have been doled out as a result of that flawed way of thinking. The conversation is particularly interesting regarding Kansas City because the franchise has traded away Marcus Peters, L’Jarius Sneed and McDuffie over the years. Will Delane spend his entire career with the Chiefs or become a trade chip down the road? Chiefs’ Trey Smith helps distribute 400 Thanksgiving meals to Kansas City families | KMBC 9 Chiefs offensive lineman Trey Smith joined forces with Giving Hope KC on Thursday night to distribute over 400 free Thanksgiving meals to families in Kansas City, Kansas. “I just wanted to give back to the city in any capacity I can,” Smith said. The event, now in its fourth year, featured Smith, KC Wolf, Chiefs cheerleaders, and volunteers handing out turkeys and all the essentials for a Thanksgiving feast. Around the NF L Texans cruise to victory over woeful Colts. Should Indianapolis bench Daniel Jones? | The Athletic Jones was pulled in the fourth quarter for Anthony Richardson Sr., with the Colts trailing by 23 points. But Richardson failed to move the offense, too, quickly going three-and-out. The Colts, who fired general manager Chris Ballard on Oct. 19 and dealt several key players ahead of the trade deadline, have now lost six of their last seven. Jonathan Taylor, whom the team retained amid trade rumors, finished with just 21 rushing yards on 11 carries. The Texans, who have won four of their last six following an 0-4 start, will next face the Baltimore Ravens (4-6) in Week 12. The Colts will take on the New York Giants (5-3-1). Studies: Blood test has potential to detect CTE in the living | ESPN One study, published Thursday by researchers at Boston University and Banner Health, was based on a small sample of former American football players who donated blood while alive. After those players died, autopsies of their brains determined they had CTE. The researchers then identified a CTE marker by examining the levels of a specific protein in the blood samples. Michael Alosco, the co-director of clinical research at Boston University’s CTE Center and co-senior author of the study, called the test a “game changer” in the ability to diagnose the degenerative brain illness in the living. Ravens CB Marlon Humphrey sent home, won’t play vs. Panthers after Baltimore comments | NFL.com Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey will not play in this Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers following derogatory comments he made recently about the city of Baltimore on his podcast, “The Marlon Humphrey Show.” Humphrey has also been sent home from the Ravens’ team facility. “After a lot of internal conversations, obviously with myself and the leadership of the organization, we’ve decided to deactivate Marlon for this game this upcoming week,” Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told reporters on Thursday. “Truthfully, I know there’s gonna be a lot of questions, most of it, again I said this yesterday, these conversations are very, very personal and private and to me, need to remain that for the good of the team and the organization.” In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Expect Travis Kelce to continue playing through his ankle injury Still, how Kelce looked limping off the field in Atlanta should not be confused with how he must be feeling as the Chiefs start another practice week. The coach also noted that Kelce’s particular ankle injury lends itself to quick recovery, even when it is aggravated. “He’s doing well now,” Reid explained. “He’s out running around. With high ankle sprains, he’s had this before. They get tweaked, literally, and then they recover fairly quick from there. That’s what this was. It just happened early in the game. So, I kind of held back on him. He was very mad. He wanted to play. That’s all part of it.” From The Feed Follow Arrowhead Pride on Social Media Facebook: Like our page Instagram: @ArrowheadPride X: Follow @ArrowheadPride AP Staff on X: See complete list

title: Dave Toub on Josh Downs: ‘Right now, he’s our punt returner’
summary: Shortly after the Kansas City Chiefs waived return specialist Nikko Remigio last week, the Houston Texans signed him to their active roster and trusted him to be the primary returner for their Week 10 game against the Cleveland Browns. In the matchup, Remigio had two punt returns, his longest being 22 yards in the first […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Shortly after the Kansas City Chiefs waived return specialist Nikko Remigio last week, the Houston Texans signed him to their active roster and trusted him to be the primary returner for their Week 10 game against the Cleveland Browns . In the matchup, Remigio had two punt returns, his longest being 22 yards in the first quarter. Special teams coordinator Dave Toub sounded happy for Remigio when he was asked about it at the podium on Thursday. However, he acknowledged the move was made with the team’s trade-deadline acquisition in mind. Wide receiver Josh Downs took all three of the Chiefs’ punt returns this last week, muffing one before quickly recovering and taking another 11 yards. “The fact that Josh [Downs] is a returner too at the same time, in our minds, we got a better receiver,” Toub explained to reporters. “Then we got better on the offense, obviously. “The return part, he’s going to get better and better at that,” Toub said. “He just tried to take off; he was excited, he wanted to get going, so he took off before he finished the catch. We have to do a better job of blocking the gunner, too.” Downs still needs to fully acclimate to the Chiefs’ return scheme, which is different compared to his former team’s. “Josh, at the Colts, they were more of a rush team,” Toub explained. “Had a lot more fair catches because they’re singling up the gunners. So we’re more of an attacking punt return… It’s going to be a little transition for him to adjust to what we do, but I think he’s a dynamic player. Give him a little bit of space, and he’s going to make something happen… we’re excited about him.” Downs is also working on settling into the offense, looking to run more than the eight routes he ran against the Atlanta Falcons . However, that will be happening as he continues to man the punt-return job; Toub pointed out the only other member of the organization who can handle the position — running back Brashard Smith — is currently on the Reserve/Injured list. “Right now, he’s our punt returner until we can develop, maybe, somebody else that’s on the roster still,” Toub explained. The other guy that can do it — and he’s not up right now — is Brashard, who’s out. He’s out, right now, and if he comes back, he’s a guy that we can get him ready to go. “We have a long way to go,” Toub said. “We still have a lot of games left and we have to slowly build this thing and get better each week.”

title: Andy Reid defends Xavier Worthy’s lack of production
summary: There was a lot to like about the Kansas City Chiefs’ offense immediately after trading for wide receiver Josh Downs. The 35-13 beatdown against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 10 showcased Downs and other receivers stepping up. However, it was a quiet day for the receiver with the most snaps: Xavier Worthy. He recorded no […]
full_text: (Photo by David J. Griffin/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images There was a lot to like about the Kansas City Chiefs ’ offense immediately after trading for wide receiver Josh Downs. The 35-13 beatdown against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 10 showcased Downs and other receivers stepping up. However, it was a quiet day for the receiver with the most snaps: Xavier Worthy. He recorded no stats on three targets; quarterback Patrick Mahomes threw none of his 348 passing yards to the speedster. A week after catching six passes for 48 yards against the New York Jets , Worthy had a quiet day in Atlanta, but on Monday, Chiefs head coach Andy Reid highlighted the attention he gets from opponents. “Depending on the coverage, you saw Worthy where they’re trying to cloud his side sometimes and take him out of the game and/or they play soft on him and rally somebody to him,” Reid explained. On Wednesday, he reiterated that sentiment during his press conference, pointing out the offense spreading the ball around with eyes on Worthy. “This was a good game to watch,” Reid began. “You can kind of see how they played him, and teams know he can run. So, they’re either going to bang him around and try to put somebody over the top of him, and then you use somebody else.” On Monday, Reid mentioned Worthy’s season-best game of seven catches for 73 yards against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 6 as proof that he can be productive. He alluded to it again on Wednesday after local media pointed out social-media criticism of Worthy. “The one game where there was nobody else, he was able to work his way through some of that, probably more scheme than anything. We were able to give him some things to work through there that other guys normally get, but we’re not down on him. “He can do all this stuff,” Reid continued. “And I hope he’s not worried about all that other thing and just keep being him. There are going to be days where he gets more balls than others, and that’s how it works.” This season, Worthy has the 89th-most receiving yards in the NFL; his teammate, rookie running back Emmett Johnson, has nearly 30 more yards. Deep ball accuracy depend on the receiver, too. On Mahomes' deep throws, Tyquan Thornton has been almost as good as Hill was at tracking deep balls (on a smaller sample). Meanwhile, Mahomes and Worthy have had a lot of trouble connecting down the field pic.twitter.com/JsMGbEJ6Ll — Tej Seth (@tejfbanalytics) November 19, 2026 When asked whether the reminder to Worthy to ignore outside noise needed reinforcement, Reid emphasized Worthy’s work ethic. “No,” Reid said. “He works his tail off, so don’t worry about all that.”
