title: Puka Nacua’s season in jeopardy due to knee surgery
summary: One day after the NFL announced a three-game suspension for Puka Nacua, the Los Angeles Rams have indicated to the media that their star receiver will miss at least two months because of knee surgery on his sprained MCL. While fans of other teams cried foul that Nacua was being suspended during a stint on […]
full_text: One day after the NFL announced a three-game suspension for Puka Nacua , the Los Angeles Rams have indicated to the media that their star receiver will miss at least two months because of knee surgery on his sprained MCL. While fans of other teams cried foul that Nacua was being suspended during a stint on IR , the truth of his injury was far more devastating to the Rams than the rest of the league. L.A. has suffered another devastating injury blow, and this one could keep their biggest offensive weapon off the field for the remainder of the 2026 season. Sean McVay’s indication that Nacua will be out for “a couple of months” means that the rest of the year is in serious jeopardy. Rams standout WR Puka Nacua is undergoing surgery on his MCL surgery and now could miss the rest of the season. Rams HC Sean McVay confirmed the surgery while saying Nacua will be out “a couple of months.” pic.twitter.com/mG572hwkWA — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 20, 2026 McVay revealed to reporters that Nacua underwent the procedure on Tuesday and is expected to miss a couple of months. With the regular season already moving toward its final stretch, there is a legitimate possibility that Nacua will not play another snap in 2026. The injury originally occurred during Los Angeles’ Week 9 victory over the Washington Commanders. Nacua suffered MCL and PCL sprains along with turf toe on the Rams’ final offensive play of the afternoon. He was subsequently placed on injured reserve. This is an especially difficult development for a Rams offense that has struggled to keep its playmakers healthy. Nacua had already missed time earlier in the season with a hip injury, making this another significant setback in an injury-plagued campaign. This news also means that Nacua may never play for L.A. again. Will the Rams franchise tag Nacua, a 2027 free agent, after undergoing knee surgery ? Or will they be too concerned about the injury history in addition to the off-field issues that got him suspended? Through seven games, Nacua recorded 70 receptions for 715 yards and four touchdowns. His absence leaves Matthew Stafford without one of the NFL’s most productive and reliable receivers. The Rams will now have to prepare for the possibility of finishing the season without their star wideout. While a return before the end of the year has not been completely ruled out, McVay’s latest update certainly makes that possibility much less encouraging.
author: Steven Ridings

title: Rams called pretenders by CBS Sports
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have won four games in a row and are squarely in the hunt for a spot in the NFL playoffs. That’s not enough for a pair of CBS Sports analysts to call the Rams contenders, however. In fact, those analysts called them “pretenders” this week instead. In a segment aptly named […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams have won four games in a row and are squarely in the hunt for a spot in the NFL playoffs. That’s not enough for a pair of CBS Sports analysts to call the Rams contenders, however. In fact, those analysts called them “pretenders” this week instead. In a segment aptly named “Contender or Pretender” on CBS Sports HQ , Damien Woody and Emory Hunt both took the negative angle for the Rams this week. Woody bemoaned L.A.’s current wide receiver situation, emphasizing the status of Puka Nacua and Davante Adams while seemingly hand waving the current state of the defense. When I look at this team, I look at two things: Puka Nacua, obviously with the suspension, dealing with a lot of injuries, and Davante Adams, we don’t even know when he’s going to come back this year. Those are two major components to their offense. We know that, yeah, they got Myles Garrett back to go along with Aaron Donald, but I think if they don’t have those pieces on offense, they’re not going to contend with the likes of the 49ers or some of these teams in the NFC North. When it comes to Adams, he’s missed a considerable amount of time but according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, he’s trying to get back for Wednesday’s game against his former team, the Green Bay Packers. The Rams have now outgained their opponents by a league-best 1,009 yards. That's the biggest yardage differential for a team through 10 weeks in the last three seasons. — Sheil Kapadia (@SheilKapadia) November 16, 2026 As for Nacua, the injuries are obviously a concern, but the suspension comment feels superfluous considering the whole thing will be served while Nacua is on injured reserve . Both of those points feel aggressive considering the facts of the case, while just brushing off Garrett returning to the lineup (and immediately dominating) seems unwise. Hunt, meanwhile, tried to argue his point using only the remaining schedule. “You have to play San Francisco again, we saw what that looked like Week 1, albeit different circumstances, but they really beat them up physically, and you still have to play Seattle twice … I think when you look at Seattle and San Francisco, in conjunction with the NFC North, I don’t see the Rams contending so I see them outside looking in so I say ‘pretender.’” The Rams upcoming schedule is BRUTAL https://t.co/sJ9tp8oeyS pic.twitter.com/gbt2YeBu6A — PFF (@PFF) November 17, 2026 To be blunt, there’s just not much analysis of any value here. Simply stating that other good teams exist doesn’t make for a useful argument. The point about San Francisco, in particular, feels largely irrelevant given the exact circumstances Hunt quickly mentioned. The thing about arguing that the Rams aren’t real playoff contenders because they have to play other good teams ignores the fact that the Rams, too, are a good team. They’re not perfect and they’ve got legitimate worries, but good teams beat other good teams all the time. Frankly, that’s an exceptionally low form of commentary and analysis. It’s entirely possible the Rams miss out on the playoffs. If they lose to the Packers the night before Thanksgiving, things will feel especially hairy for Los Angeles. But these arguments tearing them down are shallow at best, nonsense at worse.
author: Brendan Dzwierzynski

title: Did Rams know the suspension was coming?
summary: The speculation surrounding Puka Nacua and his suspension has raised questions such as when did the Los Angeles Rams know the suspension was coming? Did Nacua’s potential suspension influence L.A.‘s decision to place him on IR? One question I have, did Sean McVay know the suspension was coming, and if so, was that why Nacua […]
full_text: The speculation surrounding Puka Nacua and his suspension has raised questions such as when did the Los Angeles Rams know the suspension was coming? Did Nacua’s potential suspension influence L.A.‘s decision to place him on IR? One question I have, did Sean McVay know the suspension was coming, and if so, was that why Nacua was accounting for 100% (slight exaggeration) of the passing game while Nacua was available? Then again, Matthew Stafford has had a habit of feeding his top targets, so perhaps the two situations are unrelated. Field Yates of ESPN says that some people do find the timing of the suspension “fishy” . Maybe it is, but the rules are the rules and reportedly the NFL Players’ Association was able to help arrange this deal for Nacua, and Nacua will take it and serve his suspension. There has been precedent for this type of situation with players serving their suspension on IR, which indicates nothing truly new is happening for Nacua with regard to how his suspension is being handled. What’s done is done. Will Nacua learn from his alleged negative past behavior? That’s a big question for the young receiver. Either Nacua avoids negative headlines or he doesn’t. For now, Nacua will serve his suspension, try to get healthy and go from there. 32 teams around the league will be watching how Nacua bounces back or doesn’t. Whether he likes it or not, all eyes on Nacua. Suspension of Rams’ Puka Nacua reportedly ‘smells fishy’ to people around NFL (yardbarker) “Timing of Puka Nacua suspension is “awfully convenient” “The NFL will say that this punishment was handed down because they finally completed the process,” Yates said of the league’s investigation of Nacua. “We were wondering at the beginning of training camp whether he was going to be suspended to begin the season. …I’ve had people around the NFL reach out to me and say, ‘Funny how that works out, right? Guy gets to miss three games that he would have missed anyway.’ So this one smells fishy to a lot of people around the NFL. I find it awfully convenient. I find it awfully convenient.” Whispers about a potential Nacua suspension had hovered over the Rams ever since it was learned this past March that a woman had filed a civil lawsuit accusing him of biting her and of making an antisemitic comment on Dec. 31, 2025. While he checked himself into a rehab facility in the spring to reportedly focus on his “personal growth,” it was assumed he’d eventually have to serve a ban.“ Rams WR Puka Nacua to serve 3-game suspension while on IR (espn.com) “There is precedent for players serving suspensions while on injured reserve or otherwise unavailable because of injury. It is not a new rule or an exception created for Nacua. Most recently, in 2025 the Steelers’ Daniel Ekuale was suspended five games for a violation of the performance-enhancing substances policy following a season-ending injury. In 2024, the Cowboys’ Sam Williams was suspended three games for violating the personal conduct policy while already out for the season. The Browns’ Mike Woods was suspended six games in 2023 for violating the personal conduct policy while he was out on NFI. In 2018, the Saints’ David Parry , was suspended four games for violations of the personal conduct and substances of abuse policies while on injured reserve.“ Puka Nacua’s suspension arises from diversion program (nbcsports) “The NFL’s statement announcing the three-game suspension for Rams receiver Puka Nacua didn’t specify the reason for it. Further information provided by the league makes the basis for the ban clear. It comes from Nacua’s entry into a “diversion program,” related to the incident that triggered a civil lawsuit alleging (among other things) that he bit a woman on New Year’s Eve. In September, we explained that Nacua had begun the steps required to complete a diversion program, which happened without Nacua entering into a formal agreement to do so. It’s one of the unique facets of California law; namely, California gives some defendants the ability to embark on the steps to comply with a diversion program without the kind of express deal that would have automatically triggered review under the Personal Conduct Policy. The approach ultimately didn’t avoid the NFL scrutiny.“ NFL suspends Rams receiver Puka Nacua for 3 games (ktla.com) “The suspension is effective immediately, and Nacua will be eligible for reinstatement on Dec. 14. Nacua is currently on injured reserve after suffering MCL and PCL sprains in his right knee, along with turf toe. According to Schefter, players can serve suspensions while on injured reserve. His remaining three games on IR will count toward the three-game suspension. Nacua missed Sunday’s game against the Arizona Cardinals, the first of the mandatory four games he must sit out while on injured reserve.“ Rams defensive star has blunt message for LA’s defense ahead of Packers showdown (sports.yahoo) “”Our defense is sitting somewhere in the 20s for turnover ratio,” McDuffie told The California Post in an exclusive interview. “So it’s a big mindset this week: turnovers, turnovers.” He’s close. The Rams are currently tied for 16th in opponents’ turnovers in the NFL, and that’s before the rest of the league plays their Week 11 slate of games. But that message of needing to force turnovers carries even more weight heading into a nationally televised Thanksgiving Eve showdown between two teams tied for the NFC’s seventh and final playoff spot.“ Rams Have Cooled off Since Preseason Hype, but Stephen A. Smith is Still on the Bandwagon (sports.yahoo) “It won’t be easy. The defending champion Seattle Seahawks are still in the mix, and the San Francisco 49ers have the NFC’s best record. The NFC North is loaded, with the Detroit Lions, Chicago Bears and Minnesota Vikings all at 7-2. The Vikings may have solved their quarterback problem and have arguably the league’s best defense. But none of them has two multiple-time Defensive Player of the Year winners. “I’m picking Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett to be at SoFi for the Super Bowl , dammit, and I’m staying on that bandwagon until further notice,” Smith said Thursday on ESPN’s “First Take.” The Rams handled the softer part of their schedule, but a tougher stretch awaits in the Packers, Kansas City Chiefs, 49ers, Dallas Cowboys and Seahawks. These games carry playoff implications and will show whether Smith is right about the Rams.“ Rams haven’t given up on Super Bowl dreams despite a tumultuous start to their season (thehour.com) “Los Angeles has a top-five defense, a top-10 offense and a four-game winning streak. Several key injured players are expected back within the next few games, and those tough matchups looming on their schedule also put the Rams’ playoff destiny in their hands. Sean McVay didn’t shy from the expectations placed on his so-called superteam during the summer, and the head coach isn’t giving up on it after a half-season of drama and disappointments.“ Survival Mode: Los Angeles Rams Fighting to Stay Afloat (lastwordonsports) “Several of the Rams’ best players are currently on injured reserve, including Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. With several of their best players sidelined by injuries, McVay must find new ways to keep the team fresh. Following the Week 10 victory, McVay once again demonstrated why he is considered one of the best coaches in the NFL. He used a variety of formations to keep the Arizona Cardinals off guard and win the game. McVay said he used it as a way to keep two of their best players on the field at the same time. His use of 20 and 22 personnel was the first time he used the formations in his head coaching career, and it could not have worked any better.“ Charts show how much harder Rams’ schedule is than every other team’s (ramswire) “They’ll first face the Packers after the bye on Thanksgiving Eve, followed by games against the Chiefs and 49ers. The Rams probably need to go no worse than 2-1 in that stretch, especially with two…
author: Danny Stone

title: Konata Mumpfield might be better than he gets credit for
summary: Davante Adams has consistently praised Konata Mumpfield over the last two years. After Adams has missed the last few games, Mumpfield has taken over Adams’ specific role. While the box score proves that Mumpfield is not Adams—and it’s not a fair standard to compare a former seventh round draft choice to a future hall of […]
full_text: Davante Adams has consistently praised Konata Mumpfield over the last two years. After Adams has missed the last few games, Mumpfield has taken over Adams’ specific role. While the box score proves that Mumpfield is not Adams—and it’s not a fair standard to compare a former seventh round draft choice to a future hall of famer—he’s adequately filled the space left by Adams. It’s closer than you’d think at first glance. Data from Pro Football Focus (PFF): Stat Davante Adams Konata Mumpfield Pass snaps 248 222 Routes run 232 209 Route rate 93.5% 94.1% Avg. depth of target 15.2 14.4 Yards per reception 16.0 17.4 Touchdowns 4 1 Interceptions when targeted 2 3 Passer rating when targeted 104.1 63.0 Receptions over expected +1.6 +2.6 Catch rate over expected +3.3% +10.3% Drop rate 9.1% 6.7% Negative play rate 2.1% 1.6% Pass-block rate 0.0% 0.9% Penalties 1 2 Adams and Mumpfield lead the Rams in average depth of target (ADOT). There are only two other receivers above 10 yards: CJ Daniels and Tutu Atwell. It’s clear they both fill the vertical role in the offense, of which Mumpfield has been the most efficient in this facet: Passes aimed 20+ yards downfield: Adams: 4/11 (36.4%) for 136 yards (29 yards after the catch) Nacua: 2/11 (18.2%) for 60 yards (8 after the catch) Mumpfield: 2/5 (40%) for 92 yards, 1 TD (32 after the catch) Nacua and Adams both have two interceptions when targeted on such plays. Mumpfield doesn’t have a single one. This is an area where he role likely could expand—even if Adams does return to health as soon as the Thanksgiving Eve game against Green Bay. Despite Mumpfield’s relatively low catch rate at 56% (14 catches on 25 targets), he has caught 10.3% above expectation. This tells us that throws in his direction are difficult—such as deep passes—and that often balls coming his way are not catchable. This is another reason why the box score may suggest he’s not playing as well when there is evidence to the contrary. The Rams need all the receiving help they can get. More of Konata Mumpfield might be the right move.
author: JB Scott

title: There are worse backup plans than Beaux Limmer
summary: The starting center for the Los Angeles Rams, Coleman Shelton, is expected to miss four to six weeks with a severe hamstring injury. He will be replaced by Beaux Limmer, who watched Shelton take his job following a painful end to his Limmer’s rookie season. At one point, Limmer looked like a draft steal. LA […]
full_text: The starting center for the Los Angeles Rams, Coleman Shelton, is expected to miss four to six weeks with a severe hamstring injury. He will be replaced by Beaux Limmer, who watched Shelton take his job following a painful end to his Limmer’s rookie season. At one point, Limmer looked like a draft steal. LA swiped the former Arkansas Razorback in the sixth round. He went on to start 14 games and play 1,000 snaps as a rookie, including in the divisional round game against the Philadelphia Eagles. 2025: What do the Rams truly have in Beaux Limmer? And that is where Limmer’s reputation quickly shifted from draft steal to a problem that needed upgraded. On the final two plays of an all-important playoff matchup, Limmer left Jalen Carter unblocked for quick pressures on Matthew Stafford. The result? Two incomplete passes and the Rams flying back to Los Angeles with their heads slumped in defeat. As a consequence, the Rams prioritized a reunion with Shelton in free agency. Limmer was a nice surprise. He could return to the starting lineup one day. But center is an important position and growing pains for a young player could have jeopardized the remaining window of Stafford’s career. Now? Shelton is out. Limmer is in. It’s a full-circle story. The truth is there are worse backup plans than Limmer. He’s capable. In front of him is an opportunity to grab the starting job. This time he might not let go. Limmer saved the day in Arizona The balance helped propel Xavier Smith all the way into the end zone LARvsAZ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/W4ORlumlu1 — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Shelton has been an above average starter for LA. Left guard Steve Avila missed the most recent game against the Cardinals. Limmer earned the start at left guard. When Shelton came out, backup Dylan McMahon lasted nine plays before suffering a significant injury of his own. Limmer slid inside. Bill Murray came in at left guard. And Limmer played well. According to Pro Football Focus (PFF), Limmer played 76 snaps and earned a near-elite pass blocking grade of 88.8. He did not allow a single pressure. The run game was also marked at a plus level with a grade of 70.4 for a net offensive grade of 75.5. For comparison, that edges out Shelton’s season offensive grade of 74.7. Limmer is 25 years old. He wasn’t a finished product as a rookie. If what he put on tape through 1,000 snaps in 2024 was enough for us to be excited then, it would be foolish to write him off as a future starter moving forward. The Rams have a surplus of players they must re-sign over the next couple of offseasons. Limmer is under contract through 2027. Limmer holding onto the starting job for the remainder of the season and proving he deserves the job in 2027 would be a welcome development for the Rams.
author: JB Scott

title: Kyren Williams has message for Rams and other teams about GTA VI
summary: Kyren Williams made it clear that he does not want the massive release of Grand Theft Auto VI to be a distraction to the Los Angeles Rams as they prepare for perhaps their biggest game of the year against the Green Bay Packers in Week 12, and go from there. Williams was asked on ESPN […]
full_text: Kyren Williams made it clear that he does not want the massive release of Grand Theft Auto VI to be a distraction to the Los Angeles Rams as they prepare for perhaps their biggest game of the year against the Green Bay Packers in Week 12, and go from there. Williams was asked on ESPN how the trendy release of GTA VI could or would impact the Rams? Williams responded during the interview with laughter and glee at the thought of the game coming out, and he confessed to Peter Schrager that he hopes he and his teammates stay focused on winning, while taking some healthy time to away from football to check out the new video game. On the flip side, Williams hopes other NFL teams play the new game all day, all night and twice on Sunday. Said Williams on the release of GTA VI during L.A.’s bye week: “I hope it impacts everybody, but the Rams, you know? And so, I hope the Rams, I hope my teammates and I are able to game a little bit, but still, you know, get to bed and be on time for practice and you know be alert and whatnot. But I am super excited. I’m glad that you brought that up cause I gotta go pre-load it, I gotta go pre-download it, you know, when we get done here. But yah I’m super excited for GTA and we’re on a bye week, so it’s like, bro this is the best week ever.” NFL players across the league and people all over the world have been waiting for the pop culture phenomena that is the new Grand Theft Auto, and it’s releasing in the thick of the NFL season. Cleveland Browns’ quarterback Deshaun Watson was asked about the playoffs and the Browns chances . Watson gave the classic answer about taking it “one game at a time” before basically stating that at this point in the season, players are thinking more about the new Grand Theft Auto than playoffs . And to be fair, playoffs are still a while off while GTA VI is out now. Keep your feet where they are. "Coach don't even mention it … we're not getting ahead of ourselves. Most of the guys are thinking about GTA, for real." Browns QB Deshaun Watson on if him and his teammates are thinking about the playoffs 😅 (via @FredGreetham9 ) pic.twitter.com/dBMpg48aGW — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 18, 2026 Of course, players like Williams and Watson do have a few million reasons to put down the controller and stick with the football. While many gamers all over will be celebrating, gamers like Williams and others are in the busy part of their work season. title: Puka Nacua suspended 3 games by NFL

The Los Angeles Rams’ star receiver is already on injured reserve with a knee injury and will serve his suspension while he is unavailable, so it […]
full_text: The NFL has suspended Puka Nacua for three games, starting immediately, after a negotiation between the league and the NFL Players Association that came to a conclusion on Thursday. The Los Angeles Rams’ star receiver is already on injured reserve with a knee injury and will serve his suspension while he is unavailable, so it does not affect his ability to help the team. The timing of the suspension to coincide with his IR stint is interesting, if nothing else. Nacua will miss out on roughly $1 million worth of game checks. Here is the official NFL word on Puka Nacua’s suspension: pic.twitter.com/OJL6rzaHTw — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 19, 2026 Nacua is eligible to be reinstated after the Rams play the San Francisco 49ers in Week 14. It is a game Nacua would have missed anyway. The Rams are not known to be actively negotiating with Nacua on an extension, but the 2027 free agent is lucky to serve his suspension now while still on his rookie contract. Nacua will most likely return during the season from a knee injury suffered two weeks ago and be able to make one final statement on the field prior to becoming a free agent. The NFL and NFLPA negotiated the settlement to resolve Puka Nacua’s personal conduct case and issue a three-game suspension, which is final. The league told Nacua that any further violation of the policy, including failure to satisfy conditions of his diversion program, could… pic.twitter.com/THLLYWDkA5 — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 19, 2026 This allows the Rams and Nacua to negotiate knowing that his suspension is behind him, and not in front. That is provided that Nacua does not continue to make problems for himself off of the field. Nacua checked into rehab during the 2026 season as a show of effort that he is trying not to make any more bad headline for himself or the team. Puka Nacua is on injured reserve and would not have played in these games anyway. But he’ll lose three game checks worth about $961,167 as part of his suspension. https://t.co/HJRBTEBZCm — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 19, 2026 Whether he follows through on that promise or not is impossible to know, but Nacua has not been in the news this season … until now.

title: Raiders’ Week 10 wide receiver snap and production review
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders lost at home 21-13 to the Seattle Seahawks in Week 10. Let’s review how their wide receivers fared: Tre Tucker Tucker played a season-high 88 percent of the snaps. He was targeted just twice and had one catch for nine yards. After having 10 catches for 200 yards in Weeks 6 […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders lost at home 21-13 to the Seattle Seahawks in Week 10 . Let’s review how their wide receivers fared: Tre Tucker Tucker played a season-high 88 percent of the snaps. He was targeted just twice and had one catch for nine yards. After having 10 catches for 200 yards in Weeks 6 and 7, Tucker has just five catches for 64 yards on 13 targets in the three games since. He appeared to be open deep a couple of times against Seattle, but Fernando Mendoza was pressured too quickly. Tucker and Mendoza have deep-play potential. Jalen Nailor: He played 86 percent of the snaps, a season high. He had one catches on four targets for minus-one yard. He has 15 catches for 132 yards on 32 targets in nine games after signing a three-year, $35 million deal in the offseason. Jack Bech: The 2025 second-round pick played 56 percent of the snaps, a season high. He had two catches for 10 yards on seven targets. He has three catches for 19 yards in three games since returning from the injured reserve. Cody White: White played four snaps and had one catch for 22 yards. He doesn’t play a lot, but he does make plays. Dareke Young: He played one offensive snap. He didn’t have any targets. Conclusion: The Raiders’ wide receivers had five catches for 40 yards on 14 targets against Seattle. Their tight ends and running backs combined for 12 catches for 103 yards on 15 targets. We’ve said this before, but the Raiders need more production from their wide receivers.

title: All eyes on not only Fernando Mendoza’s growth, but Klint Kubiak too
summary: In terms of accountability, the Las Vegas Raiders have that locked down at the all-important head coach and quarterback spot with Klint Kubiak and Fernando Mendoza, respectively. After the team’s 21-13 defeat at hands of the visiting Seattle Seahawks this past Sunday — dropping the team to 4-6 overall — both Kubiak and Mendoza went […]
full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images In terms of accountability, the Las Vegas Raiders have that locked down at the all-important head coach and quarterback spot with Klint Kubiak and Fernando Mendoza, respectively. After the team’s 21-13 defeat at hands of the visiting Seattle Seahawks this past Sunday — dropping the team to 4-6 overall — both Kubiak and Mendoza went up the podium to shoulder the blame. “I thought overall when we lost Brock (Bowers), you definitely saw a big change in production,” Kubiak said after the game when asked about the simple gameplan and stagnant offense against Seattle. “So I look at myself; I have to do a much better job of moving the ball, getting and spreading the ball around.” So I got us in the wrong check, and then they sacked me, and that’s why a lot of the sacks today, if not all of them, were on me, not on the offensive line,” Mendoza said in particular of Seahawks nickel corner Devon Witherspoon sacking him twice off slot blitzes. “I thought they played great and displayed great leadership today, and I need to be better, especially with those DB blitzes.” Watching the Raiders franchise quarterback getting absolutely walloped by ‘Spoon and other Seahawks defenders was certainly not ideal. But welcoming the brunt of the blame and pointing the finger at themselves, one could even label the Silver & Black’s promising head coach and quarterback combo the “I-Twins” as their quick to pin the blame on themselves and note they must improve for the overall good of the team. And that’s an endearing trait for two key figures in the organization that are rookies in their respective roles. Fernando Mendoza: Before this sack (13 dropbacks): +0.47 EPA per dropback (would rank 1st in the NFL) 10/12, 83 yards 0 sacks After (25 dropbacks): -0.47 EPA per dropback (would be last) 7/17, 60 yards (with 38 yards coming on a Jeanty checkdown) 5 sacks pic.twitter.com/oCr4rp87PT — Ian Hartitz (@Ihartitz) November 17, 2026 While we won’t know what’s said behind closed doors at Raiders headquarters, the practice field, or in the locker room game days — there have been few instances where I was privy too and within earshot of tirades in post game locker room access — we were given a glimpse of Kubiak’s fury when the CBS broadcast captured the moment he was talking to his offensive line on the sidelines . So while it’s admirable Kubiak stands in front of media row and says it’s “my fault”, it’s good to see that Kubiak doesn’t absolve his team of their own responsibilities. But the following day, during his media session on Monday, Kubiak ensured it’s also a “we” thing. “I think overall, as an offensive line, there’s a solid first half of run game production followed by a very poor half of protection, and that’s not all on them,” the Raiders rookie head coach said. “That’s on getting open, that’s on getting rid of the ball, that’s on play calls. It’s a team thing. So, we win together and we lose together.” Kubiak was also quick to note that his side of the ball — the offense — didn’t play enough complementary football when Rob Leonard’s defense helped maintain a 10-3 advantage against Seattle — precarious as that lead may be. Sure, losing Bowers — an elite pass catcher who Kubiak deploys as equal parts wide receiver and tight end — scuttled things and plans went awry against the Seahawks. And once Mike Macdonald recognized that Mendoza can not only throw dimes but also fire lasers on the run and take off to gain yards with his legs, the Seahawks’ defensive mastermind dialed up man concepts with blitzes. And the results speak for themselves. Mendoza said getting punched in the face gives him the opportunity to watch his mistakes and grow from them. Kubiak, too. And it’s integral that duo take these tough growing pains and apply the lessons going forward. “I love Klint.” “This is well coached football team.” “This team has a future.” Mike MacDonald on seeing his former offensive Cordinator Klint Kubiak today. #RaiderNation #Seahawks pic.twitter.com/np9gKp0Fis — Armani Lingo (@armani_lingo8) November 16, 2026 Because what Seattle put on tape defensively against the rookie quarterback will become a regular occurrence — until — Mendoza shows consistently that he can identify the pressure, adjust protection, let the other 10 players on offense what’s up, and burn the defense when they bring the pain. The good old Uno reverse card, if you will. That noted, the 6-foot-5, 225-pound No. 1 overall pick from the 2026 NFL Draft showed he is NFL ready by not only standing in the pocket and progressing through his read and firing, scrambling for positive yards when he needed to, but also hanging onto the football when he got waylaid. Even when Mendoza was rocked, he didn’t suddenly see ghosts and get happy feet. He got up, went back to the huddle, barked out the play and went about his business. The mental and physical toughness are ideal. The footwork, the arm, the legs, and the mind all show Mendoza can play at the pro level and if protected, can succeed. And the miscues from the 23-year-old Indiana product are fixable. Now, it’s about Kubiak, offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko, quarterback coach Mike Sullivan, offensive line boss Rick Dennison to speak to their players and get the offense aligned. Protect the franchise and good things happen. And franchise, take care of yourself and don’t take those hits that can cause fright — for the fanbase and yourself. Kubiak provided insights on what he wants to see going forward. Fernando Mendoza on his first start: "It's good to get punched in the face because now it's a great opportunity to grow and learn… and to really unveil all the deficiencies that I have in my game as a future hopeful leader of this offense." pic.twitter.com/LT8Mf0yjwG — Arye Pulli (@AryePulliNFL) November 16, 2026 “Well, remain a passer. Number one, keep your eyes downfield. Remain a passer like he did to Jack Bech on that left sideline, like he did to Ian (Thomas) early in the game, getting through his progression,” the head coach and play caller said. “Remain a passer, and then obviously protect yourself when you start to run down the field.” “Yeah, it wasn’t up to our standard for quarterback hits and sacks,” Kubiak said about the six sacks and 12 quarterback hits Mendoza absorbed. “That’s an entire offensive stat. It’s getting open fast, that’s protecting better, and that’s him getting rid of the ball. There’s three things there.” While it’d be grand if Kubiak, Janocko, Dennison and Co. can get the run blocking to be on par with the pass protection to give their young quarterback a ground game he can rely upon, that’s been a longstanding issue when heady veteran Kirk Cousins was under center. But there’s signs that Mendoza has the ability to become the leader — not hopeful leader as he said above — of the Raiders offense. And boy, that’ll be a sight to behold, when it does happen.

full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders received good news ahead of their Week 11 matchup against the Denver Broncos . ESPN’s Ryan McFadden posted a video of tight end Brock Bowers in full pads and participating in warmups ahead of Thursday’s practice, noting that Bowers is returning to the field. #Raiders TE Brock Bowers (ankle) returns to practice on Thursday. pic.twitter.com/p467LGyArL — Ryan McFadden (@ryanmcfadden_) November 19, 2026 The Raiders’ leading receiver exited last week’s game against the Seattle Seahawks at halftime and missed Wednesday’s session with ankle and quadricep injuries. This was a step in the right direction for Bowers’ availability on Sunday against the Broncos, as the Raiders listed him as limited on the injury report (h/t The Athletic’s Sam Warren ). Also, Las Vegas’ offense really needs its top target. The ‘tight end’ has racked up 50 catches for 676 yards and six touchdowns in eight games this season, leading the Silver and Black in all three categories despite missing the first two contests with a knee injury. According to Sumer Sports , the team’s passing game averages 0.105 EPA per pass and has a 49.0 percent success rate with Bowers on the field this year. Without him, those numbers dip to 0.005 EPA per pass and 43.4 percent. Factor in that rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza will be making his second career start against a Denver defense that ranks ninth in points per game allowed ( 20.7 ), and it’s even more important that Bowers suits up on Sunday. Additionally, Warren noted that guard Trey Zuhn III (illness), defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway (stinger) and defensive tackle Foley Fatukasi (toe) weren’t spotted during the media viewing period of Thursday’s practice. Zuhn wasn’t listed on Wednesday’s report, while Hemingway was a non-participant and Fatukasi was limited on Wednesday. Neither of the three linemen participated in Thursday’s session. If Zuhn can’t go, second-year guard Caleb Rogers is likely the next man up. Rogers replaced Zuhn when the latter left the 49ers game with a concussion a couple of weeks ago. Hemingway’s and Fatukasi’s absence would really test the Raiders’ defensive tackle depth, a position that’s been an issue all season. That would likely mean more reps for Adam Butler, Tim Keenan III, Thomas Booker IV and JJ Pegues. Warren also reported that the Raiders brought in kickers Lucas Havrisik, Younghoe Koo and John Parker Romo for a workout, as Matt Gay is dealing with a hip injury and sat out of practice. Tight end Ian Thomas added an ankle injury to Thursday’s report after missing Wednesday with a calf injury, though Thomas was upgraded to limited on Thursday. As for the Broncos, they managed to get healthier for the second practice of the week. The only changes from yesterday’s injury report were cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle), defensive tackle Zach Allen (rest) and wide receiver Courtland Sutton (rest) going from limited to full participants. Brock Bowers was a limited participant in his return to practice today. Matt Gay did not participate in practice despite being present, hence the kicker tryouts today. Trey Zuhn's absence was due to an illness. pic.twitter.com/33aE5o5hJX — Sam Warren (@samwarren83) November 19, 2026

title: Las Vegas Raiders must protect Fernando Mendoza against Denver Broncos’ pass rush in Week 11 key matchups
summary: Week 11 is the start of a stretch where the Las Vegas Raiders will face a divisional opponent in three of their next four games, beginning and ending that stretch with the Denver Broncos. It will also mark rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza’s second career start, and the Raiders will need to be on point in […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 11 is the start of a stretch where the Las Vegas Raiders will face a divisional opponent in three of their next four games, beginning and ending that stretch with the Denver Broncos . It will also mark rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza’s second career start, and the Raiders will need to be on point in the trenches to pull off the 9.5-point upset on the road . That leads us into this week’s key matchups for Las Vegas. Raiders’ OTs vs. Broncos’ Edge Rushers Mendoza had a shaky starting debut last week against the Seattle Seahawks, completing 17 of 29 pass attempts (58.6 percent) for 143 yards and no touchdowns . The biggest reason for that is that he, understandably, struggled to handle Mike Macdonald’s exotic pressure looks and ended up taking six sacks. The good news for the Raiders is there probably isn’t a more difficult defensive scheme for a rookie quarterback to handle than the Seahawks’. The bad news is the Broncos also have an elite pass-rush, and defensive coordinator Vance Joseph isn’t shy about bringing the heat. According to Sumer Sports , Denver ranks fourth in pressure rate (41.6 percent) and 11th in blitz rate (33.7 percent). For comparison, the Seahawks are eighth in pressure (40.9 percent) and 28th in blitz (23.0 percent), as Macdonald uses more simulated pressures rather than pure blitzes. But more than anything, what really makes Denver’s pass-rush so effective is its edge rushers: Nik Bonitto and Jonathon Cooper. Bonitto has made Pro Bowls in back-to-back seasons by racking up 27.5 sacks over the last two years. Through nine games in 2026, he’s posted 4.5 sacks and has 30 pressures, according to Pro Football Focus . The latter ranks 19th among edges despite recording the third-fewest pass-rush snaps (228) of anyone in the Top 20. Additionally, his 19.4 percent pass-rush win rate is sixth-best and 90.5 pass-rush grade is third-best. Of the fifth-year pro’s 387 defensive snaps, 340 have come as a right outside linebacker , setting up for a long battle between him and Raiders’ left tackle Kolton Miller. While Miller has a track record of being a good pass-protector, he’s been regressing this season by giving up 32 pressures in 10 games. For comparison, the 31-year-old surrendered 38 pressures in 2024, which is the most recent season where he played in all 17 games. So, Vegas will need its left tackle to turn back the clock on Sunday. On the other side of the line, off-field issues led to Cooper spending the first six games of the campaign on the Commissioner’s Exempt List. As a result, he’s only participated in three contests this year and has underwhelming numbers with 0.5 sacks and 10 pressures. However, he has a strong track record with 27 sacks from 2023 to 2025, and finished last year tied for 25th among edge rushers with 51 pressures during the regular season. Meanwhile, Las Vegas’ right tackle, DJ Glaze, is having a career year. After giving up 99 pressures on 1,217 opportunities (about a 12.3-to-one ratio) in his first two seasons, he’s yielded just 15 pressures on 379 opportunities (about a 25.3-to-one ratio). In other words, the third-year pro is getting beaten half as frequently as he used to. Long story short, both of the Raiders’ offensive tackles are capable of keeping Bonitto and Cooper away from Mendoza. But the Broncos’ pair of edge rushers are also more than capable of winning against Miller and Glaze, setting up for an intriguing battle in the trenches. Burford/Zuhn vs. Allen Continuing with the theme above, Zach Allen has established himself as one of the best interior pass-rushers in the NFL. He’s racked up 25 sacks in 3.5 seasons with the Broncos and is coming off a first-team All-Pro campaign, where he accumulated seven sacks and led defensive tackles with 73 pressures during the regular season. Through nine games in 2026, Allen has picked up right where he left off, registering 4.5 sacks and topping the charts for his position with 38 pressures . Part of what makes him difficult to contain is that he plays on both sides of the line, with 238 of 442 snaps coming on the left this year and 175 on the right, per PFF . That allows Joseph to move the disruptive defensive tackle around and take advantage of an opponent’s weakest guard. So, both Spencer Burford and Trey Zuhn III have to be on point to keep Allen in check. That could be an issue for Burford, who enters the weekend tied for the third-most pressures ( 23 ) among guards this season. To be fair, his 379 opportunities are tied for the seventh-most at the position, so volume does play a factor in that number. However, a bottom-20 96.6 PFF pass-blocking efficiency rating isn’t much better. Meanwhile, Zuhn has only made three starts at guard and thus has only yielded five pressures on 85 opportunities. A sample size that small means the jury is still out on the rookie, and a 97.2 efficiency rating isn’t something to write home about. To paint a picture of how much the position has been a sore spot for Vegas: Zuhn’s efficiency rating is the highest of the team’s guards this season, and it ranks tied for 37th across the league . That sets up a big mismatch that Klint Kubiak will have to account for to keep Mendoza upright. Of course, the interior line having its best game of the year wouldn’t hurt, either. Crosby/Koonce vs. Bolles/McGlinchey Bo Nix has been one of the worst quarterbacks under pressure this season. According to PFF , his 10 ‘turnover-worthy plays’ under pressure are tied for the fourth-most among QBs with at least 182 total dropbacks. Also, his 8.6 percent TWP rate is the third-highest, and his 26.5 passing grade is the third-worst. However, Nix has only been under pressure on 34.9 percent of his dropbacks, which is the 12th-best rate at the position. That’s, at least partially, a testament to the two bookends the Broncos have at offensive tackle: Garrett Bolles and Mike McGlinchey. Bolles has a history of being a stingy pass-protector, and that hasn’t changed in 2026. He’s yielded just five pressures on 307 opportunities, which is the fewest of any offensive tackle with at least 239 snaps in pass protection, per PFF . Unsurprisingly, the two-time All-Pro’s 99.2 efficiency rating also tops the charts at his position this year. Meanwhile, McGlinchey doesn’t have quite as impressive a resume as Bolles does, but the right tackle is putting together a strong performance this fall. On 307 opportunities, he’s yielded just 19 pressures and has a 96.7 PFF efficiency rating. The former is one shy of the top 25 for the position, and the latter sits exactly at 25th. Seeing as Foley Fatukasi leads the Raiders defensive tackles who have at least 100 pass rush snaps this season with a 6.9 percent pass-rush win rate , which ranks 69th among NFL defensive tackles, the Silver and Black are going to have to get pressure around the edge to get to Nix. Despite facing a high rate of double teams and opponents constantly sliding their pass protection to him, Crosby still has five sacks and ranks tied for fourth among edge rushers with 46 pressures this season. His pass-rush win rate has dipped since the beginning of the year but still sits at 16.2 percent and is tied for 18th at his position. The five-time Pro Bowler isn’t the reason Vegas has a below-average pressure rate (37.4 percent), sitting at 18th in the league, according to Sumer . In fact, he’s the biggest reason the figure is even that high. But Crosby needs more help from his running mate, Malcolm Koonce, who started the campaign hot but has cooled off recently. In Weeks 1-5, the sixth-year veteran was tied for 21st among edges with 16 pressures and sixth with a 19.4 percent win rate . In the five games since then, he’s tied for 64th in pressures (eight) and tied for 65th in win rate (10.0 percent) . Clearly, the Raiders need the complementary rusher who got off to a strong start to show up on Sunday and not the guy they’ve had over the last…

title: How the Las Vegas Raiders offense can earn a tough win
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders head on the road to Empower Field to take on the division-leading Denver Broncos in a renewal of an AFC West rivalry. A win against the Broncos will go a long way to instilling confidence in rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza and the defense. Furthermore, the Raiders contest against the Cleveland Browns […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) The Las Vegas Raiders head on the road to Empower Field to take on the division-leading Denver Broncos in a renewal of an AFC West rivalry. A win against the Broncos will go a long way to instilling confidence in rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza and the defense. Furthermore, the Raiders contest against the Cleveland Browns has been flexed to Sunday Night Football and could be a game with potential playoff implications. Can the Raiders find a way to beat the Broncos? Division games are a funny thing; typically, you can throw out records and standings. Both teams are configured to beat each other, if not play to an absolute standstill. This game is no different; while the records are nearly opposite- Broncos (7-2), Raiders (4-6) their strengths cancel each other out and the weaknesses will be the difference makers. Broncos Defense by the numbers The Broncos’ defense hasn’t been what it used to be, ranking 26 th in total defense. The defense is ranked near the bottom third of the league in every category except points (9 th ) and takeaways (12 th ). Their rushing defense is ranked 23th, allowing 1119 yards in total rush yards, 26 th in yards per carry (4.5), but T-4 th in rushing touchdowns with six. Surprisingly, the Broncos have surrendered one less, (9) 20+ yard carry than the Raiders defense (10) and one more 40+ yard carry (2). Here’s where it gets rougher for the Raiders and young signal caller Mendoza: the Broncos are 4 th -lowest in completion percentage (60.2), T-5 th lowest in yards per attempt (6.5). Additionally, being T-6 th in multiple categories: in sacks (26) and interceptions (8). Ranking 8 th in quarterback rating (83.4), with the only blemish being T-6 th most passing touchdowns (14) A bunch of fancy statistical numbers to say that you can, in fact, move the ball up and down the field on this Broncos defense, unlike in years past. The flip side to that is that it’s still just as hard to score on them. Potential Raiders plan of attack Can the Raiders devise a way to beat the Broncos? Yes, they can. Possibly being without, or having a limited, Brock Bowers emphasizes a change in tactics for Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak. In a pinch, Michael Mayer has been magnificent when factored into the game plan; Tre Tucker has game-breaking speed when assigned a featured role as well. Ian Thomas has contributed in the passing game; the Raiders could also throw a friendly face in with Mendoza and play wide receiver, Malik Benson. Short yardage/ red zone conversions have been catastrophic for the Raiders in 2026; the run game hasn’t been much better. In the first half of the game against the Seattle Seahawks, they found a way to generate some success. They will need to refine what was working and continue to apply it for a complete game to bring balance to the offense. The running backs, both Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr are going to need to put on some bifocals to see the holes to run through. Until the run-blocking execution improves, both backs are going to need to be able to make at least one defender miss. Moreover, both should employ a tactic like Fred Biletnikoff’s stick-em and coat their jerseys in Pam cooking spray or some sort of slick material. Making it hard to grab hold of them and easier for them to break away from would be tacklers. Al Davis had two rules: #1 cheating is encouraged, #2 See rule #1. Need a better gameplan Kubiak must have a game plan that isn’t solely reliant on #89, more so one using him as a potential decoy until he can get into the red zone or critical situations. The need to spread the football around to keep the Broncos’ defense off balance will aid his young quarterback tremendously. He will also need to account for only being able to get roughly two quarters’ worth of success maximum out of every plan he rolls out. His opening scripts are magnificent, but when the defense makes adjustments, the struggles will begin. A razzle-dazzle play, or something creatively complex and unique to call, that hasn’t been put on tape in 10 weeks will help. Three or four such plays would be ideal, whether he already has them in the playbook or not. Perhaps tweak his wide receiver deployment and utilize Jack Bech out wide; move either Jalen Nailor or Tre Tucker into the slot. Maximize the downfield blocking ability of Bech and get looser coverage on one of the other two speedier receivers. Scheme blitz beaters in the play calls, the NFL is a copycat league, a smart defensive coordinator would try to replicate what the Seahawks did last Sunday. Shotgun draws, delayed zone runs and more running back screens can help slow down the rush. Kubiak is a passing game genius; the offensive line may be more of an obstacle, but it can be overcome.

title: More on flexed Week 12 game at Cleveland
summary: This week, the NFL flexed the Las Vegas Raiders’ game at the Cleveland Browns on November 29 has been flexed into Sunday Night Football. Kickoff is set for 5:20 p.m. PT. Here are some thoughts on the decision: Not many choices: It’s a bit surprisisng that a game featuring a 4-6 team against a 6-4 […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images This week, the NFL flexed the Las Vegas Raiders’ game at the Cleveland Browns on November 29 has been flexed into Sunday Night Football . Kickoff is set for 5:20 p.m. PT. Here are some thoughts on the decision: Not many choices: It’s a bit surprisisng that a game featuring a 4-6 team against a 6-4 team would be selected to be moved into prime time on the final Sunday of November. But there there were few choices and it’s better a Drake Maye-less New England Patriots against the one-win Los Angeles Chargers, which was the original choice. Because there are five games in a Wednesday-Friday window, there were few choices. So, this was a top option. Fernando mania: There’s no doubt the fact that No. 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza is now the Raiders’ starting quarterback was part of the appeal for NBC for this choice. There will be more more prime-time opportunities in his future. A little love for the Browns: The Browns are definitely part of the ideal for this flex as well. They are 6-4 and are currently in the playoff mix. The Dawg Pound will be alive in the Browns’ first Sunday night affair in five years. No early start: This game was originally slotted for a 10 a.m. West Coast start, The Raiders are 1-1 in that time slot this season, but traditionally has struggled. So, the later start time can’t hurt. Weather could be issue: It could be cold and rainy. The current forecast calls for low 40s and a chance of rain on the shores of Lake Erie. Any more flexes this season? Could the Raiders’ get awarded a second flex? There are not many chances. The Raiders do host the Denver Broncos in Week 15, but the scheduled prime-time games Sunday and Monday games don’t look like they will be moved. However, if the Raiders beat Denver this week, perhaps the Week 15 game could be flexed to Thursday night. But the deadline for that switch will be next Tuesday. There will be three stand-alone games on Sunday of Week 18 when the Raiders play at Kansas City and the Sunday night game is open as well. So, that final game may be the Raiders’ best chance for a second stand-alone game.

title: Miami Dolphins injuries: Will the real attrition please stand up?
summary: Someone once said, usually attributed to the British statesmen Benjamin Disraeli, “There are lies, damn lies and statistics.” Are the Miami Dolphins injury prone more than other teams? If so, are we properly “insured” against them? This is a hidden reason to draft BPAs (best player available). My questions are: This Dolphins season is perplexing, […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 11: Zach Sieler #92 of the Miami Dolphins lines up for the snap in the third quarter against the Cincinnati Bengals at Hard Rock Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by JC Ruiz/Getty Images) | Getty Images Someone once said, usually attributed to the British statesmen Benjamin Disraeli, “There are lies, damn lies and statistics.” Are the Miami Dolphins injury prone more than other teams? If so, are we properly “insured” against them? This is a hidden reason to draft BPAs (best player available). My questions are: Are injuries “hiding” when veterans don’t play much in the preseason? Does every player have a “potential hidden injury” waiting to happen? Maybe just maybe, they knew, maybe the team knew, “my knee doesn’t feel right” becomes “let’s play through it and pray your ACL doesn’t tear all the way?” Do the Dolphins have more injuries than other teams(ok, I already asked that)? Why does it seem that when we lose an important piece to injury, more injuries “expose themselves”? There is some type of “cascade” affect where the first injury is followed by an injury at the same position. Were they gonna happen no matter what? Sieler, then Jordan Phillips, the Zeek Biggers. How in the hell does this happen? How many times have we all seen starter “X” was replaced by journeyman “y” and we don’t see it until the frigging first offensive play on the tv broadcast? Then the announcer says Liam Eichenberg is in for whoever. This Dolphins season is perplexing, to say the least. We have had many seasons ruined and careers ruined due to untimely injuries. I know other teams have injuries too but I hate all of them (except I like the Bears a wee bit). Let’s take a quick trip down “Injury Memory Lane” Dolphins trade for Hugh Green via Tampa Bay…promptly blows out his knee. Major league POS cheap shots HOF Center Dwight Stevenson. End of career. Dolphins draft hometown hero U of Miami WR Yatil Green….promptly blows out his knee…career basically over. When Tua went down (sorry for bringing this up), Teddy Bridgewater went out and got hurt on the very first play against the Jets. My G.O.A.T. Daniel Constantine Marino blows out his Achilles tendon while being untouched in a game in the Cleveland dump: out for the season. Then Dolphins promote Utah QB Scott Mitchell, the Phins destroy KC, and then he lasts one or two games (can’t remember). He gets hurt. We limp into Dallas on Thanksgiving Day (beat them to go to 9-2). Then Troy Vincent blows out his knee and Buffalo scores 4,000 points on us in Miami; DeBerg played decently, I think we lose 48-34. We finish 9-7. Dallas didn’t lose again that season. Cowboys Super Bowl champs! Think about that: without Marino, we beat the eventual Super Bowl champs at home in the Leon Lett ice snow game without Marino and don’t win another game that season. Aargh! These DL injuries will present a Sullivan with a new challenge: are we ok with 3 damaged DL players next year and/or should we draft another “interior” DL? We already had a need at edge. Maybe, just maybe, we can concentrate on “fixing” the glaring holes(IOL, Elite #1 WR, corner, kicker (yikes)) keeping in mind now we have a potential problem at DT. I will remind you all that the Titans drafted ELITE DL Jeffrey Simmons in the first round, even knowing he wouldn’t be available until the second half of the year due to a knee injury at Mississippi State. He seemed to come out of that ok. Ha. So we can hope our DL triumvirate comes back strong. We need them! Go Phins!

title: Miami Dolphins vs. Buffalo Bills: Three Reasons Why
summary: This week has not been kind to the making of content for this post.  The flow of hope for getting win from here on out is down to a trickle.  Let’s see if we can salvage any for this contest. 3 REASONS THE DOLPHINS WILL WIN THE BILLS PASS DEFENSE IS SUSCEPTIBLE The Bills pass […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 04: Miami Dolphins wide receiver Malik Washington (6) muffs a punt during the first half of the NFL game between the Miami Dolphins and the Minnesota Vikings on October 4th, 2026, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images This week has not been kind to the making of content for this post. The flow of hope for getting win from here on out is down to a trickle. Let’s see if we can salvage any for this contest. 3 REASONS THE DOLPHINS WILL WIN THE BILLS PASS DEFENSE IS SUSCEPTIBLE The Bills pass defense has been the weaker part of their defense this season. They had games against Joey Fagnano and Carson Wentz where they held them to under 200 combined yards. But they have allowed 250+ passing yards to just about everyone else. Last week, Kyle McCord made his debut against a weak Colts defense and played alright. He threw for 209 yards and got the RBs involved in the passing game. I don’t expect McCord to light it up, but he has the opportunity for some success against a middle of the pack pass defense. THE BILLS TURN THE BALL OVER Despite being one of two 8-1 teams in the league, they have a turnover differential of zero. They have 14 takeaways and 14 giveaways. QB Josh Allen is playing well, particularly as a rusher, leading the team with 11 rushing TDs. He is in the middle of the pack for passing TDs. But he has 7 INTS and 4 fumbles on the season. James Cook has 4 fumbles this season. Turnovers are the great equalizer, and Miami is getting better at generating them. The Dolphins have generated at least one turnover in each of the last 5 games. All it takes is for one errant throw or fumbled ball to swing momentum and turn the tide. POTENTIAL DIVISIONAL TRAP GAME I generally don’t think divisional games can be trap games, but the odds for that are never zero. The Bills face the 7-2 Chiefs the following week. Then go on the road to face New England, Green Bay, before facing Chicago and Denver. Part of me thinks Buffalo will look at this game as a must win – the final “gimme game” before a slate of playoff bound opponents. Another part of me thinks they can be looking ahead to the Chiefs and might slip up. The 1-8 Dolphins led by Kyle McCord will be easy to overlook. But if the defense steps up just enough, they can make this a tougher out than expected. 3 REASONS THE DOLPHINS WILL LOSE DECIMATION ACROSS THE LINE Miami lost 3 of their top interior defensive linemen in the span of a week. Sieler, Phillips, and Biggers are out for the season. The Dolphins are stuck relying on Kenneth Grant and some guys. The current IDL on the roster are Grant, Keith Cooper Jr., and Jordan Jefferson. They have some bigger edge players like Eric Watts (6’5” 277) and Rodney McGraw (6’4”, 273) that can perhaps move inside on some passing downs. They can also big the bigger edge players in run defense. Miami also signed Matthew Butler to the practice squad. Butler was with the Dolphins in 2025 and in camp this offseason before being cut. He adds some depth and scheme familiarity. But the Bills have one of the better offensive lines, ranked 3rd in pass block win rate and 1st in run block win rate. The Bills are the 3rd in rushing attempts, 2nd in rushing yards, 6th in yards per attempt, and 1st in rushing TDs. The Dolphins run defense had a solid game against Jahmyr Gibbs and the Lions, but had their worst outing against the Colts, allowing 172 yards, the most in any game this season. Some good news is that Grant and Cooper both had solid games against the Colts. But even if they play out of their minds this week, it is still a horrible matchup for the Dolphins. MIAMI’S OFFENSIVE LINE IS REGRESSING The Bills are at the top in terms of winning pass and run blocks. On the defensive side, they are less so. They are currently 29th in pass rush win rate and 23rd in run stop win rate. That said, the Dolphins’ run offense is stagnating. They haven’t rushed for more than 78 yards in any of the last 3 games. Having an injured Malik Willis contributed to that. However, after an early breakout for Ollie Gordon II, he has been limited to under 4 YPC in the last 3 games. Part of that for last week could be having a backup QB as the starter – defenses will worry more about the run. But part of that is the offensive line. The Lions and Pats were better run defenses. The Colts were not – one of the worst in the league and the Dolphins still couldn’t get going on the ground The offensive line has to take their share of that blame. Starting center Aaron Brewer missed last week in concussion protocol and did not practice Wednesday. He returned Thursday, but hasn’t cleared protocol just yet. His backup, Andrew Meyer, was bad against a good-not-great Colts front. Meyer was also a problem with the batted balls for McCord that cost Miami some big plays, including a potential TD. RG Jonah Savaiinaea looked like an improved player early on but has been moving in the opposite direction. In the passing game, the Bills aren’t high at the win rate, but they are 4th in the league in pressure percentage at 28%. They are tied with 4 other teams at 17th for sacks with 21. They only have 2 players with more than 1.5 sacks on the season. BUT… they have one of the league’s top rushers in Gregory Rousseau, who is tied for 4th with 8 sacks on the season. He leads the league in pressures with 37. He is NOT in the top 22 in pass rush win rate, which would lead me to believe he is getting pressures and sacks due to volume – only 4 other teams have as many or more pass attempts against them than the Bills. This leads back to Miami’s OL and Austin Jackson. He has been a liability against every top edge rusher he has faced; Aidan Hutchinson took his lunch money 2 weeks ago. Now he has to face Rousseau, who may not win as early and as often as Hutchinson but still gets to the QB. If the Dolphins can’t keep the Bills defense honest by running the ball and/or get too far behind, the Bills pass rush is very likely to heat up McCord. MIAMI DOESN’T WIN IN BUFFALO Do you remember the last time Miami won in Buffalo? I certainly do. It was the 2016 season where the Dolphins snuck out an overtime win thanks to Jay Ajayi rushing for 206 yards on 32 carries and some heroic kicks made by Andrew Franks. Outside of that game, the Dolphins haven’t had much success on the road against Buffalo. Since 2000, the Dolphins have played in Buffalo 27 times including the playoffs and have gotten 7 wins. They haven’t beaten Josh Allen in Buffalo, but this isn’t just about the Allen-led Bills. From 2000 until 2019, when Allen took over as the full-time starter, the Bills had 3 winning seasons and they were 9-7 seasons. They had three 8-8 seasons. Their record was 127-177 and the average season was 6.7 wins and 9.3 losses. Allen has started 9 games against the Dolphins in Buffalo, so that’s still 7 wins in the other 18 attempts. When they DID win, the average record for Buffalo was 6-10. The average margin of victory in those games was 10.7, and it’s been 7 or less in the last 3 times. So even when Buffalo was mid, the Dolphins still couldn’t win there. They absolutely haven’t won there any time Buffalo has finished with a winning record. The last time the Dolphins won in Buffalo in the same season Buffalo finished with a winning record was 1996. This week, the Dolphins take a talent deficient team that is now weaker due to injuries and starting a backup QB in his second ever NFL game on the road to a place they don’t win at, even when the opponent is bad. Now… the last 2 times Miami has marched into Buffalo with a backup QB starting the game, they have a record of 1-1. They got their last win with Matt Moore starting for Ryan Tannehill. Skylar Thompson went into Buffalo in the playoffs and fell just short, losing 34-31. If there is ANY hope in this regard, it’s that recent history shows Miami backups making the game a tougher…

title: Minnesota Doesn’t Need Superhero Kirk. It Needs Consistent Kirk.
summary: The Vikings can beat the 49ers—but which Kirk Cousins will show up? That question drives this episode of The Real Forno Show, as Tyler Forness and producer Dave Stefano break down Minnesota’s offensive path to victory in Mexico City. On this Vikings 1st & SKOL production, the discussion moves beyond revenge-game narratives to the matchups […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 15: Kirk Cousins #8 of the Minnesota Vikings looks on against the Green Bay Packers during the fourth quarter at Lambeau Field on November 15, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Vikings can beat the 49ers—but which Kirk Cousins will show up? That question drives this episode of The Real Forno Show , as Tyler Forness and producer Dave Stefano break down Minnesota’s offensive path to victory in Mexico City. On this Vikings 1st & SKOL production, the discussion moves beyond revenge-game narratives to the matchups that could decide the game: pass protection, attacking single-high coverage, and keeping Fred Warner from wrecking the passing attack. “There is a pathway for the Minnesota Vikings offense to beat the San Francisco 49ers,” Forness declares. However, that pathway requires something more dependable than occasional quarterback brilliance. Cousins doesn’t need to carry the Vikings by himself. Instead, Forness argues that Minnesota needs repeatable execution from a quarterback whose best moments can rival anyone’s. “He can just be a point guard,” Forness explains. “He can just be a guy who distributes the football to the weapons.” That starts with Christian Darrisaw and Brian O’Neill protecting against a San Francisco pass rush that the hosts describe as inconsistent. From there, Minnesota can attack Cover 1 and Cover 3 with intermediate in-breaking routes, dagger concepts, and seams featuring Justin Jefferson, T.J. Hockenson, and Jauan Jennings. Warner remains the major complication: his coverage range can erase those opportunities unless Kevin O’Connell uses underneath routes to draw him forward. Meanwhile, Jennings and Jordan Mason offer compelling former-team storylines—and practical ways to move the ball. Key takeaways from the episode: Consistency matters more than perfection. Forness separates Cousins’ talent from his game-to-game execution. Stefano adds that maturity could help the veteran remain “relatively calm and collected.” Protection unlocks the passing game. Keeping Nick Bosa and the 49ers’ defensive front away from Cousins would give Minnesota more chances to exploit coverage downfield. Make Warner defend forward and backward. Shallow concepts can occupy the linebacker, creating opportunities behind him rather than allowing him to drift into throwing lanes. Jennings can expand the quick game. Forness highlights screens, stick routes, short in-breakers, and selective slants as ways to capitalize on the receiver’s physicality. Mason could influence the game script. A productive rushing attack would challenge his former team while reducing the number of demanding routes Minnesota’s receivers run at altitude. Mexico City preparation matters. The hosts debate Minnesota’s altitude-chamber training, hydration, recovery, and the benefit of sleeping at home before traveling. The prediction: Minnesota wins 24–17. Still, Forness acknowledges San Francisco’s quality and makes clear that a 49ers victory would not surprise him. Listen: View Link Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: For Vikings fans seeking more than a box-score argument, this episode connects quarterback expectations with the route concepts, blocking assignments, and personnel decisions that could shape the matchup. As Forness puts it, “It just has to be good. That’s all we’re asking, just be good.” Stefano supplies the essential addition: “Be good and score some points.” Watch or listen to The Real Forno Show with Tyler Forness and Dave Stefano, a Minnesota Vikings podcast from Vikings 1st & SKOL, for the full discussion and debate. Fan with Us!!! Tyler Forness @TheRealForno of Vikings 1st & SKOL @Vikings1stSKOL and A to Z Sports @AtoZSportsNFL , with Dave Stefano @Luft_Krigare producing this Vikings 1st & SKOL production, the @RealFornoShow found at the @BleavNetwork . So here’s the question, Vikings fans: Which will matter most against San Francisco: Cousins’ consistency, Jennings’ physicality, or Mason powering the running game?

The matchup will be at Estadio Azteca, more than 7,000 ft above sea level. The air will be thin, but the tension will be thick as two of the top teams in the NFC face each other. Series Record: 25-25-1 Road Record: 8-16-1 Streak: W2 Largest Win : 35-7, September 28, 2003 Largest Defeat : 51-7, December 8, 1984 The Vikings have won 8 of the last 12 against the 49ers Kirk Cousins played against the 49ers two weeks ago, finishing with 216 yards, 1 TD and 3 INTS in a 38-17 loss. The Minnesota Vikings have allowed touchdowns on a league low 25% of opponent red-zone trips and QBs have a measly 69.5 passer rating against them in the red-zone. Dallas Turner (8.0 sacks) and Andrew Van Ginkel (8.5 sacks) are both in the top 5 in the NFL in sacks. They will look to catch Houston’s Will Anderson with 10.5 sacks on the year. The Vikings lead the league with 37 sacks on the season. The 49ers lead the league with 399.8 Yards per Game and are 2nd with 31.2 Points per Game. They will face the Vikings who are 2nd in Yards Allowed per Game (273.3) and 1st in Points Allowed Per Game (14.0). Another Sunday and another matchup against a top offense. The Vikings will face Brock Purdy and the 49ers offense in Mexico City. I expect the 49ers to focus on the run against the average Viking run defense. McCaffrey, Kaelon Black, Deebo Samuel, and even Brock Purdy are a threat to keep the chains moving. However, the Vikings defense is deep. The Vikings will be depending on players like Domonique Orange, Elijah Williams, and Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins to rotate in a little more than they typically might see. Both teams come in with strong momentum and I’m expecting an excellent game. I believe in the Vikings with Kirk, so I am taking them on the road. full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 15: Jake Golday #41 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates with teammates after recovering a fumble during the fourth quarter against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on November 15, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin.
