The Vikings already lost to the Bills but that was mainly due to a horrendous performance by Carson Wentz. You simply have to throw that game out. I think it bodes well for the playoffs provided the team gets there which I think they should and will. No matter the outcome, this game will help the team in the march toward the postseason where you really want to be playing your best. If they team wins then everyone will be slapping backs and kissing babies but it wont mean diddly. It will be nice for all the media types to be blowing that smoke where the sun don’t shine (for most) but there is a long ways to go still. The offense still needs to get it together and be more consistent. Cousins is going to help that out a bunch but the protection has to be better for him too. Cousins was kept free of pressure on three-quarters of his dropbacks, well above the typical 30% pressure benchmark, despite Green Bay entering the game with 29 season sacks. Still, the Packers got home for three sacks and hit Cousins five times. I would like to see that cleaned up some more. The 49ers have some big names on their defensive line in Nick Bosa and DeForest Buckner. They rank 26th in defensive pressure rate through nine games (and 31st in sack rate). Over their past three games specifically, their pressure rate sits at 25.8%, which ranks 31st in the league over that span. On offense, the 49ers offensive line ranks 1st in the NFL in fewest sacks allowed (13) and 3rd in fewest pressures allowed per game (8.8) Both offensive tackles rank inside the top four in ESPN’s Pass Block Win Rate—Colton McKivitz is 1st (93%) and Trent Williams is 4th (92%) 2026 NFL pass rush, run stop, blocking win rate rankings https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/49742016/2026-win-rates-team-player-rankings-pass-rush-run-stop-blocking Is Darrisaw becoming a worry? According to Pro Football Focus, he has surrendered 8 sacks in just eight games—ranking 71st out of 72 qualified tackles and tied for the most in the NFL. Darrisaw holds a 65.9 overall PFF grade (44th among 72 tackles) and a 57.3 run-blocking grade (53rd), mirroring his compromised 2025 mark (65.6) rather than the elite 80.0+ grades he posted annually from 2022 to 2024. Despite the high sack tally, Darrisaw has allowed just 12 total pressures across 447 offensive snaps—the 9th-lowest total among starting tackles. When he does lose a rep, it has resulted in a sack at an unusually high rate rather than consistent disruption. The restructuring of his salary down to the minimum all but ensures that he will be starting in 2027. The hope is that it is just taking longer for him to get back to feeling totally 100% on that knee. I think the line of scrimmages is going to determine the game. That and doing their best to handle CMC because I do not think anyone can cover him coming out the backfield. Vikings vs 49ers Prediction, Picks & Odds https://www.squawka.com/us/nfl/nfl-news/vikings-vs-49ers-prediction-picks-odds-week-11/ Four league-leading defensive numbers against three league-leading offensive ones Minnesota’s defense is the best in football and it is not an argument. They lead the NFL in sacks at 4.1 a game, in opponent rating at 69.5, in red-zone defense at 25.0% and in touchdowns conceded at 1.3. San Francisco’s offense is the best in football on the same basis. They lead the league in touchdowns at 4.1 a game, in third down at 52.0% and in the red zone at 82.8%, and Brock Purdy rated 154.5 last week. The tiebreaker may be the other halves. Minnesota throw for 163.2 yards a game, 31st in the NFL, and San Francisco reach the quarterback 1.8 times a game, 29th — so each side’s weakness points away from the other’s strength. … Vikings vs 49ers prediction and score projection San Francisco win 24-20. Minnesota’s defense will make this uncomfortable and low-scoring, but an offense throwing for 163.2 yards a game has to find more than twenty points against an 8-1 team. … I will push back against this stat based prediction because the 163.2 yards passing per game is no longer relevant. I think the Vikings are going to need to sustain a few long drives that results in points. Minnesota Vikings News and Links Seven things Solak thinks for NFL Week 11: Takes on four QBs, Lions, Rams, more https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/50505355/week-11-seven-things-solak-thinks-burrow-mvp-rams-lions I think … Vikings-49ers is the coolest game of the season The Vikings have had a fraught three weeks. Everyone was excited to see them face the Lions in Week 8 — the best offense they’d faced in a while. Detroit stuck it to ’em with a sick schematic wrinkle for which the Vikings were not prepared — multiple tight ends lined up in the backfield as quasi-fullbacks to pave open rushing lanes. … This is quite literally the best against the best. The 49ers lead the league in points per drive (3.0), success rate and EPA per play on offense. The Vikings lead the league in points per drive (1.24), success rate and EPA per play (if you eliminate the Bucs’ rainstorm game against the Falcons, which is cheating, but I don’t care) on defense. It does not get better for offensive football than what the 49ers are doing right now. It does not get better for defensive football than what the Vikings are doing right now. Snap the pool stick, toss it down at midfield and let’s see who survives. Not only are these the most effective units on their respective sides of the ball — there’s actually some structural similarity between the two. The Flores defense has been exhaustively covered this season, but if you’ve missed them to this point of the season: The Vikings are blitzing on 72.3% of opposing dropbacks through 10 weeks. I shouldn’t need to tell you where that ranks among league defenses, but just in case: It’s first. To blitz that much sounds deranged (and likely is), but Flores has greatly deepened the meaning of blitz packages in the modern NFL. He doesn’t blitz to get the quarterback down, but blitzes to force the ball out fast to predictable hot reads. He blitzes to keep the back and tight end in protection and limit the pass-catching options the opponent can deploy. For many defensive coordinators, the blitz is an end to itself — they want to get to third-and-long so they can blitz. For Flores, the blitz is a means to many different ends depending on the opponent and context. Let’s consider the route distributions. Opposing offenses get all five routes into the concept 31.2% of the time against the Vikings, which is the lowest number in any season as far back as I have data (2017). The aggressive blitz fronts — with five or six (or seven or eight) bodies on them — keep backs and tight ends in the formation to protect, which makes the Vikings all the more dangerous when they drop bodies into coverage and only bring four on the rush. Against the Vikings’ four-man rush, opposing quarterbacks are averaging an eternity to throw the ball (3.34 seconds, highest in the NFL Next Gen Stats database) and still suffer a 44% pressure rate, which leads the league. Flip the coin to the other side, and you’ll discover that no offense gets five routes into the concept more often than the San Francisco 49ers. On 72.5% of Brock Purdy’s dropbacks this season, the 49ers have five eligible in the concept — that’s tied for the highest rate of any offense over the past two seasons with … the 2025 49ers. Why so many players out in the concept? It is indicative of a change that’s been underway in San Francisco’s offense since the Christian McCaffrey trade in 2022. When you employ…

summary: Fresh off a dominant 30–10 beating of the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field in Week 10, the Minnesota Vikings sit at 7–2 and are packing their bags for an international prime-time test on Sunday night against the 8–1 San Francisco 49ers at Estadio Azteca in Mexico City. The Vikings will not only face their […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - NOVEMBER 15: Levi Drake Rodriguez #50 of the Minnesota Vikings reacts during the third quarter against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on November 15, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fresh off a dominant 30–10 beating of the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field in Week 10, the Minnesota Vikings sit at 7–2 and are packing their bags for an international prime-time test on Sunday night against the 8–1 San Francisco 49ers at Estadio Azteca in Mexico City. The Vikings will not only face their toughest opponent, they will do so in the very thin air. When NFL teams head out west, Denver’s Empower Field at Mile High feet usually serves as the benchmark for thin air. Estadio Azteca makes Denver look like a warm-up. Sitting at roughly 7,352 feet above sea level, Azteca is more than 2,000 feet higher than Denver. At that elevation, air pressure drops to roughly 77% of sea-level norms, meaning players take in roughly a quarter less oxygen per breath. Lactic acid builds up faster, recovery between sprints takes longer, and third- and fourth-quarter conditioning becomes a battle of the fittest. Meanwhile, thinner air reduces aerodynamic drag by around 23%, which means kicked balls and deep throws can sail a little further and flatter than kickers and defenders expect. Both teams are attempting to adjust to the altitude. The 49ers have spent the week in Colorado Springs at Falcon Stadium, 6,621 ft above sea level. The Vikings routinely use an altitude training room so players can feel the effects of lower oxygen levels. Time will tell which team has prepared the best. Most games are decided in the 4th quarter, this game in particular I expect swings in momentum and the team with the higher time of possession is likely the team that pulls away late. The Vikings defense is susceptible to the run and Christian McCaffrey is going to be featured heavily no matter where the game is played. The team will be dependent on the Viking offense to sustain drives and give them some time to catch their breath. Kirk Cousins arrived just in time to help, we’ll see if he can get it accomplished on Sunday Night Football.

title: Patriots 2026 rookie class: Performance review at Pats’ bye
summary: There are multiple reasons why the New England Patriots’ 2026 season so far has been one of ups and downs. full_text: There are multiple reasons why the New England Patriots’ 2026 season so far has been one of ups and downs. Be it injuries, individual mistakes, coaching or a more challenging schedule, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel has had a tougher time playing winning football than it did a year ago. One other factor contributing to this is the impact of the rookie class. Whereas last year’s group produced three instant starters as well as other valuable contributors, the latest batch of first-year players has not changed the team on quite the same level. Even though this means that questions do remain about the group as a whole, there have been some encouraging stretches of play as well as glimpses into a bright football. So, with no football being played at One Patriot Place this week, let’s take a look at the that rookie class to see where its members stand 10 weeks into their professional careers. Draft picks OT Caleb Lomu: The Patriots traded up in the first round of the draft to select Lomu as a future starter along their offensive line. However, with Will Campbell and Morgan Moses both entrenched into the top spots at left and right tackle, respectively, the Utah product has had to start his career primarily as a backup. He has seen his most consistent action as an eligible extra blocker but did get opportunities to replace both Campbell and Moses either late in blowouts or as an injury stand-in. In total, he has played 163 snaps between left and right tackle and generally looked good. The plan therefore seemingly remains in place: he is expected to take over as New England’s right tackle as soon as this coming offseason. | 10 games (2 starts), 31.4% offensive snaps, 14.7% special teams snaps ED Gabe Jacas: “Patience” was the theme of the offseason for New England’s second-round draft pick, who, like Caleb Lomu, was also acquired following a trade up the board. Injury recovery and contract negotiations dragged on into training camp, and when he finally took the field, Jacas did not look ready to compete. However, something started to click after the end of training camp and the start of the regular season. Since then, he has played with his hair on fire and looked like one of the best rookie edges — and one of the best defenders, period — in the class. In 10 games so far, he registered 28 quarterback pressures, including 3.5 sacks, and an interception, and leads all first-year players at his position with 14 run stops. The future is looking bright. | 10 games (0 starts), 55.5% defensive snaps, 32.0% special teams snaps TE Eli Raridon: New England had been looking for a suitable second all-around tight end for years, and it finally seems to have found one. While Raridon’s run blocking remains a work in progress and he has been at the point of attack at multiple stuffed runs throughout the season, he has shown some promise in that area. More than that, however, he has shown promise as a pass catcher: in his nine games so far, the third-round pick caught 17 passes for 231 yards and a pair of touchdowns. The numbers are not eye-opening, but they and his 51.6% playing time share illustrate that he has been actively involved as a No. 2 tight end alongside starter Hunter Henry. It will be interesting to see if the rate of two-tight end sets featuring the pair will increase from its 16.8% over the first 10 weeks, and how Raridon’s role as a whole will develop. | 9 games (5 starts), 51.6% offensive snaps, 3.0% special teams snaps CB Karon Prunty: Chosen in the fifth round, Prunty was the highest-picked of the Patriots’ non-roster-lock selections in this year’s draft. Despite his status as a Day 3 pick, he did manage to make the team and carve out a role as a part-time special teamer and emergency backup at cornerback. While a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury disrupted his first half-season, Prunty has developed into a Core 4 special teamer. He also has seen the field on occasion as a perimeter cornerback, even though he remains the fifth option on the positional depth chart. | 5 games (0 starts), 4.9% defensive snaps, 34.2% special teams snaps Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create community posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . OT Dametrious Crownover: Crownover looks like a prototypical offensive tackle, but so far he has not been given any opportunities to showcase himself at his listed position. Primarily a healthy scratch for much of the year, he played only two games so far and saw no offensive snaps. His seven combined snaps in Weeks 1 and 8 came as part of the field goal and extra point protection units. The sixth-round selection enters the bye as New England’s fifth tackle. | 2 games (0 starts), 2.6% special teams snaps LB Namdi Obiazor: Although his defensive opportunities have been limited to late-game duty and he remains an emergency backup at his listed position, Obiazor has been actively and consistently involved so far: the sixth-rounder is ranked first on the Patriots with 223 special teams snaps and is tied for third with seven tackles. He is a Core 4 performer in the game’s third phase and has been since the start of the season. title: Patriots mailbag: What’s wrong with the defense?
summary: Behind back-to-back blowout losses and losing Drake Maye to injury, the New England Patriots season has quickly derailed over the last two weeks. Now, they have plenty questions to answers after a much needed bye week. So, let’s get into some of those in this week’s edition of the #PostPulpit Mailbag. What has gone so […]
full_text: Behind back-to-back blowout losses and losing Drake Maye to injury , the New England Patriots season has quickly derailed over the last two weeks. Now, they have plenty questions to answers after a much needed bye week. So, let’s get into some of those in this week’s edition of the #PostPulpit Mailbag. What has gone so wrong with the defense? They’re relatively healthy and have a lot of the same personnel as last year. Kuhr did a great job last year and really earned the official promotion to DC. So what happened? Along the same lines, do you think Gonzo is really the type of player who, now that he’s gotten his payday, is going to sit on his laurels for the remainder of his career? – TDDsDad Is the defense’s biggest problem the square peg or round hole – scheme doesn’t fit players or players don’t fit scheme – spyponder90 The Patriots defense has a litany of problems right now. Here’s how we’d break them down: Zone coverage: Statistically, the Patriots are the worst zone coverage team in football, ranking dead last in both EPA and passer rating allowed in zone coverage. Defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr was a step ahead of opposing offenses earlier this season with his disguises in the secondary, but teams have caught on while New England’s defensive backs have failed to live up to their potential. Some of the issues in zone coverage also tie back to the pass rush. The Patriots rank 20th in the league in four-man pressure rate, giving opposing quarterbacks time to find the voids in coverage. To generate pressure, New England has had to blitz, which then leaves more space for the offense to attack with at least one defender taken out of coverage — as seen on Jahmyr Gibbs’ 50-yard reception last week. Man coverage: The logical follow-up would be to play more man coverage, especially with New England’s talented cover corners. The Patriots already rank near the top of the league in man coverage rate, but no team can rely on man coverage for the majority of a game for several reasons. Without an effective changeup, opposing offenses have game-planned for man coverage and exploit it with beaters such as stacks and bunch formations. On top of that, the talented cover corners have again not been playing to their potential. Effort/tackling: New England is not a poor tackling team by the numbers, but the defense often doesn’t appear to be rallying to the football — a concern when Mike Vrabel has made effort and finish his No. 1 non-negotiable . Opponents are piling up yards after the catch and yards after contact against New England. That reached a new low last week, when the Lions generated 220 yards after the catch and another 135 yards after contact on the ground. The effort doesn’t always show up on film, either. The defensive line allowed Detroit to average 4.5 yards before contact (!). Defenders in the secondary often take poor angles and seem more focused on ripping the ball out than getting the ball carrier to the ground. Coaching: Lastly, when it comes to Christian Gonzalez, there is too much evidence to suggest he isn’t an elite cornerback in this league. The fact that he — along with other talented players such as Milton Williams and Craig Woodson — has regressed makes it difficult not to point the biggest arrow at the coaching staff. It might be time for the staff to go back to the basics to try and get things corrected. Do you feel the coaching staff is getting a pass on this season’s regression because of all the injuries? – Ricky Hot Pants They shouldn’t be, at least on the defensive side of the ball. This is the second most expensive defense in football that has largely been healthy outside of missing Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis for a handful of games. The results have been terrible over the last month. And while I’m not putting Mike Vrabel on the hot seat and believe he will be the coach next season, it’s concerning that his message does not seem to be getting through to the players currently as they are not playing to his identity, such as effort and finish. Some of his comments in the media the past two weeks have also raised eyebrows. Give us some Pats Pulpit O-line grades. How have player performed and who can be positive contributors next year. – Chu Big picture first: The Patriots’ offensive line ranks sixth in PFF pass-blocking grade but drops to 23rd in run-blocking. That largely matches the eye test. As a pass-protection unit, offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels has done a good job assisting his linemen with chip help, moving pockets, etc. Still, the group ranks near the top of the league in unblocked pressures allowed. It’s been a difficult season for this unit from a health standpoint, with 13 different offensive line combinations contributing to some of the communication issues and miscues. However, here are some individual notes on the healthy linemen: Will Campbell: Back healthy, the second-year tackle has taken a positive step forward, adding more variety to his pass sets over the offseason. He still has a handful of non-competitive quick losses that need to be cleaned up, and it’s worth noting that his two worst performances this season have come against top competition (Bills, Lions). Campbell does remain a strong run blocker. Jared Wilson: The move back to center has treated Wilson well, as the 23-year-old has developed into an impressive one-on-one pass blocker after some early-season struggles. We’d still like to see his eyes improve when he’s left uncovered, but his athleticism has stood out in space and at the second level. Morgan Moses: It’s understandable that fans want to see first-round pick Caleb Lomu get an opportunity, but nothing Moses has done this season warrants benching him. The 35-year-old has battled through injuries as usual and has allowed just 14 pressures and two quarterback hits through 10 games. Are you a tanker Brian? Do you feel sacrificing your integrity as a sportsman to cheat out another team for their earned draft spot is acceptable? – PatsHowYouDoIt Let’s face it the Pats are mediocre this year. There is no saving this season. Should the Pats just cut bait and prepare for next season? – luckyfukikentucky I’m #TeamTank in the right situation. Back in 2023, piling up losses was the best thing the Patriots could do to put themselves in position to draft Drake Maye. But now, with the coach and quarterback in place, I’d much rather see some fight from this team over the final seven games. Hey Brian. Easy one today: Will the AJ Brown trade go down as the worst trade in franchise history? – Pat in Agawam I’m not ready to go there yet because I do believe A.J. Brown can still be productive next season. He still looked like a difference-maker before suffering the high ankle sprain, which I believe derailed his season completely. He’ll be 30, and the injuries have started to pile up, so he might not be the 1,200-yard version of A.J. Brown anymore. Still, I believe he can be a useful player moving forward. That said, giving up a first-round pick for that isn’t great business regardless. Jimmy G coming back would at least be fun, right? In a Kirk Cousins in Minnesota kinda way? – slunkywontergreen Considering Jimmy G. hasn’t really played football in multiple seasons and wasn’t good when he last did, I don’t think I’d have much fun watching. I feel like the 2016 Patriots team would agree with that assessment. That’s all for this week’s #PostPulpit mailbag. If you have questions you’d liked to be answered next week, submit them online in our weekly submission post on the Feed. Make sure to follow @iambrianhines and @PatsPulpit as well.

title: Drake Maye injury: Everything we know about the Patriots QB’s status
summary: Their Week 10 game against the Detroit Lions was the worst-case scenario for the New England Patriots. Not only were they blown out with a final score of 35-10 to drop to 5-5 on the season, they also lost their starting quarterback to an injury: Drake Maye exited the game in the first quarter due […]
full_text: Their Week 10 game against the Detroit Lions was the worst-case scenario for the New England Patriots. Not only were they blown out with a final score of 35-10 to drop to 5-5 on the season, they also lost their starting quarterback to an injury: Drake Maye exited the game in the first quarter due to what was later announced as an ankle injury. Shortly after the game, information was scarce but the first bits and pieces have started to come in. Based on everything we know, here is what we can say about Maye and his injury situation. What happened? The Patriots started Sunday’s game against the Lions with the ball, and actually moved down the field relatively well; it took them only eight plays to get from their own 25-yard line to the Detroit 3. Once there, however, things started to fall apart. Two penalties bookending an incomplete pass set up a 3rd-and-goal from the 13-yard line, and that play turned into a disaster for the Patriots. Aidan Hutchinson easily got around left tackle Christian Elliss, and dragged Maye down from behind and he was climbing an increasingly collapsing pocket. Along the way, the two-time Pro Bowl edge came down on Maye’s right ankle. He did get up under his own power, but Maye showed a noticeable limp while making his way toward the sideline. Once there, he received attention from the team’s medical staff and afterwards headed into the blue medical tent. When he emerged, still clearly hobbled, backup quarterback Tommy DeVito was already getting ready to enter the game. Maye slowly walked back to the locker room shortly thereafter, and initially labeled questionable to return by the team. Midway through the second quarter, he was downgraded to out. What do we know about the injury? Neither head coach Mike Vrabel nor any of his teammates were able to provide an update on Maye’s status during their post-game media availability. “Obviously, he wasn’t able to finish the game, so we’ll have to get some more tests run and we’ll see when we come back what it ends up being and the severity of whatever injury he has,” Vrabel said at the podium. “I know that it was a low leg injury. I don’t know the exact details of it but I know he couldn’t go back in. … He couldn’t function. Couldn’t play. Couldn’t run. Couldn’t do whatever he needed to do to play quarterback, to protect himself, to execute, or function at that level.” Left tackle Will Campbell, who briefly occupied the blue medical tent before Maye went in, gave some more information in the postgame locker room. “I talked to him,” Campbell told MassLive’s Mark Daniels. “He’s in good spirits and just waiting to hear more information about what it is, and just told him I love him and praying for him and he’s going to be fine. He’s a fighter. Whatever comes his way, he’s going to attack it full head of steam and come back better.” The Patriots will fly back to the United States on Sunday, with some follow-up testing expected to take place after the team’s arrival on Monday. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] Initial reports suggest that Maye suffered a “significant lower leg injury” that might keep him out for the remainder of the season. For the Patriots, this is very much the worst-case scenario. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] The Patriots are concerned that Maye suffered a fractured ankle against the Lions. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] Drake Maye did not travel back to the United States with the rest of the Patriots, per head coach Mike Vrabel. “He’ll be traveling back here shortly. Just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely. The things that go around injuries and just wanted to make sure everything was in line for him to travel, and it seems like he is. He’ll be returning here, I think, shortly.” [UPDATE 11/16/2026] If indeed diagnosed as a fractured ankle, Drake Maye would “almost certainly” be out for the rest of the season, according to a report by Ian Rapoport. [UPDATE 11/17/2026] Appearing on local radio, Patriots safety Kevin Byard said that Maye was “probably out for the season.” [UPDATE 11/19/2026] Speaking to Scott Zolak in a 1-on-1 interview, Mike Vrabel referenced Maye’s injury being a “short term” issue : “I think he’s going to be unavailable here for the short time, and we’ll see how that goes down the road.” What does it mean for the Patriots? “Any time your starting quarterback goes out and is not able to return, there are questions,” safety Kevin Byard told the media after the game. The questions mentioned by Byard are manifold in the direct aftermath of both the injury and the contest as a whole. Information about severity or a potential recovery timeline is limited, which in turn also limits the avenues the Patriots might have to explore in the immediate or long-term future. What we do know is that for however long Maye is sidelined, Tommy DeVito will be the top quarterback on the depth chart with third-stringer Behren Morton backing him up. DeVito completed 12 of 24 pass attempts for 81 yards with one touchdown and interception each after entering the Lions game midway through the first period. DeVito described his and the offense’s performance after he took over for Maye as “not good enough.” The next chance to improve upon it will come after the Patriots’ upcoming bye, with a Sunday Night game versus the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 12. New England will not start its on-field preparation for that game until a few days beforehand; the team will return to its usual in-game schedule following the bye. [UPDATE 11/16/2026] If the injury is indeed as significant as believed, here is a rundown of how it would impact the Patriots moving forward.

title: Drake Maye injury update: Mike Vrabel makes curious statement about Patriots QB
summary: With the New England Patriots on their bye, information coming out of Foxborough about quarterback Drake Maye’s status has been limited. However, a new video posted by the team adds more pieces to the puzzle. In the clip, head coach Mike Vrabel sits down with color commentator Scott Zolak to talk about, among other topics, […]
full_text: With the New England Patriots on their bye, information coming out of Foxborough about quarterback Drake Maye’s status has been limited. However, a new video posted by the team adds more pieces to the puzzle. In the clip, head coach Mike Vrabel sits down with color commentator Scott Zolak to talk about, among other topics, Maye’s injury status. “I think he’s going to be unavailable here for the short time, and we’ll see how that goes down the road,” Vrabel said. “We’ll have to prepare to win without Drake in the short term and then how we handle and how we react to that, there’s a lot of things to be able to play for and to compete for. Adversity strikes a lot of different teams in the National Football League, and I’m excited to see how we respond to it.” Vrabel’s usage of the phrases “short time” and “short term” is curious in light of the information available about the injury so far. At the very least, he seems to leave the door open for a return at some point this season. According to reports, Maye suffered a fractured ankle against the Detroit Lions last Sunday that might keep him out for the remainder of the season; teammate Kevin Byard also hinted at that eventual outcome earlier this week. From that perspective, Vrabel’s “short term” might refer to the issue not being expected to impact the young passer’s preparation for the 2027 season. Of course, further testing also might have revealed a more optimistic prognosis. There might be a theoretical chance of Maye returning later during the 2026 season, either late in the regular season or at one point in the playoffs. Regardless of his outlook in the short and long term, the Patriots are ready to prepare backup Tommy DeVito as their starter for the time being. “Made great strides last year, great improvements,” Vrabel said in the same interview about DeVito. “But also, there are going to be some things here going into the games that are going to have to improve. I know that he’s an elite competitor with great toughness, and he’ll do anything that he can to give us a chance to win.” Coming out of their bye week, the Patriots are set to take on the Los Angeles Chargers on the road. The game was flexed out of its primetime slot to a 4:05 kickoff earlier this week.

title: Bill Belichick, Robert Kraft one step closer to Pro Football Hall of Fame induction
summary: Two key members of the New England Patriots dynasty are a step closer to Pro Football Hall of Fame induction. Former head coach Bill Belichick and team owner Robert Kraft have been selected by the Hall of Fame’s respective coach and contributor subcommittees as candidates for induction in 2027. They are now among 15 total […]
full_text: Two key members of the New England Patriots dynasty are a step closer to Pro Football Hall of Fame induction. Former head coach Bill Belichick and team owner Robert Kraft have been selected by the Hall of Fame’s respective coach and contributor subcommittees as candidates for induction in 2027. They are now among 15 total candidates, who are up for the final voting rounds in February. They will be joined by 13 as-of-yet-unannounced players at a later point. Belichick, 74, emerged from a group of five coaching nominees, beating out the likes of Tom Coughlin, Mike Holmgren, Dan Reeves and Mike Shanahan. A six-time Super Bowl champion as New England’s head coach, who also earned two rings as defensive coordinator with the New York Giants, he won a combined 69% 0f regular season and playoff games between 2000 and 2023 and earned nine conference championships and 17 division titles. Including a previous head-coaching tenure with the Browns, he ranks second all-time in NFL coaching wins with 333 and first with 31 postseason victories; he also is a member of the NFL’s 100th Anniversary Team Seemingly a lock to make the Hall of Fame based on his unrivaled résumé, Belichick was denied the honor of first-ballot induction last year in what is arguably the most controversial decision in the Hall of Fame’s history. His exclusion from the 2026 class drew heavy criticism and set the stage for the implementation of sweeping changes to the selection process . Kraft, 85, garnered the subcommittee’s support over fellow contributor nominees Ralph Hay, Virginia McCaskey, Doug Williams and John Wooten. His ownership saw the Patriots turn from a relative afterthought into the NFL’s most successful franchise. Besides winning six Super Bowls and reaching five others, he also oversaw 20 AFC East titles, 23 playoff berths, and only six losing seasons. The club has sold out every home game since he bought it in 1994, and won a combined 66% of games along the way. To make it into the Hall of Fame, Belichick and Kraft will need to garner at least 80% of votes from the full selection committee at its next meeting ahead of the Super Bowl. The group will first be reduced from 15 to 10, with between three and seven finalists ultimately receiving the honor. The expectation is that former Patriots tight end Rob Gronkowski will join them among the 15 candidates.

full_text: Mike Vrabel was introduced as the 16th head coach of the New England Patriots on January 13, 2025, and that day he outlined his vision for the team. “We’re going to ask our players to just do a few things. One is to put the team first, to know what to do, and to play fast and aggressive,” he explained at the time. “We’re going to play with detail. We’re going to play with technique. We’re going to play with fundamentals. There’s going to be a brand of football that everybody associated with our team or our fans is going to be proud of.” To his and his team’s credit, the Patriots have done so more often than not in the one and a half seasons since he took charge of the franchise. It contributed to the team going from back-to-back four-win seasons to the Super Bowl, and it also helped repair a culture that has started showing significant cracks toward the tail-end of the Bill Belichick era and the ill-fated Jerod Mayo experiment. Lately, however, Vrabel’s team has failed to deliver on his promise. The losses are one thing — the Patriots are currently 5-5 and entering their bye week off two straight blowout defeats — but the nature in which they happened is another. In Week 9 against the Green Bay Packers and Week 10 against the Detroit Lions, the Patriots were not just beaten, they were outclassed and outhit in all three phases. And they know it, too. “They played harder than us today. They played more physical than us today,” said safety Kevin Byard after Sunday’s 35-10 defeat to the Lions in Munich. “As a defense, that feels like a slap in the face that we let them play harder. We knew they were a team that play with effort and finish. The fact that we didn’t get it done is very disappointing.” “They played harder than we did,” echoed Mike Vrabel a day later. “They certainly outplayed us, they outcoached us, and they played harder. So, we’ll have to continue to find those messages and find those actions and behaviors that are positive and show them the success that it leads to, and then the ones where it doesn’t.” When Vrabel was hired, his qualities as a “CEO-type” head coach were one of the main selling points to the Patriots’ ownership. However, he couldn’t rebuild the organizational culture by himself: players both retained and added from the outside also had an active hand in that. In 2026, however, some of the key actors from his first season are no longer available. Locker room leaders like Garrett Bradbury, Jaylinn Hawkins and especially Stefon Diggs all left during the offseason, while Harold Landry has spent all year so far on the physically unable to perform list. That is not to say that their presence would have directly impacted the product on the field as well as the leadership off of it; hindsight is 20/20 in that regard. Nonetheless, somebody will have to step up in order to steady the ship and steer it out of the rough waters it currently finds itself in. First and foremost, that somebody needs to be Mike Vrabel. What his leadership response will look like remains to be seen, but it seemingly already began after the loss in Munich. Patriots players and their coach alike spoke about being 0-0, a message that originated with Vrabel and should signify a fresh start for a team at a crossroads: the playoff race starts heating up, and New England might have just lost its starting quarterback for the season. “We’ll just have to have some sort of a reset here with the bye and being 5-5. There are a lot of teams that go in different directions at this point in the season,” he explained on Monday. “I know that everybody’s searching for the right thing to say. Knowing that the more you search, the more that it gets picked apart. I think what happens is we’re used to being in positions to give ourselves a chance to win. When you’re not in those positions, it gets frustrating. It gets disappointing. It’s a lot of emotions.” In the past, Vrabel and his hand-picked roster have managed to turn emotions into performance. Of course, those emotions were mostly positive; the process at some point became self-sustaining in 2025. Now that the situation has changed, however, the pressure will be on the Patriots’ leadership and especially the head coach to find a way to harness whichever energy emanates from the locker room. If not, the last couple of weeks might just have been a preview of what lies ahead.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Saints Draft Position: NFL Week 11
summary: Last season, even when the New Orleans Saints were consistently losing, their draft pick was not moving much because of how bad other teams were. This season is similar, and as of writing this, 12 teams only have 3 wins. It creates a situation where the Saints will barely move if they lose because everyone […]
full_text: IOWA CITY, IA - NOVEMBER 22: Offensive lineman Kade Pieper #58 of the Iowa Hawkeyes before the match-up against the Michigan State Spartans at Kinnick Stadium on November 22, 2025 in Iowa City, Iowa. (Photo by Matthew Holst/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last season, even when the New Orleans Saints were consistently losing, their draft pick was not moving much because of how bad other teams were. This season is similar, and as of writing this, 12 teams only have 3 wins. It creates a situation where the Saints will barely move if they lose because everyone else is also losing. So, looking at their current draft position, the Saints are set to select at pick 11 overall. For this edition, I wanted to do a trade back to the mid-20s and look at the prospects there. OL Kade Pieper First, let’s start with the offensive line. Sadly, Jeremiah Wright has not secured the Saints RG spot, and Cesar Ruiz could be on his way out. Erik McCoy’s time in New Orleans may also be coming to an end soon, which would leave the Saints having to fill both center and right guard. In the draft, Iowa offensive lineman Kade Pieper would make perfect sense as an option. He was a star at RG for Iowa, becoming a first-team All-American. This season, he was moved to center and is playing well there. He will allow the Saints some flexibility, playing RG his rookie year and potentially moving to center if McCoy leaves in 2028. LB Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa Next is on defense. LB is an underrated need for the Saints with how well Kaden Elliss has played, but they need to find someone to put next to him. Investing a high pick in that position could set up the defense really well, and if Chris Cole is gone early in the first, trading back for Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa would be a great move. Viliamu-Asa can play throughout the defense, is an incredible run defender, is very athletic, and is a tackling machine. He has dealt with injuries and can be a target in the passing game, which is why he won’t be a higher pick, but at the back of the first round, he could be a really good option.

title: If Saints win/lose vs. Bears
summary: The New Orleans Saints are on the road again when they face the Chicago Bears in Week 11 on Sunday. Here’s what either result could mean for the black and gold. If the Saints win: A win would be one of the shocks of the week across the NFL. Odds makers give the Saints little […]
full_text: The New Orleans Saints are on the road again when they face the Chicago Bears in Week 11 on Sunday. Here’s what either result could mean for the black and gold. If the Saints win: A win would be one of the shocks of the week across the NFL. Odds makers give the Saints little chance; they’re coming off a home game in which they blew a huge opportunity to somewhat grab a hold of the division. Despite returning closer to full health at key positions, Kellen Moore’s squad continues to squander chances to win games. In Chicago, there will be no room for error. If the Saints can pull it off, it drags them straight back into the playoff picture and would certainly mark a statement victory. If the Saints lose: A defeat to Chicago wouldn’t come as a surprise to many, and it would be another step toward missing the playoffs in the weak NFC South. It feels as though New Orleans doesn’t have to be where they are. But even if they were nearer or above .500 right now, this is still a game that would be chalked up as a loss in a lot of fans’ eyes. Should the Saints continue to drift away from the division lead, it won’t be the Bears game that got them there, but the ones that have come before. Do you give the Saints a chance to pull it off in Chicago? Let us know in the comments!
author: Sam Mackenzie

summary: The 3-6 New Orleans Saints are headed to the Windy City this weekend to take on the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field. It’s a matchup in which few are giving the Saints a chance to win, but New Orleans is on a mission looking to silence the doubters and pull off a major upset on […]

It’s a matchup in which few are giving the Saints a chance to win, but New Orleans is on a mission looking to silence the doubters and pull off a major upset on the road. Chicago enters Sunday’s contest with an impressive 7-2 record, riding a four-game winning streak and are coming off a bye week. The Bears have emerged as one of the NFC’s stronger teams, averaging nearly 27 points per game. They have been dominant on defense, particularly on third down, making it difficult for opposing offenses to sustain drives. title: Our Defense vs. Their Offense: Chicago Bears
summary: The Chicago Bears and head coach Ben Johnson will be bringing the 7th-ranked offense in the NFL with them when they play the New Orleans Saints on Sunday. The Bears may have a young, budding superstar QB in Caleb Williams, but they are a ball-control, run-dominant offense. The Bears lead the league in time of […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 15: Cameron Jordan #94 of the New Orleans Saints celebrates with Kaden Elliss #55 after a sack against the Carolina Panthers during the second half of a game at Caesars Superdome on November 15, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Chicago Bears and head coach Ben Johnson will be bringing the 7th-ranked offense in the NFL with them when they play the New Orleans Saints on Sunday. The Bears may have a young, budding superstar QB in Caleb Williams, but they are a ball-control, run-dominant offense. The Bears lead the league in time of possession at 34:31 and rushing attempts with 303, and they average over 4 yards per rush. They are second in the NFL with 17 rushing TDs. The efficiency of this offense does not stop there. They are in the top 5 in rushing yards, averaging 142 yards per game, and third-down conversions at 45.3%. As dynamic as Caleb Williams is as a QB, the passing offense has not been highlight-reel explosive. That does not mean Williams cannot make those types of plays, but Johnson has done a very good job this year of keeping the offense on schedule, and Williams is creating when he needs to. The passing offense ranks 12th in the NFL, averaging 241 yards per game. They only have 10 passing TDs so far this season. Part of the reason for this is that Williams was unable to play for three weeks due to a hamstring injury. He has not missed a game since returning against Atlanta, and the Bears have not lost since his return. The Saints are bringing one of the worst defensive units in the league to Soldier Field on Sunday. The Saints’ defense will have to enter this game with the mentality that they cannot allow Chicago to run the ball. This is easier said than done because the Saints are 27th in rushing defense, allowing 129 yards per game on the ground. The advantage the Saints will have is when the Bears drop back to pass. The Saints have 26 sacks on the season so far and are tied for 9th in the NFL. If they can force Williams to throw the ball and keep him contained within the pocket, they will have a chance to cause negative plays. The Saints’ defense will have to be opportunistic and create chaos in the backfield for Chicago. Williams is getting better, but he also has 5 interceptions on the season with only 8 TDs. Can the Saints make him feel uncomfortable and force him to give the ball up? The Saints will have to slow down D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai. This running back combination has accounted for over 900 rushing yards on 215 carries and 13 rushing touchdowns. This further stresses the importance of forcing the Bears into third-and-long situations and obvious passing downs so the edge rushers and Kaden Elliss can play to their strengths. The Saints will look to shock the NFL and hand the Bears their third loss of the year. Do you think the Saints’ defense can stop the Bears’ offense?

title: Saints Rookie Report: Week 10 review vs. the Panthers
summary: The New Orleans Saints rookies had a chance to make a big impact against the Carolina Panthers, but only one player did.  WR Jordyn Tyson Well, let’s start with the one player. Jordyn Tyson was arguably the best player on the field every time the Saints offense was out there. Kellen Moore made sure to […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - NOVEMBER 15: Jordyn Tyson #0 of the New Orleans Saints celebrates after his team's rushing touchdown against the Carolina Panthers in the third quarter of a game at Caesars Superdome on November 15, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints rookies had a chance to make a big impact against the Carolina Panthers, but only one player did. WR Jordyn Tyson Well, let’s start with the one player. Jordyn Tyson was arguably the best player on the field every time the Saints offense was out there. Kellen Moore made sure to use him as much as possible, to the point it even happened too much. Tyson is just always open, and he made some really difficult contested catches. He has not been able to get in the end zone just yet, but these first two games have been excellent. I expect him to have another great game, but I would love to see more downfield shots to Tyson. DT Christen Miller Sadly, Miller is on IR and will not be playing for at least the next four weeks. TE Oscar Delp Another week, another game where Delp is not utilized enough on offense. The Saints are at a point this season where the Saints just need to try new things, and Fant may not be here next season if the team wants more cap space. We must see more of Delp soon. G Jeremiah Wright It’s clear right now that Jeremiah Wright needs time to become a certified starter. He has some good moments, but just isn’t ready yet. The issue is that the Siants have no other option at right guard until Erik McCoy can return to center. If he can’t, then Wright will have a tough job ahead of him against the Bears. WR Bryce Lance Against Carolina, Lance was very uninvolved on offense and was primarily used on special teams. His returns weren’t great, but nothing horrible, and he made a good play at the beginning of the game to let the ball go out of bounds. I expect his role to be the same this week. WR Barion Brown With Tyson having a larger role, Brown was also very uninvolved with the offense and made most of his impact on punt returns. Like with Lance, nothing incredible from him, but also nothing bad.

title: NFL Picks Week 11: A Grizzly Prospect
summary: The New Orleans Saints head to the Windy City to face the Chicago Bears this week. A week after stumbling through a terrible home loss to Carolina with first place in the NFC South on the line, the Saints now hit the road to face one of the NFC’s top Super Bowl contenders. Chicago is 3-0 against […]
full_text: The New Orleans Saints head to the Windy City to face the Chicago Bears this week. A week after stumbling through a terrible home loss to Carolina with first place in the NFC South on the line, the Saints now hit the road to face one of the NFC’s top Super Bowl contenders. Chicago is 3-0 against the NFC South this season, and are looking to go for a perfect record against the worst division in the NFL. Unfortunately for the Saints, the prospects are looking quite grizzly for the next three games, starting here in Chicago. Of all of the games on the 2026 schedule, this one always felt like the most difficult to envision a Saints win, and it only looks more bleak now. We now stare down the barrel of another lost season. Another chance for Dennis Allen to beat the Saints. Another losing streak. A grizzly prospect indeed. Let’s take a look at all of the matchups in the NFL here in Week 11. Last week I went 10-4 I told you so : Vikings over Packers! What do I know : Saints over Panthers? *** WEEK 11 Thursday, November 19th – Thursday Night Football Colts(3-7) at Texans(3-6) Desperately clinging to faint Wild Card hopes, Houston wins against their division rivals. Houston wins 25-22. Pick: Texans *** Sunday, November 22nd – Early Games Dolphins(1-8) at Bills(8-1) This game shouldn’t even be competitive, but divisional play can be a funny thing. Buffalo wins 26-22. Pick: Bills *** Ravens(4-6) at Panthers(4-5 ) Baltimore, coming off of one of their two most embarrassing losses this season, will fall again in Carolina, extending their losing streak to six games. Carolina wins 20-17. Pick: Panthers *** Titans(1-8) at Cowboys(4-6) After suffering a defensive meltdown last week, Dallas gets a nice rebound effort in this one. Dallas wins 26-12. Pick: Cowboys *** Buccaneers(3-6) at Lions(7-2) Detroit has taken some severe losses on their roster, but are seeing nothing but wins on the field. By slowing down the Tampa rushing attack, the Lions will extend their win streak to six games. Detroit wins 23-14. Pick: Lions *** Cardinals(3-7) at Chiefs(7-2) The only thing that would keep KC from winning this game is if they mentally peeked ahead to their trifecta of massive matchups coming in the next three weeks, but they won’t get caught doing that. Their gauntlet awaits, but this week will be easy work. Kansas City wins 35-17. Pick: Chiefs *** Steelers(6-3) at Eagles(2-7) The wheels have completely fallen off for Philly this season, and their losing streak will extend to eight games here. Pittsburgh wins 31-13. Pick: Steelers *** Saints(3-6) at Bears(7-2) Look, we should all be able to agree that the moment the 2026 NFL schedule was released in the offseason, this game was as close to an automatic loss for the Saints as they had on their entire schedule. Now that half of the season has played out, this game feels like even more of an automatic loss than it did all those months ago. The Saints can hope to fight and save some face in FOX’s “America’s Game of the Week”, but another national embarrassment may very well be in play here. It wouldn’t be stunning for this game to end up 56-10 Chicago, but it would be stunning for the Saints to steal a win on the road against this opponent. These Saints just aren’t built for this kind of moment. Chicago wins 31-17. Pick: Bears *** Sunday, November 22nd – Late Games Jets(2-8) at Chargers(1-8) Finally, the Chargers have a win on their record, but it’s back to their losing ways this week. New York wins 17-16. Pick: Jets *** Jaguars(7-2) at Giants(5-3-1) Jacksonville will extend their win streak to four games this week against the consistently inconsistent Giants. Jacksonville wins 24-19. Pick: Jaguars *** Raiders(4-6) at Broncos(7-2) Fernando Mendoza makes his second career start, and his second start against an elite NFL defense. With this low-scoring win over their division rivals, the Broncos will extend their win streak to six games. Denver wins 17-12. Pick: Broncos *** Sunday Night Football Vikings(7-2) at* 49ers(8-1) – Mexico City, Mexico – Game of the Week The Kirk Cousins trade back to Minnesota paid immediate dividends for the Vikings last week, winning a critical NFC North showdown that kept the Vikings in first place in the division. Following their bye week, San Francisco’s offense has kicked into its highest gear of the season, making their matchup against Brian Flores’ defense an intriguing one to watch. This game, with the fantastic backdrop of Mexico’s Estadio Banorte, will certainly live up to the hype. This one will come down to the wire, but the Niners leave Mexico City with a huge victory. San Francisco wins 21-20. Pick: 49ers *** Monday, November 23rd – Monday Night Football Bengals(7-2) at Commanders( 3-5-1 ) Cincinnati is on an absolute tear right now, and show no signs of slowing down any time soon. With this dominant win, the Bengals will extend their win streak to six games. Cincinnati wins 42-17. Pick: Bengals *** There it is Week 11 of the NFL season. Leave us your picks, comments, and insight below!

title: Expectations for Saints Were Not Based in Reality
summary: New Orleans dropped their second divisional matchup of the year in the most Saints fashion as they tied the game in the final minute on Sunday just to have a pass interference call give the Panthers 30 yards and a routine field goal situation to win the contest. The loss moved the Saints to 3-6 […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - NOVEMBER 15: Kellen Moore head coach of the New Orleans Saints hangs his head during the first half of a game against the Carolina Panthers at Caesars Superdome on November 15, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images New Orleans dropped their second divisional matchup of the year in the most Saints fashion as they tied the game in the final minute on Sunday just to have a pass interference call give the Panthers 30 yards and a routine field goal situation to win the contest. The loss moved the Saints to 3-6 on the year (0-2 in the NFC South) with the most difficult three game slate on their schedule on deck and the playoffs can be considered an unattainable dream at this point. While the Saints have gotten off to a bumpy start this year (no denying that the team has underperformed in certain areas), the frustration that many Who Dats feel should be owned by the fanbase as a product, in part, of their own making for believing undue hype. The context of the team entering the year was a second-year head coach, a quarterback with limited (yet promising) experience, and a serious lack of depth resulting from an extensive and still ongoing roster reconstruction; expectations for this year’s team were based in hope rather than reality. The Saints were a hot take for a “Surprise Team” that could make noise in the playoffs amongst the national media which inevitably bled into the minds and hearts of many Black and Gold blooded fans, but that’s all they ever were – a possible surprise team that could be better than last year (6-11). The success the Saints found at the end of last year was blinding to many as the team had chosen a young offensive minded coach (which many fans wanted at the time of the hire) and found a likeable quarterback in the draft that was the bright spot of the entire team. Polar opposites from Dennis Allen and Derek Carr. This is also a formula that the national media can and did latch onto as it is easy for anyone that has watched NFL to say “exciting coach and quarterback combination could be… exciting” and most takes when it comes to small market teams, especially the Saints, are usually just that lazy. Nostalgia of Drew Brees and Sean Payton’s success came rushing into the souls of fans that remembered the good times of 2006 and 2009 (early years of the era), and how easy they made being good in the NFL look. One must not forget the following facts, which many have, that make comparing the current team and that of the early BP (Brees and Payton) years more like comparing apples to kumquats than apples to apples. By the time Brees arrived in New Orleans he had already led a franchise to 3 – .500 or above seasons, been through two quarterback competitions, and passed for over 3,000 yards 3 times in a run heavy offense. The sights we all witnessed in the 15 years of BP were a once in a lifetime experience and should not be expected again, yet this seems to be the measuring stick that a fanbase hungry for the same level of success is using. This is a catastrophic mistake by those who have chosen that path of thought and will (already is) causing Fleur De Lis fatigue. Simply put, Shough and Moore need more time and a better roster before lofty expectations should be applied as they are still a relatively inexperienced team with a serious lack of depth. Contrary to popular belief, this season has not been a failure as the team has renewed its ability to face adversity that it lost in the last year under Dennis Allen and has shown signs that they are just a few pieces away from being the team that many expect them to be currently. The rebuild from the years of going for it all has a foundation, but the building part of the process isn’t anywhere close to being complete. Examining the First Half of the Season 4 of the 6 Saints’ losses have been 1 score games including the Detroit Debacle in week 1, an outlier occurrence in the Raiders game (4 – 4th quarter turnovers), and two games (Panthers and Steelers) where the Saints found themselves on the wrong side of games where one play could have swung the favorable result to either team. This is less of the Saints being a terrible team with no hope in the future and more of how the NFL works. Given the dynamic of the team going into the year, I knew this (3-6 start) was a possibility – as a fan I hoped it wouldn’t come true, but it also does not set the precedent to burn the house down. There is more to how a program is performing than wins and losses, despite what group think will tell you. Other than simple bad luck, the Saints have faced bad injury luck as well. To start the year, the Saints lost a vital piece of their offense that most forget in Dillon Radunz who was handpicked to be the 6th man on the offensive line as a versatile lineman that started 10 games last year and could fill in at guard or tackle if need be. This became a real issue in the 4th quarter of the previously mentioned Raiders game as the Saints were down to their 7th lineman to replace Kelvin Banks Jr. at left tackle and Asim Richards wasn’t able to hold up against the Raiders pass rush which alone led to multiple turnovers and the game being flipped on its head. Next came the injury to Kaden Ellis, whom no one seems to want to give the Saints credit for finding or re-signing which exploited the previously mentioned lack of depth as Danny Stutsman was not up for the challenge in the run game, specifically which helped lead to the Falcons having their way on the ground on Monday Night Football in the Superdome. In the Dome that night you could almost feel the tides shift as red jerseys were all that remained in the lower bowl and whispers of firing Moore, Loomis, or both started to emerge. Combine these with Bryan Breese being out the entire season from an already limited interior defensive line group, 3 wins at this point should have been more or less expected. While there are definitely places the Saints need to improve, (starting with the rushing offense) this team was always at least a year away from truly competing for anything more than winning the worst division in the NFL to start this season. Therefore, any talk of firing Moore, firing Loomis, or having Todd Graves buy the team are a waste of breath, energy and quite frankly are tired takes at this point. If the wheels fall off, there is constant weekly regression, and the team starts playing the way we saw in the last year of Aleen then sure, but that is not what the product on the field each week says.
author: AndrewLotz

title: Indianapolis Colts release QB Daniel Jones
summary: Mike Garafolo of the NFL Network is reporting that the Indianapolis Colts released quarterback Daniel Jones on Friday. Jones has played very poorly since returning from the torn Achilles that ended his 2025 season, prompting the release As pretty much everyone will remember, the New York Giants drafted Jones out of Duke with the sixth […]
full_text: Former Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones | Getty Images Mike Garafolo of the NFL Network is reporting that the Indianapolis Colts released quarterback Daniel Jones on Friday. Jones has played very poorly since returning from the torn Achilles that ended his 2025 season, prompting the release As pretty much everyone will remember, the New York Giants drafted Jones out of Duke with the sixth overall pick in the 2019 NFL Draft. The Colts will now turn to Anthony Richardson, and he’ll be the quarterback for whom the Giants will need to game plan when the two teams face off next week. The Giants’ decision to draft Jones was something of a surprise on draft night, as the 2019 quarterback class was not seen as a strong one at all. Jones would go on to replace Giants’ legend Eli Manning as the starting quarterback for the Giants game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 3 of that year. Though Jones won his first game as a starter, his time with the Giants was tumultuous, to say the least. There were flashes of the potential that caused GM Dave Gettleman to fall in “full bloom love” with Jones in his Senior Bowl MVP performance, but there were also far too many turnovers and injuries. The Giants had hoped Jones turned the corner when the team surprisingly made the playoffs in 2022, and rewarded him with a rich 4-year, $160 million contract in the spring of 2023. Unfortunately, the injuries and poor play returned that season Jones was ultimately benched following the Giants’ 2024 loss to the Carolina Panthers in Munich. Jones requested his release after being benched and landed with the Minnesota Vikings. He backing up Kirk Cousins for that team’s own playoff run. He then signed a two-year, $88 million contract with the Colts as a free agent in 2025. Jones initially played well for the Colts, taking advantage of the talents of RB Jonathan Taylor, TE Tyler Warren, and WR Alec Pierce in the Colts’ play-action and RPO-heavy offense. However, his play fell off beginning with the Colts loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers and his season was ended early by a torn Achilles. It’s anyone’s guess where Jones will land next, however he should be comfortable in the meantime. Jones has, so far, made a combined $172.8 million as a quarterback for the Giants, Vikings, and Colts.

title: Bobby Jamison-Travis, Giants ‘baby DJ Reader’, is starting to grow up
summary: New York Giants rookie defensive tackle Bobby Jamison-Travis “might end up being a baby DJ Reader at one point in his career,” according to defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson. Armed with that response to my question to Wilson about Jamison-Travis, I went to the fully grown up DJ Reader in the Giants locker room on Thursday […]
full_text: Bobby Jamison-Travis | Getty Images New York Giants rookie defensive tackle Bobby Jamison-Travis “might end up being a baby DJ Reader at one point in his career,” according to defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson. Armed with that response to my question to Wilson about Jamison-Travis, I went to the fully grown up DJ Reader in the Giants locker room on Thursday to talk about “baby DJ”. “I love Bob,” Reader said while sitting at his locker staring at the wrap I was preventing him from eating. “He’s a funny kid and he just listens. He’s really smart. “Takes it all in, like you said, with open ears, really trying to figure out the position. Playing notes can be hard at the beginning of your career just because everything moves that much faster. And so he’s doing a good job just taking it all in and listening, asking questions.” Jamison-Travis was an unheralded sixth-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. He did not play until Week 6 against the New Orleans Saints. He has, though, played more than 20 snaps (at least 30% of the defensive snaps) in each of the last three games. “I see a young guy that’s just getting better and better with every opportunity he gets,” Wilson said. “A good thing about Bobby is he’s a young player that’s playing, he’s a violent player. He’s good with his hands. He owns his gap integrity. He’s going to do his job the way he’s supposed to do it on a daily play-by-play basis.” Wilson praised Jamison-Travis for being willing to learn from Reader and 13-year veteran Harris. “When you have DJ Reader and you have Shelby Harris, who have played a ton of football, like if I’m Bobby and this is what he’s done and I see DJ has all this success throughout his whole career, why not do what he does,” Wwilson said. “And you see the older guys taking a liking to him, and he is a guy that’s a sponge in terms of gaining the knowledge on and off the field, creating habits off the field, to train, to get better, to prepare better. “I think that he’s just going to keep progressing and he might end up being a baby DJ Reader at one point in his career.” Reader, 32, is playing some of the best football in his career after a sub-par 2025 season with the Detroit Lions. He has no problem helping a young player like Jamison-Travis. “I call it DJ’s Reader School of Noseguards,” Reader said. “I got some prospects. I’ve got some guys out there who’s playing some good ball right now. I’m excited to see and watch them play. So I always love it, man. Reader name-dropped a couple of defensive tackles he has mentored — Tyleik Williams of the Detroit Lions and Roy Lopez of the Arizona Cardinals. “I just try to teach them how to really truly play that because it’s a hard position,” Reader said. Reader said he remembers how helpful Vince Wilfork was to him in Houston. Reader was a rookie fifth-round pick with the Texans that year, while Wilfork was finishing a fantastic 13-year career. “Vince was amazing,” Reader said. “Vince Wilfork would teach me how to play the noseguard position. So, I just try to pay it forward and push the agenda.” Reader said the 6-foot-3, 328-pound Jamison-Travis “has all the tools you need” to be successful. “He’s got a little bit of built-in leverage. He can run. He’s strong,” Reader said. “And he plays square, which is the biggest thing I look for in D-linemen. Not getting turned shoulders. “If your shoulder’s getting turned, are you willing to fight the hard shoulder and not take the easy way out? So Bobby does all those things really well.” Reader said Jamison-Travis “plays the run really, really well.” “In today’s league, you need that,” Reader said. “The league mind, they manipulated people a few years ago when they went to this Air-Raid offense, thinking that, all right, we need super small D tackles, rest of the pass, rest of the pass, rest of the pass, rest of the pass. And that is what you do need, but the good teams still run the ball. “So you’ve got to have somebody in there that can help force multiply and stop those runs, that can take two, that can stay square and block, keep the line flat while everybody else is fighting through. And Bobby’s one of those players.” Reader understand why Jamison-Travis has emerged as a regular part of the defensive line rotation in recent weeks. “He’s taken amazing leaps forward,” Reader said. “I remember he really couldn’t get at his stance to get across the center. I’m like, look, you’ve got to anticipate these things. “So just talking about it and him thinking about it, he’s changed so much, man. He’s just gotten so much better. It’s really fun to watch because I just know how hard it can be as a young player. So it’s fun to watch him start to get it, things slow down for him and seeing blocks a lot clearer. It’s a lot of work that he put in himself and we also put in together as a group.” It certainly sounds like “baby DJ” is starting to grow up.
author: Ed Valentine

title: NFL Betting Advice: Giants-Jaguars picks and props
summary: Welcome to the New York Giants betting angle, Week 11 edition! Each week, I’m giving you my three favorite wagers for that week’s New York Giants game. My one rule: I won’t ever give you wagers that go beyond -120. No gimmes! The Giants are coming off a very frustrating loss to the Commanders in Week 10, […]
full_text: Bring on Jax! | Getty Images Welcome to the New York Giants betting angle, Week 11 edition! Each week, I’m giving you my three favorite wagers for that week’s New York Giants game. My one rule: I won’t ever give you wagers that go beyond -120. No gimmes! The Giants are coming off a very frustrating loss to the Commanders in Week 10, and they’ll face their biggest challenge of the season this Sunday when the 7-2 Jacksonville Jaguars come to town. The Jags come in hot. They are running away with the AFC South and their margin of victory across their last three contests (all wins) is +75. Believe it or not, this is Big Blue’s first game this season against a team with a winning record. It’s an important game for the G-Men, who will try to keep some cushion atop the NFC East. But it won’t be easy. Jacksonville ranks near the top of the league in both offense and defense in advanced metrics like DVOA and EPA per play, and they’ve got one of the best kickers in the game. My picks were 1-2 in Week 10 and after a hot stretch, I’ve got a couple of losing weeks in a row. I’m still over .500 for the season, but not by much. Let’s get to this week’s picks. All lines and odds are from Fanduel , as of Friday, November 20. The line for the game is Jaguars -5.5, with a game total of 46.5. Light rain is possible during the game. Jaguars -5.5 (-120). Can the Giants win this game? Absolutely. Can they keep it close? Affirmative. They’re at home, with three extra days of rest, and the Jaguars could be due for a letdown. Still, this line feels low to me. Jacksonville is an AFC powerhouse with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations, while New York is trying to piece it together with a young roster and its third quarterback of the season. John Harbaugh’s team is well coached and last week’s late meltdown aside, New York has been very good in close games. This one could stay close for a while, but in the end, I think Jacksonville will pull away and I’m comfortable with them laying this number on the road. The Jaguars have a +125 point differential, which is the best in the NFL. Jaguars FIRST HALF -3.5 (-110). I’m double-dipping. No team has been better in the first half than Jacksonville, although they’ve been better at home. They average 15.9 points scored in the first half, and 5.6 points allowed. Both figures rank first in the NFL. I’ll ride those trends and happily give the points in the first half. Malik Nabers OVER 5.5 receptions (-120). Nabers is coming off back-to-back down games, but he still managed five catches in both. Before that, he had 30 catches across three games. The Jaguars defend the run very well, and they also defend tight ends well. I think New York is going to struggle to run the ball on the Jaguars and could be chasing points. Nabers is going to want to atone for his costly fumble last week, and he should be the focal point of the passing game. Take the over. Those are the picks for Week 11. I know, I want the Giants to win too, and I’ll be happy if my first half and game picks blow up in my face. Good luck with your wagers! And if you play fantasy football, be sure to check out my Week 11 fantasy preview, with start/sit advice and more, right here .
