title: Should the NY Giants be interested in safety Justin Reid?
summary: The New Orleans Saints are expected to release veteran safety Justin Reid, per reports from Jordan Shultz and others. It’s being reported that Reid requested to be released and is expected to sign with a playoff contender amid a messy season for the Saints. Reid, 29, is in his ninth season after being drafted by […]
full_text: New Orleans Saints safety Justin Read defends against the New York Giants. | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints are expected to release veteran safety Justin Reid , per reports from Jordan Shultz and others . It’s being reported that Reid requested to be released and is expected to sign with a playoff contender amid a messy season for the Saints. Reid, 29, is in his ninth season after being drafted by Houston out of Stanford in the 3rd round of the 2018 NFL Draft. The Giants are in a much better place than expected at the safety position. Jevon Holland is among the best safeties in the NFL at the moment, playing elite coverage as well as being a reliable tackler coming downhill — not to mention being tied for the league lead in turnovers with six (four interceptions, two forced fumbles). The Giants’ other safety spot has been in constant flux, with Tyler Nubin, Jason Pinnock, and Ar’Darius Washington all seeing time along with Holland. The Giants are among the NFL leaders in sub-package usage, using various defensive sub-packages on 73% of plays (T-7th), and are 5th in heavy box rate (31.1 percent). “I think Ar’Darius played his best game the last outing against Washington,” defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson said when asked about S Ar’Darius Washington on Thursday. “Obviously, he tackled extremely well. You saw him, in the fourth quarter in a critical situation, come up with an interception. He’s been doing everything that I know he could do, from being around him in Baltimore when he was there. He is a smaller guy that plays with a big stick. He is going to attack the line of scrimmage. He tackles well. He can cover. So he’s doing a good job. I think all the safeties are doing a good job in their role. It’s kind of safety by committee. All of them deserve the opportunity to play.” It’s worth noting that there is a connection between Reid and the Giants. He was coached by secondary coach and defensive pass game coordinator Donald D’Alesio as a member of the Kansas City Chiefs from 2022 to 2024. Reid’s 2024 season was among the best of his career and the two won Super Bowls together in 2022 and 2023. The Giants scoured the NFL for an impact player at the trade deadline, but came up empty. They currently have $7.2 million and could be interested in adding a versatile veteran safety who has played well on championship teams.
author: Chris Pflum

title: J.J. McCarthy has won at every level; will that continue in NY Giants’ playoff run?
summary: When the New York Giants traded for quarterback J.J. McCarthy following Jaxson Dart’s season-ending injury, nobody really knew what to expect. McCarthy’s 2+ years with the Minnesota Vikings did not go well, and the quarterback-needy Vikings shipped him out of town. Then, a couple of weeks into his time with the Giants, a Week 6 […]
full_text: J.J. McCarthy | Getty Images When the New York Giants traded for quarterback J.J. McCarthy following Jaxson Dart’s season-ending injury, nobody really knew what to expect. McCarthy’s 2+ years with the Minnesota Vikings did not go well, and the quarterback-needy Vikings shipped him out of town. Then, a couple of weeks into his time with the Giants, a Week 6 cameo in what looked like a blowout loss to the New Orleans Saints turned into nine minutes of mayhem that changed the Giants’ season. McCarthy went 11 of 21 for 243 yards in slightly more than 11 minutes as the Giants nearly climbed out of a 34-10 hole in a 34-27 loss. That convinced head coach John Harbaugh to name him the starting quarterback, and McCarthy went 20 of 28 for 252 yards in an overtime victory over the Houston Texans. Now, three weeks later, the quarterback scorned by a Minnesota team that was forced to make a desperation trade for Kirk Cousins to fix its own issue at the position is being asked to guide the Giants on an eight-week run that will — hopefully — end with the Giants winning their first NFC East title since 2011. Will he be up to the task? The 23-year-old has been impressive to date, and the Giants are 2-1 in his three starts. With the pressure and quality of competition about to ratchet up, will that continue? Questions have been asked about how much head coach John Harbaugh trusts McCarthy after the Washington loss, in which the Giants called a quarterback run that failed on a key third-and-3 at the two-minute mark, forcing a punt and leading to the Commanders’ game-winning drive. McCarthy has been questioned for, with receivers open underneath and only a field goal being needed to tie the game, throwing a deep shot to Malik Nabers that was intercepted near the end of the Washington game when he had receivers open underneath. “I think he’s proven that he’s capable of winning games and making the plays, and I probably feel more strongly about that now than ever,” Harbaugh said. “We’re definitely in the process of growing that confidence for sure. I mean, I understand what you’re saying, for sure. But he’s earned that right. I’m excited about where he’s going.” Harbaugh said McCarthy has been “playing winning football.” “I want him to play as good as he can possibly play. I want him to be confident. I want him to be aggressive. I want him to be smart. I want him to complete passes. I want him to handle all the blitz checks. I just want him to continue to play the best football he can play,” Harbaugh said. “I’m not sitting there like a scout saying he can work on his plant foot or his follow-through. We look at that stuff, the coaches will. All you really focus on is, let’s go play the best game we can possibly play. Let’s play a winning football game. “He’s been playing winning football. I’m really happy with the way he’s playing. Okay, let’s play winning football and go win the game. There’s going to be some plays that he’ll have a chance to make. He’ll make most of them. He won’t make them all. But I hope he makes the ones that make a difference in the game. That’s probably the biggest thing for any quarterback.” McCarthy explained this week what “winning football” means to him. “Winning the game is the number one thing, and there’s a bunch of stats, traits, how a quarterback would play that would contribute to winning the game, and that’s all about decision making, timing, accuracy, and just being smart, and knowing that you have the program in your hands every single play when you touch that ball and making the best decisions possible,” he said. “That’s the number one thing I think makes winning football, and I try to do that to the best of my ability every single week.” The numbers show a McCarthy who has clearly been better in three starts and one real relief appearance as a Giant than he was in 10 starts with Minnesota last season. Completion percentage: 2025: 57.6 2026: 63.5 Interception percentage: 2025: 4.5 2026: 1.9 Yards gained per pass attempt: 2025: 11.7 2026: 13.9 Passer rating: 2025: 72.6 2026: 90.0 QBR: 2025: 35.6 2026: 54.5 On-target percentage: 2025: 66.5 2026: 73.2 Completion percentage over expected: 2025: -4.9 2026: +4.0 Expected points added: 2025: -51.6 2026: +5.7 Expected points added per dropback: 2025: -0.18 2026: +0.05 Offensive coordinator Matt Nagy said McCarthy’s growth since coming to the Giants is “real.” “We need to make sure that we continue to just keep supporting him like we do every week with the play calls, the play designs, the players in the right spot. Let him play fast. He’s done that,” Nagy said. “Winning helps, and learning through experiences, too. The more we can get wins, the more experiences we get. He’s a positive kid. He likes to stay positive. When he’s out here at practice, he’s juiced up all the time, which I love. He’s got great energy. And then on game day, he turns that energy into a calm. So, just continue to get stuff on tape so that he can kind of see where we all grow as coaches with him and him with us.” McCarthy certainly shouldn’t be afraid of the big moments to come. He is no stranger to big games. McCarthy won state and national championships in high school. He won a national championship in college at Michigan. “When it comes to games in late November, when you’re getting closer and closer to playoffs, the attention to detail, the urgency to really make sure you’re doing your one-eleventh on every single play means the most, and especially against great teams like Jacksonville,” McCarthy said. Backup quarterback Jameis Winston, in his 12th NFL season, said it will be important for McCarthy to not try and do too much on his own. “The most important thing about big moments is keeping it simple and doing what’s required,” Winston said. “It’s not having an unreal game, but it’s being consistent and giving the best chance to win. “We’re going to make sure we do everything possible to support him. That’s a collective team thing … we view it as togetherness and how we’re going to rally together to win football games.” NFL teams using their third starting quarterback by midseason — earlier in the Giants’ case — don’t typically make playoff runs. Just three years removed from being the 10th overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, and with those high school and collegiate national titles on his resume, McCarthy doesn’t come with the typical “who the heck is that guy?” third quarterback pedigree. “Getting to know him better, and his personality, his attitude, you can see why he’s done that, why he’s won at every level that he’s been on and everywhere he’s been,” center Bryan Hudson said. “Knowing who he is, he’s the same guy every day, which is awesome and what you want to see. That’s what gives us a chance every time he steps on the field.” As the competition ramps up and the games get more important, we are about to find out if McCarthy and the Giants will be up to the challenge.
author: Ed Valentine

title: NY Giants midseason 2027 NFL mock draft
summary: We’re officially in the second half of the New York Giants 2026 season with eight games remaining this year. The Giants were very active at the trade deadline, though while they went “big game hunting” they weren’t able to land any impact players. They were hoping to add another difference maker before they got to […]
full_text: Oregon Ducks defensive tackle A’Mauri Washington against Michigan. | ISI Photos via Getty Images We’re officially in the second half of the New York Giants 2026 season with eight games remaining this year. The Giants were very active at the trade deadline, though while they went “big game hunting” they weren’t able to land any impact players. They were hoping to add another difference maker before they got to the meat of their schedule, but it wasn’t to be. The upside of that is that the Giants still have all draft capital that they came into the season with. All this year we’ve been using the NFL draft as a lens through which to evaluate the state of the Giants as well as context for a chaotic season of college football. Now the College Football Playoffs are taking shape while the NFL playoff race is heating up. The Giants are in the unfamiliar position of being in control of the NFC East and making a run to the playoffs, but this is still a good time to take stock of the Giants’ wants and needs as we head into the home stretch. I used the simulator from Pro Football and Sports Network to do this draft. Round 1 – 22nd overall – A’Mauri Washington, NT, Oregon The Giants were hot after a defensive tackle at the trade deadline, chasing after every impact lineman they thought they could pry loose. It didn’t work out, so now they’re diving into a deep draft class to add talent and depth to their defensive line. My choices here were between David Stone of Oklahoma and A’Mauri Washington from Oregon. Both were a bit disappointing to start the year, but have come on in recent weeks. I opted for Washington because I believe he fits what the Giants want in a tackle more closely than does stone. He’s an enormous young man at 6-foot-3, 330 pounds, but also has legitimately freakish power and athleticism. Washington ranked fourth on Bruce Feldman’s annual Freaks List in 2025 and moved up to third on the 2026 list. He not only has elite first step explosiveness, but also has rare long speed for his size and clocked over 20 mph in a sprint. Washington is an inconsistent defender at this stage of his development, but he flashes the ability to be an absolute rock in the run game as well as a real factor as a pass rusher thanks to his mass, strength, and explosiveness. He’s similar to a young Dexter Lawrence in that his athletic tools are overwhelming in one-on-one situations, but his technique is the limiting factor at this stage of his development. His freakish strength could make him a force on the defensive line if he can become a technician. Also considered: David Stone (iDL, Oklahoma), KJ Bolden (S, Georgia), Trey’Dez Green (TE, LSU), Jackson Harris (WR, LSU) Note: I’d like to shout out the Dallas Cowboys for taking Florida RB Jadan Baugh one pick before me, saving the Giants from themselves. I fully believe that Baugh will be high on the Giants’ draft board, and he’ll be in heavy consideration for their first-round pick if he’s on the board when they pick. I’m not sure John Harbaugh will be able to help himself, even if drafting a running back in the first never works out for the drafting team. Round 2 – 54th overall – KJ Duff, WR, Rutgers I’ve been consistent over the last year (plus) in viewing wide receiver as a significant need. The Giants only have two receivers under contract beyond this year — Malik Nabers and Malachi Fields. The Giants might prefer to run heavy personnel packages, but a good 11-personnel package is still important to any and every scheme in the NFL. I chose Duff over Alabama’s Ryan Coleman-Williams for three reasons. First, while Coleman-Williams is as much of an explosive threat as Nabers, he has struggled with consistency. Second, I want a second big-bodied outside receiver to play the X opposite Fields. Secondly, Malik Nabers has been the best slot receiver in the NFL , and much better from the slot than out wide. The Giants need to build the kind of receiving corps that will allow him to play where he’s so devastatingly effective. And finally, Duff himself has the potential to be special in his own right. He has great size at 6-foot-6, 225 pounds (listed), and appears to have good explosiveness, long speed, and agility for his size. He excels at the catch point, with a catch rate over expected of 17.7% and a miniscule 1.3% drop rate. Duff has an impressive 1,858 yards (105 catches, 17.6 per catch) and 16 touchdowns over the last two years, despite playing on a Rutgers team that’s probably most charitably described as “unfortunate”. It’s exciting to think of what he could do in the same offense as Nabers, Fields, Isaiah Likely, and Jaxson Dart. Also Considered: Reed Harris (WR, Arizona State), Ryan Coleman-Williams (WR, Alabama), Ty Benefield (S, LSU) Round 3 – 86th overall – Bray Hubbard, S, Alabama Back to the defensive side of the ball we go. I was hunting for an offensive lineman or running back at this spot, but the board didn’t fall my way. Instead, I picked up Alabama’s versatile STAR to help take the Giants’ defense to the next level. Dennard Wilson has taken the Ravens 2.0 defensive model and remixed it with a healthy dose of “Ryan style” aggression. The “Ravens style” defense loves to use a versatile safety hybrid as a force player to dictate terms to the offense and adapt to different personnel packages and looks. The Giants don’t really have that, but Hubbard brings an excellent blend of size (6-foot-2, 217 pounds) and athleticism (estimated 4.4 speed). He has plenty of experience in Alabama’s sophisticated defense and playing against elite competition in the SEC, which should allow him to step in and contribute right away. He brings great run defense, solid pass coverage, physicality, and ball-hawking ability. Hubbard is a tackling machine with 193 tackles to go with 9 interceptions and 10 passes defensed over the last 3 years. Also considered: Vicari Swain (CB, South Carolina), LJ Martin (RB, BYU)
author: Chris Pflum

title: NY Giants news:  Matt Nagy takes accountability, Abdul Carter sacks, more
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as Big Blue hosts Jacksonville Jaguars this Sunday. Midseason reports on every NFL team’s offensive coordinator, playcaller | ESPN.com What has gone right? A lot. The Giants’ offense has five games of 27 or more points. They had six all of […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know as Big Blue hosts Jacksonville Jaguars this Sunday. Midseason reports on every NFL team’s offensive coordinator, playcaller | ESPN.com What has gone right? A lot. The Giants’ offense has five games of 27 or more points. They had six all of last season. New York has been productive on offense despite being on its third quarterback (Jaxson Dart, Jameis Winston, J.J. McCarthy). It’s a credit to Nagy and quarterbacks coach Brian Callahan. Key to second half: Continue to get more out of McCarthy, who has made three starts to date. If he takes his game to the next level and improves on getting through his progressions, this can be a potent Giants offense throwing the ball to WR Malik Nabers and TE Isaiah Likely. McCarthy has the talent. Nabers: It’s on us to execute "It comes down to as players, we've got to execute the play call that's being played" Malik Nabers talks about Matt Nagy taking responsibility for the Giants not getting a first down on 3rd and 3 late in their loss to the Commanders: pic.twitter.com/BO2M8EXqcs — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) November 19, 2026 Who are the NFL’s contenders and pretenders? Sorting out Giants, Steelers, Rams and more | The Athletic New York Giants (5-3-1) — Pretenders. John Harbaugh’s team has definitely exceeded expectations. But the sad state of the NFC East — where injuries plague the Philadelphia Eagles, displays of late-game ineptitude hobble the Washington Commanders and defensive incompetence derails the Dallas Cowboys — has helped the Giants. They rank fifth in total defense, but offensive inconsistency with quarterback J.J. McCarthy will doom this team against quality foes. Inside the Numbers: Tale of the tape for Week 11 | Giants.com J.J. McCarthy is averaging 8.80 yards per pass attempt this season, third-most in the NFL (minimum 100 attempts). He trails only San Francisco’s Brock Purdy (8.97) and Jacksonville’s Trevor Lawrence (8.82). The Giants, who allow the second-fewest yards per pass attempt (6.16), are set to face both quarterbacks over the next three weeks. Cam Skattebo has at least 120 scrimmage yards and a touchdown in back-to-back games. The last Giant to do it in three consecutive games is Tiki Barber (Weeks 3-5, 2004). Giants only behind Vikings on sending rushers in passing downs Average number of pass rushers by pre-snap alignment Dennard Wilson sneaking into Brian Flores territory pic.twitter.com/9xrjqHLDwz — Doug Analytics (@Doug_Analytics) November 19, 2026 One Abdul Carter stat tells the story of what Giants truly need from their Metrics Monarch | New York Post Abdul Carter is a Metrics Monarch. He dominates all sorts of deep-dive analytics but he very rarely cashes in with sacks. The Giants need more from the No. 3 pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. He does not think it will happen. He knows it. “I’m 100 percent confident it will come,’’ Abdul Carter said Wednesday after practice. “Hopefully in the playoffs.’’ NFL rookie rankings: Highest-graded players after Week 10 | PFF 4. LB Arvell Reese, New York Giants (79.8). Reese didn’t generate any pressures from 16 pass-rushing snaps this week, but he did impress against the run once again. Through the first 10 weeks of the season, he has recorded 35 tackles resulting in a defensive stop and has earned an 81.4 PFF grade against the run. NFL defensive rookie rankings: Giants LB Arvell Reese hits No. 1 | NFL.com Reese’s NFL position was one of the biggest topics of debate prior to last April’s draft. Would the 6-foot-4, 243-pounder be better served as an off-ball linebacker or pass rusher? The answer, it turns out, is YES. Yes to all! As evidenced by his three-sack game against the rival Eagles, the 21-year-old has a knack for hunting quarterbacks. And yet, he also clearly excels in traditional linebacking duties, considering he’s made a league-high 50 solo tackles. Add in eight tackles for loss, five QB hits, four passes defensed, an interception and a forced fumble, and the man is filling up the stat sheet like an odds-on favorite for Defensive Rookie of the Year (which he is). Banks: Giants future QB is Dart Its real, if anything this should tell you how sold on Dart they are. They are fully confident that everything JJ is doing Dart could do if not better. pic.twitter.com/fsrmm0wM6Q — LetsGeaux (@LSUisjustbetter) November 19, 2026 Giants get positive update on Jaxson Dart’s knee injury | NJ.com There’s a good chance the Giants will win the NFC East, despite losing quarterback Jaxson Dart early in Week 2 to a season-ending knee injury. While it’s an extreme long shot that Dart will be ready to play in the playoffs, the Giants did recently receive a positive update on his knee. Dart’s girlfriend, Marissa Ayers, posted on TikTok that Dart is “off crutches & walking.” From Big Blue View Giants DC Dennard Wilson: ‘The sacks will come’ for Abdul Carter Giants OC Matt Nagy takes accountability for end of game vs. Commanders Giants signed Xavier Gipson to provide ‘spark’ in return game Giants-Jaguars matchup: Will New York defense live, or die, by the blitz? title: Fantasy Football 2026: Week 11 preview — Start/sit and more
summary: Welcome to Week 12 of the college football season! full_text: A performance for the ages | Getty Images Welcome to Week 12 of the college football season! Hang on, I got confused because when I looked at this week’s betting lines, I saw five double-digit point spreads, with two in excess of 15 points. What??? Apparently, the Chiefs are playing Appalachian State while the Bills square off against Coastal Carolina. And on and on. The talent differential in the NFL isn’t that great, and it’s rare to see a slate that looks like this. Welcome to Week 11 of the NFL season! Last week gave us an explosion of scoring and some epic fantasy performances. If you were up against Christian McCaffrey, Jahmyr Gibbs, George Pickens, Emmett Johnson, Patrick Mahomes, or Dak Prescott, among others, it was a long day. We might get more of the same in Week 11. Favorites are 24-4 outright the last two weeks and a lot of those games haven’t been close, with the winners running up the score. The game of the week is Minnesota (7-2) at San Francisco (8-1), which pits the league’s #2 scoring offense (31.2 points per game) against the league’s top scoring defense (14 points per game). Something’s gotta give, right? It’s the Sunday night game and it’s being played in Mexico City. Did Brock Purdy make my Fades list? Read on to find out. Six teams are on bye this week, for the only time this season. Throw in all the injuries and the challenge for fantasy managers is clear. I’ll try to help you navigate it. St ats of the Week Every team in the NFC North is over .500 and every team in the NFC South is under .500. 2. NFC South teams are a collective 4-17 at home. 3. All six of the Browns’ wins have been by four points or less. No team in NFL history has done that across their first six wins of a season. 4. The 49ers are the first team since the 2000 “Greatest Show on Turf” Rams to have three touchdowns of 60+ yards in one game. I don’t think Dallas defenders laid a hand on the ball carrier on any of those plays. 5. Josh Allen has 88 rushing TDs, halfway through his ninth season. Eric Dickerson had 88 rushing TDs through his first nine full seasons. 6. Jahmyr Gibbs has the most TDs through four seasons (62) of any player in NFL history. 7. In the Bengals’ curb-stomping of the Steelers, Joe Burrow was 26 for 34 for 304 yards. At halftime. Late in the third quarter, net passing yards read as follows: Bengals 356, Steelers (-9). 8. Fernando Mendoza is the first rookie QB in NFL history to make his starting debut against the defending Super Bowl champions. 9. The Ravens – who have a healthy Derrick Henry – put up 16 rushing yards at home against a previously winless team. 10. Over their last three games (all wins), the Jaguars have outscored their opponents by 75 points. Bye Weeks: Falcons, Browns, Packers, Rams, Patriots, Seahawks Week 11 Rides, Fades and Sleepers For those who are familiar with this column, you know the drill. For everyone else: The Rides, Fades, and Sleepers is an analysis of players that I think are primed for an especially strong or poor performance, often as compared to consensus expectations. This isn’t a straight-up Start/Sit exercise. As a general rule, start your studs. I’ll rarely list the most obvious names at a position as “Rides” because those players are almost always expected to have strong performances. You don’t need me or anyone else telling you to start Jahmyr Gibbs . While this analysis is intended for season-long play, it works for DFS formats too. Half PPR scoring and Expert Consensus Rankings (ECR) are used for the column. Each week, I’m picking a Ride, Fade, and Sleeper of the Week. The rules: The Ride of the Week can’t be a truly elite option, the Fade can’t be someone who nobody is starting anyway, and the Sleeper must be an actual sleeper, from down in the rankings. Last week, my Rides, Fades, and Sleepers did well, with a lot more hits than misses. Ride of the Week James Cook ran for 157 yards and a TD, and Fade of the Week Ashton Jeanty was held to 18 rushing yards and 8.4 fantasy points (Half PPR). You can check my work here . *** Ride of the Week: Tony Pollard (@DAL). This selection isn’t about a revenge game narrative. The analysis is straightforward: Pollard has been great over the last month, and Dallas’s defense is horrific. Christian McCaffrey has had a lot of incredible games in his brilliant career, but perhaps none better than what he did to the Cowboys last week (44 fantasy points in Full PPR). With that game on its resume, Dallas has allowed the most fantasy points per game (FPPG) and total TDs (16) to opposing running backs. As for Pollard, his last three games have produced RB1, RB3, and RB8 weekly finishes yet he’s still flying a little under the radar. This is a perfect marriage of red-hot player and excellent matchup. Enjoy the wedding vows and don’t overthink it. Fade of the Week: Tyler Warren (@HOU). Warren has been a major disappointment this season. He was drafted as a Top-5 TE, and through ten weeks, he’s the TE12 on the season, at just 8.3 FPPG. He’s been especially cold lately, even with the Colts jettisoning receivers at the trade deadline. He’s averaging 3 catches for 21 yards over his last three outings, with no trips to the end zone. Houston’s defense has been a huge disappointment, but they allow the seventh fewest FPPG to opposing tight ends and have yielded just one touchdown to the position. Throw in how badly Daniel Jones is playing and the short week, and Warren is a sit for me on Thursday Night Football. Sleeper of the Week: Justin Herbert (vs. NYJ). Yup, I’m going here, after fading Herbert week after week. Cam Ward’s weekly ranking is too high (QB15) to put here. More on him later. Herbert and the Chargers have been a punchline all season, but they finally broke through at Baltimore on Monday night. Herbert is ranked as the QB20 this week, even with six teams on bye and multiple starting QBs hurt. Come on! I get that he’s been awful, and he wasn’t exactly great on Monday night. But there were signs. He didn’t turn the ball over for the first time all year, used his legs to make big plays, and put up his best result of the season (16.3 fantasy points). He didn’t have Ladd McConkey, who could be back this week. Do I think the Chargers’ offense turned a corner? No. But they’re hosting the equally hapless Jets and should make it two in a row. New York is a Bottom-10 defense against opposing QBs, and importantly, they’ve allowed the most rushing TDs to the position (4). The Chargers are finally getting healthier along the line. Lock Herbie in for a finish in the QB 8-12 range. Quarterback: Elite options this week – Josh Allen , Patrick Mahomes, Dak Prescott, and Joe Burrow ; the analysis starts below them. Rides: Three QBs ranked in the Top-10 this week who I think will outperform projections: Caleb Williams (vs. NO), Trevor Lawrence (@NYG), and C.J. Stroud (vs. IND). The last two listed are playing at a very high level and have lots of weapons to choose from, and neither matchup is all that scary. Williams has had two weeks to get past his 4-INT nightmare game against the Bucs (which the Bears still managed to win), and I think he’ll play a clean game at home against a defense that can’t stop the run and will be easy to exploit with play-action. Play all your Bears this week. Sleepers: Cam Ward (@DAL) is ranked as the QB15 this week but he’s going to be a very popular streamer for those without a QB in Week 11. He’ll have high usage in DFS too. He’s averaging 23 FPPG over his last two games, and the Cowboys are about as generous as it gets. They’ve allowed the third most passing yards and fourth most FPPG to opposing QBs, and this game has shootout potential. Wan’Dale Robinson is gone for the season, but Ward should get Carnell Tate back this week. Bo Nix (vs. LV) has been extremely hard to trust, but he’s got a very nice matchup against the Raiders and might have all of his receiving weapons healthy for the first time in a while. title: NY Giants DC Dennard Wilson: ‘The sacks will come’ for Abdul Carter
summary: When the New York Giants made Abdul Carter the third overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, it was believed that they had selected the next Micah Parsons. After all, the two wore 11 for Penn State, were linebackers who became edge defenders, and have similarly incredible athletic traits. And like Parsons, Carter has quickly […]
full_text: New York Giants defender Abdul Carter rushes against the Washington Commanders. | Getty Images When the New York Giants made Abdul Carter the third overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, it was believed that they had selected the next Micah Parsons. After all, the two wore 11 for Penn State, were linebackers who became edge defenders, and have similarly incredible athletic traits. And like Parsons, Carter has quickly become one of the most feared pass rushers in the NFL… Except Carter hasn’t produced the sacks expected of him. Carter’s lack of sack production became a hot topic of conversation around the Giants’ media ecosystem this week. So much so that they prompted questions about the second-year defender when defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson spoke to the media on Thursday. “I think he’s played extremely well,” Giants’ defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson said when asked for his assessment of Carter’s play through nine games. “If you watch him, he’s been extremely disruptive,” he continued. “He’s making a lot of plays.” Of course fans want to see him make plays, but what they want to see even more is Carter putting the opposing quarterback on the ground. That, however, hasn’t happened much to date and he has just 2.0 on the season. But it’s also difficult to watch a Giants’ game and not see Carter have an impact. “The sack numbers aren’t there, but he’s affecting the game,” Wilson said. “A lot of holding calls, a lot of pressures. He’s getting the quarterback off the spot, so the sacks will come. We’re trying to put him in positions for him to get some touches on the quarterback, but he’s doing everything he’s supposed to do. In the run game, he’s been excellent. He’s holding force. The ball isn’t circling outside of him. So, I love where he’s at. I just wish the production was a little bit more for him right now, because he deserves it, especially the work that he’s putting in.” Wilson is adamant that the sack numbers will improve as Carter continues to be disruptive during games. He also continued to praise Carter’s work ethic. “He’s still a young player,” he said. “He’s progressing. I think he’s at a good point in his career right now, and he still has more to come. So I’m excited where he’s at. He just going to continue to get better. Man, you should see the guy. He works so hard in the meeting rooms, trying to understand the game plan, and he’s taking pride in just being a disciplined football player. So everything else will take care of itself.” The discipline Carter has shown is of particular importance to the Giants’ defense. Dennard Wilson has become one of the most aggressive defensive coordinators in the NFL, and is in the Top 5 in the NFL in blitz rate. Wilson’s blitzes aren’t just sending an extra man and letting everyone do their own thing. No, instead he thinks in terms of patterns to create opportunities for specific players, and every defender has his role to play in the blitz. “We present a lot of different looks,” he said, “but for us, from a conceptual teaching standpoint, guys are doing the same things from different spots at times. The blitz patterns can change. I’m a firm believer in ‘you can mess with the front in terms of plugging people in different places, but you don’t mess with coverage’. So in the cover standpoint, we don’t change our cover structures because teams do certain things. “But we’ll do things up front to attack their known protection and their standard operating procedures on how they’re going to protect certain looks, how they’re going to slide,” Wilson said. “So that’s what we come up with our blitz patterns off of kind of what they do. We try to check their water a little bit, and if they have another answer, we get something for it. That’s the attack.” Wilson added that that his blitz patterns are driven by a variety of factors that can change on a weekly basis. However, the Giants do have blitz packages designed to make use of Carter’s prodigious athleticism, as well as that of players like star rookie Arvell Reese. “There are certain things that we’ll have set up for him [Crarter], but you kind of move to pieces around,” Wilson said. “Because if you move to pieces around, they never know which ones are the known rushers. You have certain things we’ll have for certain players depending on the blitz pattern. Some days it might be (Inside Linebacker) Arvell (Reese). Sometimes it’s matchup driven. If we feel that we can attack a certain player on the line of scrimmage, we might put a guy there, because he can win fast right now, or whatever it is. “It’s a little bit of skill set. It’s trying to get some of these guys some blitzes where they can come free, so they feel good about the blitz plan, and they attack it a certain way. So it’s a little bit of both. With the guys that we have, we try to make them be interchangeable, so you don’t know where we’re come from.” It’s also a bit difficult at times to remember just how new Carter still is to the position he plays. This is only his third year as a full-time edge defender, having only transitioned from off-ball linebacker in 2023 at Penn State. And while he might not be stuffing the box score in a way that’s easy to write about, his incredible get-off makes him one of the most disruptive players in the NFL. That, combined with his unselfishness as a teammate, has helped make the Giants one of the best pass defenses in the NFL. Though Carter has been under a bit of fire lately, Wilson had nothing but praise for him or the standards to which Carter holds himself. “One thing about Abdul is this, he has high expectations,” Wilson said. “I hope every player that we have has high expectations. I hope everybody in the building has high expectations. But Abdul is a team player. And that’s what sometimes doesn’t get noticed. And what Abdul is doing right now, he’s doing his job to the best of his ability. And other things will happen for him. He’s still progressing. You look at him from last year to this year and how he’s playing, how dependable he is, how accountable he is. He’s doing the little things correct. “Everything else is going to take care of itself because he has that dynamic ability and that dynamic trait. It will turn on. And when it turns on, watch out.”

title: NY Giants signed Xavier Gipson to provide ‘spark’ in return game
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The New York Giants signed Xavier Gipson off the Philadelphia Eagles’ practice squad this week because they “need a spark” in the kick return game, special teams coordinator Chris Horton said on Thursday. “When we had X during the spring, during the training camp, I mean, he’s got a lot of […]
full_text: Xavier Gipson with the Giants during training camp. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images This is why the #NYG signed Xavier Gipson, via ST coach Chris Horton: pic.twitter.com/WPT5f8rcBI — Big Blue View (@bigblueview) November 19, 2026 EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The New York Giants signed Xavier Gipson off the Philadelphia Eagles’ practice squad this week because they “need a spark” in the kick return game, special teams coordinator Chris Horton said on Thursday. “When we had X during the spring, during the training camp, I mean, he’s got a lot of skill,” Horton said. “So, just bringing a guy in that we feel like we need a spark. And it’s nothing that Charlie (Jones) did not do. I don’t want to seem like we’re not doing that, but we feel like we need a spark. We need a guy back there to maybe give us a little bit more juice.” The Giants are 21st in the NFL in kickoff return average, at 25.4 yards. They are 24th in punt return averaged, at 8.5. Jones had a fumble and muffed punt in recent weeks, and Gregory Desrosiers fumbled a punt in Week 10 against the Washington Commanders. “We just got to find a way to really just try to create some more explosive plays throughout the game,” Horton said. Gipson, 25, has extensive experience as a returner. He has averaged 9.1 yards on 74 punt returns and 25.9 yards on 51 kickoff returns. He was cut by the Giants at the end of the preseason and landed on Philadelphia’s practice squad. Now, he is back for his third stint with the Giants. Gipson has 12 fumbles in 163 career touches, one every 13.6 touches, and has lost jobs with the New York Jets and Eagles largely because of those issues. Horton said he will believe Gipson can overcome those ball security issues … at least until he shows he can’t. “What gives me confidence is the same thing that gives me confidence in all the players. Just belief in their abilities. I truly believe that no player is the same player until he shows you he’s the same player,” Horton said. “So, it’s our job to go out there and allow him to grow from those things that might have set him back. But I also know that this guy, when that ball has not been on the ground, he’s made teams pay. “So, just believing in the guys and continue to believe in the guys, that’s strong for me, and just to give those guys an opportunity. And until he shows us that he can’t do that, I don’t see that player. I didn’t see that player in training camp. I didn’t see that player this spring. So, that’s why I have the confidence and belief that this guy’s going to go out there and he’s going to show people.” The mystery of the right hash mark It has been well-documented that all six of placekicker Dominic Zvada’s missed field goals this season have come from the right hash mark. It is a technique issue that Zvada has been working to correct. “I think it’s one of those things, you just go out there and you just execute in the situation. We’re not going out there and saying we need to be on this hash in order for us to make kicks, right?,” Horton said. “We’re going out there and saying, hey, we have the confidence in our abilities to go out there and no matter where we are to make the kick. Dom’s made kicks from the right hash. So, we have to find that consistency in making those kicks because he’s doing a really good job. What are those little details that we got to iron out? Because we have made kicks from that hash. So, we’re not thinking about all those things. We’re going out there like they put us out there, let’s go execute and let’s go make the kick.” What kinds of things has Zvada been working on? “Just from as far as plant foot, what’s our target line? Where are we aiming and things like that? Everything comes back down to, I kind of talked about this before with kickers, the consistency in foot to ball and where the foot is,” Horton said. “Sometimes he’s too tight. Sometimes he’s too wide. We’ve got to find that happy medium spot and we’ve got to get him there. So, that’s one of the things that we’re working on. We came out here yesterday and he hit the ball well and we script plays from the right hash. We do those things a lot. So, we’re working on those things to get them fixed.”

title: What will make the 2026 Eagles season a successful one following the bye week?
summary: The 2026 Philadelphia Eagles season won’t be resulting in a Super Bowl championship. The playoff streak is also likely ending at five seasons. This season is a lost cause in terms of expectations from the summer. That doesn’t mean the 2026 season can’t be deemed a success. Bear with me here. Since the Eagles are […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 08: Joe Milton #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles passes the ball against the New York Giants during the first quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on November 08, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 Philadelphia Eagles season won’t be resulting in a Super Bowl championship. The playoff streak is also likely ending at five seasons. This season is a lost cause in terms of expectations from the summer. That doesn’t mean the 2026 season can’t be deemed a success. Bear with me here. Since the Eagles are 2-7 and aren’t expected to make the playoffs this year, there are some factors remaining in this season that can carry over into 2027. The wins and losses aren’t as important (well maybe the losses), but some aspects from 2026 can play into how the 2027 Eagles shape out. So what can make the remainder of this Eagles season a success? There are a few things to hope for in this lost season. 1. Finding the No. 2 QB One of the biggest developments heading into the season was the Eagles’ handling of the backup quarterback. They didn’t have a backup quarterback, so they used the “competitive advantage” charade between Andy Dalton and Tanner McKee up until the Week 1 inactives were posted. Dalton isn’t with the Eagles anymore and McKee was benched after three subpar starts. The backup quarterback “competition,” played out to the Eagles’ biggest fear. Joe Milton is making his second start on Sunday and Cole Payton is waiting in the wings for his opportunity once he’s ready to play. The Eagles need to hope one of the two can play well enough to be Jalen Hurts’ backup in 2027 — assuming Hurts is able to play football again. The perfect scenario for the Eagles? Milton plays fine the remainder of the season, or good enough to keep around. 2. A top-5 draft pick Easy one right? Losing more games actually helps the Eagles in a lost season. The Eagles still have talent and core players on this roster that will contribute in 2027, but this season has been a disaster with all the injuries, the subpar offensive line (with trades and retirements), and discombobulation on offense. The Eagles have eight games remaining in this season. as the .504 opponents win percentage is the rest of the season is 14th-hardest in the NFL. They likely won’t lose out, but a 4-13 record could wrap up a top-5 draft pick. The Eagles currently have the No. 5 pick in the draft, per Tankathon. They’re currently in position to get that top-5 pick. 3. Continued growth of Makai Lemon Lemon has finally acclimated to the NFL after missing the majority of the spring and summer with a hamstring injury. Even though the Eagles were banking on Lemon to be an instant impact player in the offense, a slow start for the rookie was expected. Over the last three games, Lemon has 20 catches for 185 yards and a touchdown. The 9.3 yards per catch isn’t great, but Lemon was the WR1 in a depleted offense with the QB3 from Week 1 and a quarterback signed a month ago. With Devonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks back, the Eagles should see more production from Lemon in the slot. He won’t be the primary option in the offense, but Lemon can be a more efficient pass catcher as the WR3 — which is expected to be his role in 2027. Lemon has shown he can play in the NFL. The next step is to catch passes consistently and for the Eagles to expand his route tree. One of the two should come to fruition in the final eight games. 4. Markel Bell’s development at right tackle Bell might be the worst offensive tackle in the league. He wasn’t supposed to play significant snaps this season, as this year was supposed to be the final one for Lane Johnson. Turns out it was, but Johnson retired after four games and didn’t finish out the year. Bell wasn’t ready, and it’s shown in pass protection. He’s allowed five sacks, 18 pressures, and has been beaten by a defender 25 times in 253 pass-blocking snaps — a beat rate of 9.9%. Only the Green Bay Packers’ Anthony Belton has a higher beat rate amongst offensive linemen with 100+ pass-blocking snaps. The Eagles have to see improvement out of Bell in the final eight games to determine if he’s worth building around at right tackle. If Bell doesn’t improve, a new offensive line coach may be coming (Chris Kuper may likely be gone anyway) and the Eagles will have to seriously consider selecting a tackle with that top-10 pick in the NFL Draft. If Bell can improve and become a competant right tackle in the final eight games, that’s a significant win for the Eagles in 2027. 5. Dontayvion Wicks showing he can be a WR2 The early returns for Wicks as a WR2 have been positive, but an ankle injury has hurt Wicks’ progress in what was looking to be a promising year. Wicks has been productive in his six games, having 19 catches for 284 yards and a touchdown — 14.9 yards per catch. He was on pace for 805 receiving yards prior to the injury. While Wicks has been a deep-ball receiver, most of that productivity came when Jalen Hurts was the quarterback. Wicks has only played one game post-Hurts, having two catches for 24 yards before missing the past three games with that ankle injury. With Joe Milton at quarterback, there should be opportunities for Wicks to be a deep-ball threat — even with the offensive line struggling in pass protection. Wicks should open up the offense, as he has 25 games (this year and next) to showcase to the Eagles he can be a core player in the offense going forward. 6. Jonathan Greenard becoming an impact player Like Lemon this summer, Greenard wasn’t going to be in football shape at the start of the season due to the pectoral injury that kept him out of camp. A slow start was expected, but Greenard didn’t get his first sack until Week 8 against the New York Giants. The Eagles started Greenard on a pitch count, and he’s slowly worked his way to 50% of the snaps (which occurred in the Giants game). The production hasn’t been ideal — even for a part-time player — as Greenard has just a sack, 10 pressures, and an 11.9% pressure rate this season. Greenard appears to be back in football shape, with the pectoral injury behind him. It’s time to see the player the Eagles are paying $24.5 million a season for, the version of Greenard that had a 16.7% pressure rate over the past two seasons. Greenard was an elite pass rusher two years ago. Shoulder and pectoral injuries have taken away that elite status. The Eagles need Greenard to be close to elite if they want to get the pass rush going. Philadelphia is 27th in the NFL in pressure rate (32.3%) and 28th in sack rate (5.1%). Greenard returning to a Pro Bowl level would increase those numbers. 7. Jihaad Campbell showing why he was a first-round pick Campbell was handed the keys to a starting job at off-ball linebacker this summer, and is the reason why the Eagles moved on from Nakobe Dean. Philadelphia couldn’t pay everyone, and Dean was a casualty of having to pay other premium players. This is why the Eagles drafted Campbell two years ago, preparing for the inevitability they were going to lose Dean. Campbell was solid in his rookie season as a linebacker and pass rusher, but is strictly an off-ball linebacker this season. Poor performance and injuries have led to Jeremiah Trotter Jr. outperforming Campbell, but the Eagles are giving the first-round pick a long leash (as expected). Campbell has to improve in coverage, as he’s allowed 73.1% of passes thrown his way as the primary defender to be caught, with opposing quarterbacks having a 112.7 passer rating targeting him. This is on Campbell to get himself in position and improve in coverage, or else he’ll be playing for his job in 2027. 8. Jalyx Hunt living up to the training camp hype Hunt was arguably the best defensive player in training camp. That production — against the Eagles offensive line — hasn’t come close to translating in the regular season. Hunt doesn’t have a sack through eight games, and has…

title: Eagles opposing player to stop, Week 11 edition
summary: The Eagles have managed to become No. 1 in something in the NFL this season. They currently hold the longest losing streak in the league at seven-straight games, after the Los Angeles Chargers won their first of the season in Baltimore on Monday night. But the Eagles will be primed to have another streak snapped […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - NOVEMBER 15: Quarterback Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on during an NFL football game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles have managed to become No. 1 in something in the NFL this season. They currently hold the longest losing streak in the league at seven-straight games, after the Los Angeles Chargers won their first of the season in Baltimore on Monday night. But the Eagles will be primed to have another streak snapped this Sunday, when they host in-state Pittsburgh Steelers at 1 p.m. at Lincoln Financial Field in a game that flexed up from a nationally televised 4:25 p.m. start to the regionalized 1 p.m. start. The Steelers have not won in Philadelphia since October 24, 1965, winning 20–14 at Franklin Field. Lyndon Johnson was president, and it was two stadiums and 61 years ago. Eagles own an 11-game home winning streak over the Steelers, going 3-0 at Franklin Field, 4-0 at Veterans Stadium and 4-0 at Lincoln Financial Field. The tie-in with this game is that falls tragically on November 22, the annual anniversary of the assassination of President John F. Kennedy, who was succeeded by Johnson. Currently, the Steelers have an AFC North Division title to play for, and the Eagles are fighting to work their up the draft order by continuing to lose. It looks like the return of receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks this week against the Steelers, but they will both still have Joltin’ Joe Melton throwing to them, which gives the Eagles a greater chance to lose. There may be as much black-and-gold as midnight green in the stands. The NFC East is deplorable this season, though it is the Eagles who sit at the bottom, which speaks volumes as to how bad their situation is. Adding to that will be facing future Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers this weekend. Rodgers is 42, but even he would be a considerable upgrade as to who the Eagles have now at quarterback. He’s thrown 15 touchdowns against six interceptions this season, completing 190 of 317 passes for 2,014 yards. Rodgers has also been sacked been sacked 26 times, which is the sixth highest in the NFL this season. Not that it will help the Eagles, who are 28th in the NFL in sacks with 16 for minus-104 yards, which is 26th in the NFL. Rodgers may not be able to move like he once did, but he is good enough to beat the Eagles. Eagles’ defensive coordinator Vic Fangio has seen his share of Rodgers through the years and thinks that the ancient one is still dangerous. “ Yeah, obviously I’ve seen a lot of him over the years,” Fangio said about Rodgers. “I mean, I don’t think anybody can make a top five list of quarterbacks all time without him on it. Just a very pretty passer, great release, super knowledgeable, great anticipation. Just a guy I have a total lot of respect for.” When asked this week if Rodgers brings an advantage at the line of scrimmage, will he make it more difficult on the Eagles’ defense, especially with his ability to get free plays by drawing defenses offsides. “ Yeah, it can,” Fangio said. “He’s really good at it. He does a great job with the cadence and making you think the play’s ready to go and then pull out of there and change it when you’ve played as long as he has. And now he’s back with [Steelers Head Coach] Mike [McCarthy] in the same system he grew up in. So, it’s like back to the good old days.” The Eagles are in a state of making things look good, making them seem competitive. They are arguably the worst team in the NFL and aiming for a higher pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, knowing this season is lost. Offensively, the Eagles are the worst team in the NFL, with 2,342 yards of total offense, which translates into a season-low 260.2 yards a game average. Staying consistent, the Eagles are the 25th-ranked defense in the NFL, giving up 353.4 yards a game. Two weeks ago, the New York Giants snapped their 13-game losing streak at Lincoln Financial Field, while the Eagles lost their seventh-straight game, bringing them closer to that magic number of 12-straight losses. The longest Eagles’ losing streak in the Super Bowl era is 11-straight games, which goes to the infamous 1968 Eagles, who lost their first 11 games that season. The 2026 Eagles are in the running for records. Now, it is the Steelers’ turn to break an 11-game, 61-year losing streak by beating the hapless Eagles. The Eagles remain consistent this season. Consistently bad.

The Steelers will move Watt around a little bit, but he mostly rushes against the RT, where the Eagles had to replace a now retired Lane Johnson with third-round rookie Markel Bell. As noted in our rookie progress report on Monday, Bell has had growing pains in his rookie season, which of course is to be expected. But he also hasn’t yet faced anyone as good as Watt, who has 7.5 sacks this season, and who ranks 31st all-time with 122.5 career sacks. This will be an extremely difficult challenge for Bell, obviously. When the season is over, the Eagles will have to decide if they think Bell showed enough as a rookie to trust him as the starting RT going forward, and this game against Watt could be one that helps make that determination. Mannion was dealt some tough circumstances with injuries, surprise retirements, and trades. The offense is a shell of what it was supposed to be. The test for Mannion now is to see if he was able to take advantage of the bye week and come up with some ways to improve the offense. His focus was improving communication. Eagles backup DTs ready for opportunity after Jordan Davis trade – NBCSP Ty Robinson and Byron Young miss Jordan Davis already. They became close to the former Eagles’ first-round pick who was traded to Jacksonville at the trade deadline last week. But they know what that trade means for them: More playing time. “It’s a bittersweet opportunity, obviously, because it sucks losing Jordan, especially in our room,” Robinson said. “But it’s an opportunity for me to get out on the field a little bit more. I’m excited and I’m ready.” In the Eagles’ first nine games of the season, Davis played 323 defensive snaps (52%). Those snaps are now up for grabs. NFL Week 11 picks: Upset and score predictions, matchup breakdowns for every game – NFL.com Why Gennaro picked the Steelers: Because I envision Terrible Towels flying across The Linc in this battle of Pennsylvania. The Eagles entered their Week 10 bye with a seven-game losing streak and came out of it without their best run-stuffer. Eight months after handing Jordan Davis a $78 million extension, Howie Roseman traded the hulking nose tackle for draft currency. Not only did that move underscore the obvious — that Philadelphia is punting on 2026 and planning for the future — but it stripped Vic Fangio’s defense of a key cog against this particular opponent. These Steelers are clearly at their best when the offense runs through Jaylen Warren, who leads all qualified RBs with an average of 5.7 yards per carry. But this past Sunday night, Pittsburgh ran into a Bengals buzzsaw, and Warren was quickly game-scripted out of the blowout loss, finishing with a season-low seven carries. I expect Mike McCarthy to feed his star back early and often against a Philly front that had struggled to stop the run with Davis. Now that the 6-foot-6, 336-pound space-eater is in Jacksonville, Warren is poised for a bounce-back performance. And like I alluded to at the top, this will please the scores of Steelers fans who’ve presumably hoovered up tickets from a downtrodden Eagles fan base. title: Eagles-Steelers Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 11 enemy
summary: Can the Philadelphia Eagles make it two weeks in a row where they don’t lose?! Their bye was the easy part of that equation. Now the Birds have to go out and beat the Pittsburgh Steelers to snap a seven-game losing streak. In order to preview this Week 11 Keystone State matchup, I reached out […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 13: Head coach Mike McCarthy of the Pittsburgh Steelers talks with Aaron Rodgers #8 prior to the game against the Green Bay Packers at Acrisure Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Can the Philadelphia Eagles make it two weeks in a row where they don’t lose?! Their bye was the easy part of that equation. Now the Birds have to go out and beat the Pittsburgh Steelers to snap a seven-game losing streak. In order to preview this Week 11 Keystone State matchup, I reached out to our enemies over at Behind The Steel Curtain . The ravishing Ryan Parish kindly took the time took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let’s take a look at the answers. [For my answers to Ryan’s questions about the Eagles, stay tuned to BTSC .] 1 – Aaron Rodgers is playing worse than he did last year. To what extent is he cooked? Are there other reasons for his struggles? I would push back slightly on the notion that Rodgers is playing worse this year. That isn’t to say he’s playing well; I just think this has felt like nearly the same exact experience as last year. He is no longer a top-tier passer, but I think most reasonable people knew that before the 2025 season. There is not much wrong with Rodgers’ arm. He can still uncork an impressive throw once or twice a game. The issues largely come from his lack of mobility and, frankly, his mentality. The mobility speaks for itself; Rodgers struggles to get out of messy pockets. That’s tough enough on its own, but his desire to avoid any kind of hits at his advanced age also has him hearing footsteps and seeing ghosts several times a game, resulting in him often fleeing a reasonably clean pocket and into pressure that otherwise wouldn’t have gotten home. He doesn’t consistently target the middle of the field. He insists on throwing fade routes to D.K. Metcalf that result in some of the least effective targets in the NFL. He doesn’t like pre-snap motion or play action, which handcuffs a receiving corps that already struggles at creating separation. And despite the success the team has had running the ball with jumbo packages and man/gap running schemes, he and head coach Mike McCarthy inexplicably like to periodically abandon that identity for prolonged stretches, instead trotting out nostalgia-laden spread shotgun looks from their Packers’ heyday that have been catastrophically ineffective each time Pittsburgh has tried to make it work with this roster. It’s maddening that Rodgers is playing so poorly, and yet is still probably the best quarterback play the team has had during the 2020s. 2 – Eagles fans have familiarity with Mike McCarthy from his time in Dallas. How are Steelers fans feeling about the job he’s done thus far? Two weeks ago, when the Steelers were riding a winning streak and thoroughly dominated the Browns to get to 6-2, fans couldn’t sing Big Mike’s praises enough. Now, following an embarrassing beatdown on primetime at the hands of the Bengals, the fanbase is back to lamenting the purgatory this franchise has been stuck in for at least the last decade and arguably longer. That the “offensive guru” in McCarthy on Sunday seemed to completely forget the style of offense that got the Steelers on a winning streak in the first place has many questioning him on the heels of such an embarrassing loss. It’s been a rollercoaster, to say the least, and one I expect to have several more peaks and valleys over his tenure. 3 – The Steelers haven’t had a losing season in 23 years … but they also haven’t had a playoff win in 10 years. Do fans feel like this team is stuck in purgatory? I swear I didn’t read ahead, but as you might have gleaned from my previous answer: YES. Gee, thanks for noticing. 4 – What’s the biggest matchup in the Steelers’ favor and the biggest matchup against their favor? The Eagles currently rank 25th in rushing yards allowed per game, and the Steelers have had a dominant run game when they’ve leaned into that identity. That might be impacted now that starting left guard Mason McCormick is out of the lineup, likely for the year, as Spencer Anderson is set to take his place. Anderson started the season as the Steelers’ starting right guard, but it only took two weeks for the team to yank him and right tackle Dylan Cook from the starting lineup and replace them with Brock Hoffman and rookie right tackle Max Iheanachor. I could also point to Joe Milton against this pass rush as possibly favoring Pittsburgh. As for a matchup that favors the Eagles? I think the Eagles’ secondary will give these receivers and Rodgers fits. 5 – Who wins this game and why? With the Steelers currently listed as 4.5-point road favorites, what’s your score prediction? And is it interesting to Steelers fans at all that they might see the franchise’s first win in Philly since 1965? I think Steelers fans care less about that factoid — though I think that’s a cool trivia fact and I salute your pull — and more about winning this game, period. Heading into this season, I think many Yinzers would have penciled this game in as a Steelers loss, but with all that has transpired with the Eagles this season, I think a loss to Philadelphia’s injury-depleted roster would be considered inexcusable. With games coming up against Denver, Houston, and Jacksonville, I think a loss this week would cause levels of doom and gloom in Pittsburgh I’m not prepared to deal with. As for the final score? I will predict a Steelers win, but I expect it to be ugly. Steelers 20 – Eagles 17.

title: Eagles News: No major changes coming out of the bye
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! The Eagles are sticking with Sean Mannion at offensive coordinator and Joe Milton at quarterback. Of course, it’s always possible there are changes going on behind the scenes that we’re not yet privy to. The Eagles didn’t formally announce they were […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 04: Philadelphia Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion looks on during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 4th, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Center in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! The Eagles are sticking with Sean Mannion at offensive coordinator and Joe Milton at quarterback. Of course, it’s always possible there are changes going on behind the scenes that we’re not yet privy to. The Eagles didn’t formally announce they were demoting Sean Desai in 2023 when they took play-calling away from him to give it to Matt Patricia instead. Not saying the same scenario will definitely happen here, nor necessarily should it after that experience three years ago was such a disaster. But it’ll be interesting to see to what extent, if at all, the offense looks aesthetically different in the second half of the season. Also, I’m not sure why Milton staying the quarterback is considered news? Why would the Eagles start him only to bench him after one game? He might start the rest of the season, though it seems ideal to mix in Cole Payton at some point. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Sean Mannion to continue calling offensive plays for Eagles, Joe Milton to remain at QB – PFT Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said that the team would talk about changes to roles and responsibilities on the coaching staff during their bye week, but he said on Wednesday that they decided against any major ones. That means offensive coordinator Sean Mannion will continue calling the team’s offensive plays when they face the Steelers this week. Sirianni explained why he’s staying the course at a Wednesday press conference. Eagles Injury Report: DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks return to practice – BGN The Eagles listed seven players under LIMITED PARTICIPATION: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Will Shipley, Nolan Smith, Michael Carter, Britain Covey, and Jonathan Jones. Smitty and Wicks returned to practice after missing multiple games. Nick Sirianni indicated the Eagles have hope they can return to game action this week. Smith told reporters that he’s “100% healthy.” Getting their top two receivers back would be a nice development for Philadelphia’s offense. Midseason reports on every NFL team’s offensive coordinator, playcaller – ESPN What has gone right? It’s not a long list. The Eagles are third in red zone efficiency (73% touchdown rate) and are tied for 10th in turnover rate (9.2%). But they struggle mightily sustaining drives and lead the league in three-and-out percentage (35.7%). They’re bottom-five in passing (171.7), rushing (88.6) and points (16.4) per game. Mannion, in his first year as an OC and third year in coaching overall, has seen his unit struggle in the second half in particular, which points in part to inadequate adjustments. What has gone wrong? It’s been far from ideal conditions for Mannion. Right tackle Lane Johnson retired, quarterback Jalen Hurts was lost for the season with blood clots in his lungs, center Cam Jurgens was traded to the Ravens and a number of skill position players missed time due to injuries, including WR DeVonta Smith, RB Saquon Barkley and WR Dontayvion Wicks. Mannion was brought in to implement a Sean McVay/Kyle Shanahan-like system, but the outside zone run — a staple of that offense — has largely fallen flat and things have gone so poorly overall it’s hard to even identify what the current scheme is. Some Changes – Iggles Blitz Paganetti worked for the Eagles for 10 years, handling multiple roles. His most prominent role was helping Jeff Stoutland coach the OL. Paganetti went with Kellen Moore to New Orleans in 2025 to serve as the Saints run game coordinator. He was fired a couple of weeks ago, as their run game was really struggling. He felt like a sacrificial lamb to appease angry fans and the media. The run game has continued to struggle. We don’t know exactly what Paganetti’s role will be with the OL. He is a smart coach and good communicator so maybe he can help the players and coaches finally get on the same page so the missed blocking assignments will go away or at least go down. They have been an overwhelming issue for the offense all season long. Paganetti isn’t going to have some magic bullet solution that will solve everything, but he can help the situation. He has coached Jordan Mailata, Landon Dickerson, and Tyler Steen. Paganetti also coached Saquon Barkley, Will Shipley, and Dallas Goedert. Those guys play key roles in pass pro and blitz pickup. He will know how to communicate with them. The run and pass blocking have been so erratic this year that anything is worth trying. Arnold Ebiketie: No hard feelings after trade to Bengals falls through – NBCSP Arnold Ebiketie was at breakfast last Tuesday when he got the call. The Eagles were trading him to the Bengals for a 2027 sixth-round draft pick. As Ebiketie drove home to pack his bags, his mind was racing. He was already thinking about how he was going to ship his car to Cincinnati, pack up his belongings and spend some time with his kids before heading to Ohio. His flight had already been booked. But about two hours later, Ebiketie got another call. The deal fell through. “It’s the NFL, the business-side of it,” Ebiketie said on Wednesday as the Eagles began their preparations to play the Steelers. “I felt like one call I was going to Cincinnati, another call I was staying here. I wasn’t mad at the fact that I was staying so I got back to my bye week. That was the best part about it.” The Best Bets of NFL Week 11 – The Ringer The Eagles also traded away one of their best run-stopping defensive tackles, Jordan Davis, prior to the bye week. Pittsburgh couldn’t run the ball at all in Cincinnati last week, but before that, the Steelers were the most efficient running offense by EPA per play this season. The Steelers have been a disaster in true road games this year, but I’m tempted to go back to my reliable strategy of fading the Eagles, at least for one more week. The Eagles are winless (0-9) as a home underdog in the Sirianni era, and they’re also now 2-14 against the spread in the second halves of their last 16 games. Their offense has averaged 0.8 points per drive in the second half this season. No other team is worse than 1.19. You can bet the second-half line prior to kickoff, and Pittsburgh second half –2.5 is staring right at you. Bet: Steelers second half –2.5 (–110) What should Eagles fans watch in the next 8 games? The development of these 8 players – The Athletic WR Makai Lemon — Even with DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks expected to return, Lemon should have opportunities to show why the Eagles made him a first-round pick. Lemon ranks No. 2 among rookies with 37 receptions, yet he ranks No. 7 with 312 receiving yards because of how the Eagles used him. His average depth of target this season is 6.2 yards. That pales in comparison to outside receivers such as Smith, who has an ADOT of 12.3 yards. High-end slot receivers (and generous player comps in the draft process) such as Amon-Ra St. Brown and Puka Nacua have ADOTs of 8.4 yards and 8.2 yards, respectively. That’s the type of neighborhood Lemon can approach if the Eagles expand his role in the second half of the season. “I think he’s got the ability to do multiple things,” Sirianni said. “There’s no question about it. I think that, especially this last month of the season, he’s really been productive with things that you can obviously see, how strong his hands are and his ability to catch the ball in traffic. I think that, again, I’ve told you guys what I’ve thought about him, and I just think that he takes everything that’s given to him, and he’s able to handle a lot, and we can continue to add to his plate. I just think he’s got a unique skill set.” NFL QB rankings,…

title: Steelers news: The Steelers have a DK Metcalf problem
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers moved on from disgruntled wide receiver George Pickens with a trade to the Dallas Cowboys two seasons ago. The front office answered by adding former Seahawks receiver D.K. Metcalf to the room with Aaron Rodgers as the quarterback. After signing him to a lucrative extension, Metcalf has been inconsistent, to say the […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers moved on from disgruntled wide receiver George Pickens with a trade to the Dallas Cowboys two seasons ago. The front office answered by adding former Seahawks receiver D.K. Metcalf to the room with Aaron Rodgers as the quarterback. After signing him to a lucrative extension, Metcalf has been inconsistent, to say the least. The receiver had his issues in Seattle, but after a contract extension, the Steelers should be concerned about Metcalf and his future with the team. From an analytical standpoint, Metcalf is 45th (!!) in the NFL with an EPA/target of 0.05. For reference, he’s tied with Laquan Treadwell and just ahead of Eagles receiver Makai Lemon. Another troubling data point is the 19 contested targets for Metcalf, which is good for ninth in the NFL. Now, that isn’t exactly a black-and-white metric, but you’d hope to see more separation. As far as targeted success rate, Metcalf sits at 38.6%. Playing receiver is twofold, as the quarterback has to deliver the football, and Rodgers has a 61.4% on-target rate when targeting Metcalf. The drops have been discussed and can’t happen, but with only 432 receiving yards, it’s hard not to be concerned about his future with the potential quarterback change next season.
