title: Raheem Morris won’t make excuses for the 49ers’ defense; explains missed opportunities
summary: San Francisco 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris was asked what some of the biggest takeaways and teaching points were from watching the Dallas Cowboys game: Extending drives early. Some of the penalties to get those guys to go down there, particularly on the first drive, we gave up three I believe, on that first one. […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images San Francisco 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris was asked what some of the biggest takeaways and teaching points were from watching the Dallas Cowboys game: Extending drives early. Some of the penalties to get those guys to go down there, particularly on the first drive, we gave up three I believe, on that first one. We got the big penalty to get those guys down there. They’ve got a big-time field goal kicker. A couple of big plays, you know, in the first half, the two big plays were the ones that killed us there early. Got a pretty good grip on it after that. Kind of held it down after that. I thnk t was like 38-19. That finishing moments, we didn’t do a very good job of getting the finishes off. Usually, the finishes happen when you’re able to generate those finishes with sacks, or you’re able to get interceptions. The Cowboys did a nice job, give them credit, of getting the ball out of their hands. Did a nice job of getting it into their good players hands, keeping drives going, extending drives. They had about three or four drives there were it was almost like overtime play for them, where it was going to be 4-down territory, regardless. And they were able to go down and score. You would like to be able to stop some of those plays and get off the grass at those moments. Then that score, when they got to where it was, those things didn’t happen. We didn’t execute that way. And it’s a collective group. I know Bosa stood in front of you guys and took all the accountability, but I really think it was all of us. Some of it could have been better play calls for them. Some can be better what we can do for those guys. Some of it can be better plays made by us. Some of it, we just ran out of a little bit of gas; got a little tired. Let’s not kid ourselves, human nature as well. Fortunate to get out of there with a win. Definitely want to learn those lessons and do those things in those moments when you get wins. File the 49ers’ defensive performance under “close, but no cigar” against Dallas. Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams forced a couple of would-be turnover-worthy plays, but the players in the back-7 couldn’t hold onto the football. Morris was asked whether that’s encouraging or discouraging, knowing that his defense was in a position to make a play, despite the result: “Both. The Mykel one was frustrating immediately. You got your corner sitting there, and whether you agree or disagree with the call or not, it doesn’t matter. But that was a big-time play in the factor of the game that would get you off the grass and allow your offense to go out there and eat up more time and more clock. At the rate they were going, they were probably going to score anyway, but it would allow us to go out there and buy some more time so you don’t get to that number of 84 plays. The games that you want to be frustrated on are where you got a lot of plays. That was an opportunity for us to go sit on the sideline, and we missed it.” Morris believes his unit is “much healthier” this week, but didn’t want to make excuses, saying, “nobody cares.” He was talking about his cornerbacks, Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir, who battled injuries leading up to Week 10.

title: Brock Purdy has golden opportunity to shake up MVP race vs. Vikings
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are facing off against the Minnesota Vikings in an NFC heavyweight battle on Sunday night in Mexico, with the No. 1 seed in the NFC on the line. The 49ers have shown several different versions of themselves this year. We’ve seen dominant offensive performances throughout the year, as well as some […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - NOVEMBER 15: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy throws a pass during the NFL game between the San Francisco 49ers and the Dallas Cowboys on November 15, 2026 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Brian Rothmuller/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are facing off against the Minnesota Vikings in an NFC heavyweight battle on Sunday night in Mexico, with the No. 1 seed in the NFC on the line. The 49ers have shown several different versions of themselves this year. We’ve seen dominant offensive performances throughout the year, as well as some strong defensive performances, like against the Denver Broncos. Last week, it was the offense that led the way, as Brock Purdy threw for 389 yards and three touchdowns en route to the 46-40 win over the Dallas Cowboys. Normally, those numbers could be game-changing in the MVP race, especially considering how consistent Purdy has been this year. But Cincinnati Bengals star Joe Burrow has also played exceptionally well to date and is now the runaway favorite for MVP. He’s thrown for 2,795 yards (second in NFL), 27 touchdowns (first in NFL), and six interceptions, while completing an astounding 74.7 percent of his passes. With Cincinnati sitting at 7-2, it makes sense that Burrow is the favorite for MVP, but that doesn’t mean other quarterbacks like Josh Allen and Purdy still don’t have a chance at the award. We saw how close the race between Drake Maye and Matthew Stafford ended up last year, and there is still a ton of regular-season football to play. So far, Purdy has thrown for 2,369 yards, 20 touchdowns, and five interceptions, while his QBR is second in the NFL to Burrow. The biggest advantage for Purdy is that he’s been the primary reason for the success of an 8-1 team. And this weekend, he’ll take on the league’s toughest coordinator and defense with the Minnesota Vikings, who just stifled the Green Bay Packers 30-10 on the road. If there’s any game the rest of the way that could really boost Purdy’s odds for MVP, it would be this one: a primetime showdown between two top NFC teams with a ton of eyeballs on the game. The Vikings have been excellent at throwing quarterbacks off their game defensively this season, with Brian Flores using a blitz-heavy approach to thwart quarterbacks and keep them off their game. Purdy, however, has been excellent against the blitz this season, ranking first in the NFL in passer rating against the blitz. On Wednesday, Kyle Shanahan attributed a big part of the 49ers success amid all the moving parts to Purdy’s poise. “I just feel Brock plays the right way. Like, he just truly plays the position,” Shanahan said. “He’s not ever like, ‘Hey, this guy’s better than that guy, so I’m just going to force the ball to that guy.’ Or, ‘That guy didn’t make the play last time, so I’m going to ignore him and go somewhere else.’ Brock keeps a clear mind and just plays each play one at a time and does what he’s supposed to do. If nothing’s there or he can’t see something or something doesn’t work, then he tries to compete and make a play on his own. “So, I don’t think much changes. It’s not like, ‘Hey, I know you’ve been going to this guy all day, but he’s not there so you’ve got to change something on you.’ Brock, to me, it’s the same for him, his same plan every week, regardless of who’s in there. It can make it harder when some people aren’t in there, but the plan never changes for him.” General manager John Lynch shared a similar sentiment this week, while believing in Purdy’s preparation for the tough matchup ahead. “I just can’t say enough about Brock. Brock can play on time and rhythm, and he can also create and make things happen, as we saw the other day. You saw all of it on full display,” Lynch said. “He’s playing at an incredibly high level, and it’s just really what we’ve come to expect. He’s having an unbelievable season, and he knows the challenge he’ll have this week against Minnesota, but I know that he’ll be up for it.” This is the perfect game for Purdy to jump back into consideration for the MVP race alongside Joe Burrow, and the 49ers offense could potentially get Mike Evans back, although resting him for Week 12 against the Seattle Seahawks makes sense. A lot will be on Purdy’s shoulders, as well as Kyle Shanahan’s, to devise a game plan against a defense that not many have had answers for, and it could be instrumental for the 49ers the rest of the season with the NFC race.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: Inside the looming chess match between Kyle Shanahan and Brian Flores this weekend
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are back in primetime on Sunday night, as they’re taking on the Minnesota Vikings in a battle between Top NFC contenders. San Francisco, sitting at 8-1, is coming off a 46-40 win over the Dallas Cowboys, where its offense was unstoppable, while the defense had a ton of holes. Minnesota, on […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - NOVEMBER 8: Head Coach Klint Kubiak of the Las Vegas Raiders with Head Coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers on the field after the game at Levi's Stadium on November 8, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. The 49ers defeated the Raiders 38-17. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are back in primetime on Sunday night, as they’re taking on the Minnesota Vikings in a battle between Top NFC contenders. San Francisco, sitting at 8-1, is coming off a 46-40 win over the Dallas Cowboys, where its offense was unstoppable, while the defense had a ton of holes. Minnesota, on the other hand, just traded for Kirk Cousins at the trade deadline and blew out the Green Bay Packers in his first game back. While Minnesota’s offense has raised questions this year, it’s the defense that has remained elite under coordinator Brian Flores, who has continued to find different ways for his defense to excel. This year, it’s with a blitz-heavy approach. Flores has been able to neutralize teams all year long. No team has scored more than 25 points against the Vikings, and that lofty defense was what propelled Minnesota while its offense was struggling. Flores has had head coach Kyle Shanahan’s number in the chess match between play-callers over the past few years. Regardless of the circumstances of the previous matchups, this is a perfect opportunity for Shanahan and the 49ers to establish themselves in many ways. It would continue to provide a boost in the NFC race, while also giving Shanahan another game to bolster his Coach of the Year case. But Shanahan acknowledged the difficulty that Flores and his game plan will provide on Sunday. “He just, he does it. He’s more unique than all the other 31 guys,” Shanahan said of Flores. “He’s the one guy who commits to this and it’s not just a fad for these nine games or whatever. He’s been doing it his whole time in Minnesota. He did the same thing in Miami. He’s as good as it gets at that stuff. Anybody who lives in that world as much as he does, it’s usually a matter of time. “I think offensive coaches used to like to say that early on, but it’s too many years of it, and it’s too many games in this year that they’re sound. They put so much pressure on the quarterback, the play caller, the O-Line, the receivers, on everybody. A lot of times, when you go into an NFL game, the pressure’s really on people on third down and stuff like that because those are things where everything can come and when you play against Brian, it’s 70-straight plays of that.” One position that Flores’s defenses have done really well to neutralize is the tight end position because of how much the Vikings blitz, forcing another blocker to stay in-line. That’s critical with Mike Evans currently not trending to play, leaving George Kittle as the team’s top weapon. But overall, this game will be a chess match between the two brilliant minds who have arguably been the best play callers in the NFL this season. And there’s a lot on the line on both sides with the NFC race heating up.

full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images In a surprise to nobody, it’s been a brutal year for the San Francisco 49ers on the injury front. They signed veteran wide receiver Christian Kirk this past offseason to add speed and stretch the field both vertically and horizontally. Kirk strained his calf during the first training camp practice. Kyle Shanahan confirmed Kirk suffered multiple setbacks , which is why he remained out until Week 7. Kirk played 20 snaps, but was not targeted. Less than two weeks later, Kirk injured his right knee meniscus in a Thursday practice. Two days later, on November 7, Kirk landed on the injured reserve for the second time this season. Kirk celebrated his 30th birthday Wednesday by posting a picture on his Instagram, sharing with fans that he underwent meniscus surgery. #49ers WR Christian Kirk, who was placed on Injured Reserve two weeks ago for the second time this season, recently underwent meniscus surgery. pic.twitter.com/tN7FKBNsYL — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 19, 2026 During the regular season, teams can bring back eight players from the injured reserve. The 49ers already used one of their designations on Kirk. They’ve also designated Demarcus Robinson, Nate Hobbs, and CJ West to return. With one already used on Kirk, it makes you wonder whether they’ll use another. Keenan Allen taking over Kirk’s No. 3 might be another sign of the Niners’ intentions. Kirk, along with De’Zhaun Stribling, Nick Martin, Austen Pleasants, and Sam Okuayinonu, could all return. In theory, they could use a second designation on Kirk, while still bringing back Stribling, who was seen working on the side of Wednesday’s practice, along with Sam O. Martin and Pleasants seem like emergencies in case of an injury. That leaves you two in the event an injury happens over the next couple of weeks. So, while unfortunate, the Niners still have a little bit of a cushion in terms of managing their designations.

title: Buccaneers at Lions: Thursday injury report for Week 11
summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers received some encouraging news Thursday as they continued preparations for their Week 11 matchup against the Detroit Lions. After missing Wednesday’s practice, quarterback Baker Mayfield (foot/right thumb) returned to the practice field Thursday as a limited participant. It’s a positive development for the veteran quarterback, whose availability for Sunday has been […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 8: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers warms up before the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on November 8, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tampa Bay Buccaneers received some encouraging news Thursday as they continued preparations for their Week 11 matchup against the Detroit Lions. After missing Wednesday’s practice, quarterback Baker Mayfield (foot/right thumb) returned to the practice field Thursday as a limited participant. It’s a positive development for the veteran quarterback, whose availability for Sunday has been in question since suffering a foot injury against the Chicago Bears. Mayfield revealed Thursday that the injury occurred early in the game against Chicago during a scramble that resulted in a completion to running back Kenny Gainwell. He played through the discomfort for the remainder of the contest. When asked about his readiness to play against Detroit, Mayfield responded, “I feel ready.” While his return to practice is certainly encouraging, the Buccaneers are expected to make a determination on his availability Friday. Rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels remains the next man up should Mayfield be unable to play. Unfortunately for Tampa Bay, safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (ankle) missed his second consecutive practice, while outside linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) remained limited. Wide receiver Chris Godwin Jr. and running back Bucky Irving were added to Thursday’s injury report as non-participants, while defensive lineman A’Shawn Robinson was limited. All three received rest designations. Cornerback Josh Hayes (knee), tight end Cade Otton (thumb) and left tackle Tristan Wirfs (toe) remained full participants. For Detroit, there were no changes to its injury report from Wednesday. Center Cade Mays (ankle) remained sidelined, while six players, including cornerbacks D.J. Reed (hip) and Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (shoulder), remained limited. Safety Kerby Joseph (knee) was once again a full participant. Both teams will release their final injury reports Friday, with much of the attention in Tampa Bay continuing to surround Mayfield and whether he will be healthy enough to lead the Buccaneers’ offense Sunday in Detroit.

title: How to win, how to lose: Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions week 10 game preview
summary: “Hey hey Tampa Bay,” the Bucs know how to… Stay hurt. Tampa Bay is entering another important game against a very quality opponent and they will be dealing with another major injury. The Buccaneers, for the second time this season, will be navigating their way through a Baker Mayfield injury. From hands to feet, it […]
full_text: Sep 15, 2024; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving (7) runs the ball against the Detroit Lions in the second quarter at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con “Hey hey Tampa Bay,” the Bucs know how to… Stay hurt. Tampa Bay is entering another important game against a very quality opponent and they will be dealing with another major injury. The Buccaneers, for the second time this season, will be navigating their way through a Baker Mayfield injury. From hands to feet, it has been a challenging season for the Buccaneers’ franchise quarterback . Injured or not, the Buccaneers and the lions will be the teams featured in this week’s, “ How to win, how to lose. ” “ Defense wins championships. ” Bear Bryant How can the Buccaneers win? Play defense like the 2002 Tampa Bay Bucs. Can anybody get Derrick Brooks on the line? Do we have his number? The Bucs’ defense in 2026 has been the highpoint. Outside of Chase McLaughlin, a strong argument could be made Tampa’s defense is the best part of the team. Todd Bowles has his group playing at an elite level, maybe near the best they have under his watch in west Florida. The Bucs are coming off of a bye week, but their defense is coming off a résumé building performance. The Bucs did not shutdown Caleb Williams, Ben Johnson, and the Chicago Bears, but they did humble them. Williams’ back-to-back touchdown drives to open the game turned out to not be foreshadowing of the way the remainder of the game would unfold. Tampa Bay stayed calm while the young star quarterback saw pressure and started unraveled. Williams was rushed and forced into an uncomfortable playstyle— He heaved (in most every sense of the word) four interceptions. Not so star rookie Rueben Bain Jr. even popped onto the scene, forcing a fifth turnover, when he smashed into Luther Burden III late in the contest. That 2002 Buccaneers-esque outing is the type of performance that Bowles’ defense will need to put forward (again) in order to have any hopes of victory in this week’s matchup with the Detroit Lions. Once more, the Buccaneers will be entering this game as the underdogs and having very little room for error. Even with their team at full health, this game would not be one where they could roll the ball out and expect to win—With Baker Mayfield’s status being what it is, this game becomes even more of a hike without a trail. If Jalon Daniels (or a severely hampered Baker Mayfield) is going to beat the Detroit Lions, Tampa Bay’s defense will need to be at its best. Can they duplicate or exceed their quality performance from two weeks ago? “Three things can happen when you pass, and two of them are bad.” Woody Hayes How can the Buccaneers lose? Get into a shootout. Tampa Bay’s NFC South duels against the Carolina Panthers and Atlanta Falcons were great and fairly recent, but they feel a far ways away. The good vibes and juju the Buccaneers had been working to manifest spiraled away like water down an open drain when their offense was back to not offense-ing against the Chicago Bears. The 2026 Tampa Bay Buccaneers have had this weird dichotomy of being such a brilliant running football team and simultaneously being truly atrocious when it comes to throwing the football. This might not be as big of a problem if the team were playing their games in the mid 70’s or even the 1990’s, but as mentioned above this is the 2026 Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Football sort of requires a passing game at this point. The passing game doesn’t need to be as dynamic as the 2007 Patriots or prime Peyton Manning with the Denver Broncos, but right now Tampa looks like they are playing with Tim Tebow— Which actually (for the way the team is built), may not be the worst thing if they had quarterbacks who could run like Tebow— Unfortunately, they don’t. Jalon Daniels does have mobility and the benefit of some playing time under his belt this go around. After playing, he also had the opportunity to sit back down for a month and evaluate himself and self reflect about his time on the field. Hopefully, that time was not wasted because back on the field again he will likely be. Even still, he is an undrafted rookie free agent— Expectations are and should be fairly low. Even if it is Baker Mayfield defying the odds and suiting up for Sunday’s game, Tampa’s passing attack has been a wet noodle this year. There is no reason to have any confidence that the Buccaneers are going to all of a sudden emerge as a team that can throw the football— They can’t. The failures in the passing game are theory-test, thesis level, and study worthy. Whether you lay the majority of the blame at the feet of the quarterback; who has spent as much time running in circles behind the line scrimmage as he has missing throws down field, the receivers who can’t even conceptualize separation— who also manage to drop the ball even when they do get open and it is delivered accurately, or the coach who can somehow scheme up a legendary, record-setting run game with zero ability to capitalize off of that in the passing game, it’s bad— Truly bad and baffling. Not all teams have 1,000-yard receivers. Sure the Bucs usually do, but still, that’s not a given. Not all teams have a 3,000-yard passer. Sure the Bucs usually do, but still, that’s not given either— However, if you’re thinking it’s just a semi bad season for passing the football in Tampa Bay, stop. Some perspective, in case reading the stats hasn’t been a steady past time. A majority would agree 1,000 yards receiving is sort of the standard or the goal in most people’s eyes— Well, the Buccaneers might not have a receiver that reaches 600 yards. It’s entirely possible each of the team’s two starting pass catchers will not combine for 1,000 yards in total. Let that sink in before you realize that a lot of quarterbacks throw for 3,000 yards in a season— 21 did it last year. Baker Mayfield, the franchise quarterback of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, making it to 3,000 would be an impressive feat, considering his current data point. Mayfield, very well may not hit 2,000 yards passing by the time the season reaches finality— Even more insane, all of this could happen on a team that is qualifying for the postseason. Playoff absurdities aside, the easiest way the Buccaneers can lose this game is by getting themselves into a shootout with a team that has actual weapons while the Bucs’ offense has a couple of Red Ryders and a low-budget airsoft collection. Tampa Bay cannot go score for score with the Detroit Lions— They must run the ball, keep the score down, ensure the time of possession stays in their favor, and try to win an ugly game.

That probably means we are in for a letdown. We are all very familiar with the struggles the Titans’ pass defense has. They cannot get pressure on the quarterback with Jeffery Simmons gone, and they cannot cover anyone on the back end. Dak Prescott and the Cowboys’ offense should move the ball down the field at will. The total for this game opened at 53.5 at FanDuel Sportsbook . It currently sits at 54.5. It is the highest total on the board for Week 11. I’m not sure the Titans have ever been in a game that featured the highest total for a week. This game sets up to look a lot like the Cincinnati Bengals game from a few weeks ago. The Titans lost that one 43-36 in overtime. Joe Burrow threw for 462 yards and 5 touchdowns. Ward threw for 304 yards and 2 touchdowns. To me, having an entertaining game to watch where Ward plays well but the Titans ultimately lose is a win, win, win scenario. That is probably what will happen here, but I have a feeling the Titans are going to pull off an upset…. Titans fans, Titan Up your game-day experience! title: Commanders news: Dexter Lawrence brings huge test for Commanders OL
summary: The Daily Slop – 20 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Last Man Standig […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - NOVEMBER 15: Dexter Lawrence #97 of the Cincinnati Bengals reacts after a sack during the third quarter against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Daily Slop – 20 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Last Man Standig (paywall) The Commanders went from the NFL’s least-blitzed team to its most-blitzed; now they’re fighting back “Teams noticed that we had a 14-point lead, that they got us off the field and then put points on the board when they had the ball,” Allegretti said. “That Week 5 game influenced a lot.” The Commanders faced a similar trend last season. They entered Week 6 against the Bears at 3-2 but without injured starting receivers Terry McLaurin and Noah Brown. Washington then struggled when Chicago pressed its perimeter receivers at the line of scrimmage, daring them to win downfield. The strategy showed promise. Dallas deployed its version the following week, beginning a stretch of four consecutive Commanders losses by at least 21 points. Injuries aside, Washington never solved the press-coverage problem. This time, Washington may be finding answers before the latest defensive trend becomes another season-long issue. For more from Ben Standig, click here From Commanders Roundtable: There is no gentle way to say it: Dexter Lawrence has been a problem for every offensive line he has faced this season. The three-time Pro Bowler arrived in Cincinnati via trade this past spring and has looked fully rejuvenated in his first year with the Bengals. Through ten weeks, Lawrence holds an 87.6 PFF overall grade — second among all interior defensive linemen in football — with a 89.6 pass-rush grade that ranks first at the position. He has racked up 22 total pressures, four sacks, three hits, and 15 hurries. Teams have been double-teaming him on nearly 80% of his pass-rush snaps, and he still wins. After seeing lot of blitzes since Wk 5, Washington's OL may face a different test on Monday night #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/VIGdQndPNk — Bill-in-Bangkok (@billhorgan2005) November 20, 2026 Which is exactly why the center situation matters so much heading into Monday night. Lucas Patrick missed last week with injury but returned to practice Wednesday, though Dan Quinn stopped short of declaring him the starter. That leaves the door open for Nick Allegretti, who stepped in against the Giants on Thursday night and delivered one of the offense’s cleaner weeks in terms of protection and communication. The offense visibly flowed better — fewer high snaps derailing Daniels before plays even started, and cleaner interior windows for the run game to operate through. The question now is whether Washington rolls with what’s working or returns to Patrick in a spot where continuity matters. Lawrence’s ability to collapse the pocket from the inside forces quick decisions and kills run lanes. If whoever is playing at center cannot get a hat on Lawrence consistently, the Bengals will dictate tempo all night. The Commanders know this. What they decide at center will be one of the biggest pregame storylines on Monday. To read more of this Commanders Roundtable article, CLICK HERE Wire Report Commanders cut pressure rate to 23% behind Daniels, revamped protection The schematic turnaround addresses a recurring early-season issue for Washington, transforming pass protection from a liability into a platform for downfield efficiency. Establishing reliable pass blocking allows the offense to dial up vertical concepts with Burks while keeping Daniels protected in the pocket. The win solidifies Washington’s offensive identity following an inconsistent start. By the numbers: Washington’s pressure rate dropped from 46% (seventh-worst in the NFL in Week 5) to 23% in Week 10 (third-best mark in the league). Daniels has completed 138 of 213 passes for 1,499 yards with 10 touchdowns and two interceptions in 2026 through seven games. Sinnott has caught five passes for 48 yards and one touchdown in 2026 through nine games. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) Commanders Learn Lesson vs Cover-0 One of the biggest turnarounds from the Commanders tie back in Week 5 against the Giants and their win over the Giants on Thursday night was the plan of attack against Cover-0. In Week 5, the Giants spammed Cover-0 blitzes throughout the second half and overtime and the Commanders just couldn’t handle it. They continually attempted to take shots down the field to try and hit explosive plays rather than just finding a simple quick solution. Daniels was seeing those blitzes a lot better and it showed in the most critical moment. Back in Week 5, the Giants spammed the Commanders with Cover-0 blitzes and Washington just completely failed to handle it. On Thursday, OC David Blough and QB Jayden Daniels showed they had learned their lesson. I broke it down: https://t.co/U1yrDEyKUZ pic.twitter.com/kMh2rjFdSU — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) November 15, 2026 Having thrown two late interceptions, it looked like the Commanders season was over, but the defense bailed Daniels out and gave him another opportunity, which he wasn’t going to pass up. On third and four with under a minute remaining in the game, the Giants of course show Daniels another Cover-0 blitz. This time, Daniels doesn’t adjust the protection, but instead signals to Stefon Diggs in the slot to change his route. In the first game, when Daniels saw Cover-0, he often checked into a shot play to try and attack the blitz and throw a big touchdown over the top of it. But clearly this time they were looking to play smarter, and it worked out much better for them. Daniels adjusts Diggs route, having him run a slant against the slot corner. When he snaps the ball, the defense comes on the blitz, but the defensive tackle to the right side of the line pops up and drops out into coverage, trying to take away a hot throw over the middle. Daniels just checked into a hot throw over the middle with Diggs running a slant, so that could potentially be a problem. But Daniels does a great job adjusting his throw to beat that defensive lineman dropping into coverage. Diggs runs a great route, beating the corner with a nice stutter move before sharply cutting across his face to get inside. The throw from Daniels has to be slightly behind him because of that defensive lineman dropping into coverage, but Diggs does well to adjust to the pass and make the grab. Diggs breaks a diving tackle from the slot corner and gets some help from fellow receiver Van Jefferson, who helps block the other nearby defender. With both defenders out of the picture, Diggs runs uncontested into the end zone for a 32-yard game-winning touchdown. It goes to show that you can still score a big touchdown against Cover-0 without having to try and take a deep shot constantly. As I said back in Week 5, I don’t mind that their philosophy against Cover-0 is to go on the attack, in fact I quite like it. It offers you one-on-one matchups and I like that they feel like they can take shots with those matchups. But they clearly went too far in Week 5 in trying to throw bombs down the field. This game proved there’s more ways to go about it. Winning a one-on-one doesn’t have to be 20 yards down the field, it can be a quick slant like this when you have Stefon Diggs or Antonio Williams in the slot. With it being Cover-0, if you win that one-on-one quickly, there’s every chance the receiver can run freely after the catch and score as there’s no safety help over the top. So credit should go to David Blough and Jayden Daniels for making that adjustment. It’s a shame they couldn’t have made it back in Week 5…

title: How QB Jayden Daniels, Commanders offense can keep up with Bengals
summary: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels took 17 questions in his weekly press conference. Three of them were about Sam Hartman as the next Bachelor. Another was about Grand Theft Auto VI. And four more focused on a game that happened two years ago.    Their relevance came from Monday night’s game against the Cincinnati Bengals. Washington hasn’t […]
full_text: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels took 17 questions in his weekly press conference . Three of them were about Sam Hartman as the next Bachelor . Another was about Grand Theft Auto VI. And four more focused on a game that happened two years ago. Their relevance came from Monday night’s game against the Cincinnati Bengals. Washington hasn’t played Cincinnati since the 2024 campaign, also on a Monday night. And it was a freaking barnburner. Daniels came up huge in that 38-33 Commanders victory , with a game cemented in the legend that was his rookie year. He and Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow, both LSU products, traded blows during a game with zero punts. Daniels delivered the knockout. It came on this 27-yard dagger to Terry McLaurin with 2 minutes, 15 seconds left. JAYDEN DANIELS. TERRY MCLAURIN. THE COMMANDERS. 📺: #WASvsCIN on ABC 📱: Stream on #NFLPlus and ESPN+ pic.twitter.com/bP5qrpGN8q — NFL (@NFL) September 24, 2024 Daniels was borderline invincible on that night, completing 21-of-23 passes for 254 yards , two touchdowns, no picks and a (checks notes) 141.7 passer rating. That came in just his third professional game. Daniels doesn’t like looking backwards, not even to the good stuff, so much so that the game’s topic was broached with, “I know you don’t like talking about the past, but…” “I think it was a good moment for myself and my career,” Daniels said, “especially up to that point for everybody to go in a tough environment on the road and pull out a win versus a very good team.” Commanders fans remember that game for its high drama, an incredible finish and it’s back-and-forth nature. Commanders vs Bengals Week 3 matchup from 2024 🍿 pic.twitter.com/M7N0TLxtK3 — Kalshi Football (@KalshiFB) May 23, 2026 In order to beat the Bengals on Monday night, It might require a similar effort this time around. That’s even true with both teams experiencing a defensive resurgence in recent weeks. That brings up an important question leading into an important contest for both teams. Can Daniels and this Washington offense keep up with a Bengals team that has scored 30-plus points in five straight games? “I think just as a competitor, as a QB, I think it’s just like the pressure of the moment,” Daniels said. “You want those moments where all eyes are on you, with the pressure and you go out there and execute. So, I think that’s kind of just the biggest thing, from that game two years ago. But we go out there and hopefully we don’t punt. And they do, but you gotta be prepared for everything.” The Commanders should be prepared to put up lots of points. Burrow deals with the blitz well, a bad combo for a Washington team that struggles getting home rushing four. They also feature Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins and a passing game that is truly next level. The Commanders have been good at taking the ball away but have struggled giving up yards. While there’s certainly a path to victory that involves a stout Commanders defensive effort, odds of that should be considered low. That’s why this offense needs to run the ball well – that’s Cincinnati’s defensive soft spot – for the first time in a while on designed runs. Consistency will be key in this one despite heavy losses on that side of the ball. “We talked a lot today about our team, like how do we win?” head coach Dan Quinn said. “And so, on the, what we call our Wednesday, we put a big tape together of how we win. These are the things that we’re going to do. So it wasn’t just one side of it. And so, I want everybody to know this is what we’re gonna do to prepare to go win. And so, a complementary game is what we need. And that doesn’t mean that one side has to carry all this on their own, all of us doing those together. So that’s what we’ll do, and that’s over the next four days, we’ll put all that work in to go do that.” It’s hard to expect another no-punt instant classic like what happened in 2024, but Jayden Daniels must put an excellent game (and plenty of points) forth to keep up with the Bengals. “We feel like, I mean, every game, regardless of who’s on the other side, we gotta put up points,” Daniels said. “So, that’s our mindset each and every week is to go out there and score points. They got really good guys over on their team, so, you know, we gotta execute and really focus on us.” Can Jayden Daniels and the Commanders offense put forth a performance capable of keeping up with the electric Bengals offense? Let us know in the comments below:

title: Draft buzz: Interest in Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker could spur draft trade
summary: If the Titans or Chargers wind up with the No. 1 selection and stick with their franchise quarterbacks, interest in Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker could lead to a team seeking to trade up for the top overall pick.
full_text:
Drew Mestemaker 's meteoric rise through the 2026 season has seen the Oklahoma State  quarterback climb to No. 2 on ESPN's Mel Kiper Jr.'s Big Board , which might be an undersell on his eventual draft position.

 On Thursday's episode of "The Adam Schefter Podcast," Schefter examined the current 2027 NFL draft order that includes two teams that already have some confidence in their starting quarterbacks at the top.

 "There is going to be an auction, I believe, for the No. 1 pick for the right to draft Drew Mestemaker," the ESPN NFL Insider said. " Dolphins , Jets , Cardinals , Browns , whoever. Someone's going to want to trade up with the Titans or the Chargers ."

 

 Entering Week 11, the Titans (1-8) and Chargers (1-8) would have the top two picks in April's draft. With Tennessee and Los Angeles expected to stick with former top-six picks in  Cam Ward and Justin Herbert , respectively, the auction scenario could come into play for quarterback-needy teams if the Titans or Chargers wind up with the No. 1 selection.

 "Tennessee, I believe, even at the 1-hole, would stick with Cam Ward," Schefter said on the podcast. "I think that there's enough belief and conviction within that organization that they feel like right now -- and there's still eight games to go for the Titans this season -- they feel like they have a quarterback here. Cam Ward's had three head coaches and three coordinators in under two years. They want to give him some consistency."

 The "home run scenario" for Tennessee, Schefter said, would be the Dolphins, Jets or Cardinals landing the No. 2 pick and giving the Titans an additional asset to move up one slot. Tennessee could then bring in Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith -- Kiper's No. 1 player -- to join Ward and Smith's former college teammate, wide receiver Carnell Tate .

 Last week, Mestemaker deferred any talk about whether he would enter the 2027 draft, telling reporters that "there's nothing I can do about it right now."

 

 Entering the season, Kiper identified Mestemaker as among his "maybe" candidates for first-round consideration. Mestemaker, a North Texas transfer who followed coach Eric Morris to Oklahoma State, has since put up 3,239 passing yards and 30 passing touchdowns, plus another four rushing touchdowns, in his first 10 games for the Cowboys.

 There's an annual increase in value for quarterbacks in draft season. Schefter noted that Notre Dame 's CJ Carr , who also has college eligibility remaining, could be a draft riser because of his physical talent and his team's ceiling.

 "Quarterbacks are currency," he said. "If there's a quarterback you love, you take him."

 ESPN's Pete Thamel conducted a  midseason QB1 poll of 25 NFL scouts and executives  last month, asking who the top quarterback will be in next year's NFL draft. Seventeen of the 25 responses were for Mestemaker, with Carr finishing second with four votes.

 What we're hearing on the Cardinals: Sunday will be quarterback  Carson Beck 's second career start, but it'll be his first chance to build on his NFL debut. His goal is to get to "elite communication," which he described as being better at relaying the plays to the huddle, knowing what the plays are within the first few words and having a better understanding of what defenses are trying to do. "Being that level of prepared and having elite communication and then ultimately just going out and letting it rip," Beck said. "I think that's something that I did decent in the last game, but that's something that I want to build up to my standard where I see the defense, I see the play and you already know the ball's coming out." -- Josh Weinfuss 

 What we're hearing on the Chiefs: Much of Sunday's game for the Chiefs is about managing injuries, especially before their Thanksgiving showdown against the Bills. Several veterans are not expected to play against the Cardinals, including right tackle  Jaylon Moore (right ankle), right guard  Trey Smith (concussion protocol) and running back  Kenneth Walker III ( groin ). "He had a sore groin [last week]," coach Andy Reid said Wednesday of Walker. "It's getting better. We just don't want to do something stupid and put him out there. It's still bugging him a little bit, but he's feeling a lot better than he was." -- Nate Taylor 

 Stat to know: The Cardinals ran season-high 82% of plays out of shotgun in Beck's first start. The Chiefs' defense has the second-best touchdown-to-interception rate (three passing TDs, six INTs) against shotgun in the NFL behind Vikings (4 TDs, 10 INTs, 0.4), per NFL Next Gen Stats. -- ESPN Research

summary: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 11, led by Houston debuting its Rivalries combination.
full_text:
A primetime game can be a perfect opportunity for a team to send a message with its play. It also helps when it is looking its finest on the gridiron. The Houston Texans and Washington Commanders enter Week 10 with one part of that down with the debut of their respective uniforms.

 

 It's the Texans' turn first, as they will wear their Rivalries threads against the Indianapolis Colts on "Thursday Night Football." The look is primarily white, but includes H-Town blue and battle red with details that pay homage to Houston's streets. The city's signature blue street tiles appear on the uniform's helmet, name plate, sleeve, collar and pant stripes in a two-tone battle red and blue finish. Houston's "be someone" bridge is the inspiration for the blue jersey numbers.

 For the first time, the Texans will wear a liberty white helmet, paying tribute to the white prototype founder Robert C. McNair revealed in 1999 before shifting to a deep steel blue lid. The white helmet's face mask includes a chrome H-town blue finish, a nod to Houston's car culture. 

 As part of the Commanders' redesign of their uniform closet last offseason , they unveiled the all-black "Hail Raiser" alternates, which debut against the Cincinnati Bengals on "Monday Night Football." It features a black helmet with a "Spear W" logo on both sides, as the spear and "W" are interwoven at their center. Burgundy and gold stripes appear on the sleeve and pants, while the lid includes a three-stripe look on top of similar colors. Solid burgundy block numbers are outlined by gold. 

 The Buffalo Bills are also rocking a Rivalries look against the Miami Dolphins . Buffalo debuted its all-white "Cold Front" combination last season, but it returns with icy details throughout. The shoulder sleeve features a chrome charging buffalo, the first time a Bills uniform incorporates this element. The white helmet similarly includes a frosty metallic-filled charging buffalo logo, while the shoulder and pant leg patters boast a cracked-ice texture with a pattern that resembles snowfall on a bison's fur. 

 It's an alternate week for the Detroit Lions as well. Detroit is going all-black against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Complete with a Honolulu blue matte helmet, the "Motor City Muscle" threads were first unveiled in 2024. The lid also includes a leaping lion logo in silver with a black stripe down the middle. The Lions wore these threads in Week 7 against the Green Bay Packers .

full_text:
The forecast affects the game plan for how NFL players put together their Week 11 looks.

 The Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans kick things off Thursday night in Houston, where evening temperatures in the upper 60s should leave room for light layers.

 With morning temperatures near freezing expected in Denver before an afternoon climb into the 40s, players arriving for the  Raiders - Broncos  game have an opening for coats and chunky knits. Morning temperatures in the 50s in Buffalo should give Miami Dolphins and Buffalo Bills players an opening for sweaters and light jackets, while Jacksonville Jaguars and New York Giants arrivals in East Rutherford, New Jersey, call for similar layers under cloudy skies, with rain possible later in the day.

 From practical layers to outfits built for the spotlight, here are the standout arrivals from Week 11.

 

 Thursday night fashion 
Texture did the talking in C.J. Stroud 's arrival. The Texans quarterback sported a gray knit polo paired with relaxed light-wash jeans, while a black woven bag, brown shoes and a blue-faced watch added the finishing touches.

title: Chiefs are flying high but can ill afford to overlook the lowly Cardinals when they meet Sunday
summary: — If ever there was a time for an NFL team to overlook somebody, it just might be Sunday afternoon at Arrowhead Stadium, where the Kansas City Chiefs will continue their pursuit of another AFC West title against the injured, downtrodden Arizona...
full_text:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- — If ever there was a time for an NFL team to overlook somebody, it just might be Sunday afternoon at Arrowhead Stadium, where the Kansas City Chiefs will continue their pursuit of another AFC West title against the injured, downtrodden Arizona Cardinals .
The Chiefs (7-2) have moved back into first place in the division thanks to tiebreakers over the Broncos, who have an identical record through the first nine games. But a slip-up against the Cardinals (3-7) could be downright disastrous considering the Chiefs are staring at a five-week meatgrinder that includes the likes of first-place Buffalo, Cincinnati and San Francisco.
“They've had a lot of injuries, obviously, but they still have a lot of NFL talent on the roster,” Chiefs linebacker Drue Tranquill said. “At this point, the message is just about us stacking wins in November and December, and we're going to try to do that on Sunday.”
The Chiefs have bounced back nicely from back-to-back losses in Seattle and Denver, taking advantage of what was long perceived to be the soft part of their schedule. They blew out the Jets 35-12 at home a couple of weeks ago, and they beat the Falcons by an almost identical 35-13 score last week — their fifth win by at least two touchdowns this season.
Even without ailing running back Kenneth Walker , and injuries along their offensive line, the Chiefs have been able to score at a high clip. Patrick Mahomes is playing like an MVP again, throwing five touchdown passes last week in Atlanta, and the acquisition of wide receiver Josh Downs in a trade with Indianapolis is already paying dividends for Kansas City.
Its defense has been stingy, too, holding Atlanta running back Bijan Robinson in check last week.
Juxtapose that with the Cardinals, who were waylaid 34-6 by the Rams last weekend.
Arizona put safety Andrew Wingard and linebacker Jordan Burch on injured reserve this week, pushing their total to 16 players on injured lists, tied with the 49ers for most in the NFL. That includes quarterback Gardner Minshew II , first-round pick Jeremiyah Love , fellow running back Trey Benson , wide receiver Michael Wilson and offensive tackle Paris Johnson II.
The injury to Minshew means that Carson Beck will make his second consecutive start this week. The third-round pick out of Miami endured a rough NFL baptism last weekend, going 11 of 18 for 108 yards with two interceptions against the Rams.
“It’s us coming up with the best plan possible to put these guys in position to be successful, and then them going and executing the job," Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said. "Every single guy, if you ask them — if they have a jersey and they’re in the National Football League, they’re going to tell you they belong, and they’re going to tell you that they can make the plays.
"They have another opportunity this week to get that done.”
Arizona (3-7) at Kansas City (7-2)
When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EST, CBS.
Latest odds: Chiefs by 15 1/2.
Against the spread: Cardinals 4-6, Chiefs 5-4.
Last week: Cardinals lost to Rams 34-6; Chiefs beat Falcons 35-13.
Last meeting: Chiefs beat Cardinals 44-21 on Sept. 11, 2022.
Series record: Chiefs lead 10-3-1.
Chiefs RB Emmett Johnson against the Cardinals run defense, which allows 129.9 yards per game, fifth worst in the NFL.
Walker is expected to miss his second game because of a groin injury, which means the fifth-round pick out of Nebraska will once again be the featured back. Johnson filled in on short notice last week in Atlanta, running for 101 yards and catching six passes for 70 yards and two touchdowns. He has 519 yards from scrimmage this season, second most among all rookies.
The Cardinals, meanwhile, have allowed at least 120 yards rushing in six of their 10 games, and they were especially bad against the Rams. Blake Corum ran for 100 yards, Ronnie Rivers ran for 81, and the Rams finished with 202 yards rushing as a team.
— The Chiefs have won five of the past six in the seldom-played series. They are 4-0 against the Cardinals at Arrowhead Stadium.
— Chiefs TE Travis Kelce has caught a pass in 200 straight games, the longest streak in franchise history and the longest active streak in the NFL. The longest streak by a tight end in NFL history is 211, set by Tony Gonzalez.
— Downs had four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown in his Chiefs debut in Atlanta. The Chiefs acquired him for a pair of draft picks from Indianapolis early last week, and he should be more comfortable with a full week of practice this week.
— Chiefs WRs Cyrus Allen and Andrew Armstrong each caught their first career touchdown pass against the Falcons. Allen's was from 39 yards and Armstrong's was from 43.
— Beck will be facing a former MVP and Super Bowl-winning quarterback for the second straight week in Mahomes. Beck faced the Rams' Matthew Stafford in his first career start last week.
— Cardinals S Budda Baker is the only player who was on the team when they last visited Arrowhead Stadium in 2018.

title: Midseason reports on every NFL team's offensive coordinator, playcaller
summary: Here's the good and the bad for each offensive coordinator or playcaller through Week 10, plus keys to their success the rest of the way.
full_text:
We've seen the good and bad of offensive coordinators and playcallers across the league throughout the first half of the 2026 NFL season.

 With Dan Pitcher coordinating the offense and coach Zac Taylor calling plays, Joe Burrow has the Cincinnati Bengals ' offense humming. The same goes for Trevor Lawrence and the Jacksonville Jaguars , with Grant Udinski as OC and coach Liam Coen the playcaller. Both QBs are in the MVP conversation.

 On the other side of things, the Los Angeles Chargers ' offense under OC/playcaller Mike McDaniel has been a disaster. The Minnesota Vikings had struggled to put points on the board until they acquired QB Kirk Cousins , which had an immediate impact on coach Kevin O'Connell's playcalling in Sunday's win over the Green Bay Packers .

 There are eight weeks left this season, and the pressure will continue to build for coordinators and playcallers looking for winning formulas, while those who shine might be in position to become head coaches in 2027.

 With that in mind, here is what has gone right, what has gone wrong and the key to the second half for every offense in the NFL.

 
 Jump to: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF 
 SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 

 
 

 

 

 AFC EAST 
 

 Buffalo Bills 
 Offensive coordinator: Pete Carmichael

 Playcaller: Joe Brady

 What has gone right? Just about everything. The Bills lead the NFL in scoring (31.9 points per game) and are doing so with a varied attack that features RB James Cook III handling a career-high workload and QB Josh Allen leading his most explosive passing attack since arriving in Buffalo. Most encouragingly, this offense has proved just as capable of winning in slow-paced ball-control games as in up-tempo shootouts.

 What has gone wrong? Pre-snap sloppiness is a recurring problem. Between false starts, illegal shifts, delays of game, offsides and too many men in the huddle calls, the Bills are averaging close to three pre-snap offensive penalties per game, and that's not to mention the 132 yards the Bills have had nullified by holding penalties.

 Key to second half: Allen has always benefited from the abnormal consistency, continuity and health in front of him on the offensive line. In recent weeks, tackles Dion Dawkins and Spencer Brown and guard Alec Anderson have dealt with injury concerns. Keeping the line together, especially with cold weather coming and how the Bills are already leaning on Cook, is paramount.  -- Nick Suss 

 

 

 
 

 Miami Dolphins 
 Offensive coordinator: Bobby Slowik

 Playcaller: Bobby Slowik

 What has gone right? The Dolphins entered this season vowing to run the ball and they've done so successfully -- remarkably, even without starter De'Von Achane , who tore his left ACL in September. Second-year back Ollie Gordon II  has filled in nicely for Achane, at one point scoring a rushing touchdown in four straight games. Miami's offensive line has been physical at the line of scrimmage and leads the league in average rushing yards before first contact per rush attempt.

 What has gone wrong? Miami has largely struggled to move the ball consistently through the air, averaging the third-fewest passing yards per game in the NFL this season. Third-round rookie Caleb Douglas looks like a definite starting receiver, but the Dolphins are still looking for consistent production from the rest of the room. Some of that also falls on quarterback Malik Willis , who will be on injured reserve until at least Week 14 with a groin/core injury.

 Key to second half: Continue to get receivers Douglas, Chris Bell and Kevin Coleman Jr . involved in the passing game. Their development will be worth keeping an eye on with Willis sidelined and second-year quarterback Kyle McCord starting in his place. With the playoffs out of the picture, the Dolphins' focal point should center on their three rookie receivers and continuing to sharpen their run game.  -- Marcel Louis-Jacques 

 

 
 

 New England Patriots 
 Offensive coordinator: Josh McDaniels

 Playcaller: Josh McDaniels

 What has gone right? Explosive plays. They are among the league leaders in passing plays of 20 yards or more, and running plays of 20 yards or more. They've also received solid contributions from a young core of players who project to be a big part of their future -- OTs Will Campbell and Caleb Lomu , C Jared Wilson and TE Eli Raridon 

 What has gone wrong? Too many injuries. WR A.J. Brown sustained a high right ankle sprain in the third quarter of the season opener, which foreshadowed what was to come -- a run of injuries across the offense that has challenged finding continuity and consistency, and now includes Drake Maye . The Patriots are expected to use all eight of their return-from-IR designations and Maye might be done for the season.

 Key to second half: Supporting QB  Tommy DeVito . He is being thrust into the starting role and that means everyone else needs to raise their level of play to lift him up. The return of starting left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker and No. 2 receiver Romeo Doubs should also help.  -- Mike Reiss 

 

 
 

 New York Jets 
 Offensive coordinator: Frank Reich

 Playcaller: Frank Reich

 What has gone right? The veteran Reich, in Year 1 with the Jets, has done a nice job of helping QB Geno Smith curb his turnovers. Smith, who had more interceptions (52) than any quarterback from 2022 to 2025, has reduced his picks to three. Smith is having the best statistical season of any Jets QB since Ryan Fitzpatrick in 2015. Reich, himself a former QB, deserves some credit for that.

 What has gone wrong? Reich has above-average talent, including gifted skill players in WR Garrett Wilson and RB Breece Hall , and yet the Jets are only 26th in points per game (19.4). The main reasons: poor red zone efficiency (31st), vanilla game plans, questionable halftime adjustments and inconsistency in getting the ball into the hands of their top players.

 Key to second half: The Jets can start off by scoring a touchdown; they've gone nine straight quarters without one, tied for the second-longest drought in the league this season. Reich needs to create an identity for the offense. They want to be physical and run-oriented, but they stray from that during games. Another key: Get Kenyon Sadiq more involved. The talented rookie tight end has been a nonfactor over the past seven games. -- Rich Cimini 

 

 

 AFC NORTH 
 

 Baltimore Ravens 
 Offensive coordinator: Declan Doyle

 Playcaller: Declan Doyle

 What has gone right? Getting RB  Derrick Henry in the end zone. The Ravens have failed to consistently run and throw the ball this season, but Henry continues to pile up touchdowns. By midseason, he recorded his ninth season of 10 or more touchdowns, which ties LaDainian Tomlinson for the most in NFL history.

 

 What has gone wrong? Injuries at quarterback. It has gotten so bad that the Ravens became the third team since 1950 to start four different quarterbacks in four weeks (excluding the 1987 strike season), according to the Elias Sports Bureau. Lamar Jackson is out until at least mid-to-late December after having surgery on his right thumb and Tyler Huntley is out for the season with turf toe. After one start with undrafted Joe Fagnano , Baltimore was in desperation mode when it traded for Jacoby Brissett .

 Key to second half: Getting the offense on track with Brissett. Entering Monday night's game, the Ravens had gone four straight games without scoring more than 14 points for the first time in team history. The Ravens have praised Brissett for his ability to drive the ball downfield. Since the start of the 2025 season, Brissett has thrown 33 touchdown passes, which is more than Justin Herbert (32), Baker Mayfield (29) and Jackson (27).  -- Jamison Hensley 

 

 
 

 Cincinnati Bengals 
 Offensive coordinator: Dan Pitcher

title: Can Ravens keep the Marlon Humphrey controversy from becoming a distraction?
summary: While there's more to the cornerback's story, one Baltimore teammate says: "We have enough things to worry about."
full_text:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Three days before a pivotal game in their season, the Ravens learned cornerback Marlon Humphrey was being benched for a week after his derogatory comment about the city of Baltimore on his podcast. 
 
 Will the Humphrey controversy become a distraction for a team that so desperately needs a win? 
 
 "No, I don't think so," Ravens offensive tackle Ronnie Stanley said. "I think everyone's focused on getting the win. We have enough things to worry about. It's something that came up one day, and we talked about it, but today, no one's talking about it." 
 
 The Ravens (4-6) have lost five straight games, including Monday's loss to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers . Ravens coach Jesse Minter told his players that they have a two-game stretch before the bye -- at the Panthers on Sunday ( 1 p.m. ET, Fox ) and at the Houston Texans on Nov. 29 -- to "stay alive." 
 
 
 Then, on his podcast Wednesday, Humphrey quipped that Baltimore is "best at making criminals." He later apologized for his remarks , but the situation gained more attention when Baltimore mayor Brandon Scott issued a statement that took a shot at Humphrey. 
 
 On Thursday, Minter announced that Humphrey would be inactive for Sunday's game and not practice the rest of the week. 
 
 How much has Humphrey been talked about in the locker room? 
 
 "Well, I mean, enough," defensive end Calais Campbell said. "At the end of the day, we're trying to win a football game. So, you try to keep the main thing the main thing, and obviously, the circumstances are what they are. So, it was discussed, but then you get the right mindset." 
 
 Humphrey, 30, has been named to four Pro Bowls, which are the most by a Ravens cornerback. But he will likely be remembered as a distraction himself. 
 
 Before home games, he doesn't get introduced with the defensive starters because he has a different pregame routine where he enters from another tunnel. Last month, Humphrey created a stir when he rode in the same car as President Trump - who has been publicly critical of Baltimore - on his visit to the city. 
 
 And, last month, Humphrey said on his podcast that safety Kyle Hamilton called his shot that he would make an interception in overtime when he saw struggling quarterback Tua Tagovailoa enter the game. This story, which came across as disrespectful to Tagovailoa, was later refuted by Hamilton . 
 
 Three players this week described Humphrey as "unapologetic." 
 
 "Marlon is a unique personality," Campbell said. "But he's a teammate that I've enjoyed playing with for my four years I've been teammates with him, and I know he's competitive and he's going to compete, and we're going to miss him out there this week."  
 
 
 Humphrey's performance has declined over the past two years. Since the start of the 2025 season, Humphrey has allowed 1,158 yards in coverage, which are the second most in the NFL, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. 
 
 With Humphrey out Sunday, the Ravens will increase the playing time for Chidobe Awuzie and T.J. Tampa . 
 
 "I think a lot of his errors have been a product of technique and fundamentals, which is weird to say for a guy that's been at his stature for such a long time," Ravens defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver said. "But it's one of those things where you're constantly sharpening and making sure your tires are aligned as a player. It's very easy to get comfortable and start to let those things kind of, you just get like, you go by the wayside a little bit. 
 
 "When that happens, you give up plays like that. Particularly as you age, you're just not able to rely on your pure athleticism, maybe as you once did." 
 
 Even though Humphrey was gone from the team facility Thursday, his teammates still had to answer more questions about remarks than about the Panthers. 
 
 "I think Marlon is unapologetically himself, and he's always been like that since he's been here," Stanley said. "But, at the same time, I think he's taken a step back and realized the maturity that he needs to take to say things the right way."

title: Fantasy buzz: Stroud has Houston fans over the moon, Colts continue to crumble
summary: Adam Rank waxes nostalgic about Houston football and the reinvigorated C.J. Stroud.
full_text:
It feels fitting that the  Houston Texans  were wearing uniforms on Thursday night that paid homage to those great Oilers teams of the past, conjuring images of some of those great "Luv Ya Blue" quarterbacks of old. We're talking the Warren Moons, Steve McNairs and Kenny Stablers of the world.

 Yes, on the off chance that you know who Ken Stabler is, you might be shocked to find out he was once a member of a team called the Houston Oilers. Sure, I could have gone with Dan Pastorini, but I've been told before that I tend to lose you by going more obscure with the history.

 

 I only bring this up because this version of the Texans is a lot more fun than they have any right to be -- if you can call Thursday's game fun. Houston won in a blowout, which was a surprise to nobody except for me as I talked myself into thinking the  Indianapolis Colts  would keep it close because divisional games on Thursday night tend to be closer than people think. Of course, I also think Metallica was truly at its best during the Cliff Burton era, so what do I know? Again, obscure. Stopping now.

 The biggest takeaway from this very much not-so-close game?  C.J. Stroud . He was good again, finishing with three touchdowns in his fifth consecutive game with multiple TDs. Stroud is now a must-start quarterback every week, even in a game where many of you (and definitely not me) expected a blowout, he still racked up a ton of fantasy points. There is no quarterback I would start over him beyond the usual suspects. It's been a tremendous transformation for Stroud, who started the season as "extremely ordinary" and is now extraordinary .

 Here are a few more notes from Thursday night:

 
 My guy David Montgomery is back! It's not a moment too soon, with "Bye-mageddon" having arrived this week.  Nov. 20: 11 key fantasy football stats for Week 11 
 

 We're officially in Week 11 of the NFL season, and fantasy playoffs are right around the corner. In order to make the best lineup decisions to make sure managers are maximizing their rosters for that final playoff push, here's 11 of my favorite fantasy stats so far this season. 

 1.  Baltimore Ravens TE Mark Andrews had his best game of the season in his first game with Jacoby Brissett starting at QB. He turned eight targets into eight catches for 82 yards and 16.2 fantasy points, all of which were season highs. Brissett has thrown 14% of his passes to tight ends since 2022, much higher than the league-average rate of 11%. That number would be even higher if not for Trey McBride running such a high percentage of his routes from the slot. Brissett elevates tight ends and a fantasy resurgence could be underway for Andrews.

 2.  Jacksonville Jaguars WR Parker Washington leads the NFL in yards against man coverage (262) while Trevor Lawrence is fifth in the NFL in yards per attempt against man coverage (8.4). This week they get the  New York Giants , who play man at the fifth-highest rate in the NFL (32%), which sets up what could be another big week for the duo.

 3.  Seattle Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba currently has picked up 52% of his team's receiving yards. Not only is that the most in the Next Gen Stats era (since 2016), there has only been one other season where a player recorded over 40% of their teams receiving yards: Smith-Njigba in 2025, when he picked up 44%. If there was ever a season for a wide receiver to win MVP, JSN is having it.

 4. The "something's got to give" matchup of the week is Brock Purdy against the Minnesota Vikings defense. Minnesota blitzes a league-high 72% of the time (the next closest is 44%) and a QB hasn't scored more than 13 fantasy points against them since Week 1. Purdy leads the league in touchdowns (12), passer rating and yards per attempt against the blitz.

 

 5. Vikings WR Justin Jefferson saw 13 targets in his first game back with Kirk Cousins . That is the most targets he has had in any game since 2024's Week 16. He saw 11 of those targets against zone coverage, and this week he gets the San Francisco 49ers , who play zone at the second-highest rate in the NFL (87%).

 6. QB Cam Ward has thrown at least 39 times in each of the last two games, scoring 26.26 and 19.14 fantasy points. In fact, he has thrown multiple passing TDs in two straight games, something he did not do in any of the first seven games. He gets a chance to stay hot against the Dallas Cowboys defense, who are top four in passing TDs allowed and QB fantasy PPG.

 7.  Los Angeles Chargers RB Omarion Hampton has played on over 60% of snaps just twice this season, going for 115 and 105 rushing yards (respectively) with a touchdown in each. Hampton has an excellent chance to keep producing against the New York Jets , who have allowed the second-most rushing yards per game (116) and rush yards before contact per attempt (1.6) to RBs.

 8.  New Orleans Saints WR Jordyn Tyson saw elite usage in his first NFL game with no limitations. He saw 13 targets, which is good for a 38% target share and 50% air yard share. He split his time out wide (50%) and in the slot (45%). He has league-winner potential on the team that throws at the fifth-highest rate. He should be (at worst) a WR3 for fantasy.

 9.  Kansas City Chiefs WR Josh Downs only played on 10 snaps in his debut and he still saw five targets, catching four of them for 53 yards, a touchdown and 15.3 fantasy points -- his best fantasy performance of the season. All 10 came from the slot, where  Patrick Mahomes  throws 28% of his passes. There is a lot of fantasy potential here.

 10.  Buffalo Bills QB Josh Allen is currently on pace for 25 passing and 21 rushing touchdowns. That would be the first 20-20 season in NFL history. There have been two 20-15 seasons in NFL history: Allen (29 passing, 15 rushing TDs) and Jalen Hurts (23 passing, 15 rushing), both in 2023.

 11.  Cincinnati Bengals QB Joe Burrow is on pace for 5,279 passing yards and 51 touchdowns. The only QB to ever top those numbers in a season was Peyton Manning in 2013 (5,477 yards, 55 TDs).

 --  Michael F. Florio

title: Panthers aim to hold NFC South lead while Ravens look to keep playoffs hopes alive, end 5-game skid
summary: — The Carolina Panthers needed a walk-off 54-yard field goal from Ryan Fitzgerald to beat the New Orleans Saints 20-17 last Sunday and remain in first...
full_text:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- — The Carolina Panthers needed a walk-off 54-yard field goal from Ryan Fitzgerald to beat the New Orleans Saints 20-17 last Sunday and remain in first place in the NFC South.
Now the goal is finding a way to stay there.
The Baltimore Ravens (4-6), on the other hand, are simply looking to win a game when they travel to Charlotte, North Carolina, to face the Panthers (4-5) on Sunday.
The Ravens have lost five straight, including a 23-20 defeat to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers on Monday night after being bullied at the line of scrimmage . The loss leaves coach Jesse Minter's team on the verge of falling out of playoff contention in the much more competitive AFC North, where all three division foes have a 6-4 record or better.
The Panthers started the season relying on the strength of Bryce Young 's arm, but it was Chuba Hubbard who helped deliver the knockout blow against the Saints.
The Canadian-born running back ran for 92 yards and two touchdowns and caught five passes for 80 yards as Carolina overcame 17 penalties for 152 yards to snap a three-game losing streak.
“We didn’t play the perfect game,” Hubbard said of the Panthers, the NFL's most-penalized team . “Obviously, we won and it feels good, but there’s a lot of things we got to clean up. ... At at the end of the day, a win is a win.”
Wins have recently eluded the Ravens, who've struggled to find consistent quarterback play since the injury to Lamar Jackson .
Baltimore traded for veteran Jacoby Brissett and the passing game made strides against the Chargers.
But the running game, which has long been Baltimore's bread and butter, can't seem to get on track. Derrick Henry has failed to eclipse 60 yards rushing in his past five games, and was limited to 10 yards on 10 carries by the Chargers, although he did score twice.
Minter called the team's struggles in the run game “unacceptable.”
“There’s to me just a combination of a lot of factors that we need to figure out how to be able to run the football,” Minter said. “There’s been spurts of it, but the last few games, it’s obviously not where it needs to be. It starts with me, starts with the coaches, goes down to the players."
The Panthers have been one of the league's worst run defenses this season, but have shown signs of improvement the past two weeks under interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash.
Carolina held the Denver Broncos and Saints to a combined 131 yards on 50 carries, a 2.62-yard average per carry.
Baltimore (4-6) at Carolina (4-5).
When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m., EST, FOX.
Latest odds: Panthers by 2 1/2.
Against the spread: Ravens 2-8, Panthers 4-5.
Last week: Ravens lost to Chargers 23-20; Panthers beat Saints 20-17.
Last meeting: Ravens beat the Panthers 13-3 on Nov. 20, 2022 in Baltimore.
Series record: Panthers lead 4-3.
Ravens WR Zay Flowers vs. Panthers CB Mike Jackson . Flowers is sure to be plenty motivated after a costly late fourth-quarter fumble against the Chargers prevented the Ravens from having a chance to tie the game and send it into overtime. Jackson returns from a six-game absence with a groin injury, giving the Panthers some much-needed experience in the secondary. He led the NFL in pass breakups last season with 19.
— Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey was deactivated this week and will not play Sunday after derogatory comments he made about the city of Baltimore on his podcast. Humphrey had said the city was “best at making criminals.”
— The Ravens have failed to score more than 20 points in their past five games.
— Brissett finished 33 of 49 for 340 yards against the Chargers with no touchdowns and one interception.
— TE Mark Andrews had a season-high 82 yards receiving on eight catches against the Chargers with Brissett at the helm.
— If the Ravens lose, it will be their longest losing streak since the end of the 2021 season.
— Hubbard needs 42 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown on Sunday to match Christian McCaffrey as the only players in franchise history with 1,000 yards from scrimmage and 10 touchdowns in the first 10 games of the season.
— The Panthers are expecting three players back from injuries this week.
— The Panthers are 4-1 all time in overtime games under head coach Dave Canales .
— WR Jalen Coker failed to catch a pass last week against the Saints and has just seven catches on 18 targets for 74 yards and one touchdown reception over the past four games. That's a huge drop-off in production from the first four games when he was targeted 35 times and caught 24 passes for 319 yards and two touchdowns.
— Panthers OLB Jaelan Phillips earned NFC Defensive Player of the Week honors after having five tackles, one sack, two quarterback hurries, and a fumble recovery against the Saints.
— Carolina is 22-13 in one-score games since Canales took over in 2024.
