title: Bills get chance to feast on another backup QB with Kyle McCord and Miami Dolphins up next
summary: — Ed Oliver bristled at the notion of the Bills’ defensive turnaround being the result of Buffalo spending the past three weeks feasting on backup...
full_text:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- — Ed Oliver bristled at the notion of the Bills’ defensive turnaround being the result of Buffalo spending the past three weeks feasting on backup quarterbacks — and another on deck with Miami hitting town on Sunday.
“Who cares. I mean, if I got to choose who I could play I guess it would be a starter. But you don’t get to choose,” the defensive tackle said. “All we get to choose is to take advantage of our opportunities.”
The AFC-leading Bills (8-1) have certainly done that over a three-game stretch in which they’ve allowed one touchdown and a combined 28 points. That’s a marked improvement for a defense that allowed 28.5 points per outing through its first six games.
A contributing factor could well be the level of competition, with Buffalo having faced the likes of Baltimore’s Tyler Huntley and Joe Fagnano , Minnesota’s Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer , and New York Jets rookie Cade Klubnik , who took over after Geno Smith was sidelined in Buffalo’s 31-12 win last weekend .
And now come the Dolphins (1-8), with Kyle McCord set to make his second career start in place of Malik Willis .
Bills coach Joe Brady declined to speculate on the injury-filled state of the AFC East's quarterbacks that also includes New England's Drake Maye — so long as Josh Allen is not among them.
A healthy Allen, the NFL’s active leader among QBs with 131 consecutive starts, is why the Bills are once again Super Bowl contenders. And Allen isn’t looking any further beyond Sunday, even with a Thanksgiving night showdown looming against Kansas City.
“This isn’t just a cakewalk. It’s a team that’s hungry. They’re looking to upset,” he said. “And the way their defense is playing gives them a shot every game they’re in.”
The rebuilding Dolphins have improved since dropping their first three games by a combined score of 86-36.
Four of their past five losses have been one-score outings, and in a 19-9 loss to Detroit two weeks ago, they limited the NFL’s third-ranked offense to a season-low 270-yards.
Injuries are an issue, with Miami losing its top three defensive linemen over a two-week stretch.
For rookie coach Jeff Hafley, the injuries represent the next challenge for a team that’s faced plenty of growing pains already.
“It doesn’t mean that you’re not sad and disappointed, but you have to move on and you can’t look back,” Hafley said.
With 39 players with three or fewer seasons of experience, Dolphins rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez is part of a youth movement that has few ties to Miami’s past struggles against Buffalo. Including playoffs, the Bills have won 14 of the past 16 meetings and 10 straight at home.
“Traditionally, we haven’t done very well playing up there. But we have to find a way to change that,” Rodriguez said.
Miami (1-8) at Buffalo (8-1).
When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EST, CBS.
Latest odds: Bills by 16 1/2
Against the spread: Dolphins 5-4; Bills 7-2.
Last week: Dolphins lost to Colts 24-22; Bills beat Jets 31-12.
Last meeting: Dolphins beat Bills 33-13 on Nov. 9, 2025, at Miami.
Series record: Dolphins lead 63-61-1.
Bills RB James Cook vs. Dolphins D. Cook is one game shy of becoming the NFL’s second player to score a TD and top 75 yards rushing in nine straight outings. Washington’s Terry Allen leads the list with a 10-game streak spanning the 1995-96 seasons. And Cook faces a depleted Dolphins front that allowed 172 yards rushing against the Colts.
— Buffalo’s 10 straight home wins against Miami is the longest against any opponent in team history. Buffalo hasn’t lost to Miami at home since a 34-31 overtime decision on Dec. 24, 2016, in what became Rex Ryan’s last game as Bills coach.
— The Bills have a chance to open 9-1 or better for just the fifth time in team history, and first since a 10-1 start in 1991.
— Allen’s 14 wins and 45 TDs passing against Miami are the most against any opponent in his nine-year career.
— Allen is one rushing TD from the 100th of his career, including playoffs. Only five players, all running backs, have scored that many through their first nine seasons.
— Buffalo has not trailed over the span of 217 minutes and 13 seconds, going back to the second quarter of a 33-30 win at Las Vegas on Oct. 25.
— The Dolphins are off to their worst start since going 0-13 to open 2007.
— McCord’s 209 yards passing against Indianapolis were the second most by a player in his Dolphins’ debut.
— Miami has allowed just three TDs rushing in its past six outings, and seven overall.
— The Dolphins have seven interceptions, with six by rookies, led by safety Michael Taaffe’s three.

title: Whether it's against backup QBs or not, the Bills' defense is rolling
summary: Buffalo will face another backup QB in Week 11 with Kyle McCord set to start in place of Malik Willis for the Dolphins.
full_text:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- The Buffalo Bills are executing something about as close to a midseason worst-to-first transformation as you'll ever see, albeit with a massive caveat.

 Less than one month ago, the Bills trudged through their bye week with the NFL's 30th-ranked scoring defense and 31st-ranked total defense. So naturally in the weeks since, the Bills have allowed the fewest points and second fewest yards among the teams that have played three games.

 It's been a steep turnaround for a Bills defense that's gone from the unit holding back the highest-scoring offense to a strength in its own right. But that turnaround has also coincided with the Bills playing almost exclusively against backup quarterbacks, a trend that'll continue when the Bills (8-1) host the Miami Dolphins (1-8) at Highmark Stadium on Sunday ( 1 p.m. ET, CBS ).

 So, as obvious as the answer might seem, it's worth asking the question: Is the game really that different when you're facing an NFL backup quarterback rather than a starter?

 

 "It's definitely not the starters," Bills safety Amani Hooker told ESPN. "Nothing's easy. But it's just like anything else. The better talented guy is off the field in any position, it's not good for their team. I'm sure they feel the same way."

 "I don't get to choose who I play. I just play," defensive lineman Ed Oliver adds. "Hell, who cares? If I got to choose who I could play, s---. I guess it would be a starter. But you don't get to choose. That's kind of how football works. People get hurt. Next man up."

 Ask Bills players and coaches alike and they'll say there's real belief the defense is executing better regardless of the opposing quarterbacks. Defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard points to how the defense is steadily getting better at holding strong on second- and third-and-long.

 Communication has improved in the secondary. Turnovers are up. Sacks are up. Third-down conversion rates are down. The defense is playing better in just about every way.

 But again, it's tough to separate those improvements from the circumstances. Before the bye, the Bills played games against the likes of C.J. Stroud , Jared Goff , Drake Maye and Matthew Stafford .

 Since, it's been games against rookie  Joe Fagnano  (after Lamar Jackson was injured on the Ravens' first offensive play and backup Tyler Huntley went out early in the second quarter) and Carson Wentz -- two quarterbacks who've since been replaced by trade acquisitions. Then it was rookie  Cade Klubnik  (for about half of the game with  Geno Smith  going out) making his NFL debut, with  Kyle McCord , who also made his debut last week, up next.

 "Just like anything in this profession, you can make a reason or an excuse and try to point to, well, we're only having success because of this," Bills coach Joe Brady says. "Our job is to go out there and play to our capabilities and to our standard, regardless of who's on the other side of the football.

 "I think [our defense is] playing at a high level right now and they have a lot of trust in one another and the communication is at a high level. That's correlating to the success regardless of who's on the other side of the ball."

 

 In a situation like this one where it's so tough to separate the chicken from the egg, it's helpful to look to an outsider. That's where Hooker comes in. Barely a week into his Bills tenure following his Nov. 10 trade from the  Tennessee Titans , Hooker says he didn't have the luxury of time to diagnose what's working and not working for the Bills' defense before being thrust into the starting lineup. He's heard a couple of stray coaching points about areas where the team had been struggling.

 Otherwise, anything he has observed has come from the perspective of an eight-year veteran figuring things out in real time.

 "It really just [feels like] no matter what's going on we always feel like we're in the game," Hooker said. "There's really no panic, which I'm not used to. In Tennessee, it's 'The defense has to win the game' in order for us to win. That was the feel. Here, it's really just no panic. We've got Josh Allen on the other side. We just do our job and communicate, tackle, no big plays, we probably have a good chance of winning."

 That, fundamentally, is the one thing that hasn't changed pre-bye to post-bye. The Bills have the best record in the AFC to go along with the second-best strength of victory in the AFC. They were beating good quarterbacks despite the defense's struggles in September and October, and they've been beating bad quarterbacks with good defensive play in November.

 "Fortunately or unfortunately, we've injured some quarterbacks in the [last three weeks] to where things have changed really fast within the game," Leonhard says. "To me, put on the tape, and are our guys executing? Is it clean football? Is it physical football? Are we stopping the run? Are we forcing teams into advantageous situations for us? I think we've been doing that."

title: NFL offseason free agent and trade acquisitions that have and have not worked
summary: Kenneth Walker III and Devin Lloyd look great with their new teams in 2026. But Jaylen Waddle and Alontae Taylor haven't quite found their groove.
full_text:
Everyone loves the NFL offseason hot stove. Fans get super excited about outside players joining their favorite team, whether through trade or free agency. Those holes on the roster have finally been filled by wily veterans!

 Unfortunately, those moves don't always work out. Some players excel in new surroundings, bringing strong production. Others struggle with their new situation, confirming why they were made available in the first place.

 Here's a look at five players who are working well with their new teams and five who are not. How are the successful new players helping their teams? Which teams find themselves on the hook for bad contracts? Let's start with a quarterback who has helped two teams this season.

 

 Jump to a section: 
 Moves that have worked out 
 Moves that have not yet worked out 

 

 Five players who are working 
 

 Kirk Cousins , QB, Raiders / Vikings 
 How he got there: Signed a one-year, $11.3 million contract with the Raiders before being traded to the Vikings on Nov. 10 
 2026 stat to know: 65.0 QBR (10th out of 31 qualifying QBs) 
 Comparable 2025 stat: 47.6 QBR (not enough passes to qualify)

 This is a bit of a special case, because Cousins is thriving in his second new city of the season. Or perhaps we should say one new and one old city, because Cousins played for Minnesota from 2018 to 2023.

 

 His performance this season is further proof that it takes a long time to recover from an Achilles tear. Cousins tore his Achilles in 2023 on the last play of his previous stint with the Vikings. He went to Atlanta in 2024 and was completely immobile on plays such as rollouts and play-action fakes. He put up a career-low QBR of 47.0 and lost the starting job to then-rookie Michael Penix Jr . toward the end of the season. In 2025, Cousins came in after Penix was hurt and looked a bit better. He was able to avoid turnovers, but his yards per attempt average dropped from 7.7 in 2024 to 6.4. It resulted in his QBR virtually being the same as it was the previous season.

 But Cousins is back to being his old self this season. His yards per attempt is up to 7.4, and his 22 passing touchdowns rank second in the NFL. His sack rate of 3.9% is also the lowest of any starting quarterback.

 The Raiders were able to get four wins out of Cousins (one more than they earned all last season) until they were ready to transition to rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza . Then they got an additional third-round pick by trading Cousins to Minnesota. Cousins won his first start with the Vikings in Week 10 and dramatically improved their chances of winning the Super Bowl by taking Minnesota's offense from horrific to slightly above average.

 
 

 Kenneth Walker III , RB, Chiefs 
 How he got there: Signed a three-year, $43.1 million contract 
 2026 stat to know: 1.66 rushing yards over expected per attempt (second out of 45 qualifying RBs) 
 Comparable 2025 stat: 0.25 RYOE/attempt (30th out of 51 qualifying RBs)

 Do running backs matter? Well, special running backs are only special when they get enough blocking to do great things. Last season, the Chiefs had the blocking but didn't have a back who could fully take advantage. This season, they have two in Walker and rookie Emmett Johnson .

 Walker has always been good at breaking tackles, but he's in another universe this season. According to FTN charting , Walker leads the league with a 35.2% avoided tackle rate and is third with 3.14 yards after contact per carry.

 The biggest question about Walker in Kansas City was whether he could handle the workload of a clear No. 1 running back after being in a committee in Seattle. Although Walker missed last week with a groin injury , he's on pace for 318 carries, which would easily exceed his previous career high of 228 set as a rookie in 2022.

 

 
 

 Mike Evans , WR, 49ers 
 How he got there: Signed a three-year, $42.4 million contract 
 2026 stats to know: minus-12.2% DVOA (63rd out of 79 qualifying WRs), 10.8 yards per target 
 Comparable 2025 stats: 45.1% DVOA (first out of 58 qualifying WRs), 6.0 yards per target

 Evans had a difficult final season in Tampa Bay. Oft-injured QB Baker Mayfield had a hard time getting Evans the ball in places where the receiver could excel. He hit career lows in yards per reception (12.3) and catch rate (48%). Last year was the first season of his career in which he failed to reach 1,000 receiving yards.

 Evans has been refreshed and renewed in San Francisco's powerful offense. His catch rate is up to 69%, which would be the highest of his career. He's also averaging 15.6 yards per reception. He had 23 first downs on 62 targets in 2025; this season, he's up to 25 first downs on only 39 targets so far.

 The only problem is the Achilles tendinitis that has sidelined Evans since Week 6. The 49ers are being very careful so they can have Evans back and 100 percent for their playoff run. They are hoping he can return in the next couple of weeks and continue to demonstrate why he was such a good signing.

 
 

 Quincy Williams , LB, Browns 
 How he got there: Signed a two-year, $13 million contract (up to $17 million with bonuses) 
 2026 stat to know: Tied for lead among LBs with 20 defeats 
 Comparable 2025 stat: 15 defeats in 13 games

 Williams was a first-team All-Pro for the Jets in 2023 but is still not as well known as his younger brother, Cowboys defensive tackle Quinnen Williams . Quincy had only 12 starts for the Jets last season and turned 30 in August, so it was reasonable to assume that he was at the tail end of his career.

 

 The Browns brought him in on a reasonable contract and stuck him next to Defensive Rookie of the Year Carson Schwesinger , and Williams has been an outstanding playmaker in that role. I keep track of a stat called defeats, which measures defensive splash plays. It combines tackles for loss, turnovers and any play that prevents a third- or fourth-down conversion. Williams has 20 defeats so far this season, tied with the Vikings' Blake Cashman for the lead among all linebackers. (Quinnen leads all players with 24.)

 Williams is known for speed and has been excellent in pass coverage, with four passes defensed and 15 pass tackles, which prevented a successful yardage gain despite a reception. Opposing running backs have fewer than 20 receiving yards per game against the Browns.

 
 

 Devin Lloyd , LB, Panthers 
 How he got there: Signed a three-year, $42 million contract 
 2026 stats to know: 16 defeats, three interceptions, average run tackle at 3.3 yards 
 Comparable 2025 stats: 14 defeats, five interceptions, average run tackle at 4.0 yards

 Unlike Williams, Lloyd entered the 2026 season with big expectations. He was one of the NFL's top linebackers last season and signed the largest contract of any free agent off-ball linebacker this past offseason. So far, Lloyd has lived up to that contract.

 Entering the season, it was hard to imagine Lloyd getting five interceptions again, but his Week 10 interception already puts him at three. Lloyd already has more defeats than he did last season, too, and he was part of two combined tackles to prevent Saints running back Audric Estime from converting on third-and-short last week. With the NFC South still up for grabs, the Panthers are counting on more big plays from Lloyd to get them back into the postseason.

 

 

 Five players who are not working 
 

 Jaylen Waddle , WR, Broncos 
 How he got there: Acquired from the Dolphins along with a 2026 fourth-round pick for 2026 first-, third- and fourth-round picks 
 2026 stat to know: minus-17.6% receiving DVOA (52nd out of 58 qualifying WRs) 
 Comparable 2025 stat: 11.6% receiving DVOA (19th out of 79 qualifying WRs)

 Trading for Waddle was supposed to unlock the Broncos' intermediate passing game and help Bo Nix  complete passes over the middle. Instead, Waddle has been victim of Nix's struggles. Right now, Nix ranks 26th in DVOA  on passes over the middle and 28th on…

title: Week 11 betting preview: Analysis, best bets, TD predictions for Sunday
summary: Our experts dive into the odds and player props for Week 11 and offer their betting tips and favorite plays.
full_text:
Week 11 of the NFL season features several games where the spread would indicate a mismatch, but this league is full of surprises. 

 Eight remaining games have teams that are favored by at least six points, and four of them are double-digit favorites. What will that mean for game bets and prop plays? We've looked at it all in hopes of trying to find the best values.

 Ben Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Seth Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Matt Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. Also included are fantasy projection creator Mike Clay's top predicted anytime TD scorers.

 Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. Let's get into it.

 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change. 

 

 Jump to: 
 Solak's plays | Bowen's bets  | Walder's props 
 Clay's TD projections 

 

 Solak's plays 

 

 Tampa Bay Buccaneers +6 (-110) at Detroit Lions 

 It's a good spot here for the Buccaneers, who are coming off of their bye week and are one of the healthiest teams in football. It sounds like quarterback Baker Mayfield will go, but safety Antoine Winfield Jr . (ankle) isn't ready to return to action. Meanwhile, the Lions are coming off a trip to Munich and will be without star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson on a defense that was already absent one key star in Jack Campbell . Center Cade Mays also looks like he's out for this one, and though safety Kerby Joseph might make his long-awaited return, I'm not sure how effective he'll be.

 

 I like this matchup for the Buccaneers' defense. Tampa Bay is elite against the run, and stopping Jahmyr Gibbs is the first priority when facing Detroit. Todd Bowles has also historically had success against Jared Goff . In four games against Bowles' Buccaneers over the last three seasons, Goff averages 0.08 EPA per dropback and an adjusted net yards per attempt of only 6.1. For perspective, Goff is at 0.21 EPA per dropback and 7.6 adjusted net yards per attempt for the season. The Buccaneers have the big defensive line necessary to handle this Lions front and the blitz-heavy approach to disrupt Goff in the pocket.

 I expect a low-scoring game that the Bucs try to control with their own rushing attack. This one ends on a field goal attempt.

 Minnesota Vikings +3.5 (-118) at San Francisco 49ers 

 Happy to get the hook here on a Vikings team that might be the best team in football, so long as their quarterback is not actively limiting the offense. Minnesota's defense is so exotic that it's almost worth throwing stats out the window. Brock Purdy is the league's best quarterback against the blitz by expected points and yards per attempt, but what does that really mean against a defense like Minnesota's, which blitzes in unique ways on totally different downs than all other defenses?

 

 The high-flying 49ers offense has struggled with Brian Flores' unit a couple of times -- Minnesota won 22-17 in 2023 against a 5-1 49ers team and again in 2024 in Week 2 by a final score of 23-17. Purdy is accustomed to making quick escapes against lumbering defensive linemen; the blitzers Minnesota sends tend to be better at getting him down. And because Purdy throws with so much anticipation, he's liable for a bad pick against Flores' group as well. He has taken seven sacks and thrown three picks over two games against Minnesota's defense.

 If Purdy successfully avoids those big negatives -- which I believe he can -- it's likely because the 49ers have taken a run-heavy approach on offense with a healthy smattering of quick passes. I'm not expecting huge points from San Francisco's side, while the Vikings have the potential for big offensive outputs with Kirk Cousins under center. Remember, Cousins just faced this defense a few weeks ago with the Las Vegas Raiders , and now he gets to port over all his takeaways into an entirely new offense. That feels like a big edge here.

 

 Jahmyr Gibbs rushing yards UNDER 87.5 (-111) 

 Hello, it's me, the idiot, taking a Gibbs under.

 The Buccaneers are the best run defense in football. They're allowing 3.6 yards per carry to opposing running backs and a league-low 65.9 yards per game overall. And the Buccaneers' run-heavy approach on offense should help them limit the number of possessions the Lions get.

 Given the shakiness of the Buccaneers' linebackers in coverage, I think we see a bigger day for Gibbs through the air and a quieter day on the ground.

 Ashton Jeanty receiving yards OVER 29.5 (-105) 

 Receiving backs against the Denver Broncos tend to be a good bet, as Denver's heavy dose of man coverage gives dangerous receivers out of the backfield big opportunities in space. The Raiders definitely fit into this category, as Tre Tucker , Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech are not a sufficient enough receiver room to test the Broncos' corners in coverage. Volume in the passing game will be funneled to Brock Bowers , of course, but after him, Jeanty, against linebackers Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad , is the best matchup option the Raiders have.

 Running backs are averaging 1.40 yards per route run against the Broncos this season, the seventh-highest rate among all defenses (their 8.8 yards per reception is also seventh). Jeanty saw only four targets in Fernando Mendoza 's first start, which is tied for his season low in a game. I imagine the Raiders will make a priority of getting the ball to the checkdown more frequently in Mendoza's second start, especially given the negative matchup for the wideouts in this one.

 
 Check out the latest Super Bowl odds and major NFL awards futures . 

 

 Parker Washington receptions OVER 4.5 (-101) 

 Since Brian Burns went down with a torn right ACL in Week 3, the New York Giants have the second-highest blitz rate in football (47%). That's good news for Washington, who sees a 35% target rate against the blitz this season, relative to a 26% target rate on non-blitzed dropbacks. And on the season, the Giants run the fifth-highest rate of man coverage. More good news for Washington: He has a 38% target rate against man coverage and a 20% target rate against zone coverage.

 In this particular matchup, Washington will be the primary wide receiver option for quarterback Trevor Lawrence , as he lines up most frequently in the slot. Outside cornerbacks Greg Newsome II and Deonte Banks have been a wonderful duo for the Giants, but slot corner Dru Phillips is gettable in space. I waffle on receptions and receiving yards here, as the Lawrence-Washington connections tend to be further down the field, but I think receptions is the safer play.

 Chimere Dike receiving yards UNDER 28.5 (-115) 

 Dike has run 31 and 34 routes in the past two weeks, respectively, with Carnell Tate out with a shoulder injury. But Tate was back at practice Wednesday and Thursday (limited) and could take a huge bite into Dike's snap counts moving forward. Dike averaged only 3.1 routes per game in the seven weeks Tate was healthy.

 Wan'Dale Robinson  was just placed on injured reserve, but a majority of Robinson's routes were coming from the slot, and Dike's game of straight-line speed doesn't necessarily lend itself to the slot. Dike ran eight routes from the slot last week in Robinson's absence, and backup Xavier Restrepo ran another seven. With Tate back in the starting lineup, it's likely he'll bite into some of those snaps as well.

 Even if Dike gets a bigger route share than I'm anticipating, he went over this number only once in the two weeks in which he saw 30-plus routes. As a speed threat, he does more to stretch the field and draw coverage than draw really high-value targets. I'll buy the number now with the assumption Tate plays. And even if Tate doesn't go, I'll have some outs.

title: Bears' Jeffery Simmons says knee injury a non-issue, expects to play vs. Saints
summary: Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons said the knee injury that held him to limited participation in practice this week wouldn't keep him from playing Sunday against the Saints.
full_text:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- Chicago Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons dispelled concerns about his availability for Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints after a knee injury held him to limited participation in practice.
"Like 99 problems, but this ain't one," he said, referencing his No. 99 jersey and a popular T-shirt that Bears fans created when he was traded to Chicago. "I'll be out there Sunday."
Simmons' remarks came after he missed Tuesday's practice and showed up on the team's injury report as a limited participant on Wednesday (an estimation) and Thursday. He sported a brace on his left knee when he returned to the field Thursday.
"Things happen in this league. It's kind of like when I put the elbow brace on, there was a lot of questions," Simmons said, referring to his 2024 ulnar collateral ligament injury with the Titans. "But I feel fine, practiced today. Practice went great. I've been seeing a lot of things on Twitter about the '99 problems.' That won't be a problem this Sunday."
Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen said he does not believe Simmons' knee injury will impact his availability against the Saints.
"I don't anticipate any issues with him," Allen said.
The Bears sent their 2027 and 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fourth-rounder to Tennessee on Oct. 29 in exchange for the All-Pro defensive tackle. Chicago also received a 2028 fifth-round pick.
Simmons had an immediate impact on the Bears' defense upon his arrival. He logged 87% of defensive snaps in his debut at Seattle, where he tallied six tackles, two tackles for loss, a sack and a defended pass in Chicago's 34-17 win. He followed that performance with another four tackles (one TFL), one sack and a defended pass in the Bears' Week 9 win against the Buccaneers when he played 97% of defensive snaps.
The Bears have allowed 4.5 yards per play with Simmons on the field (in 110 snaps) compared with 11.4 yards per play when he's not in the game (10 snaps). In two games, Simmons has faced a double-team on a team-high 24 pass rushes.
"With him commanding that much attention, it opens up some one-on-one opportunities for some other guys and I think some other guys have benefited from that," Allen said. "I think that's a positive thing that we have. I think the more really good players you have that have the ability to win their matchup -- whether that's a matchup in coverage, a matchup in the run game, a matchup in the passing game -- winning these one-on-one matchups are big in our league.
"Obviously when we can get him in a one-on-one, it's a great thing for us and a lot of times the offense is going to give a lot of attention to him, and so some other guys are going to have to step up."
Bears general manager Ryan Poles described Simmons' addition as "a shot in the arm" for a defense that was forced to work around injury constraints along the defensive line to generate pressure on opposing quarterbacks.
Since Simmons' arrival in Week 8, the Bears' defense has recorded a blitz rate 20 percentage points lower across 69 dropbacks with the defensive tackle on the field, blitzing on 21.7% of those plays compared with 41.7% of the 230 dropbacks with him off the field, according to Next Gen Stats.
Simmons' off-field impact has been felt as strongly as his contributions in games. When asked Thursday whether the Bears' defense needed a leader like Simmons after seeing the response since his arrival, Allen agreed.
"Well, maybe to that extent, yeah," Allen said. "And yet, look, we've always had a group of guys that come in and work and do the things that they're being asked to do to perform at a certain level. I think he just accentuates that."
If Simmons records a sack against the Saints, he will tie the longest streak of his career at three games.
Coming off a Week 10 bye, Chicago is expecting the return of running back Kyle Monangai , who missed five games with turf toe and a thumb injury. Monangai has been a full participant in practice along with wide receiver Luther Burden III , who is out of the concussion protocol, and cornerback Malik Muhammad (toe).
Nickel corner Kyler Gordon is the only player on the 53-man roster who has not practiced this week as he recovers from an injury to his left shoulder sustained in Week 9. Coach Ben Johnson classified Gordon's injury as "day-to-day."

title: Commanders' defense preparing for high-flying Bengals offense
summary: — Washington Commanders coach Dan Quinn knows the challenge facing his defense for Monday night's game against the Cincinnati Bengals.
full_text:
ASHBURN, Va. -- — Washington Commanders coach Dan Quinn knows the challenge facing his defense for Monday night's game against the Cincinnati Bengals .
When asked on Thursday why Cincinnati quarterback Joe Burrow and the Bengals' offense has been so good this season against the blitz, Quinn chuckled.
“I feel like they’ve been good against everything right now,” Quinn said.
Washington's head coach certainly has reason to feel that way.
The Bengals are coming off a 38-18 drubbing of the Steelers and have scored at least 31 points in their past five games, and in six of their nine games this season. They currently rank third in the NFL in points per game (30.9).
Led by Burrow and the one-two punch at receiver of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins , the Bengals have proven to be one of the league's best teams once again on the back of its offense.
Burrow has a 74.7% completion rate, is second in the league in yards at 2,795 and first in touchdown passes at 27.
“He’s decisive,” Commanders safety Jeremy Reaves said. “He’s one of the guys that gets the ball out of his hands quick and trusts what he sees. At the same time, he’s also just going to give his guys a chance. He trusts those two really well. He trusts all those guys really well. He’s going to give those guys the opportunity, and when he does, we got to make the plays that we’re able to make. One of the quickest release points in the game.”
Burrow has relied on Chase and Higgins heavily so far this season, as they rank sixth and 11th in receptions, respectively, as well as fourth and sixth in yards.
“Those dudes can run anything on the route tree," Reaves said. "They can line up anywhere. They present a challenge to any coverage, two-high, single-high (safety). They do a great job. We just got to be at our best when our best is required. They’re going to give those guys opportunities. Those dudes are two superstars in this business, so they’re going to have opportunities and when we get chances to make plays, we just want to make them.”
After an important win over the Giants last week, the Commanders have their hands full against a Bengals team that is aiming for the top seed in the AFC.
“It's a difficult challenge,” Quinn said. “The running back ( Chase Brown ) has targets, tight end ( Mike Gesicki ) does down in the red zone. So, everybody’s got difficult downs, so you can’t double up everybody. But you do have to take your shots of where to go and how to go about that. We’ll have our ways, but definitely one of the biggest challenges with them is multiple people, and performing at a high level.”

title: With Titans, Eagles up next, it's now or never for Cowboys
summary: Thanks to the scuffling NFC East and a friendly schedule the next week, the Cowboys still have a playoff shot.
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- The fate of the Dallas Cowboys ' season will come into focus over the next two games.

 Beat the Tennessee Titans on Sunday ( 1 p.m. ET, Fox ) and the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving, and the Cowboys (4-6) will have a path forward to potentially winning the NFC East . Split the games, and they will need even more help from the division-leading  New York Giants  (5-3-1). Lose both and it could be time to ponder more changes to the coaching staff.

 The math might still work with either of the last two options, but it would strain credulity if the Cowboys are unable to beat the one-win Titans and the two-win Eagles -- with  ESPN's FPI  currently giving Dallas a 42.9% chance to reach the postseason.

 Coach Brian Schottenheimer acknowledged Wednesday, when confirming the news that senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine would take over playcalling duties from coordinator Christian Parker, that the season would be a failure if the Cowboys don't make the playoffs.

 

 He was asked, in extension of that comment, if the season is on the line in the next two games.

 "I think they're very important games," Schottenheimer said. "Yes, I do."

 It's not quite former Cowboys coach Jimmy Johnson's "We will win the game. Put it in 3-inch headlines" statement prior to the 1993 NFC Championship Game.

 It's not former Giants coach Jim Fassel with his team at 7-4 and having lost two straight, saying, "This is a poker game, and I'm shoving my chips to the middle of the table. I'm raising the ante. ... This team is going to the playoffs."

 It wasn't even Aaron Rodgers in 2016. The Green Bay Packers were 4-6 and the quarterback said they would "run the table" before they won their final six games to make the playoffs.

 But those teams had something of a track record and all three teams answered the challenge.

 These Cowboys are coming off a 7-9-1 finish last season under Schottenheimer and have been unable to win back-to-back games or beat a team with a winning record since last Thanksgiving.

 

 "You want to have the battle cry: 'There's a lot of football left to be played.' But there's less and less to be played as we move down the road toward Thanksgiving," executive vice president Stephen Jones said on 105.3 The Fan this week. "Certainly, when people say, 'Is it a must? Do you got to have it?' I don't go there unless it's mathematically, but we're making this hard on ourselves and we're digging a hole.

 "I think it starts with we've got to have the game against the Titans, we've got to have the game against the Eagles, and then our schedule gets real difficult, but you got to start somewhere."

 After this two-game run, the Cowboys' next three opponents are at the Seattle Seahawks  (6-4), at the Los Angeles Rams  (6-4) following their bye and home against the Jacksonville Jaguars  (7-2).

 The Seahawks are the defending Super Bowl champions and difficult to play at home. The Rams were considered a Super Bowl contender with their offseason moves and have a recent Super Bowl pedigree. The Jaguars are in contention for the top seed in the AFC.

 It has been a strange week around the Cowboys with the Pettine-for-Parker move in a season filled with inconsistencies across the board.

 While a good portion of the blame can go to a defense that ranks last in yards allowed and 30th in points allowed and has given up a league-high nine plays of 50-plus yards, there were significant offensive failures in the losses.

 Yet winning can help alleviate a tenseness brought about by not living up to external and internal expectations.

 

 Wide receiver CeeDee Lamb said there is an urgency now that the Cowboys are in this position with seven games to go.

 "I want to win. I don't see it going any other way," Lamb said. "So as for us, we just got to do what we got to do, and let's win as many games as we possibly can. Let's see how many we can win in a row."

 Hall of Fame coach Bill Parcells used to say a team's season does not come into focus until Thanksgiving. Win the next two games, get to 6-6 and the vision would be clearer. 

 Quarterback  Dak Prescott isn't taking a two-week view of the Cowboys' season.

 "For me, it's about 'let's win this game.' If we don't win this game, what the hell are we looking forward two weeks and to get to 6-6 and to get to .500 if we don't take care of our business now?" Prescott said. "Let's just focus on what's in our hands right now and do the absolute best job that we can do with that. And then we'll worry about what comes and what results come after that.

 "We just got to take care of this week."

title: Raiders rookie Fernando Mendoza to face another elite defense in the sack-hungry Broncos
summary: — Top draft pick Fernando Mendoza's first career road start comes against Denver's dominant defense, one week after he was sacked half a dozen times by the Seattle Seahawks in his
full_text:
DENVER -- — Top draft pick Fernando Mendoza 's first career road start comes against Denver's dominant defense , one week after he was sacked half a dozen times by the Seattle Seahawks in his NFL starting debut .
“I believe getting thrown in the fire is the best way to learn, and the Seahawks and the Broncos both have considerably elite defenses,” the Las Vegas rookie said as he prepared to lead the Raiders (4-6) against the host Broncos (7-2), who have won five straight.
Of course, Mendoza has high praise for everybody else, too.
“I really believe every NFL defense is elite because when you’re playing at this level, the margin for error is so small, and all the defensive coordinators are geniuses,” Mendoza said in his aw-shucks kind of way.
“So, I’m honored and blessed to go against a great defensive coordinator in coach Robbie (Rob Leonard) every single day, especially in OTAs and fall camp and training camp. So, I believe that’s helped prepare me, and now I’m excited to embark on this journey with my teammates.”
Vance Joseph's defense has an NFL-best 157 sacks over the last 2 1/2 seasons, and the Broncos are coming off a bye week, so they're healthier with starting safeties Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) and Brandon Jones (hamstring) both returning to practice this week along with cornerbacks Riley Moss (concussion) and Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle).
Broncos QB Bo Nix is making his 45th career start Sunday and he was asked this week to look back on his second career start, against Pittsburgh in 2024.
“It's night and day,” Nix said. “My second start wasn't what I'm doing now. It's hard for a rookie quarterback. I don't care if you're sitting behind a guy like Kirk (Cousins) who you can learn from. You still have to go out there and ultimately play and ultimately do it.
“And to his credit, he played a really good defense last week. He's going to play a really good one this week,” Nix added. “And it's just not easy and unfortunately the world's not going to give him any time to go through the obstacles that it takes as a rookie quarterback. But he'll continue to develop, he's a smart kid and he's played in big moments in college and I think that does translate.”
The Raiders' 21-13 loss to Seattle last week marked Mendoza's first loss as a starter since Nov. 16, 2024, when he was playing for California and Syracuse defeated the Golden Bears 33-25. Mendoza went undefeated last season in leading Indiana to the national championship and capturing the Heisman Trophy.

— Broncos coach Sean Payton can move into sole possession of 10th place on the career NFL victories list with a win Sunday. He's tied with Dan Reeves and Mike Tomlin with 201 wins, including the playoffs.
— The Raiders are the 11th team to be 4-6 or worse after opening a season 3-0. Of the other 10 teams, only the 2009 New York Jets made the playoffs.
— The Broncos have won an NFL-record 16 consecutive one-score games dating to last season. That's one more than the Peyton Manning-led Colts from 2008-09.
— Mendoza became the fourth No. 1 draft pick at quarterback to have a rushing touchdown but no TD passes in his first start. Joe Burrow , Matthew Stafford and Steve Bartkowski were the others.

title: Fantasy football last-minute pickups: Flournoy, Ayomanor among top candidates
summary: There is no busier bye week than this one. Matt Bowen lists potential options if you need a fill-in.
full_text:
With six teams on bye this week ( Atlanta Falcons , Cleveland Browns , Green Bay Packers , Los Angeles Rams , New England Patriots  and  Seattle Seahawks ), managers likely have some spots to fill in their lineups.

 If you need wide receivers, this is a good place for you, as I have six pass catchers (with varying levels of value) to pick from. Based on the matchups and player availability (focusing on those under 50% rostered), it's pretty lean at quarterback and running back, but there are still a couple of options. We'll wrap things up with the tight ends and a D/ST to stream.

 

 Wide receivers 

   Ryan Flournoy , Dallas Cowboys (36.5% rostered; vs. Titans) 

 In the Week 10 shootout loss to the 49ers, Flournoy had a season-high 19.1 points, catching six of seven targets for 91 yards and a score. Sure, game script impacted his totals, but Flournoy has at least 11 points in five of his past six games, with a touchdown reception in three of them. With a matchup against a Titans defense allowing 42.8 PPG to wide receivers (most in the league), Flournoy should be in lineups as a WR3.

   Adonai Mitchell , New York Jets (40.8% rostered; at Chargers) 

 

 Mitchell had a breakout game in Week 8 versus the Raiders, scoring 27.2 points, but he has caught only three of 15 targets over the past two games. However, there is opportunity for Mitchell this week as the No. 2 option opposite Garrett Wilson with Omar Cooper Jr . (ankle) questionable for Sunday. If Cooper sits, Mitchell gets a boost in volume and brings big-play upside versus a Chargers defense that allows the seventh-most fantasy points per game to wide receivers.

   Elic Ayomanor , Tennessee Titans (9.8% rostered; at Cowboys) 

 Ayomanor scored a season-high 12.9 points last week against the Jaguars, leading the team with 79 yards receiving while catching five of 10 targets. With Wan'Dale Robinson  done for the season, Ayomanor should be in line to see steady volume from quarterback Cam Ward , who has played his best football of the season during the past two games. And managers should be all over the matchup versus a Dallas defense that is allowing the sixth-most fantasy points per game to wide receivers.

   Caleb Douglas , Miami Dolphins (33.7% rostered; at Bills) 

 I wrote about Douglas last week in this spot as a deeper-league flier/big-play target and not much has changed. With backup quarterback Kyle McCord under center last week against the Colts, Douglas caught only three of eight targets, but he finished with 71 yards (10.1 points). Douglas has scored 10 or more points in three of his past four games. He's a WR3 option versus Buffalo on Sunday.

   Antonio Williams , Washington Commanders (19% rostered; vs. Bengals) 

 Williams saw just two targets in the Week 10 win over the Giants, but he caught both for 42 yards, with one going for a touchdown (12.2 points). Williams has posted double-digit points in two of his past three contests, catching 10 of 15 targets during that stretch. He matches up with the Bengals on Monday night, and there is value here if you need a good route runner in the lineup.

   Malachi Fields , New York Giants (8.8% rostered; vs. Jaguars) 

 I'll throw Fields in here as a bye week fill-in versus the Jaguars. He has at least three catches in each of the three games with J.J. McCarthy under center for the Giants. Fields is a 6-foot-4, 222-pound boundary target who can create explosive plays and is an upside play for deeper formats.

 

 Quarterbacks 
 

   Cam Ward, Tennessee Titans (23.8% rostered; at Cowboys) ]/p>

 

 It's a great matchup Sunday in Dallas for Ward, whose numbers have jumped the past two games. Ward scored a season-high 26.26 points versus the Bengals in Week 8 (before the bye) and followed that up with 19.14 points in the Week 10 loss to Jacksonville. Ward has thrown for multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games (for the first time this season), and his rushing totals are up (two straight games with 39 or more yards rushing). With six teams on a bye this week, Ward should be viewed as a top streaming option.

   Aaron Rodgers , Pittsburgh Steelers (37% rostered; at Eagles) 

 Rodgers' numbers have declined over his past four games (12.4 PPG), but he has thrown multiple touchdowns passes in two of them. Sunday, he'll face a Philly defense that is ninth worst in fantasy versus quarterbacks. Managers will need Rodgers to be throwing in red zone situations. He's a deeper league superflex option.

 

 Running backs 

   Kaelon Black , San Francisco 49ers (37.1% rostered; vs. Vikings) 

 I don't love the matchup versus the Vikings' defensive front, but it's hard to ignore the volume Black is seeing as the No. 2 behind Christian McCaffrey . Black has at least 11 carries in three straight games and 10 or more points (and a touchdown rush) in two. He's a downhill hammer with flex upside in deeper leagues.

   Justice Hill , Baltimore Ravens (18% rostered; at Panthers) 

 Hill will see limited rushing volume behind Derrick Henry , but he has value as a pass-catching flex option. Hill caught five passes from Jacoby Brissett in the Monday night loss to the Chargers, and he has at least three receptions in five straight games. He has a positive matchup Sunday versus the Panthers, who allow the third-most points to running backs.

 

 Tight ends

title: Lions moving on after Hutchinson joins Campbell on IR and they face Bucs aiming for 6th straight win
summary: — Dan Campbell does not want to let the Detroit Lions become miserable in the Motor City by lamenting the losses of All-Pro linebacker
full_text:
DETROIT -- — Dan Campbell does not want to let the Detroit Lions become miserable in the Motor City by lamenting the losses of All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell and two-time Pro Bowl edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson to season-ending injuries this month.
“I’m not going to do it. We’re not doing it,” Campbell said. “I refuse to look at it that way. Does it stink? It sure did in the moment. It’s time to move on. We have to.”
The Lions (7-2) host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) on Sunday, looking for their sixth straight win to at least remain in a tie with Minnesota and Chicago atop the highly competitive NFC North.
The Bucs, meanwhile, have lost twice as many games as they've won this season and are still favored to be division champions in the NFC South , which does not have a team with a winning record.
“We’re right there,” Tampa Bay coach Todd Bowles said.
Baker Mayfield has a banged-up foot and right thumb and his status was uncertain for the game at Ford Field.
“He's a lot better than he was a week ago,” Bowles said.
If the veteran quarterback can't play, undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will make his fourth start this season.
Even though the Lions and Bucs are not in the same division, they are playing for the fifth time — including a playoff game — in three-plus years.
“It feels like we play them every week," Bowles joked.
The Lions will have a short week to prepare for their next game, a matchup against the Bears on Thanksgiving. That game may prove to be very important for Detroit with three road games looming against NFC North teams over the last four weeks of the season.

title: C.J. Stroud stays in 'groove' with another 3-TD night in Texans' blowout of Colts
summary: C.J. Stroud had his third straight game with at least three touchdown passes and led the Texans to their fourth win in six games Thursday night against the Colts.
full_text:
HOUSTON -- C.J. Stroud continued his resurgent season Thursday night, tossing three touchdowns in the Houston Texans ' 26-3 win over the Indianapolis Colts .
Stroud had his third straight game with at least three touchdown passes, adding 194 passing yards and an interception to post a passer rating of 118.2. He has reached at least three passing touchdowns in four out of his past five games, totaling 16 touchdowns and four interceptions in that stretch.
"I knew what type of player I could be in this league," Stroud said. "And to just get in that groove and have a rhythm, it's been amazing. Honestly, I would be lying to you if I said it didn't feel good."
The Texans (4-6) have won four of their past six games as they look to become the second team in NFL history to reach the playoffs after an 0-4 start (1992 Chargers , then in San Diego). Houston has a 38% chance to make the playoffs after Thursday's win, according to ESPN Analytics, and will host the Baltimore Ravens next week.
A big reason for the Texans' recent bounce-back is because of Stroud's play, but he isn't taking all of the credit.
"I'm very grateful for this opportunity to even play in the NFL," Stroud said. "People probably think I'm crazy for always saying that, but, man, I really did not expect my life to be like this. It's nothing but the grace of God that I'm sitting up here and to be playing the way that I am.
"It's nothing but the credit to the team. Just the way the defense prepared us in training camp. The way the offensive line's been blocking their tail off giving me a shot. The way the receivers have been running routes, getting open."
Defensive Player of the Year contender Will Anderson Jr. , who had a sack for a safety and two tackles for loss, had the highest praise for Stroud, who he said has "continued to take that leap every year."
"He's a top quarterback in this league, no matter what his year may have looked like," Anderson said. "Trust me, it's 32 other teams that would love to have C.J. Stroud on their team. So, I'm just happy he's here."
Stroud got back on track after a shaky performance in a Week 10 loss to the Cleveland Browns . Even though he threw for three touchdowns, the offense struggled in the second half, totaling only seven points after jumping to a 17-0 first-half lead.
Through 10 games in his fourth season, Stroud is up to 2,656 passing yards, 22 touchdowns and only four interceptions with a 103.6 passer rating. He is on pace to throw for 4,515 passing yards and 37 touchdowns, both of which would be career highs.
Texans coach DeMeco Ryans attributed Stroud's success to his offseason work.
"All of that is paying dividends now from the work prior to these moments," Ryans said. "He's been ready for these moments, and he's executing at a high level in these moments, scoring the points that we need to score, making the plays we need to make. Just keeping the offense out there on the field, making great decisions with the football. That's probably the one thing I'm most proud of him making great decisions."

title: C.J. Stroud, defense star as Texans get critical win over Colts on TNF
summary: C.J. Stroud and a swarming defense helped Houston beat Indy on 'Thursday Night Football.'
full_text:
HOUSTON -- The game was competitive for only the first quarter. After the Houston Texans went up 14-3 in the second quarter, they cruised to a 26-3 win against the Indianapolis Colts on "Thursday Night Football."

 It was a complementary effort as Houston's offense scored 24 points, the defense notched a safety and special teams made plays, including a blocked field goal. It was the type of outing coach DeMeco Ryans had been yearning for all season.

 Winning this matchup was a nonnegotiable for the Texans, who improved to 4-6. They couldn't afford to lose another winnable game. Houston is fighting for its playoff life after losing last week to the Cleveland Browns in shocking fashion, blowing a 17-0 lead. But the Texans shook off the demoralizing loss and handled their business against Indianapolis.

 Here are the most important things to know for both teams:

 

 

 

 Houston Texans  (4-6) 

 What to make of the QB performance:   Quarterback C.J. Stroud got back on track after a shaky Week 10 loss against the Browns. Stroud looked in control outside of a couple of plays that resulted in an interception and a near interception. He finished the night with 194 yards and three touchdowns.

 This is Stroud's third straight game with at least three touchdowns. And he has notched at least three scores through the air in four of his past five games. The Week 12 game presents a great opportunity for Stroud to continue his hot streak as Houston faces a struggling Ravens squad.

 Trend to watch: Running back David Montgomery played how Houston hoped its major offseason acquisition would in his first game back since he hurt his groin in Week 4. Montgomery finished with 107 yards on 26 carries -- a season high for any Texans running back. Overall, the Texans' rushing attack finished with 167 yards, also a season high. If the Texans want any hopes of making a magical run to the playoffs, the ground game must assist them on an uphill journey.

 Stat to know: Texans cornerback Kamari Lassiter shined Thursday, catching an interception and allowing zero receptions on six targets, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Lassiter has been up and down in 2026, but against Indianapolis, he played like the Pro Bowl player he was in 2025.

 Next game: vs.  Baltimore Ravens (Nov. 29, at 1 p.m. ET)

 

 

 

 Indianapolis Colts  (3-8) 

 The Colts had one of their more embarrassing performances of the season as their offense failed to reach the end zone and their defense was victimized by repeated big plays in a division loss to Houston.

 The Colts have now lost 15 of their past 18 games dating back to November last season, when their 8-2 start devolved into a seven-game losing streak to end what began as a promising 2025 season.

 Now, injuries are mounting, with running back Seth McGowan sustaining a hamstring injury in the game; he did not return in the second half. Combined with the injuries to the offensive line and the secondary, the health of their starters is already hampering the Colts' chances at finishing above .500.

 What to make of the QB performance: Daniel Jones remained the Colts' starter despite his deep struggles in recent games, and his odds of success in this game were minimal, at most. The Colts were missing both starting offensive tackles and rejiggered their lineup to make things work against a Texans front featuring NFL sacks leader Will Anderson Jr . It went about as well as one would expect. Jones completed 12 of 27 passes for 144 yards, marking a seventh game in 11 starts with less than a 60% completion rate. It was also the first game this season in which the Colts did not score a touchdown.

 Key stat to know: Colts running back Jonathan Taylor had one of the roughest performances of his career Thursday. With a makeshift offensive line in front of him, and with the passing game experiencing its usual struggles, Taylor averaged 1.9 yards per carry, the second-lowest average of his career. This has not been a season to remember for Taylor, who entered the game on pace for more than 1,200 rushing yards but has seen his production slip of late.

 Trend to watch:  The Colts have given up 608 rushing yards in their past four games, averaging 151.8 yards in each of those contests. It is becoming a noticeable issue as the Jaguars, Cowboys and Texans all surpassed 150 rushing yards in their recent meetings with the Colts. The trend coincides with the trade of defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers last month, and that means there aren't any easy solutions with the personnel the Colts have left.

 Next game: vs. New York Giants (Nov. 29, at 1 p.m. ET)

title: C.J. Stroud throws for 3 TDs as the Texans roll past the Colts 26-3
summary: — C.J. Stroud had another big game to help the Houston Texans finally get a victory at home.
full_text:
HOUSTON -- — C.J. Stroud had another big game to help the Houston Texans finally get a victory at home.
Stroud threw for 194 yards and three touchdowns and the Texans used a strong defensive performance to coast to a 26-3 win over the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday night.
With the roof at Reliant Stadium open for the first time since 2024, the Texans won a home game for the first time this season after losing their first four.
“To have a home game win is very good for us and exciting,” Stroud said. “I think this is a start to something that we need to go on a run with.”
Stroud picked apart a Colts secondary that was missing injured starting cornerbacks Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward to help the Texans bounce back from a 27-24 loss to Cleveland last weekend.
It was the third straight game in which Stroud had at least three touchdown passes and the fourth in his last five.
“C.J. is producing the way he is producing because of the work he put in throughout the offseason,” coach DeMeco Ryans said. “All of that is paying dividends now. He’s been ready for these moments and he’s been executing at a high level in these moments.”
Stroud gave the Texans a 7-3 lead when he connected with Nico Collins for a 42-yard touchdown late in the first quarter.
Kamari Lassiter intercepted Daniel Jones on the first play of the second quarter. The Texans (4-6) then capped a 12-play, 85-yard drive with a 24-yard TD reception by Kayshon Boutte to extend their lead to 14-3.
The Texans were up by 14 early in the third when Will Anderson Jr . sacked Jones in the end zone for a safety that made it 19-3. Anderson leads the NFL with 11½ sacks and had two tackles for loss Thursday to move into first place with 17.
“Obviously, 51 (Anderson) is a problem,” Indianapolis coach Shane Steichen said. “We were trying to have a game plan for wherever he was. We were trying to see if he was going right or left. When he was playing right, he was going left. We were trying to keep it away from him as much as we possibly could.”
Stroud found rookie Marlin Klein for a 13-yard TD on the next possession.
Ryans was proud of his team for playing a complete game after the Texans fell apart last Sunday against the Browns, blowing a 17-0 lead.
“It’s fulfilling to finally see that happen,” he said. “We’ve been in these games a ton where we were up at halftime and come out in the second half and for whatever reason not finish. So for them to actually see it and go do it, I think it will bode well for them to gain confidence for showing that they can do it.”
Jones was 12 of 27 for 144 yards with the interception as the Colts (3-8) lost for the sixth time in seven games. Anthony Richardson took over with about seven minutes left and didn't complete either of his passes.
Steichen was asked if Jones will remain the starter.
“We’ll evaluate everything,” he said.
The Colts had their worst offensive performance of the season, finishing with a season-low 167 yards and just 38 yards rushing, which was also their fewest this season. They failed to score a touchdown for the first time since a 24-6 loss to Detroit on Nov. 24, 2024.
“I understand where we are as a team,” Jones said. “I understand it’s an issue to score three points. We have to be better offensively. I am the quarterback, and so, I am responsible. I have to play better. I know that. That’s the job.”
Houston’s David Montgomery had 26 carries for a season-high 107 yards in his return after missing four games with a groin injury.
The Colts led early after Spencer Shrader’s 34-yard field goal on the game’s first drive.
Stroud’s pass was tipped four times by three players before A.J. Haulcy intercepted it on Houston’s first possession. But the Colts couldn’t cash in when Shrader’s field goal attempt from 56 yards was wide left.
A 62-yard field goal attempt by Shrader was blocked by Logan Hall with about 2½ minutes left in the first half.
Houston DE Chris Braswell was carted off with a right knee injury after the opening kickoff. … Indianapolis RB Seth McGowan injured his hamstring in the second quarter and didn’t return.

Texans: Host Baltimore on Nov. 29.

title: How Bhayshul Tuten became the clear No. 1 running back for the Jaguars
summary: After a lackluster rookie season, Tuten ranks 14th in NFL in rushing yards entering Sunday's game against the Giants.
full_text:
JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- In the offseason, no one was completely sure if  Jacksonville Jaguars running back Bhayshul Tuten  could replace  Travis Etienne Jr . as the Jaguars' lead back. The team signed Chris Rodriguez Jr . (who played for coach Liam Coen at Kentucky) as a free agent to help with the loss of Etienne.

 Fast forward 10 weeks into the 2026 season, and nobody's doubting whether Tuten can carry the Jaguars' run game now.

 "We could see the glimpse of a true RB1, but he hasn't done it on that type of level yet for being that consistent for an entire year of being the guy" running backs coach Chad Morton said. "So we were unsure about what he's going to be able to handle and [if he could] just figure everything out and deal with the whole playbook and just the consistency. Can he block? Can he catch passes?

 "So that was always going to be a concern from him, but we knew that he had the ability to do it. It's just, can we bring him along enough to get him to that point?"

 

 He's there. Entering Sunday's game against the  New York Giants  (4:25 p.m. ET, CBS), Tuten leads the Jaguars with 609 rushing yards and has accounted for 64% of the running back carries. He's on pace for 1,150 yards, which would be 25 more than Etienne posted in any of his five seasons in Jacksonville. His 67.7 rushing yards per game ranks 12th in the NFL.

 Tuten has also established himself as one of the league's toughest running backs to bring down, ranking seventh in rushing yards after first contact (360) and sixth in yards per rush after first contact (2.43). 

 "I think the guy is probably mentally and physically tougher than I would've maybe imagined in ways," Jaguars coach Coen said. "I mean, I kind of knew it a little bit off the Virginia Tech tape because he's getting whacked in the backfield [and] he's getting extra yards.

 "It's not always perfect [in the run game]. You don't see him getting tackled for loss and throwing the ball on the ground and getting ticked off at people. He just kind of keeps staying the course and playing."

 Tuten rushed for 307 yards and five touchdowns as a rookie in 2025 and he hit double-digit carries only once (12). This season, Tuten has at least 12 carries in every game and already has five rushing touchdowns.

 His past three games show how much he has grown in his second season: He ran for a career-high 104 yards and a touchdown and caught two passes for 55 yards and a touchdown in a 42-7 victory over Indianapolis . He hurt his foot against the Colts and did not practice before the Jaguars' Thursday night game in Baltimore -- but he toughed it out and had 12 carries for 29 yards and a touchdown in a 33-10 victory . After practicing just once last week, Tuten had a career-high 29 touches against the Titans .

 "It means a lot," Tuten said of the staff trusting him to play even though he hadn't practiced. "It also comes with a lot of preparation. It's a lot of meetings, a lot of mental reps and just talking through a lot of stuff, a lot of film review, and watching a lot of things to make sure I'm out there and mentally 100%."

 That has been one of Tuten's biggest areas of growth, Morton said.

 

 "His ability to adjust, take in information and then being able to handle everything that we're giving him and then him being able to process it all and figure stuff out," Morton said. "It was a little bit harder when he's a rookie ... but now this is Year 2, he's way more detailed in how he prepares, how he studies, practice habits, and then just being able to regurgitate the information I'm giving him and then applying it on the field."

 The other area in which Tuten has gotten better, Morton said, is cutting way down on over-analyzing everything he sees on the field. He has done what Coen encouraged quarterback Trevor Lawrence to do last season: Cut it loose.

 "He sees everything," Morton said. "If the runs to the right, he knows exactly what's going on to the left. He sees things almost like in slow motion. ... But the problem with that is he would see it and I'm trying to narrow his focus because he saw so much and then we narrow his focus. You don't need to see everything -- just read your keys -- because then he'll over-anticipate stuff, and that's the times that he's missed things in the past."

 As Tuten prepares to take on the Giants -- who rank 26th in opponent yards per carry (4.5) but 13th in defensive rush success rate (59.7%) -- he's embracing the improvements to his game.

 "I'm definitely more comfortable," Tuten said. "Just being more comfortable and composed during the game, I think is the biggest [improvement] so far."

title: Jaguars visit the Giants in a matchup of two unexpected division leaders
summary: — John Harbaugh had no time this week for analyzing what has made the Jacksonville Jaguars one of the NFL's top teams.
full_text:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- — John Harbaugh had no time this week for analyzing what has made the Jacksonville Jaguars one of the NFL's top teams.
“I don’t care,” the New York Giants ' coach said. “We don’t even look at that. All you do is you look at the team they are right now.”
The Jaguars now are atop the AFC South at 7-2 after winning three in a row, while Harbaugh's Giants remain in first place in the NFC East despite a bad home loss to Washington that dropped them to 5-3-1. After neither team was favored to win its division at the start of the season, they meet in Week 11 in a game with real playoff implications.
"This is a tough football team," Jacksonville coach Liam Coen said. "It’s going to be a great challenge for us. This game needs to be, in a lot of ways, won in the trenches.”
Those trenches look different, particularly on the Jaguars' side. On offense, they won't have starting center Robert Hainsey , who's out with a strained left knee, and on defense they're adding top trade deadline acquisition Jordan Davis .
This is set to be the debut for Davis and safety Jessie Bates after they were given off last weekend to rest and acclimate.
“What I really hope to see is obviously them to know what they’re doing and have that be priority No. 1: alignment, assignment, communication,” Coen said. “And then just go cut it loose, let it rip, you go be who got you here.”
Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars are looking to set the franchise record with a fifth consecutive 30-point game if they scores that many again Sunday. The Giants rank third in the NFL defending against the pass.
“They’re rushing with a purpose every snap, and then (they have) the ability to match that with how well the secondary’s playing, really, at every position,” Lawrence said. "Their scheme is really good. They’re well-coached. They know what they’re doing. You mix that with some really, really good players, and I think you’re seeing that’s a good defense.”
Giants edge rusher Abdul Carter , who has gone four games without a sack and has just two this season, is out to silence critics, pledging to show them what he can do.
“But I’m not going to chase,” Carter said. "I’m not going to do nothing that’s outside my job. As long as I’m doing everything to contribute to winning, I’ll be all right. We’ve just got to win. That’s all.”

title: Reeling Jets head to LA to face Chargers, who are coming off their first win of the season
summary: — The New York Jets and Los Angeles Chargers are in the same predicament, but the conversation around the two teams could not be more different heading into their matchup on Sunday.
full_text:
EL SEGUNDO, Calif. -- — The New York Jets and Los Angeles Chargers are in the same predicament, but the conversation around the two teams could not be more different heading into their matchup on Sunday.
The Chargers (1-8) are talking about making the unlikeliest playoff push in NFL history, while the Jets (2-8) are being asked about tanking for a better draft pick.
With New York having dropped its past five games, trying to avoid its second losing streak of at least six games in the past two seasons under embattled coach Aaron Glenn, much of the fan base is actively rooting for defeats to keep on coming for the best possible chance to potentially land a franchise quarterback.
According to Glenn, that ideology doesn’t carry over into the locker room.
“I don’t think anybody in this business is here to lose,” Glenn said. “I don’t think anybody in this business can stomach just going out there and trying to lose, that’s just not the way that we’re built, and I’ve said this before, regardless of the record, regardless of what the scoreboard says, anytime anyone of these men go out and they get across that white line, man there’s something that’s in you that stirs up that I’m going to compete my (expletive) off and I’m going to go play and give everything I’ve got. So, it’s just not in these guys’ nature.”
Whether that intrinsic fire is enough for the Jets to overcome their shaky quarterback situation this week is another matter.
Veteran Geno Smith hurt his left ankle in a 31-12 loss to the Bills on Sunday, leaving his status to play this week in question . Rookie Cade Klubnik would make his first career start if Smith isn’t available.
The Chargers have their franchise quarterback in Justin Herbert , and his first turnover-free game of the season helped them end an 11-game winless stretch at the Baltimore Ravens on Monday. The one-two combination of a breakout game from running back Omarion Hampton and tenacious rush defense that conceded just 16 yards sparked the 23-20 victory.
Los Angeles safety Tony Jefferson said the performance validated the team’s belief that they were closer to success than their record had indicated. With a favorable upcoming stretch to try and build some momentum, nobody in their locker room is treating the season as done for, as improbable as it might seem.
“You never know,” said Jefferson, who is in his 12th professional season. “This league is made for crazy stuff like that. So I think the most important part is just keep trying to get wins. Now we got one, try and go on a roll.”

Chargers’ offensive line vs. Jets’ defensive front. Despite starting three rookies up front, Los Angeles paved the way for a season-high 160 yards rushing in the win over Baltimore. That success shortened the game, reducing the pressure on Herbert and an overtaxed defense, and showed the formula for how an underachieving offense can get on track. Following a strong start in their first two games, the Jets have allowed an average of 152.8 yards on the ground in their past eight, including 201 to the Bills last week.

title: Rams' Puka Nacua needs MCL surgery, likely done for season
summary: Rams receiver Puka Nacua, who is currently serving a three-game suspension while on IR, needs surgery to repair his MCL and is likely done for the season.
full_text:
LOS ANGELES -- Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua , who is serving a three-game suspension while on injured reserve, will likely miss at least the rest of the regular season after having surgery on his MCL, coach Sean McVay said Friday.
McVay said Nacua will miss "a couple months" after having the procedure Tuesday. Nacua suffered an MCL sprain and turf toe injuries on the Rams' final offensive snap of their Week 9 victory over the Washington Commanders and was placed on IR on Nov. 12.
"There's a lot of thought and conversations that go into whether you're going to [have surgery] and what's the best plan of action for return to performance for him, not exclusive to this year, but for his career moving forward," McVay said. "And so he was very thorough and deliberate about that, but I did think that this was a possibility.
• March 2026: Woman in Los Angeles files lawsuit accusing Nacua of "unprovoked antisemitic statement," biting her on shoulder. Nacua denies, later enters rehab center. • Nov. 8: Suffers PCL/MCL sprain, turf toe injury in game vs. Washington. • Nov. 12: Nacua placed on injured reserve, to miss at least next 4 games. • Nov. 19: NFL suspends Nacua for three games for personal conduct policy violation. WR to serve ban while on IR; eligible for reinstatement Dec. 14. • Nov. 20: Announced Nacua had MCL surgery on Nov. 17 and is likely out for at least the rest of the regular season. NFL unaware of surgery when it imposed suspension, source tells Adam Schefter.
"I knew that that was a serious injury that he sustained, whether he got it fixed or not with the shot that he took to his knee, he had the toe injury. And so in my mind, this was kind of always a direction that we had to plan upon anyways."
The NFL on Thursday announced Nacua has been suspended for three games for violating the league's personal conduct policy. The suspension came after a woman in Los Angeles filed a lawsuit in March alleging Nacua made an "unprovoked antisemitic statement" and bit her on the shoulder.
The NFL was unaware that Nacua had already undergone surgery when it imposed its suspension, a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter on Friday.
"Based on the steps and the protocols that took place, [the suspension was] something that we thought was a possibility," McVay said. "And it's an unfortunate thing. It's a learning op. It's something that obviously happened a while ago that there's been a lot of discussion and dialogue behind the scenes and we'll learn from it, we'll grow."
In seven games this season, Nacua had 70 catches for 715 yards and four touchdowns.
His injuries happened on a third-down play with the Rams attempting to end the game with a conversion. Nacua rushed for 5 yards but took a hard hit and briefly stayed on the ground before walking off the field.
When asked whether Nacua could return for a possible playoff run, McVay said, "That would be getting way far ahead, so haven't thought about that."
Nacua is playing on the final season of his rookie deal and is scheduled to be an unrestricted free agent this offseason.
