title: How Vikings brought Mexico City's elevation to Minnesota
summary: Rather than spending the week in high altitude like Denver, the Vikings trained in a facility at home.
full_text:
EAGAN, Minn. -- The Minnesota Vikings have moved mountains to prepare for their game Sunday night against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City, which sits at an altitude eight times higher than their team headquarters. 

 Instead of practicing at a higher elevation this week, as the 49ers are doing at the Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs, Colorado, the Vikings brought the altitude to them.

 About five weeks ago, they constructed a temporary altitude room on the second floor of their training center. Players have been doing weekly cardio workouts in altitude settings as high as 12,000 feet ever since, according to vice president of player health and performance Tyler Williams. The team has also provided access to beet juice, which adds nitrates to the bloodstream and could help circulate oxygen more efficiently, as well as sodium bicarbonate supplements to reduce muscle acidity.

 The ideal timeframe for acclimating to extreme altitudes is two weeks, according to Dr. Laura Lewis, the science director of the U.S. Anti-Doping Agency. In other words, neither the Vikings (7-2) nor 49ers (8-1) will be completely adjusted for the conditions they'll encounter Sunday night ( 8:20 p.m. ET, NBC ) at Estadio Azteca, which sits 7,352 feet above sea level -- more than 2,000 feet higher than the most elevated NFL market, Denver at 5,280 feet.

 "There's no smoking gun, home run recipe to attack these trips," Williams said. "Every strategy you look at, you slice and dice and find the benefits and the considerations."

 

 After playing back-to-back games in Europe last season, the Vikings were surprised to learn in May that they would have another international game in 2026. Sunday night's game will be the fifth time they have played outside of the United States in the past five seasons. Co-owner Mark Wilf said in training camp that the team did not "seek out" a game in Mexico City, and coach Kevin O'Connell noted the NFL did not provide any advance notice.

 Williams led the organization's efforts to craft the travel and preparation plan. The Vikings considered multiple options, including spending the week in a region with higher altitude than in Minnesota, which is anywhere between 850-950 feet above sea level, depending on the precise location. But by late spring, they chose to exchange any additional acclimation benefits for conducting their preparation in their home environment.

 They tested some of their plans during an off-site, team-wide workout in Denver prior to the Vikings' Aug. 28 preseason game there. But the decision to remain in Minnesota this week had been based in part on feedback from players who last season spent the week living and practicing in the English countryside, where they were far away from the their usual recovery routines, their personal chefs and bodywork people, and even their own beds.

 

 Williams said he believes "travel fatigue is real" and would have been part of the calculus had the Vikings departed last Sunday's game in Green Bay and spent the week practicing elsewhere. 

 Said Lewis: "If they aren't going to be able to get that exposure, they're best served making sure that they're in as healthy and rested state as possible before traveling."

 In the Vikings' view, altitude is the only substantive difference for a trip to Mexico City compared to what the schedule otherwise would have dictated: a trip to play the 49ers at Levi's Stadium. The flight to Mexico City is about 20 minutes longer, and there is an added benefit of no time change. The Vikings' flight will depart Saturday, as it normally does for Sunday road games, and return immediately after the game.

 "If you do go from Green Bay, Wisconsin, to another destination," O'Connell said, "you basically turn that into any other [full] international game. It is an international game. I'm excited to play in Mexico City. I think the fans are going to be phenomenal, but we are playing on Central Time."

 

 The biggest impact of the altitude, Lewis said, will be elevated breathing rates. Oxygen molecules are more spread out, so each breath takes in less oxygen and thus requires the body to breathe more. That increased rate can lead to quicker dehydration. Common practice in those situations, she said, is to expand the time between exertions in a game. In football, that means more substitutions -- something defensive coordinator Brian Flores said he addressed with the defensive staff this week.

 "It's certainly something that we're going to have to deal with," Flores said, "but there's always elements that we're dealing with, whether it's cold or rain or things like that. ... That's the environment we're going to be in.

 "We'll prepare them to play in that environment, but I'm not going to be silly and say, 'Hey everybody, you got to go in there for 12 straight plays.' We're not doing that. So we'll have rotations. We'll have a plan in place. Inevitably we're going to have to fight through some of that."

 Lewis was less convinced that beet juice will make much of a difference, saying she believes the quantities needed for real impact are unrealistic. She said she encourages athletes of all sports to utilize pure oxygen tanks during competition at altitude, which the NFL will provide Sunday on the sidelines in Mexico City. 

 

 The Vikings have pushed players to use the sauna at their training facility two or three times per week during this ramp-up period, on Williams' belief that heat stress can expand the body's ability to circulate oxygen. But the centerpiece of their efforts is the altitude room, which Williams said is designed as much to familiarize players for what elevated breathing will feel like as it is to achieve a physiological transformation.

 The room contains treadmills, stationary bikes and elliptical trainers, among other equipment, and has room for up to 12 players at a time. By the end of this week, players will have participated in 450 training sessions at altitude since the room was built. 

 "Even though you're not doing a full practice at altitude," Williams said, "you're trying to gain a lower rate of perceived exertion. So, how your body feels. The more often you're exposed to that, you have a lower rate of perceived exertion.

 "You also have a behavioral adaptation. It's how your body responds. How you know how to pace yourself at altitude. How you use breathing strategies in your first exposure compared to your fifth is totally different. It's a learned adaptation."

 Receiver Justin Jefferson said "you feel it every time you go in there, for real." But ultimately, linebacker Eric Wilson said players will just have to "thug it out."

 "There's a science to it they say," Wilson added, "but we've just got to go out there and ball."

title: Bill Belichick, Robert Kraft named Hall of Fame finalists for 2nd straight year
summary: Bill Belichick and Robert Kraft have both advanced to the final round of voting for the Pro Football Hall of Fame for the second straight year.
full_text:
Bill Belichick and Robert Kraft, key to the New England Patriots ' dynasty of six Super Bowl titles, will be considered side by side once again for the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
Belichick and Kraft have both advanced to the final round of voting for the second straight year, the Hall of Fame announced Thursday. Belichick, currently the coach at North Carolina , and Kraft, the Patriots owner, advanced from the coach and contributor subcommittees, respectively, earlier this week to be considered for the Class of 2027.
They will join 13 players, from all eras, to be chosen in the coming weeks by the Hall's Board of Selectors. Those 15 candidates, all considered and voted on together, will be trimmed to the Hall's Class of 2027 in the weeks before the Super Bowl. A class can now have between three and seven inductees, with the most likely class size to be four or five each year. It takes an 80% vote from the selectors in the final voting for enshrinement.
Neither Belichick nor Kraft was selected for the Hall's four-member Class of 2026, resulting in a firestorm of criticism about the selection procedures and committee makeup.
Belichick, the second-winningest coach in NFL history (333 wins, regular season and playoffs combined) behind Hall of Famer Don Shula, won six Super Bowls with the Patriots as a head coach and two more as a New York Giants assistant coach. His omission last year, in his first appearance on the ballot, was a key topic around Super Bowl week in February.
Kraft advanced from the contributor subcommittee last year for the first time. The Patriots' owner since 1994, Kraft hired Belichick in 2000 and the team went on to win six Super Bowls and play in nine Super Bowls overall in their time together. With Kraft as owner, the Patriots have won 20 AFC East titles and played in 11 Super Bowls, including last season when the Patriots advanced to Super Bowl LX.
In September, after a 2½-year review of the selection process that began before Belichick and Kraft's 2026 snub, the Hall announced a smaller group of selectors -- 28, down from 50, with no regional designations -- and the removal of the seniors category for players. The subcommittees for the coach and contributor categories remained in place.
Each year, 25 of the 28 selectors, with three alternates, will vote for the induction class. The alternates will be determined on an annual basis.
The selectors will narrow the final list of candidates from 15 to 10 to seven. Selectors then may vote for six of the seven. Any candidate receiving 80% approval would be inducted.
The Class of 2027 will be announced during the NFL Honors show in Los Angeles during Super Bowl week. The induction ceremony will be held in August in Canton, Ohio.
During Kraft and Belichick's 24-year run together in New England, the franchise was punished twice by the NFL. In 2007, the Patriots were penalized for videotaping New York Jets coaches' signals during a game. Dubbed "Spygate," the Patriots were fined $250,000, Belichick was fined $500,000, and the team forfeited a first-round draft pick.
In 2015, as a result of the "Deflategate" investigation, quarterback Tom Brady was suspended for four games (served in the 2016 season) and the Patriots were fined $1 million in addition to the loss of two draft picks.
Kraft has chaired the NFL's media/broadcast committee for more than 10 years. He helped secure an 11-year broadcast rights deal worth $113 billion in 2021 and was a key figure in labor negotiations with the NFL Players Association for the current collective bargaining agreement that runs through 2030.
He was picked as a finalist from a group that included Doug Williams; late Chicago Bears owner Virginia McCaskey; longtime NFL player, scout and personnel executive John Wooten; and former Canton Bulldogs owner Ralph Hay.
Belichick advanced from the coaching subcommittee over a group that included Tom Coughlin, Mike Holmgren, Dan Reeves and Mike Shanahan.
Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

title: Saints, Justin Reid 'working through' potential release
summary: Saints and safety Justin Reid are "working through some things" regarding the veteran safety's potential release, defensive coordinator Brandon Staley said Thursday.
full_text:
METAIRIE, La. -- The New Orleans Saints and safety Justin Reid are "working through some things" regarding the veteran safety's potential release, defensive coordinator Brandon Staley said Thursday.
"I think that's going to come to a resolution here shortly," Staley said.
Staley said Reid's request took him by surprise, and said Reid has mostly spoken with Kellen Moore about it this week.
"Justin's been a professional since he's been here and I know that I've really enjoyed working with him. There's some things that we all want a little bit more of from a productivity standpoint. But in terms of the fit, in terms of how he's been here, he's been a pleasure to coach. So we'll just leave it at that," Staley said.
Reid, 29, had been with the Saints for two seasons after signing a 3-year deal worth $10.5 million annually during the 2025 free agency period. Reid had one year remaining on the contract, which he restructured in March to lower his cap number to $5.2 million.
He is the second team captain to ask for his release in a year after wideout Brandin Cooks asked for and was granted his release a year ago. It took several days after Cooks was granted a release by the team to become official as both sides worked out a resolution.
"I think the football business side of things is different than the culture of the locker room," Staley said. "I think just speaking for our defensive culture, it's been strong for two years. I think that we have a very close group. I think that this group of guys has really come together the right way. I think last year, losing Demario [Davis], there were a lot of questions on what our defense would look like. And I think that we've been able to answer that so far with the production of our group and then also the connection of our group.
"I think that that's been a strength of ours and we continue to play the right way, practice the right way. I think this is just one of those things ... it's just a football business matter and these things happen. And again, I'll leave those specifics to Kellen."
Reid was voted a team captain in both of his seasons in New Orleans, but struggled this season with the Saints secondary giving up an average of 231 yards per game (21st in the NFL). Reid publicly argued with fans on X after the Saints gave up more than 400 yards in a 45-24 primetime loss to the Atlanta Falcons in Week 4.
Reid pushed back against a fan that said he didn't make any plays. He followed up with a now-deleted post the next day saying "I'm a grown man FROM Louisiana. I don't need coddling from nobody but some of yall trying to make it seem like I don't care or show low effort. On the contrary I probably care the most!! I probably should not of got on twitter so quickly after the game but I'm upset too. I got pride and I ain't just gonna be punching bag for negativity and be silent about it."
"Justin has been a professional since he's been here. I know I've really enjoyed working with him," Staley said.
Reid was selected by the Houston Texans in the third round of the 2018 NFL draft. He also spent three seasons with the Kansas City Chiefs , where he was a part of two Super Bowl winning teams.
"We never know what people are going through," safety Jordan Howden said. "So like I said, it's the next man up and we all got a job to do. Somebody has to go out there and play. We got to step up and be ready for this weekend. So he's my brother and I hope everything's good, but we still got a job to do."
New Orleans.Football first reported the news that Reid had requested his release.

title: Pass rush part of the focus for the Saints and Bears going into Sunday's game
summary: — Carl Granderson and Chase Young form a potent 1-2 punch on defense for the New Orleans Saints. Jeffery Simmons is a force on the defensive line for the Chicago Bears.
full_text:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- — Carl Granderson and Chase Young form a potent 1-2 punch on defense for the New Orleans Saints . Jeffery Simmons is a force on the defensive line for the Chicago Bears .
Granderson and Young are two of the biggest concerns for Chicago coach Ben Johnson going into Sunday's game against New Orleans. Same goes for Saints coach Kellen Moore and Simmons.
“They’re good not just only in the pass game, they’re great edge setters in the run game as well,” Johnson said. “So big challenge there on both sides.”
Granderson has a team-high 8 1/2 sacks in eight games in his eighth season with New Orleans, matching his career high set in the 2023 season. He had one of the Saints' three sacks in Sunday's 20-17 loss to Carolina.
Young has eight sacks in nine games in his third year with New Orleans. He had a career-best 10 sacks last season.
Granderson and Young are a potent outside duo, and Kaden Elliss also contributes to the pass rush. He had a team-high 15 tackles and a sack against the Panthers.
“I think he’s one of the better pressuring linebackers in the NFL,” Johnson said. "And so, they’re not afraid to plug him in A or B gap and make it tough on your protection scheme. That combination, I think, from the interior with him with those two edge rushers is what makes their pressure package so dangerous.”
Chicago returns from its bye week with a four-game winning streak, helped by the acquisition of Simmons in a blockbuster trade with Tennessee on Oct. 29. The All-Pro defensive tackle has one sack in each of his first two games with his new team.
Beyond his pass-rushing abilities, Simmons also has made life easier on Chicago's linebackers and defensive ends through the attention he demands up front.
“He’s one of the top interior defensive linemen in the league," Moore said. "We saw him last year in Tennessee. ... He impacts every game he’s in and it’s going to be something we obviously have to have awareness with.”
A fast start could provide a big lift for New Orleans when it comes to dealing with Simmons and the rest of Chicago's defense on the road. But fast starts have been hard to come by for the Saints this season.
New Orleans has scored an NFL-low nine points in the first quarter of games this season while Chicago leads the league with 76 points in the opening period.
“It really frustrates us, as players, because we understand you can’t go into a game, a first quarter, a first half, and not put any points on the board, and expect to play clean, winning football," Saints quarterback Tyler Shough said.

title: The Steelers last won in Philadelphia in 1965. Can they top an Eagles team on 7-game losing streak?
summary: — Perhaps the Steelers should have stayed attached at the hip pads with the Eagles — as they were when they merged for the 1943 season to form the Steagles — to avoid such an ignominious losing streak in Philadelphia.
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA -- — Perhaps the Steelers should have stayed attached at the hip pads with the Eagles — as they were when they merged for the 1943 season to form the Steagles — to avoid such an ignominious losing streak in Philadelphia.
Pittsburgh's losing streak in Philly spans 11 games over six decades, three stadiums, four Steelers coaches including Chuck Noll, Bill Cowher and Mike Tomlin and has even predated — wait for it — the Super Bowl.
That's right, the Steelers haven't won in Philadelphia since 1965. The first Super Bowl was played after the 1966 season on Jan. 15, 1967.
Philadelphia beat Pittsburgh on Dec. 4, 1966, the first of four straight wins at Franklin Field. The Steelers won three more times at Veterans Stadium and all four games at their current home, Lincoln Financial Field.
The average margin of victory for the Eagles over the last three games (2016, 2022 and 2024) is 22.3 points, while the overall margin of victory since the streak started is 11.7 points.
“We feel like we need to take care of that,” coach Mike McCarthy said.
Good news for the Steelers: This should be their best chance to win in Philly in years, even as Pittsburgh is reeling from a 38-18 beatdown at the hands of Joe Burrow , Ja’Marr Chase and the scorching Cincinnati Bengals .
The Steelers are the betting favorite to win Sunday and snap the streak, and for good reason.
This anticipated showdown when the NFL schedule dropped has instead turned into such a must-miss contest as the Eagles slog through a seven-game losing streak that the game was bumped from the national TV window to a pedestrian 1 p.m. EST kickoff.
If a losing streak falls in Philadelphia, and no one is around to watch it, does it count?
“I’d have to look and really study to see what those glaring weaknesses are,” Steelers defensive tackle Cam Heyward said. “But a lot of respect for what they got over there. They’ve won Super Bowls, they’ve had some really good teams, some really great fronts, so we’re going to have our hands full.”
While Pittsburgh appears plenty capable of reaching the playoffs for the sixth time in seven seasons, the Eagles are set for their first losing season under sixth-year coach Nick Sirianni.
Sirianni promised a deep dive into the Eagles' woes during their bye week and returned with no obvious answers. He reaffirmed his commitment to quarterback Joe Milton for a second straight game — replacing the ineffective Tanner McKee , who replaced the injured Jalen Hurts — and offensive coordinator Sean Mannion remains the play-caller even as he leads one of the worst offenses in the NFL.
“I think we have a good plan of action moving forward of the things that we want to do to move forward and to get better,” Sirianni said. “Obviously, we haven’t been good enough on offense, but I like our plan of attack and our process that we went through last week.”
Playing against a stale offense should be more good news for the Steelers.
If the Steelers are looking for one more sign that this should be the year they snap the streak, consider this: The Giants lost 13 straight games in Philadelphia until they finally won two weeks ago.
Yeah, it's been that kind of year for the Eagles.

Rodgers has been sacked just six times in Pittsburgh's four home games this season (all wins). The Eagles are playing for the first time since they traded defensive tackle Jordan Davis to Jacksonville. title: Vikings-49ers matchup in Mexico features the best defense vs. the best offense
summary: When Brock Purdy last walked off the field after playing Minnesota in 2024, he sought out Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores an complimented him on...
full_text:
When Brock Purdy last walked off the field after playing Minnesota in 2024 , he sought out Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores an complimented him on his “crazy” scheme.
Flores has dialed it up even more in the two years since that game, setting up one of the most intriguing matchups of the season when the Vikings (7-2) take on the San Francisco 49ers (8-1) on Sunday night in Mexico City in a matchup of the game's most efficient offense against the league's fiercest defense.
“He’s more unique than all the other 31 guys,” 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said of Flores' heavy blitz packages. “He’s the one guy who commits to this and it’s not just a fad for these nine games or whatever. He’s been doing it his whole time in Minnesota. He did the same thing in Miami. He’s as good as it gets at that stuff. ... They put so much pressure on the quarterback, the play-caller, the O-Line, the receivers, on everybody.”
The Vikings have been dominant defensively with 37 sacks and 17 takeaways, becoming the first team to reach those marks in the first nine games since Tampa Bay in 2000.
Minnesota has allowed 23 points or fewer in every game this season and leads the league in points per game allowed (14), passer rating allowed (69.5) and ranks second in yards per play allowed (4.55).
San Francisco is at the top of the rankings when it comes to offense after putting up 584 yards and three touchdowns of at least 65 yards in a 46-40 win at Dallas last week .
The Niners are second in the league in scoring (31.2 points per game) and rank first in yards per play (6.66) with an intricate offense coached by Shanahan, expertly run by Purdy and featuring dynamic playmakers such as Christian McCaffrey , George Kittle and Deebo Samuel.
Flores said the Niners are “elite” at almost everything on offense and facing Shanahan will offer a stiff challenge.
“Where do I start? Everything is high level,” he said. “It’s thought out. There’s a rhyme and reason behind it all. There’s complementary plays. ‘Oh, you think I’ve got something? No, I don’t.’ ... He’s done a great job for a long, long time, and they’ve got a lot of great players. But we’ve got to play well. It makes you play honest.”
Minnesota (7-2) vs. San Francisco (8-1) in Mexico City
When/where to watch: Sunday, 8:20 p.m. EST, NBC.
Against the spread: Vikings 6-3; 49ers 5-4.
Last week: Vikings beat Green Bay 30-10; 49ers beat Dallas 46-40.
Last meeting: Vikings beat 49ers 23-17 on Sept. 15, 2024, in Minneapolis.
Series record: Tied 25-25-1.
Vikings blitzes against Purdy. Minnesota blitzes at the highest rate in the league at 72% according to NFL NextGen stats, more than double the league average. No QB has handled the blitz as well as Purdy, who is 41 for 58 for 728 yards, 11 TDs, one INT and a 145.5 passer rating when blitzed, according to Sportradar. He has been sacked nine times for the fourth-highest rate when blitzed.
— The Vikings are 5-1 in international games, while the 49ers are 4-1, including a win in Week 1 against the Rams in Australia. San Francisco has split two games in Mexico, losing to Arizona in 2005 and beating the Cardinals in 2022.
— San Francisco is scoring TDs on 82.8% of red zone drives for the highest rate of any offense since at least 2000. Minnesota is allowing TDs on 25% of red zone drives for the lowest rate of any defense since at least 2000.
— Vikings QB Kirk Cousins will start against the 49ers for the second time in three weeks after being acquired in a trade from Las Vegas. This will be the 10th time a QB started against the same opponent for two different teams in a season. Cousins was 22 for 32 for 212 yards, one TD and three INTs against San Francisco in a Week 9 loss.
— The Vikings are allowing a 69.5 passer rating this season. The only team this decade to finish a season below 70 was Buffalo in 2021 at 65.3.
— Minnesota's Andrew Van Ginkel (8 1/2) and Dallas Turner (8) both rank in the top five in the NFL in sacks.
— San Francisco has 2,662 yards from scrimmage and 30 TDs from players age 30 or older. That’s more than double the next highest in yards (Ravens, 1,172) and TDs (Ravens, 13).
— McCaffrey is tied for the league lead with 13 TDs this season and is the fifth RB ever with at least six seasons with 12 or more TDs.
— The 49ers have had at least 190 yards rushing in back-to-back games for the first time since the final two games of 2014.
— The 49ers lead the NFL by converting 52% of third downs.

title: Bucs QB Baker Mayfield hopes to play Sunday despite foot injury: 'I feel ready'
summary: Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is hoping to play Sunday against the Lions after he sustained a foot injury two weeks ago against the Chicago Bears.
full_text:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is hoping to play Sunday against the Detroit Lions after he sustained a foot injury two weeks ago against the Chicago Bears .
Mayfield didn't participate in the Buccaneers' practice Wednesday because of the injury but was a limited participant Thursday.
"I feel ready," Mayfield said after practice.
Mayfield said he sustained his foot injury early in the 27-24 loss to the Bears in Week 9. He said Thursday the Buccaneers' bye last week came at the perfect time because of his injury.
Mayfield said he "felt good" in Thursday's practice and hopes to do more in Friday's session.
Asked what he needs to do to be confident that he can play Sunday, Mayfield said he just has to continue what he's been doing since the Bears game.
"Doing everything I can to get all the treatment and rehab possible and prepare like a professional," he said. "So, for me ... if I continue that, I imagine being able to play."
Buccaneers offensive coordinator Zac Robinson said Thursday that Mayfield "moved around fairly well" in Thursday's practice and that the team would see how he responds Friday to back-to-back practices.
Mayfield said he would have "no shame" if it comes to the point he has to admit that rookie Jalon Daniels gives the Buccaneers a better chance to win at Detroit.
Daniels started three games for the Buccaneers earlier this season when Mayfield was sidelined by a dislocated thumb.
Mayfield has thrown for 922 yards, completing 60.6% of his pass attempts, with three touchdowns and four interceptions this season. Daniels has thrown for 501 yards, completing 61.2% of his attempts, with three touchdowns and five interceptions.
The Buccaneers are just 3-6 this season, but that makes them contenders in the NFC South, where they are tied with the New Orleans Saints with both teams one game behind the division-leading Carolina Panthers (4-5).

title: Titans defense crumbling post-Jeffery Simmons, Amani Hooker trades
summary: The moves Tennessee made might have helped the rebuilding process, but it also impacted the current team.
full_text:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- Getting off to a 1-8 start is disappointing in itself, but the way the Tennessee Titans are losing games as of late is even more dispiriting.

 Titans coach Robert Saleh is known for his success as a defensive coordinator with the San Francisco 49ers , so it's reasonable to expect Tennessee to be solid on that side of the ball.

 Yet the Titans find themselves having lost three consecutive games with the defense giving up at least 400 total yards of offense in each of them. Trading defensive tackle  Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears and safety  Amani Hooker to the Buffalo Bills took away two of Tennessee's best defensive players in the weeks leading up to the Nov. 10  NFL trade deadline might have helped the rebuilding process, but it didn't help the current team.

 The Titans gave up 43 points to the Cincinnati Bengals  in Week 8 without Simmons, even though Hooker finished with three interceptions in his final game with the team. The Jacksonville Jaguars dropped 40 points on the Titans the next game out of their Week 9 bye after Hooker was traded. 

 "I really felt like we were trending towards being a top-10 defense after the Indianapolis game," Saleh said Wednesday. "These last three weeks, it hasn't been good enough, not even close. It has been disappointing, and obviously the objective is to get back to where we were trending a few weeks ago."

 

 The secondary has been one of the biggest contributors to the defensive shortcomings. Blown coverages, poor tackling and simply getting beaten by better players have led to opposing quarterbacks finishing with 300-plus yards passing in each of the past three games. 

 Cincinnati's passing game featuring Joe Burrow , Ja'Maar Chase and Tee Higgins ' production was video game-like. Burrow threw for 462 yards and five touchdowns. Higgins caught 10 passes for 155 yards and two touchdowns. Chase posted his first 100-yard game (155) of the season on 11 catches, including a touchdown. 

 Given how elite Cincinnati's offense is, it's understandable that the trio put up numbers. But Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson passed for 308 yards rookie wideout KC Concepcion surprisingly exploded for a career-high 129 receiving yards in Cleveland's 27-24 win against the Titans. 

 Trevor Lawrence 's 352 passing yards and three touchdowns, along with a career-best 152 receiving yards from Parker Washington , led to the Jaguars handing Tennessee its third loss.

 "There's going to be moments where you've got to win a one-on-one [in coverage] if we want to be able to get pressure on the quarterback and do those things," Saleh said. 

 "That's something that we're not proud of," linebacker Cedric Gray added. "What we can do is just try to step up and figure out what the problems are, what the disconnect is in certain situations and why we're not delivering and making plays when we need to make those plays."

 The offense and the defense are going in different directions.

 Titans QB  Cam Ward and the offense are averaging 27.7 points over the past three games, pushing their season average to 18.6, up from their 14-point average the first six games of the season. That helped spark the recent offensive surge, but it hasn't resulted in wins because the defense has allowed 36.7 points per game over that span, dropping their season average from 21.6 points per game (13th in the league) to 26.6 (27th). 

 "You can't win allowing 30, 40 points, either one of those," Titans safety Kevin Winston Jr . said. "We want to make sure we limit that to below 20 if we can to give our offense a chance. Our mindset is: if the offense scores 20-plus, we should win. We've got to get that fixed."

 Edge defender Jacob Martin has been one of the few bright spots on the defense. Martin has already set a career high with 7.5 sacks in nine games. He has played for Saleh before when they were with the New York Jets in 2022, so there's familiarity. Martin believes the Titans' success on defense comes down to processing things faster.

 

 Saleh decided to make a philosophical shift on offense so Ward would have more command and show that he can be the franchise quarterback the team desperately needs. Martin indicated that perhaps a similar shift should be made to allow the defense to process and play faster.

 The losing streak has caused Saleh and the defensive staff to consider if they're "pushing the envelope too much" with the number of checks to get the right call against the right formation to create the right player positioning. That takes a lot of pre-snap thinking and communication, which could be putting the guys in the wrong headspace and keep them from playing the fast, violent style of defense Saleh wants. The coaching staff's solution is to simplify things by delivering the call to the players in a way that allows them to get the call knowing exactly what they're asked to do without worrying what the formation is.

 "As a player on the field, it's good getting simplified playcalls or things that have easy answers," Martin said. "Like it's not a whole bunch of one-offs; if they line up here we do this or line up there, and we do that. I think it allows guys to play faster with their feet on the ground and not in the middle of communication while the ball's being snapped. I think it will allow guys to play faster for sure."

 The first test will be when the Titans face the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Sunday ( 1 p.m. ET, Fox ). The Cowboys' offense is scoring 28.6 points per game. The road doesn't get easier after Dallas, with visits to Jacksonville (which ranks fourth in the league at 29.9 points per game) and in Week 14 the Detroit Lions , who are tied with Dallas for the fifth-best scoring offense. Buckle up.

title: Titans' Calvin Ridley facing misdemeanor assault charge over airport incident
summary: Titans wide receiver Calvin Ridley is facing a misdemeanor assault charge as a result of a Nov. 7 incident at Nashville International Airport.
full_text:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- Titans wide receiver Calvin Ridley is facing a misdemeanor assault charge as a result of a Nov. 7 incident at Nashville International Airport, according to records obtained Thursday from the Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority.
The Class B misdemeanor assault charge involves intentional or knowing physical contact that a reasonable person would consider extremely offensive or provocative. It carries a penalty of up to six months in jail and a fine of up to $500.
Ridley is due in Metropolitan General Sessions Court on Dec. 7.
Ridley gave his account of the incident to the media on Nov. 11, saying he took his truck keys from an airport valet attendant who had refused to give them to him because he didn't have the valet ticket. He said he had shown the attendant multiple forms of identification and a photo as proof of ownership of the truck.
According to Ridley, when he took the keys, the attendant yelled that Ridley had broken his finger.
The Titans said they have been in communication with the Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority.
Ridley signed a four-year, $92 million contract with the Titans in 2024. The veteran receiver has six receptions for 91 yards through seven games this season.

title: Washington Commanders unveil 'Beer Spear' ahead of 'Hail Raiser' debut on 'MNF'
summary: The limited-edition collectible vessel can hold 16 ounces of beer, equipped with a gold spear at the end of it.
full_text:
Monday marks the Washington Commanders ' debut of their new alternate uniforms, the "Hail Raiser."  The Commanders will be ringing in the all-black threads with a similarly themed concession item: the "Beer Spear."

 

 It's a limited-edition collectible vessel that can hold 16 ounces of beer, equipped with a gold spear at the end of it. Featured on the vessel is the Commanders' new W-spear logo, which also appears on the Hail Raiser helmet. The logo includes a gold spear interwoven into a burgundy "W" with gold outline.

 The Commanders announced the new item Thursday. It will be available for purchase at select concession stands during the rest of the Commanders' home games, starting on "Monday Night Football" against the Cincinnati Bengals .

 

 Washington already boasts a crab stuffed pretzel at its concession stands. The pretzel is shaped like a crab and is filled with lemon tarragon crab dip topped with garlic butter and grated parmesan cheese.

 The beer spear is just another in the list of creative sport-related concession items that deal with beer. Some MLB teams have the "beer bat." The NHL's Buffalo Sabres introduced the "beer sabres" last season, while the Philadelphia Flyers countered with the "beer skate." Each of them became instantly popular among fans and collectors alike.

 Teams haven't stopped experimenting for similar items, and with a beer spear now off the table, the natural evolution could be a beer shield.

title: Sam Hartman's next drive: 'The Bachelor' questions answered
summary: A guide to the Commanders quarterback's upcoming search for love and how his NFL commitments could shape the season.
full_text:
At the Washington Commanders ' Thursday practice, a dozen or so cameras trained on the club's fourth quarterback. Normally, this player would be ignored during a shooting period, but Washington's fourth quarterback is Sam Hartman , who despite having never played in an NFL regular-season game, will be the next lead of "The Bachelor" in the 30th season of the show.

 After a good throw, Hartman said to the other three quarterbacks: "I hope they post that one."

 At the end of the throwing session, a Commanders player said to the media focused on Hartman, "Do you guys want a hair flip?"

 When Hartman, the practice squad quarterback known for his movie-star quality hair, was announced as the next Bachelor last week, he became the second active NFL player to take the lead title. His short and sweet "Good Morning America" appearance left both football and "The Bachelor" fans with many pressing questions and hilarious hypotheticals. 

 What happens if the 3-5-1 Commanders miraculously make the postseason and they need Hartman but he has to go film "The Bachelor"? With the show premiering on March 21, just 10 weeks after Week 18 and nine weeks after the wild-card round, will Hartman have to leave for the Bachelor mansion in California to begin filming? Though Hartman hasn't played in a regular-season game, he has served as the emergency third quarterback for a stretch in each of the past two seasons, and with the state of the Commanders' often-injured quarterbacks room, does this production schedule mean the backup to the backup position could end up in jeopardy? (this might seem farfetched but the Commanders played their third-in-line quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis in London this season, when starter Jayden Daniels was out and then backup Marcus Mariota got hurt).

 And "The Bachelor" franchise has historically had a no phones policy for participants. While Hartman will not be demanding a huge crowd of clubs in free agency, how will he stay updated of any new offers if he finishes the season on the practice squad and becomes a street free agent? Will he have his phone to talk to his agent?

 Fear not, for Hartman addressed the media Thursday after practice and ESPN has attempted to answer these extremely urgent questions for the sake of Commanders fans and contestants vying for his attention, who might be curious about his NFL obligations and financial status going forward.

 Let's start with the basics.

 

 How did he become a candidate for "The Bachelor"? 

 Hartman told reporters Thursday that ABC reached out to him, "just kind of out of the blue." He said Wake Forest is a "pipeline" for "The Bachelor."

 Hartman is the third Wake Forest football alumni to participate in "The Bachelor"  franchise. Matt James and Tyler Cameron also played for Wake Forest.

 The ACC Network called Wake Forest "Bachelor U" on Instagram after Hartman's announcement. 

 
 Has an active NFL player done this before, and what distinguishes Hartman's situation from previous athletes in the franchise? 

 The current host of "The Bachelor" franchise, Jesse Palmer, was the first professional athlete to appear on the show. His season aired in April 2004 when he was the Giants ' backup quarterback. Palmer, a fourth-round draft pick, started in three NFL games during his career.

 Former NFL tight end and "The Bachelor" contestant Clay Harbor (100 games played, 39 starts) recently vented on Chicago station 104.3 The Score about Hartman's lack of NFL playing experience. "You present yourself as an NFL player and you have never taken an NFL snap in an NFL football game," Harbor said. "I take a little bit of an exception, that's a little bit of false advertisement."

 
 What should viewers know about his college and NFL career? 

 Not much to see here in terms of NFL action. Hartman went undrafted and has never played in a regular-season game, but he has seven preseason appearances.

 In college, Hartman played five seasons at Wake Forest and transferred to Notre Dame for his final year of eligibility in 2023. He led Notre Dame to a 9-3 season where they outscored opponents 509-207 .

 
 What is his current roster status? 

 Hartman is currently on the Commanders' practice squad, which means he attends meetings and participates in practice like every player on the active roster, but he does not dress on game days and he cannot play in a game unless he is elevated to the active roster.

 Hartman has been elevated to the active roster twice in his three seasons with the Commanders and has served as the club's emergency third quarterback for the first five games of his rookie season in 2024 and the last two games of the 2025 season, when Daniels and Mariota were injured. As the emergency third quarterback, Hartman was a game-day inactive and did not count toward the 53 active players on game day.

 
 How much money does he make? 

 Hartman's practice squad contract pays him $247,500 for this season if he remains on the practice squad for the rest of the season. If he is elevated to the active roster, he would earn more money. As an undrafted free agent in 2024, the Commanders reportedly paid Hartman one of the biggest guarantees of all undrafted free agents: a $20,000 signing bonus and $225,000 base salary guarantee. 

 
 What will happen to him after the NFL season? 

 When Hartman's practice squad contract expires (one week after the final game of the season) he becomes a street free agent. This means he will be immediately available to sign with any other club and does not have to wait for the new league year to begin on March 11, like an unrestricted free agent. The Commanders have the option to sign him to a futures contract to hold his rights, like they did in 2024 when he also finished the season on the practice squad. In this scenario, phone access could be important because he might have offers from other NFL clubs to consider.

 If he is elevated onto the 53-man roster this season (a real possibility since he has been in each of his past two seasons), then he will become an exclusive rights free agent, meaning the Commanders have the first right to "tender" him to a new contract, and if they choose to do that, he will not be able to negotiate with any other club.

 
 Has Hartman ever seen an episode of the show? 

 No. He told reporters he is open to advice, and to please let him know any dos and don'ts.

 "I'm gonna probably do some tape watching after the season's over, and study up, get the DVSport clicker going kind of break down, go from first down to second down, third down, and finally end at the fantasy suites."

 
 How will he balance football and filming? When does filming begin? 

 There is no set schedule for filming yet, but Hartman told reporters, "Once the season's over, I'll head out." ESPN also confirmed with ABC that "The Bachelor" will start filming after the Commanders' season ends. So, breathe easy, Commanders fan, your quarterback depth is safe, all the way down to QB4.

 Hartman's NFL agent Brian McLaughlin told ESPN that the "Filming schedule is still being worked out to accommodate the [Commanders'] schedule. He did run it by the team and they understood."

 ABC declined to comment what locations Hartman would be traveling to, but historically the show begins filming in L.A. and then travels -- both domestic and international -- as the season progresses.

 
 How long is production expected to last? 

 Unknown. The production timeline varies from season to season. "The Bachelor" is filmed in advance, rather than airing live, so Hartman's time in front of the cameras will be wrapped before it premieres.

 
 Does filming overlap with team workouts, minicamp, training camp? 

 No. After the Commanders' season ends, Hartman has no further obligations to the team until April, which is the start of voluntary offseason training activities.

 Before being cast, did he discuss participating with his team and did he need permission? 

 Hartman said Thursday that…
